TL;DR

Renders every authored reference document, the tabular crosswalks, and a live descriptives + QA sheet into one self-contained output/docs/index.html.

How it works

Design rule: nothing is written twice.

The markdown files under reference/ stay the canonical prose; this script only renders them. Every number on the Descriptives and QA sheets is computed from data/final at build time — never typed. That is deliberate: the 2026-07-16 audit found that every stale claim in the project (a README two reorgs out of date, a "91 %" that was really 68 %, a documented illegitimacy_rate that did not exist, a linkage "~90" that was 144) was a hand-maintained copy of a fact that lived somewhere else. A hand-written HTML would have been the most authoritative-looking copy of all.

So: if a fact is wrong here, fix its source (the markdown, or the pipeline) and rebuild. Do not edit the generated HTML.

Contents

Overview (README + build stamp + module index) · Descriptives (live) · QA (live invariants) · Pipeline · Place matching · Ranks · Variables · Data dictionary · Census codebook · Data sources · Decisions · Audit.

Dependencies: markdown, pygments, jinja2 (all already required). Optional: latex2mathml → self-contained offline math; without it the page falls back to KaTeX from a CDN (needs a network on first view).

Run: python utils/docs/build_docs.py # -> output/docs/index.html Rebuild after any pipeline change or notebook re-run.

def ix_head(text: str, *, level: int = 2, ix: bool = False, hover: bool = False,
            attrs: str = "") -> str:
    """A section heading carrying its affordance chips.

    Args:
        text: Heading text, already HTML-safe.
        level: Heading level, 2 or 3.
        ix: The block has controls — click, toggle, drag, filter.
        hover: The block is static but reveals exact values on hover.
        attrs: Extra attributes for the tag (``id=…``, ``class=…``).

    Returns:
        The complete ``<hN>…</hN>`` element. Both chips may apply at once: a figure with a
        view toggle whose bars also carry tooltips is honestly both.
    """
    chips = (" " + IXBADGE if ix else "") + (" " + HOVERBADGE if hover else "")
    a = (" " + attrs.strip()) if attrs else ""
    return f"<h{level}{a}>{text}{chips}</h{level}>"

def favicon_href() -> str:
    """The favicon as a data: URI, ready for ``<link rel="icon">``."""

def md_to_html(text: str) -> str:
    """Convert markdown to HTML, protecting fenced code and $…$ math from the parser."""
    fences: list[str] = []
    def _stash_fence(m):
        fences.append(m.group(0))
        return f"\n\nZZFENCEZZ{len(fences)-1}ZZ\n\n"
    text = re.sub(r"```.*?```", _stash_fence, text, flags=re.S)

    maths: list[tuple[str, bool]] = []
    def _stash(tex: str, disp: bool) -> str:
        maths.append((tex.strip(), disp))
        return f"ZZMATHZZ{len(maths)-1}ZZ"
    text = re.sub(r"\$\$(.+?)\$\$", lambda m: _stash(m.group(1), True), text, flags=re.S)
    text = INLINE_MATH_RE.sub(lambda m: _stash(m.group(1), False), text)

    out = _md.markdown(text, extensions=["tables", "sane_lists", "attr_list", "toc", "def_list"],
                       output_format="html5")

    for i, block in enumerate(fences):
        rendered = _render_fence(block)
        out = out.replace(f"<p>ZZFENCEZZ{i}ZZ</p>", rendered).replace(f"ZZFENCEZZ{i}ZZ", rendered)
    for i, (tex, disp) in enumerate(maths):
        rendered = _render_math(tex, disp)
        if disp:
            rendered = f'<div class="mathblock">{rendered}</div>'
        out = out.replace(f"<p>ZZMATHZZ{i}ZZ</p>", rendered).replace(f"ZZMATHZZ{i}ZZ", rendered)

    # Any surviving "$...$" means the stash regex missed it (inline maths must sit on one
    # line). Markdown will then have eaten its underscores as emphasis — which is how a
    # stray </em> once leaked italics across a sheet. Surface it instead of shipping it.
    for stray in STRAY_MATH_RE.findall(re.sub(r"<(code|pre)[\s>].*?</\1>", "", out, flags=re.S)):
        MATH_WARNINGS.append(f"unconverted inline maths (wrap it onto one line): {stray[:60]!r}")

    # markdown tables get a scrolling wrapper — a wide table (the 9-column legal-sources
    # one) must scroll, not squeeze its columns until the headers break apart
    out = re.sub(r"<table>(.*?)</table>",
                 lambda m: f'<div class="tblwrap"><table>{m.group(1)}</table></div>',
                 out, flags=re.S)

    # cross-document links → anchors; dead relative links → inert code spans
    def _fix_link(m):
        href, inner = m.group(1), m.group(2)
        path = href.split("#")[0]
        for tail, anchor in _MD_PATH_ANCHORS.items():
            if path.endswith(tail):
                return f'<a href="{anchor}">{inner}</a>'
        base = href.split("/")[-1].split("#")[0]
        if base in _MD_ANCHORS:
            return f'<a href="{_MD_ANCHORS[base]}">{inner}</a>'
        if href.startswith(("http://", "https://", "#", "mailto:")):
            return m.group(0)
        return f"<code>{inner}</code>"                 # local path — not navigable from the HTML
    out = re.sub(r'<a href="([^"]+)">(.*?)</a>', _fix_link, out, flags=re.S)
    return out

def build_stamp() -> dict:
    """Provenance of this build: when, from which commit, and whether the tree was clean.

    Shown in the sidebar so a reader can always tell what they are looking at. ``dirty``
    means the page was generated from uncommitted work — the numbers are real, but they
    correspond to no commit. ``data_built`` is the newest mtime under ``data/final``, so a
    page older than the data is visible at a glance.
    """
    sha = _git("rev-parse", "--short", "HEAD")
    branch = _git("rev-parse", "--abbrev-ref", "HEAD")
    dirty = bool(_git("status", "--porcelain"))
    newest = max((p.stat().st_mtime for p in FIN.rglob("*") if p.is_file()), default=0)
    now = _dt.datetime.now()
    return {
        "built": now.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M"),
        "built_epoch": int(now.timestamp()),
        "sha": sha or "—", "branch": branch or "—", "dirty": dirty,
        # False on a machine that holds the files but not the repository (a synced copy).
        # Without it an empty `git status` read as "clean tree" — a claim about a history
        # the build could not see.
        "git": bool(sha),
        "data_built": (_dt.datetime.fromtimestamp(newest).strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M")
                       if newest else "—"),
        # data newer than the page can only mean the pipeline was re-run after this build
        "data_epoch": int(newest),
        "mathml": HAVE_MATHML,
    }

def collect_scripts(dirty_files: set[str]) -> tuple[list[dict], list[dict]]:
    """Per-module sheets + a flat record of every public symbol (for the usage index)."""
    corpus = _searchable_corpus()
    sheets: list[dict] = []
    symbols: list[dict] = []

    for p in sorted(ROOT.joinpath("utils").rglob("*.py")):
        if "_archive" in p.parts or p.name == "__init__.py":
            continue
        rel = str(p.relative_to(ROOT)).replace("\\", "/")
        src = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
        try:
            tree = ast.parse(src)
        except SyntaxError:
            continue
        doc = ast.get_docstring(tree) or ""
        ver = (re.search(r'^__version__\s*=\s*"([^"]+)"', src, re.M) or [None, "—"])[1]
        mid = rel.replace("/", "-").replace(".py", "")

        funcs = [n for n in tree.body
                 if isinstance(n, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef, ast.ClassDef))
                 and not n.name.startswith("_")]
        # public module constants: plain AND annotated assignments (RANK_ORDINAL_HABSBURG:
        # dict[str,int] = {...} is an AnnAssign — missing these would hide the rank ladders)
        consts = []
        for n in tree.body:
            names = []
            if isinstance(n, ast.Assign):
                names = [t.id for t in n.targets if isinstance(t, ast.Name)]
            elif isinstance(n, ast.AnnAssign) and isinstance(n.target, ast.Name):
                names = [n.target.id]
            for nm in names:
                if nm.isupper() and not nm.startswith("_"):
                    consts.append((nm, n))

        used_by = _callers(p.stem)
        doc_body = _module_doc_body(doc) if doc else ""
        tldr, rest = _split_tldr(doc_body)

        # TL;DR card — the summary paragraph promoted, with the facts you would otherwise
        # have to hunt for (role in the pipeline, size, API surface, who calls it)
        facts = [f"<b>{_html.escape(SCRIPT_ROLE.get(p.stem, 'Output & support'))}</b>",
                 f"v{_html.escape(ver)}", f"{len(src.splitlines()):,} lines",
                 f"{len(funcs)} public function{'s' if len(funcs) != 1 else ''}"]
        if consts:
            facts.append(f"{len(consts)} constant{'s' if len(consts) != 1 else ''}")
        facts.append("used by " + (", ".join(f"<code>{_html.escape(u)}</code>" for u in used_by[:3])
                                   + (" +%d" % (len(used_by) - 3) if len(used_by) > 3 else "")
                                   if used_by else "nothing else"))
        body = [f'<div class="tldr"><div class="tldr-h">TL;DR</div>'
                + (_docstring_html(tldr) if tldr else f"<p><code>{rel}</code></p>")
                + f'<p class="tldr-facts">{" · ".join(facts)}'
                + (' · <span class="pill dirty">uncommitted</span>' if rel in dirty_files else "")
                + f" · <code>{rel}</code></p></div>"]

        # contents strip — chips, not a table
        chips = "".join(f'<a class="chip" href="#fn-{mid}-{n.name}">{n.name}</a>' for n in funcs)
        chips += "".join(f'<a class="chip const" href="#c-{mid}-{c}">{c}</a>' for c, _ in consts)
        if chips:
            body.append(f'<div class="chips">{chips}</div>')

        if rest:
            body.append("<h2>How it works</h2>" + _docstring_html(rest))

        if funcs:
            body.append("<h2>Functions</h2>")
            for n in funcs:
                fdoc = ast.get_docstring(n) or ""
                fsrc = ast.get_source_segment(src, n) or ""
                ext, internal = _call_sites(n.name, rel, corpus)
                symbols.append({"Module": rel, "Symbol": n.name, "Kind":
                                "class" if isinstance(n, ast.ClassDef) else "function",
                                "Called by": ", ".join(ext) if ext else
                                ("(internal use only)" if internal else "— no call site found —")})
                blk = [f'<div class="fn" id="fn-{mid}-{n.name}">',
                       f'<pre class="sig">{_sig_html(_sig_of(n))}</pre>']
                if fdoc:
                    blk.append('<div class="fndoc">' + _docstring_html(fdoc.strip()) + "</div>")
                if ext:
                    blk.append('<p class="calls"><b>Called by</b> '
                               + " ".join(f"<code>{_html.escape(x)}</code>" for x in ext) + "</p>")
                elif internal:
                    blk.append('<p class="calls muted">Used only inside this module.</p>')
                else:
                    blk.append('<p class="calls warn">No call site found in the notebooks or '
                               "<code>utils/</code> — possibly superseded or reserved for interactive use.</p>")
                if fsrc:
                    nlines = len(fsrc.splitlines())
                    blk.append(f'<details><summary>source · lines {n.lineno}–'
                               f"{n.lineno + nlines - 1} ({nlines} lines)</summary>"
                               + _code(fsrc, n.lineno) + "</details>")
                blk.append("</div>")
                body.append("\n".join(blk))

        if consts:
            body.append("<h2>Constants</h2>")
            for name, node in consts:
                kind, literal = _const_summary(node)
                nl = len(literal.splitlines())
                body.append(f'<div class="fn" id="c-{mid}-{name}">'
                            f'<pre class="sig">{_html.escape(name)}'
                            f'<span class="kind">{_html.escape(kind)}</span></pre>'
                            + (f"<details><summary>value</summary>{_code(literal)}</details>"
                               if literal and nl <= 400 else
                               f'<p class="muted">{len(literal):,} chars — read it in the source.</p>')
                            + "</div>")

        if used_by:
            body.append("<h2>Used by</h2><p>"
                        + " ".join(f"<code>{u}</code>" for u in used_by) + "</p>")

        commits = _file_commits(rel)
        body.append("<h2>History</h2>")
        if commits:
            body.append(df_table(pd.DataFrame(
                [{"Commit": c, "Date": d, "Subject": re.sub(r"\bA-H\b", "Habsburg", s)}
                 for c, d, s in commits])))
        else:
            body.append('<p class="muted">No commits touch this file yet.</p>')
        if rel in dirty_files:
            body.append('<p class="note">This file has <b>uncommitted</b> changes; the reasoning '
                        "is recorded in <a href='#decisions'>Decisions</a> and the diff is "
                        "summarised on <a href='#changelog'>Commits &amp; versions</a>.</p>")

        body.append(f"<h2>Full source</h2><details><summary>{rel} · "
                    f"{len(src.splitlines()):,} lines</summary>{_code(src, 1)}</details>")

        sheets.append(dict(
            id="script-" + mid,
            group="Pipeline scripts", title=p.name,
            blurb=(re.sub(r"^[\w./]+\.py\s*[—-]\s*", "", _module_doc_body(doc).split("\n")[0])[:70]
                   if doc else rel),
            src=rel, kind="script", role=SCRIPT_ROLE.get(p.stem, "Output & support"),
            html="\n".join(body),
        ))
    sheets.sort(key=lambda s: (SCRIPT_ORDER.index(s["role"]) if s["role"] in SCRIPT_ORDER else 99,
                               s["title"]))
    return sheets, symbols

def graph_sheet(dirty_files: set[str] | None = None) -> str:
    """Draw the import graph as interactive inline SVG (no library, no CDN).

    Two layouts of the same data, toggled in the browser:

    * **Flowchart** — modules in columns by pipeline role, left→right from the orchestrating
      notebooks to the leaf parsers; the idiom for a directional dependency graph.
    * **Network** — a build-time force-directed layout that lets clusters and hubs emerge by
      position; role is shown by colour instead of column.

    Hovering a node isolates its neighbourhood; clicking a module opens its sheet.
    """
    dirty_files = dirty_files or set()
    mods: dict[str, dict] = {}
    for p in sorted(ROOT.joinpath("utils").rglob("*.py")):
        if "_archive" in p.parts or p.name == "__init__.py":
            continue
        rel = str(p.relative_to(ROOT)).replace("\\", "/")
        src = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
        ver = (re.search(r'^__version__\s*=\s*"([^"]+)"', src, re.M) or [None, "—"])[1]
        try:
            doc = _first_doc_line(ast.parse(src))
        except SyntaxError:
            doc = ""
        # strip a leading "module.py — " prefix that many docstrings repeat, and the
        # markdown emphasis/code markers the docstrings use (rendered as plain text here)
        doc = re.sub(rf"^{re.escape(p.name)}\s*[—-]\s*", "", doc).strip()
        doc = re.sub(r"[*`]+", "", doc)
        mods[p.stem] = {"rel": rel, "role": SCRIPT_ROLE.get(p.stem, "Output & support"),
                        "sheet": "script-" + rel.replace("/", "-").replace(".py", ""),
                        "lines": len(src.splitlines()), "ver": ver, "doc": doc,
                        "dirty": rel in dirty_files}
    known = set(mods)
    edges: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
    for stem, meta in mods.items():
        try:
            tree = ast.parse((ROOT / meta["rel"]).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        except SyntaxError:
            continue
        for dep in _module_imports(tree, known) - {stem}:
            edges.append((stem, dep))
    nb_nodes = []
    for nb in sorted(ROOT.joinpath("notebooks").glob("*.ipynb")):
        deps = _notebook_imports(nb.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"), known)
        if deps:
            nb_nodes.append(nb.stem)
            edges += [(nb.stem, d) for d in deps]

    cols = ["Notebooks"] + SCRIPT_ORDER
    members: dict[str, list[str]] = {c: [] for c in cols}
    members["Notebooks"] = nb_nodes
    for stem, meta in sorted(mods.items()):
        members[meta["role"]].append(stem)

    NW, NH, VG, CG, PAD, TOP = 158, 26, 9, 62, 16, 46
    layered: dict[str, tuple[float, float]] = {}
    for ci, c in enumerate(cols):
        x = PAD + ci * (NW + CG)
        for ri, stem in enumerate(members[c]):
            layered[stem] = (x, TOP + ri * (NH + VG))
    W = PAD * 2 + len(cols) * NW + (len(cols) - 1) * CG
    H = TOP + max(len(v) for v in members.values()) * (NH + VG) + PAD

    deg: dict[str, int] = {}                   # in-degree = how many things import it
    for _a, b in edges:
        deg[b] = deg.get(b, 0) + 1

    def role_of(stem: str) -> str:
        return "Notebooks" if stem in nb_nodes else mods[stem]["role"]

    # network view: node area scales with the module's size, so ranks.py (764 lines) visibly
    # outweighs theater.py (129). sqrt keeps *area* roughly proportional to lines.
    lines = {s: mods[s]["lines"] for s in mods}
    lo, hi = (min(lines.values()), max(lines.values())) if lines else (1, 1)
    def scale_of(stem: str) -> float:
        if stem in nb_nodes:
            return 1.0
        f = (lines[stem] - lo) / (hi - lo) if hi > lo else 0.5
        return round(0.74 + 0.72 * (f ** 0.5), 3)

    scales = {s: scale_of(s) for s in layered}
    dims = {s: (NW * scales[s], NH * scales[s]) for s in layered}

    # the network view needs a taller canvas than the flowchart so the collision pass has
    # vertical room; JS swaps the SVG viewBox to NETH when that view is shown
    NETH = max(H, 40 + 12 * (NH + 16))
    all_nodes = list(layered)
    force = _force_layout(all_nodes, edges, W, NETH, dims)

    # cluster hulls: one soft blob per role, from the corners of that role's boxes
    hulls = []
    by_role: dict[str, list[tuple[float, float]]] = {}
    for stem, (fx, fy) in force.items():
        w_, h_ = dims[stem]
        by_role.setdefault(role_of(stem), []).extend(
            [(fx, fy), (fx + w_, fy), (fx + w_, fy + h_), (fx, fy + h_)])
    for role, pts in by_role.items():
        fill, stroke = _ROLE_COLOUR.get(role, _ROLE_COLOUR["Output & support"])
        hulls.append(f'<path class="hull" data-role="{_html.escape(role)}" '
                     f'd="{_hull_path(pts)}" fill="{fill}" stroke="{stroke}"/>')

    svg = [f'<svg id="archsvg" viewBox="0 0 {W} {H}" width="{W}" height="{H}" '
           f'data-w="{W}" data-flowh="{H}" data-neth="{NETH}" '
           f'xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">']
    svg.append('<defs><marker id="ah" viewBox="0 0 8 8" refX="7" refY="4" markerWidth="7" '
               'markerHeight="7" orient="auto"><path d="M0 0 L8 4 L0 8 z" fill="#9fb0bf"/>'
               "</marker></defs>")
    svg.append(f'<g id="archhulls">{"".join(hulls)}</g>')
    for ci, c in enumerate(cols):              # column labels (hidden in network mode via CSS)
        x = PAD + ci * (NW + CG)
        svg.append(f'<text class="collab" x="{x}" y="24">{_html.escape(c)}</text>')
    svg.append('<g id="archedges">')
    for a, b in edges:
        if a in layered and b in layered:
            svg.append(f'<path class="edge" data-a="{a}" data-b="{b}" marker-end="url(#ah)"/>')
    svg.append("</g><g id='archnodes'>")
    for stem, (lx, ly) in layered.items():
        fx, fy = force[stem]
        is_nb = stem in nb_nodes
        sheet = "" if is_nb else mods[stem]["sheet"]
        cls = "node nb" if is_nb else "node"
        if not is_nb and mods[stem]["dirty"]:
            cls += " dirty"
        label = stem if len(stem) <= 21 else stem[:20] + "…"
        svg.append(
            f'<g class="{cls}" data-id="{stem}" data-role="{_html.escape(role_of(stem))}" '
            f'data-lx="{lx:.0f}" data-ly="{ly:.0f}" data-fx="{fx:.0f}" data-fy="{fy:.0f}" '
            f'data-deg="{deg.get(stem, 0)}" data-sheet="{sheet}" data-scale="{scales[stem]}" '
            f'data-lines="{mods[stem]["lines"] if not is_nb else 0}" '
            + f'style="transform:translate({lx:.0f}px,{ly:.0f}px)">'
            f'<rect width="{NW}" height="{NH}" rx="4"/>'
            f'<text x="9" y="17">{_html.escape(label)}</text>'
            + (f'<text class="deg" x="{NW - 8}" y="17">{deg[stem]}</text>' if deg.get(stem) else "")
            + "</g>")
    svg.append("</g></svg>")

    legend = "".join(
        f'<button class="lg on" data-role="{_html.escape(r)}" onclick="archRole(this)">'
        f'<span class="sw" style="background:{f};border-color:{s}"></span>{_html.escape(r)}</button>'
        for r, (f, s) in _ROLE_COLOUR.items())

    hubs = sorted(deg.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])[:5]
    meta = {stem: {"role": role_of(stem), "ver": mods[stem]["ver"],
                   "lines": mods[stem]["lines"], "doc": mods[stem]["doc"],
                   "sheet": mods[stem]["sheet"], "deg": deg.get(stem, 0),
                   "dirty": mods[stem]["dirty"]}
            for stem in mods}
    meta.update({nb: {"role": "Notebooks", "ver": "—", "lines": 0,
                      "doc": "Stage notebook — orchestrates the modules for this pipeline stage.",
                      "sheet": "", "deg": deg.get(nb, 0), "dirty": False} for nb in nb_nodes})
    return (
        ix_head("How the scripts fit together", ix=True, hover=True)
        + '<p class="note">Every arrow is a real <code>import</code>, read from the source at build '
        "time — <b>A → B</b> means A imports B. Two views of the same graph: the "
        "<b>flowchart</b> lays modules out in columns by pipeline role (the natural reading of a "
        "directional dependency graph); the <b>network</b> is a force-directed layout where "
        "tightly-coupled modules pull together and the hubs settle in the middle. <b>Hover</b> a "
        "box to isolate what it touches; <b>click</b> a module to open its sheet.</p>"
        '<div class="archbar">'
        '<div class="seg"><button id="archFlow" class="on" onclick="archLayout(\'flow\')">Flowchart</button>'
        '<button id="archNet" onclick="archLayout(\'net\')">Network</button></div>'
        '<div class="seg"><button id="archHull" onclick="archHulls()">Clusters</button>'
        '<button id="archImpact" onclick="archImpact()">Change impact</button></div>'
        f'<div class="archlegend">{legend}</div></div>'
        '<div class="archhint" id="archPinned">Hover to trace · <b>click</b> a box to inspect it · '
        "<b>shift-click</b> a second box to trace the import path between them · "
        "<b>double-click</b> opens the module · Esc clears</div>"
        f'<div class="archstage"><div class="archwrap">{"".join(svg)}</div>'
        '<aside class="archpanel" id="archpanel">'
        '<div class="aempty">Click a module to inspect it — its role, size, one-line purpose, '
        "and exactly what it imports and is imported by.</div></aside></div>"
        f"<script>window.ARCHMETA={json.dumps(meta, ensure_ascii=False)};</script>"
        '<p class="note"><b>Most depended-on:</b> '
        + ", ".join(f"<code>{k}</code> ({v})" for k, v in hubs)
        + f" · {len(mods)} modules, {len(nb_nodes)} notebooks, {len(edges)} import edges. "
        "In the network view the number on a box is its in-degree; the hubs are the boxes "
        "everything points at.</p>")

def usage_sheet(symbols: list[dict]) -> str:
    """Render the symbol-usage index and the dead-code list.

    Args:
        symbols: one record per public symbol, from :func:`collect_scripts`.
    """
    df = pd.DataFrame(symbols)
    dead = df[df["Called by"] == "— no call site found —"]
    S = ["<h2>Where every public symbol is used</h2>",
         '<p class="note">Each public function/class in <code>utils/</code>, and every notebook or '
         "module that calls it. Found by searching for <code>name(</code> across the notebooks and "
         "<code>utils/</code>, so it cannot see dynamic dispatch, and a few deliberately generic "
         "names are excluded. Treat it as a strong hint, not proof.</p>"]
    if len(dead):
        S.append(f'<h3>No call site found <span class="bad">{len(dead)}</span></h3>')
        S.append('<p class="note">Public, but never called from a notebook or another module. '
                 "Either superseded, or a standalone/interactive helper — worth a look before it "
                 "quietly rots. (This is how <code>wikidata.add_birth_coords</code> was found to be "
                 "superseded by <code>records_geo.add_settlement_attrs</code>.)</p>")
        S.append(df_table(dead[["Module", "Symbol", "Kind"]].reset_index(drop=True)))
    S.append("<h3>Full symbol index</h3>")
    S.append(df_table(df, searchable=True))
    return "\n".join(S)

def changelog_sheet(dirty: pd.DataFrame, scripts: list[dict]) -> str:
    """Render what git and the working tree actually know about the project's history.

    Deliberately modest: this repository has a shallow, lumpy history (most modules were
    added in one commit and never revised), so the sheet reports the uncommitted tree, the
    commit list and current versions, and points at the audit for the reasoning rather than
    pretending to derive it.
    """
    S: list[str] = []
    S.append('<p class="note"><b>What this sheet can and cannot tell you.</b> The tables below are '
             "read from git and the working tree at build time, so they are always true — but they "
             "are only as informative as the history itself. This repository has a <b>shallow, lumpy "
             "history</b>: most modules were introduced in a single commit and never revised in git, "
             "so a per-file log shows one line. This sheet is the <b>machine</b> half of the record "
             "and deliberately says nothing about <i>why</i>: the calls are listed in "
             "<a href='#decisions'>Decisions</a>, the narrative is on "
             "<a href='#whatsnew'>What's new</a>, and each module's own docstring records its design "
             "choices. If you want this sheet to become genuinely useful, commit in meaningful units "
             "with messages that say <i>why</i>.</p>")

    if not _git("rev-parse", "--short", "HEAD"):
        # A synced copy of the files without the repository. Say so, rather than print
        # "clean" and "0 commits" about a history this build could not read.
        S.append('<h2>Built without git history</h2>'
                 '<p class="note">This page was built on a machine that holds the project\'s '
                 "files but not its repository, so the working-tree and commit tables that "
                 "normally stand here could not be read. That says nothing about the state of "
                 "the repository: the work described on <a href='#whatsnew'>What's new</a> may "
                 "be uncommitted. The module versions below are read from the source files and "
                 "are current.</p>")
    elif len(dirty):
        S.append(f'<h2>Uncommitted working tree <span class="bad">{len(dirty)} files</span></h2>')
        S.append('<p class="note">These changes exist on disk but in <b>no commit</b> — so their '
                 "rationale is not recoverable from git. It is written up in "
                 "<a href='#decisions'>Decisions</a> and on <a href='#whatsnew'>What's new</a>. "
                 "Committing them is what turns that write-up into durable history.</p>")
        S.append(df_table(dirty, searchable=True))
    else:
        S.append('<h2>Uncommitted working tree <span class="ok">clean</span></h2>')

    commits = [l.split("\x1f") for l in
               _git("log", "--format=%h\x1f%ad\x1f%an\x1f%s", "--date=short").splitlines() if l]
    if commits:
        S.append(f"<h2>Commit history <span class='muted'>({len(commits)} commits)</span></h2>")
        rows = []
        for sha, date, who, subj in commits:
            n = len([x for x in _git("show", "--name-only", "--format=", sha).splitlines() if x])
            # display-only: expand the "A-H" abbreviation to its full form so the site's
            # terminology is uniform (identical meaning; git history itself is untouched).
            subj = re.sub(r"\bA-H\b", "Habsburg", subj)
            rows.append({"Commit": sha, "Date": date, "Files": n, "Subject": subj})
        S.append(df_table(pd.DataFrame(rows), searchable=True))

    S.append("<h2>Module versions</h2>")
    S.append('<p class="note">Every module carries a <code>__version__</code>. Bumps are not '
             "individually logged in git (the history predates that discipline), so treat this as "
             "the <i>current</i> state — the <a href='#audit'>audits</a> record what changed in the "
             "2026-07-16/17 and 2026-09-22 passes.</p>")
    vt = pd.DataFrame([{"Module": s["src"], "Version": re.search(r"Version ([\w.]+)", s["html"]).group(1)
                        if re.search(r"Version ([\w.]+)", s["html"]) else "—",
                        "Role": s["role"],
                        "Uncommitted": "yes" if "uncommitted changes" in s["html"] else ""}
                       for s in scripts])
    S.append(df_table(vt, searchable=True))
    return "\n".join(S)

def module_index() -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Every importable module with its version and one-line purpose, read from source.

    Generated rather than listed by hand, so it cannot drift as modules are added.
    """
    rows = []
    for p in sorted(ROOT.joinpath("utils").rglob("*.py")):
        if "_archive" in p.parts or p.name == "__init__.py":
            continue
        txt = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
        ver = (re.search(r'^__version__\s*=\s*"([^"]+)"', txt, re.M) or [None, "—"])[1]
        doc = re.search(r'^"""(?:\s*\n)?(.+?)$', txt, re.M | re.S)
        first = ""
        if doc:
            for line in doc.group(1).splitlines():
                s = line.strip()
                if s and not set(s) <= {"=", "-", "~"}:
                    first = s
                    break
        first = re.sub(r"^[\w./]+\.py\s*[—-]\s*", "", first)
        rows.append({"module": str(p.relative_to(ROOT)).replace("\\", "/"),
                     "version": ver, "purpose": first})
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

def df_table(df: pd.DataFrame, cls: str = "tbl", searchable: bool = False) -> str:
    """Render a DataFrame as an HTML table, optionally with a client-side row filter.

    Used for genuinely tabular content (the dictionary, the codebook, coverage counts).
    Deliberately *not* used for code: signatures and source belong in ``<pre>``, where
    they can be syntax-coloured and cannot be mangled by cell wrapping.

    Args:
        df: rows to render; NaN becomes an empty cell.
        cls: CSS class for the table element.
        searchable: prepend a filter box and a row count.
    """
    head = "".join(f"<th>{_html.escape(str(c))}</th>" for c in df.columns)
    body = []
    for _, r in df.iterrows():
        tds = "".join(f"<td>{_html.escape('' if pd.isna(v) else str(v))}</td>" for v in r)
        body.append(f"<tr>{tds}</tr>")
    filt = ('<input class="tblfilter" placeholder="Filter these rows…" '
            'oninput="filterTable(this)">') if searchable else ""
    n = f'<p class="muted">{len(df):,} rows</p>' if searchable else ""
    return (f'{filt}{n}<div class="tblwrap"><table class="{cls}"><thead><tr>{head}</tr>'
            f"</thead><tbody>{''.join(body)}</tbody></table></div>")

def certification_power() -> str:
    """Is the sealed sample large enough? — computed from each certification score on disk.

    The scorer's page-clustered bootstrap is the result of record, but with eight clusters and
    four errors its upper end sits at 1.000, so this adds what the claims alone can bound
    (exact binomial, not clustered) and what each symbol's count can bound — the question a
    reader of the headline asks next.
    """
    blocks = []
    for f in sorted((ROOT / "output" / "frozen").glob("*_certification/certification_score.json")):
        s = json.loads(f.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        a = s["as_printed"]
        errs = a["false"] + a["missed"]
        rows = [("false claims, of the route's claims", a["false"], a["claims_route"]),
                ("missed claims, of the printed claims", a["missed"], a["claims_gold"]),
                ("any error, per printed claim", errs, a["claims_gold"])]
        over = "".join(
            f"<tr><td>{lab}</td><td>{k} of {n}</td><td>{100 * k / n:.2f} %</td>"
            f"<td>{100 * _exact_bounds(k, n)[1]:.2f} %</td></tr>" for lab, k, n in rows)
        bands = [("ten or more", 10, 10 ** 9), ("three to nine", 3, 9), ("one or two", 1, 2)]
        sym = []
        for lab, lo, hi in bands:
            ts = [t for t in a["symbols"] if lo <= t["gold"] <= hi]
            if not ts:
                continue
            worst = min(_exact_bounds(t["hit"], t["gold"])[0] for t in ts)
            sym.append(f"<tr><td>{lab}</td><td>{len(ts)}</td><td>{sum(t['gold'] for t in ts)}"
                       f"</td><td>{sum(t['missed'] for t in ts)}</td><td>{worst:.2f}</td></tr>")
        # instances of a symbol needed for its sensitivity's lower bound to clear a bar,
        # read with no miss: (α/2)^(1/n) ≥ bar
        need = {bar: math.ceil(math.log(0.025) / math.log(bar)) for bar in (0.90, 0.95)}
        blocks.append(
            f"<h3>Is the sample large enough? — "
            f"{ {'cz': 'Czech half', 'de-bohemia': 'German Böhmen', 'de-moravia': 'German Mähren', 'de-silesia': 'German Schlesien', 'de-pooled': 'German half, pooled (D-136)'}.get(s['edition'], s['edition'])}, "
            f"scored {_html.escape(s['scored'][:10])}</h3>"
            "<p>Computed at build time from <code>certification_score.json</code>. The "
            "page-clustered interval above is the result of record; the bounds here count "
            "claims as independent, so they are the floor of the uncertainty, not its "
            "ceiling.</p>"
            '<table class="tbl"><tr><th></th><th>observed</th><th>rate</th>'
            "<th>95 % upper bound (exact)</th></tr>" + over + "</table>"
            '<table class="tbl"><tr><th>instances of the symbol on the sealed pages</th>'
            "<th>symbols</th><th>claims</th><th>missed</th>"
            "<th>lowest 95 % lower bound on sensitivity</th></tr>" + "".join(sym) + "</table>"
            f"<p>A symbol needs about <b>{need[0.90]}</b> instances, read without a miss, for "
            f"its sensitivity's lower bound to reach 0.90, and <b>{need[0.95]}</b> for 0.95.</p>")
    return "".join(blocks)

def rank_reset_hist(L: pd.DataFrame, mask: pd.Series | None = None) -> str:
    """Diverging histogram of ``rank_reset`` — the headline regressor's distribution.

    One bar per integer reset on the ALT-1 common scale: negative = demoted on Legion
    entry (red, left), 0 = unchanged (grey), positive = promoted (navy, right). Bar
    height is √count, because the unchanged bar (~77 %) would otherwise flatten the whole
    tail — the tail (who was demoted, and how far) is the part that carries the identifying
    variation. Exact counts are in each bar's tooltip. ``mask`` optionally restricts the
    rows (used for the combat-ranks-only view).
    """
    import math

    r = (L if mask is None else L[mask])["rank_reset"].dropna().astype(int)
    if r.empty:
        return ""
    vc = r.value_counts().sort_index()
    lo, hi = int(vc.index.min()), int(vc.index.max())
    vals = list(range(lo, hi + 1))
    counts = {int(k): int(v) for k, v in vc.items()}
    n = int(vc.sum())
    mx = max(counts.values())

    BW, GAP, PLOTH, TOP, PAD, LBL = 17, 4, 176, 14, 30, 26
    W = PAD * 2 + len(vals) * (BW + GAP)
    BASE = TOP + PLOTH
    H = BASE + LBL + 16

    def col(v):
        return (CU_RED, "#e88") if v < 0 else ((CU_NAVY, "#7fa0b8") if v > 0 else (CU_GREY, "#bcc3c9"))

    svg = [f'<svg viewBox="0 0 {W} {H}" width="{W}" height="{H}" class="rrhist" '
           'xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">']
    svg.append(f'<line x1="{PAD-6}" y1="{BASE}" x2="{W-PAD+6}" y2="{BASE}" stroke="#c9d4de"/>')
    for i, v in enumerate(vals):
        c = counts.get(v, 0)
        x = PAD + i * (BW + GAP)
        h = (math.sqrt(c) / math.sqrt(mx) * PLOTH) if c else 0
        fill, _ = col(v)
        if c:
            svg.append(f'<rect x="{x}" y="{BASE-h:.1f}" width="{BW}" height="{h:.1f}" rx="1.5" '
                       f'fill="{fill}"><title>reset {v:+d}: {c:,} ({c/n*100:.1f}%)</title></rect>')
        if v % 2 == 0 or abs(v) <= 3 or v in (lo, hi):
            svg.append(f'<text class="rrx" x="{x+BW/2:.0f}" y="{BASE+13}">{v:+d}</text>')
        if c and (c == mx or c >= 0.02 * n):
            svg.append(f'<text class="rrn" x="{x+BW/2:.0f}" y="{BASE-h-3:.1f}">'
                       f'{c/1000:.0f}k</text>' if c >= 1000 else
                       f'<text class="rrn" x="{x+BW/2:.0f}" y="{BASE-h-3:.1f}">{c}</text>')
    svg.append(f'<text class="rrax" x="{PAD}" y="{H-2}">← demoted on Legion entry</text>')
    svg.append(f'<text class="rrax" x="{W-PAD}" y="{H-2}" text-anchor="end">promoted →</text>')
    svg.append("</svg>")

    dem, unc, pro = int((r < 0).sum()), int((r == 0).sum()), int((r > 0).sum())
    return (
        '<div class="rrwrap">' + "".join(svg) + "</div>"
        f'<p class="note">{n:,} records have both ranks resolved. '
        f'<b style="color:{CU_RED}">{_pct(dem, n)} demoted</b> · '
        f'{_pct(unc, n)} unchanged · '
        f'<b style="color:{CU_NAVY}">{_pct(pro, n)} promoted</b> · mean {r.mean():+.2f}. '
        "Bar height is √count so the tail stays visible; the flat majority at 0 is the "
        "reset the Legion did <i>not</i> impose. The asymmetry — a longer left tail — is the "
        "raw material for the relative-deprivation story (hover a bar for its exact count).</p>")

def rank_reset_areas(L: pd.DataFrame, theatres=("Russia", "Italy", "France"),
                     mask: pd.Series | None = None) -> str:
    """Overlaid area chart of the rank-reset *shape* by theatre.

    One translucent area per theatre (solid border, 18 % fill), plotting the share of
    that theatre's resolved resets at each integer value — shares, not counts, so the
    theatres are comparable despite very different N. Height is √share for the same
    reason as the histogram: the ~75–88 % mass at 0 would otherwise flatten the tails,
    and the tails (how much more Russia demoted than Italy) are the comparison. Legend
    toggles each theatre.
    """
    import math

    r = (L if mask is None else L[mask])
    r = r[r["rank_reset"].notna()]
    if r.empty:
        return ""
    lo, hi = int(r["rank_reset"].min()), int(r["rank_reset"].max())
    vals = list(range(lo, hi + 1))
    series = {}
    for th in theatres:
        s = r[r["theater"] == th]["rank_reset"].astype(int)
        if len(s) < 200:
            continue
        vc = s.value_counts(normalize=True)
        series[th] = ({v: float(vc.get(v, 0.0)) for v in vals}, len(s))
    if not series:
        return ""
    peak = max(sh for sh, _ in series.values() for sh in sh.values())

    STEP, PLOTH, TOP, PAD, LBL = 20, 176, 14, 34, 30
    W = PAD * 2 + (len(vals) - 1) * STEP
    BASE = TOP + PLOTH
    H = BASE + LBL + 16

    def X(v): return PAD + (v - lo) * STEP
    def Y(sh): return BASE - (math.sqrt(sh) / math.sqrt(peak) * PLOTH if sh > 0 else 0)

    svg = [f'<svg viewBox="0 0 {W} {H}" width="{W}" height="{H}" class="rrarea" '
           'xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">']
    svg.append(f'<line x1="{PAD-6}" y1="{BASE}" x2="{W-PAD+6}" y2="{BASE}" stroke="#c9d4de"/>')
    svg.append(f'<line x1="{X(0)}" y1="{TOP-4}" x2="{X(0)}" y2="{BASE}" stroke="#dfe3e8" '
               'stroke-dasharray="3 3"/>')
    for i, (th, (sh, n)) in enumerate(series.items()):
        line, fill = _THEATRE_COL.get(th, ("#555", "#555"))
        pts = " ".join(f"{X(v):.0f},{Y(sh[v]):.1f}" for v in vals)
        area = f"M{X(lo)},{BASE} L" + pts.replace(" ", " L") + f" L{X(hi)},{BASE} Z"
        svg.append(f'<path class="rra" data-th="{_html.escape(th)}" d="{area}" '
                   f'fill="{fill}" fill-opacity="0.18" stroke="none"/>')
        svg.append(f'<polyline class="rral" data-th="{_html.escape(th)}" points="{pts}" '
                   f'fill="none" stroke="{line}" stroke-width="1.6"/>')
    for v in vals:
        if v % 2 == 0 or v in (lo, hi):
            svg.append(f'<text class="rrx" x="{X(v):.0f}" y="{BASE+13}">{v:+d}</text>')
    svg.append(f'<text class="rrax" x="{PAD}" y="{H-2}">← demoted</text>')
    svg.append(f'<text class="rrax" x="{W-PAD}" y="{H-2}" text-anchor="end">promoted →</text>')
    svg.append("</svg>")

    legend = "".join(
        f'<button class="rrlg on" data-th="{_html.escape(th)}" onclick="rrToggle(this)">'
        f'<span class="sw" style="background:{_THEATRE_COL.get(th, ("#555",""))[0]}"></span>'
        f'{_html.escape(th)} <i>{n:,}</i></button>' for th, (_s, n) in series.items())

    return (
        '<p class="note">The same reset, split by theatre and drawn as overlapping areas '
        "(share of each theatre's resolved resets; height is √share so the tails read). The "
        "shapes are not alike: Russia carries a visibly heavier <b>demotion</b> shoulder than "
        "Italy, whose mass sits almost entirely at 0. Click a theatre to toggle it.</p>"
        f'<div class="rrbar">{legend}</div>'
        f'<div class="rrwrap">{"".join(svg)}</div>'
        '<p class="note">Russia <b>−0.62</b> mean reset (23% demoted) vs Italy <b>−0.03</b> '
        "(7%) vs France <b>−0.23</b> (16%). The theatre that did the most rank-resetting is "
        "also the one that saw essentially all the desertion — which is exactly why the reset "
        "has to be read against theatre, not on its own.</p>")

def render_bib() -> str:
    """The whole bibliography as biblatex, ordered by citekey."""
    out = [_BIB_HEADER]
    for _, e in sorted(BIBTEX.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1]["_key"]):
        fields = {k: v for k, v in e.items() if not k.startswith("_")}
        width = max(len(k) for k in fields)
        body = ",\n".join(f"\t{k.ljust(width)} = {{{v}}}" for k, v in fields.items())
        out.append(f"@{e['_type']}{{{e['_key']},\n{body},\n}}")
    return "\n\n".join(out) + "\n"

def references_sheet() -> str:
    """The bibliography in APA 7 — Literature and Data sources — each with a source link."""

    def _block(keys: set[str]) -> str:
        items = sorted((e for e in BIB if e["key"] in keys), key=lambda e: e["apa"])
        out = []
        for e in items:
            src = (f' <a class="refsrc" href="{e["url"]}" target="_blank" rel="noopener">'
                   "source ↗</a>") if e["url"] else ""
            out.append(f'<div class="refitem" id="ref-{e["key"]}">{e["apa"]}{src}</div>')
        return f'<div class="reflist">{"".join(out)}</div>'

    lit_keys = {e["key"] for e in BIB} - _BIB_DATA_KEYS - _BIB_LAW_KEYS
    return (
        "<h2>References</h2>"
        f'<p class="note">Every work cited anywhere on this site — {len(BIB)} entries, in APA '
        "style. This list is the <b>master</b>: <code>reference/references.bib</code> is "
        "generated from it at build time, so the two cannot disagree and neither can omit a work "
        "the other has. Inline mentions elsewhere — "
        '<span class="cite">Author (year)</span> — are clickable and preview the full '
        "reference on hover.</p>"
        "<h3>Literature</h3>" + _block(lit_keys)
        + "<h3>Statutes &amp; standards</h3>"
        + '<p class="note">The interwar Czechoslovak statutes behind the rank framework, and the '
          "NATO code standard the common scale is expressed in. Full treatment on the "
          "<a href='#ranks-legal'>Rank recognition 1918–38</a> sheet.</p>"
        + _block(_BIB_LAW_KEYS)
        + "<h3>Data &amp; reference sources</h3>" + _block(_BIB_DATA_KEYS)
        + '<p class="note">Full provenance, licences and access notes for each dataset are '
        "on the <a href='#sources'>Data sources</a> sheet; dataset citations here follow "
        "APA data-set style (retrieval year for the live databases).</p>"
        "<script>window.BIB="
        + json.dumps({e["key"]: {"apa": e["apa"], "url": e["url"]} for e in BIB},
                     ensure_ascii=False) + ";</script>")

def waterfall_block(L: pd.DataFrame, f: pd.DataFrame) -> str:
    """Legionnaire analysis-sample waterfall — decide which borderline records to keep."""
    strict = int((f["theatre"] & f["unit_verified"] & f["birthplace"] & f["rank_reset"]).sum())
    helper = (
        '# Fidler unit cross-check — reads the external reference table, not data/final:\n'
        '_a = pd.read_csv("reference/units/unit_authority.csv")\n'
        '_rg = _a[(_a["kind"] == "unit") & _a["number"].notna()\n'
        '         & _a["unit_cs"].str.contains(r"\\bPLUK\\b", na=False)\n'
        '         & ~_a["unit_cs"].str.contains("ZVLÁŠTNÍ", na=False)]\n'
        '_exp = {}\n'
        'for _n, _t in zip(_rg["number"].astype(int), _rg["theatre"]):\n'
        '    _exp.setdefault(_n, set()).add(_t)\n'
        '_num = df["regiment"].astype("string").str.extract(r"^(\\d+)\\.")[0].astype("Float64")\n'
        '_cs  = df["legion_army"].astype("string").str.startswith("CS Legion", na=False)\n'
        '_nb  = _num.notna() & df["regiment"].astype("string").str.contains(r"(?:stř|p)\\.pl\\.", na=False)\n'
        'def _stat(n, th, cs, nb):\n'
        '    if not (cs and nb) or pd.isna(n): return "n-a"\n'
        '    w = _exp.get(int(n));  return "n-a" if w is None else ("match" if th in w else "conflict")\n'
        'unit_status = pd.Series([_stat(n, t, c, b) for n, t, c, b in\n'
        '                         zip(_num, df["theater"], _cs, _nb)], index=df.index)\n')
    ah_helper = (
        '\n# Habsburg unit at capture → does it resolve to a real 1914 regiment (Ehnl Tabelle I)?\n'
        '_p = "reference/units/"\n'
        '_S = {"p":   set(pd.read_csv(_p+"ehnl_tabelle1_infantry.csv")["reg_no"]),\n'
        '      "zem": set(pd.read_csv(_p+"ehnl_tabelle1_landwehr.csv")["reg_no"]),\n'
        '      "hon": set(pd.read_csv(_p+"ehnl_tabelle1_honved.csv")["reg_no"])}\n'
        'def _ahm(v):\n'
        '    if pd.isna(v): return False\n'
        '    m = re.match(r"(\\d+)\\.?\\s*(.+)", str(v))\n'
        '    if not m: return False\n'
        '    n, r = int(m.group(1)), m.group(2)\n'
        '    if r.startswith(("p.pl.","pp")):          return n in _S["p"]\n'
        '    if r.startswith(("zem.p.pl.","zem.pl.")): return n in _S["zem"]\n'
        '    if r.startswith("honv.p.pl."):            return n in _S["hon"]\n'
        '    return False   # (cavalry/Feldjäger arms add a few more; infantry shown here)\n'
        'ah_matched = df["habsburg_unit_capture"].apply(_ahm)\n')
    cfg = dict(
        flags=f, order=["deserted", "theatre", "unit", "unit_verified", "unit_conflict",
                        "birthplace", "rank_reset", "ah_unit", "ah_matched"],
        highlight_label="deserters", rate_label="desertion rate",
        title="<h2>Analysis sample — legionnaires</h2>",
        intro='<p class="note">Desertion is the <b>outcome</b>, so non-deserters are the '
              "controls, not losses — the cuts below are about <b>covariate coverage</b>. "
              "Bars are cumulative; the deserter count on each confirms the signal survives.</p>",
        build_note='<p class="note">Tick the requirements an estimation sample should impose. '
                   "The count updates instantly and breaks down by theatre; each unticked box "
                   "shows what it would cost to add. The link and pandas snippet reproduce the "
                   "sample you build.</p>",
        steps=[
            ("All legionnaires", pd.Series(True, index=L.index), "the full scraped population"),
            ("Theatre resolved", f["theatre"], "theatre ≠ Unknown"),
            ("Unit label present", f["theatre"] & f["unit"], "an enrolment unit is recorded"),
            ("Unit not contradicted by Fidler", f["theatre"] & f["unit"] & ~f["unit_conflict"],
             "drops the 266 records whose regiment never existed in their theatre"),
            ("Birthplace linked (okres/járás)",
             f["theatre"] & f["unit"] & ~f["unit_conflict"] & f["birthplace"],
             "a 1910 census district, so covariates can be merged"),
            ("Rank reset resolved",
             f["theatre"] & f["unit"] & ~f["unit_conflict"] & f["birthplace"] & f["rank_reset"],
             "both ranks parsed — the headline regressor is defined"),
            ("Habsburg unit at capture recorded",
             f["theatre"] & f["unit"] & ~f["unit_conflict"] & f["birthplace"] & f["rank_reset"]
             & f["ah_unit"],
             "the pre-capture Habsburg unit string is present"),
            ("Habsburg unit matched to Tabelle I",
             f["theatre"] & f["unit"] & ~f["unit_conflict"] & f["birthplace"] & f["rank_reset"]
             & f["ah_matched"],
             "that unit resolves to a real 1914 regiment → its home district & nationality"),
        ],
        extra_note=f'<p class="note wfnote"><b>Borderline:</b> requiring the unit positively '
                   f'<b>verified</b> in Fidler (not merely un-contradicted) drops the sample to '
                   f'<b>{strict:,}</b> — but most of that loss is support/rear units that carry '
                   f'no regiment number to check, <b>not</b> wrong data.</p>',
        toggles=[
            ("Deserters only", 0, "set", "restrict to Code-D records (the outcome, not a covariate)",
             "des", 'df["deserted"]'),
            ("Theatre linked", 1, "set", "theatre resolved",
             "theatre", '(df["theater"].notna() & df["theater"].ne("Unknown"))'),
            ("Unit linked", 2, "set", "an enrolment unit recorded", "unit", 'df["regiment"].notna()'),
            ("Unit verified in Fidler", 3, "set", "regiment number confirmed to exist in its theatre",
             "verified", '(unit_status == "match")'),
            ("Exclude Fidler conflicts", 4, "clear", "drop regiment/theatre combinations Fidler rules out",
             "noconflict", '(unit_status != "conflict")'),
            ("Birthplace linked", 5, "set", "okres or járás resolved",
             "birth", '(df["birth_okres_id"].notna() | df["birth_jaras_id"].notna())'),
            ("Rank reset resolved", 6, "set", "both ranks parsed", "reset", 'df["rank_reset"].notna()'),
            ("Habsburg unit recorded (present)", 7, "set",
             "the pre-capture Habsburg unit string is present (not yet checked against Ehnl)",
             "ahunit", 'df["habsburg_unit_capture"].notna()'),
            ("Habsburg unit matched to Tabelle I", 8, "set",
             "the unit resolves to a real 1914 regiment → its Ergänzung home district & nationality",
             "ahmatch", "ah_matched"),
        ],
        snippet_parquet="data/final/persons/legionnaires_clean.parquet", helper=helper + ah_helper)
    return _waterfall("legion", L, cfg)

def waterfall_block_habsburg(H: pd.DataFrame) -> str:

             "unit", 'df["ah_unit_primary"].notna()'),
            ("Habsburg unit matched to Tabelle I", 6, "set",
             "unit resolves to a real 1914 regiment → home district & nationality",
             "unit_matched", "unit_matched"),
            ("Cause of death known", 5, "set", "death category defined",
             "cause", 'df["cause"].notna()'),
        ],
        snippet_parquet="data/final/persons/habsburg_clean.parquet", helper=ah_helper_hab)
    return _waterfall("habsburg", H, cfg)

def provenance_sheet() -> str:
    """Interactive bipartite map: each source (left) → the mechanisms it grounds (right).

    Positions are computed at build time and baked into the SVG, so nothing depends on
    runtime geometry (which would read as zero while the sheet is hidden). Clicking a
    node highlights its incident edges and the nodes at their far end; the highlight is
    pure CSS keyed on ``data-*`` attributes.
    """
    NW, NH, VG, PAD, TOP = 236, 34, 12, 14, 52
    GAP = 300                                  # horizontal room for the edge bundle
    src_y = {sid: TOP + i * (NH + VG) for i, (sid, *_1) in enumerate(_PV_SOURCES)}
    mech_y = {mid: TOP + i * (NH + VG) for i, (mid, *_2) in enumerate(_PV_MECH)}
    Lx, Rx = PAD, PAD + NW + GAP
    W = Rx + NW + PAD
    H = TOP + max(len(_PV_SOURCES), len(_PV_MECH)) * (NH + VG) + PAD

    def _node(nid, cat, label, note, x, y):
        fill, stroke = _PV_COLOUR.get(cat, _PV_COLOUR["data"])
        disp = label if len(label) <= 30 else label[:29] + "…"
        return (f'<g class="pvnode" data-id="{nid}" data-cat="{cat}" '
                f'transform="translate({x},{y})"><title>{_html.escape(label)} — '
                f'{_html.escape(note)}</title>'
                f'<rect width="{NW}" height="{NH}" rx="6" style="fill:{fill};stroke:{stroke}"/>'
                f'<text x="12" y="{NH/2+4:.0f}">{_html.escape(disp)}</text></g>')

    svg = [f'<svg id="pvsvg" viewBox="0 0 {W} {H}" width="{W}" height="{H}" '
           'xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">']
    svg.append('<text class="pvcol" x="%d" y="30">SOURCES</text>' % Lx)
    svg.append('<text class="pvcol" x="%d" y="30">MECHANISMS · LADDERS · MAPPINGS</text>' % Rx)
    svg.append('<g id="pvedges">')
    for s, m in _PV_EDGES:
        y1, y2 = src_y[s] + NH / 2, mech_y[m] + NH / 2
        x1, x2 = Lx + NW, Rx
        mx = (x1 + x2) / 2
        cat = next(c for i, c, *_ in _PV_SOURCES if i == s)
        svg.append(f'<path class="pvedge" data-s="{s}" data-m="{m}" data-cat="{cat}" '
                   f'd="M{x1},{y1:.0f} C{mx:.0f},{y1:.0f} {mx:.0f},{y2:.0f} {x2},{y2:.0f}"/>')
    svg.append("</g><g id='pvnodes'>")
    for sid, cat, label, note in _PV_SOURCES:
        svg.append(_node(sid, cat, label, note, Lx, src_y[sid]))
    for mid, cat, label, note in _PV_MECH:
        svg.append(_node(mid, cat, label, note, Rx, mech_y[mid]))
    svg.append("</g></svg>")

    legend = "".join(
        f'<button class="pvlg on" data-cat="{c}" onclick="pvCat(this)">'
        f'<span class="sw" style="background:{_PV_COLOUR[c][0]};border-color:{_PV_COLOUR[c][1]}">'
        f'</span>{_html.escape(lbl)}</button>' for c, lbl in _PV_CATLABEL.items())

    # per-node detail baked for the side panel (robust — notes may contain " — ")
    adj_src: dict[str, list[str]] = {sid: [] for sid, *_ in _PV_SOURCES}
    adj_mech: dict[str, list[str]] = {mid: [] for mid, *_ in _PV_MECH}
    for s, m in _PV_EDGES:
        adj_src[s].append(m)
        adj_mech[m].append(s)
    pvinfo: dict[str, dict] = {}
    for sid, cat, label, note in _PV_SOURCES:
        d = dict(label=label, cat=cat, catLabel=_PV_CATLABEL[cat],
                 note=note, role="src", links=adj_src[sid])
        bk = _PV_REF.get(sid)
        if bk and bk in _BIB_BY_KEY:                       # bake the citation for the panel
            d["ref"] = bk
            d["refApa"] = _BIB_BY_KEY[bk]["apa"]
        pvinfo[sid] = d
    for mid, cat, label, note in _PV_MECH:
        pvinfo[mid] = dict(label=label, cat=cat, catLabel=_PV_CATLABEL[cat],
                           note=note, role="mech", links=adj_mech[mid])
    pv_data = ("<script>window.PVINFO=%s;window.PVCOL=%s;</script>"
               % (json.dumps(pvinfo, ensure_ascii=False), json.dumps(_PV_COLOUR)))
    panel_empty = ('<aside class="pvpanel empty" id="pvpanel"><div class="pbody">'
                   '<p class="pnote">Click any box to open its detail here — what it is, the '
                   'kind of source, and every link it makes.</p></div></aside>')

    return (
        ix_head("What each mechanism rests on", ix=True, hover=True)
        + '<p class="note">The pipeline’s ladders, mappings and validations are only as good as '
        "the sources under them. Each line runs from a <b>source</b> (left) to a <b>mechanism</b> "
        "it grounds (right). <b>Click</b> any box to isolate its links <i>and open a detail panel "
        "on the right</i> — a source lists everything it feeds; a mechanism lists everything it "
        "depends on, each entry clickable. Colour is the kind of source. <b>Esc</b> or click empty "
        "space clears.</p>"
        f'<div class="pvbar">{legend}'
        '<span class="pvhint" id="pvhint">Click a box to trace its provenance.</span></div>'
        f'{pv_data}<div class="pvlayout"><div class="pvwrap">{"".join(svg)}</div>{panel_empty}</div>'
        "<p class='note'>Sources are catalogued in <a href='#sources'>Data sources</a>; the "
        "validation that added Fidler as a check is on the <a href='#validation'>External "
        "validation</a> sheet.</p>")

def place_flow() -> str

The place-matching cascade: a funnel, a filter and a map, all off data/final.

Three things a reader needs that a static waterfall cannot give. The funnel carries the residual down the left of each lane as a tapering ribbon, so the fact that one tier does almost all the work is visible before a single number is read. The filter lets the tiers be ticked off — this sheet has always claimed an analysis can drop the weak ones and see what moves, and this is where that becomes an action rather than a sentence; the readout hands back the exact pandas mask. The map shows where each tier's matches land, because a rule resting on a bare unique name is only trustworthy if what it matched is spread like a population rather than piled on one district.

Every count, ribbon width and example string is recomputed at build time, so the picture cannot drift from the data it describes.

Used only inside this module.

def place_flow() -> str:
    """The place-matching cascade: a funnel, a filter and a map, all off ``data/final``.

    Three things a reader needs that a static waterfall cannot give. **The funnel** carries
    the residual down the left of each lane as a tapering ribbon, so the fact that one tier
    does almost all the work is visible before a single number is read. **The filter** lets
    the tiers be ticked off — this sheet has always claimed an analysis can drop the weak
    ones and see what moves, and this is where that becomes an action rather than a sentence;
    the readout hands back the exact pandas mask. **The map** shows where each tier's matches
    land, because a rule resting on a bare unique name is only trustworthy if what it matched
    is spread like a population rather than piled on one district.

    Every count, ribbon width and example string is recomputed at build time, so the picture
    cannot drift from the data it describes.
    """
    F = {"l": _place_frame("legionnaires_clean.parquet"),
         "h": _place_frame("habsburg_clean.parquet")}
    geom = _district_map()

    BW, BH, VG, TOP = 258, 54, 14, 104
    LX = [64, 452]                            # box left edge; the ribbon runs to its left
    RW, SPD = 38, 46                          # max ribbon width · ribbon offset left of box
    W = LX[1] + BW + 96
    H = TOP + (len(_CZ_STAGES) + 1) * (BH + VG) + 34

    def fmt(key: str, fr: str) -> str:
        n = F[fr]["t"].get(key, 0)
        return f"{n:,} · {_pct(n, F[fr]['n'])}" if n else "—"

    def entry(fr: str, lane: int) -> int:
        """Records the lane actually runs on: everything, then the Czech lane's residual."""
        return F[fr]["n"] if lane == 0 else F[fr]["t"]["_handoff"]

    # ── the ribbon: what is still unplaced, as a staircase area ─────────────────────
    # Left edge straight, right edge stepping inward — an area chart stood on end. The step
    # at a stage IS what that stage placed, so `okres` collapsing the ribbon by two thirds
    # is the finding rather than a caption about it.
    def ribbon(fr: str, lane: int) -> str:
        stages = _CZ_STAGES if lane == 0 else _SK_STAGES
        pre = "cz" if lane == 0 else "sk"
        total = max(F[fr]["n"], 1)
        left = LX[lane] - SPD

        def wide(v: int) -> float:
            return max(0.7, RW * v / total)

        run = entry(fr, lane)
        d = [f"M{left},{TOP - VG}", f"L{left + wide(run):.1f},{TOP - VG}"]
        for i, stage in enumerate(stages):
            tier = stage[1]
            if tier == "coord":                                # a layer over the lane, not a step
                continue
            y = TOP + i * (BH + VG) + BH / 2
            d.append(f"L{left + wide(run):.1f},{y:.0f}")
            run -= F[fr]["t"].get(f"{pre}:{tier}", 0)
            d.append(f"L{left + wide(run):.1f},{y:.0f}")
        y_end = TOP + len(stages) * (BH + VG) - VG / 2
        d.append(f"L{left + wide(run):.1f},{y_end:.0f}")
        d.append(f"L{left},{y_end:.0f}Z")
        return "".join(d)

    parts: list[str] = [
        f'<svg id="pfsvg" viewBox="0 0 {W} {H}" width="{W}" height="{H}" '
        'xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><defs>'
        '<marker id="pfar" viewBox="0 0 8 8" refX="7" refY="4" markerWidth="7" markerHeight="7" '
        'orient="auto"><path d="M0,0 L8,4 L0,8z" fill="#b4bcc2"/></marker></defs>']
    info: dict[str, dict] = {}
    bars: dict[str, dict[str, float]] = {"l": {}, "h": {}}

    lanes = [(_CZ_STAGES, LX[0], "CZECH LANDS → political okres", "runs on every birth record"),
             (_SK_STAGES, LX[1], "UPPER HUNGARY → járás",
              "runs only on what the Czech lane left unplaced")]
    for lane, (stages, x, head, sub) in enumerate(lanes):
        pre = "cz" if lane == 0 else "sk"
        parts.append(f'<path class="pfrib" data-lane="{lane}" d="{ribbon("l", lane)}"/>')
        parts.append(f'<text class="pfhead" x="{x}" y="46">{head}</text>')
        parts.append(f'<text class="pfsub" x="{x}" y="64">{sub}</text>')
        tail = " in" if lane == 0 else " in — the Czech lane's residual"
        parts.append(
            f'<text class="pfribcap" x="{x - SPD}" y="{TOP - VG - 9}" data-lane="{lane}" '
            f'data-l="{entry("l", lane):,}{tail}" data-h="{entry("h", lane):,}{tail}">'
            f'{entry("l", lane):,}{tail}</text>')

        for i, (key, tier, label, slab, what, refus, sym) in enumerate(stages):
            y = TOP + i * (BH + VG)
            fill, stroke = _TIER_COLOUR[tier]
            tkey = f"{pre}:{tier}"
            step = tier != "coord"
            for fr in ("l", "h"):
                mx = max((F[fr]["t"].get(f"{pre}:{t}", 0) for _k, t, *_r in stages), default=1)
                bars[fr][key] = round(F[fr]["t"].get(tkey, 0) / max(mx, 1), 4)
            legion, hab = fmt(tkey, "l"), fmt(tkey, "h")
            if i:
                parts.append(f'<path class="pfarrow" d="M{x + BW / 2:.0f},{y - VG} '
                             f'L{x + BW / 2:.0f},{y - 3}" marker-end="url(#pfar)"/>')
            tick = ""
            if step:
                tick = ('<g class="pfkeepbox" onclick="pfKeep(event,this)">'
                        f'<rect x="10" y="{BH / 2 - 8:.0f}" width="16" height="16" rx="4"/>'
                        f'<path class="pftick" d="M14,{BH / 2:.0f} l3,3.4 l6.5,-7.6"/>'
                        "<title>Tick to keep this tier in the sample below</title></g>")
            tx, keepattr = (34, ' data-keep="1"') if step else (12, "")
            parts.append(
                f'<g class="pfstage{"" if step else " layer"}" data-id="{key}" '
                f'data-tier="{tier}" data-key="{tkey}"{keepattr} '
                f'transform="translate({x},{y})" onclick="pfPick(this)">'
                f'<rect class="pfbox" width="{BW}" height="{BH}" rx="6" '
                f'style="fill:{fill};stroke:{stroke}"/>' + tick +
                f'<text class="pflab" x="{tx}" y="21">{_html.escape(label)}</text>'
                f'<text class="pfstat" x="{tx}" y="37" data-l="{_html.escape(legion)}" '
                f'data-h="{_html.escape(hab)}">{_html.escape(legion)}</text>'
                f'<text class="pftier" x="{BW - 12}" y="21">{tier}</text>'
                f'<text class="pfslab" x="{BW - 12}" y="37">{_html.escape(slab)}</text>'
                f'<rect class="pfbart" x="{tx}" y="{BH - 12}" width="{BW - tx - 12}" height="4" '
                'rx="2"/>'
                f'<rect class="pfbarv" data-k="{key}" x="{tx}" y="{BH - 12}" '
                f'width="{(BW - tx - 12) * bars["l"][key]:.1f}" height="4" rx="2" '
                f'style="fill:{stroke}"><title>this tier against the largest in its lane</title>'
                "</rect></g>")
            if refus:
                cx, cy = x + BW + 26, y + BH / 2
                parts.append(
                    f'<g class="pfveto"><path class="pfvl" d="M{x + BW},{cy} L{cx - 11},{cy}"/>'
                    f'<circle cx="{cx}" cy="{cy}" r="11"/>'
                    f'<text x="{cx}" y="{cy + 4}">⊘</text>'
                    f'<title>{len(refus)} refusal rule(s) — click the stage</title></g>')
            # label/sub are plain text and go through innerHTML in the panel — escape them;
            # what/refus are authored HTML above and are passed through as written
            info[key] = dict(label=_html.escape(label), tier=tier, sub=_html.escape(slab),
                             what=what, refus=refus, sym=sym, tkey=tkey if step else "cz:coord",
                             lane="Czech lands" if lane == 0 else "Upper Hungary")

        y = TOP + len(stages) * (BH + VG)
        f2, s2 = _TIER_COLOUR["none"]
        if lane == 0:
            # the hand-off: the second lane does not run on the dataset, it runs on this
            parts.append(
                f'<g class="pfstage term" data-id="handoff" data-tier="none" data-key="_handoff" '
                f'transform="translate({x},{y})" onclick="pfPick(this)">'
                f'<rect class="pfbox" width="{BW}" height="{BH}" rx="6" style="fill:{f2};'
                f'stroke:{s2};stroke-dasharray:4 3"/>'
                '<text class="pflab" x="12" y="21">Handed to the second frame</text>'
                f'<text class="pfstat" x="12" y="37" data-l="{fmt("_handoff", "l")}" '
                f'data-h="{fmt("_handoff", "h")}">{fmt("_handoff", "l")}</text>'
                f'<text class="pfslab hand" x="{BW - 12}" y="37">= what the second lane runs on'
                "</text></g>")
            info["handoff"] = dict(
                label="Handed to the second frame", tier="none", sub="no Czech-lands candidate",
                what="What the Czech lane cannot corroborate is not a failure — it is the input "
                     "to the Upper-Hungary lane, which is why the ribbon starts again over there "
                     "at exactly this width. The two frames are <b>exclusive</b>: notebook 02 §4 "
                     "asserts that no record is placed in both.",
                refus=[], sym="", tkey="", lane="between the frames")
            # No routed connector: a line from the bottom of one lane to the top of the next
            # has to loop around the whole figure and reads as a box drawn round lane two.
            # The link is carried by the number instead — this box and the second lane's
            # inlet caption are the same count, and the caption says so.
        else:
            parts.append(
                f'<g class="pfstage term" data-id="none" data-tier="none" data-key="_none" '
                f'transform="translate({x},{y})" onclick="pfPick(this)">'
                f'<rect class="pfbox" width="{BW}" height="{BH}" rx="6" style="fill:{f2};'
                f'stroke:{s2};stroke-dasharray:4 3"/>'
                '<text class="pflab" x="12" y="21">Left unplaced, on purpose</text>'
                f'<text class="pfstat" x="12" y="37" data-l="{fmt("_none", "l")}" '
                f'data-h="{fmt("_none", "h")}">{fmt("_none", "l")}</text>'
                f'<text class="pfslab" x="{BW - 12}" y="37">no honest candidate</text></g>')
            info["none"] = dict(
                label="Left unplaced, on purpose", tier="none", sub="no honest candidate",
                what="Every guard above prefers &lt;NA&gt; to a plausible-looking guess. The "
                     "residual is mostly Subcarpathian Rus, region labels rather than places, and "
                     "names that collide across the two frames.",
                refus=["&lt;NA&gt; is a decision, not a gap — it is what refusal looks like "
                       "in the data."],
                sym="", tkey="", lane="both")
    parts.append("</svg>")

    # ── the map: static geometry, fills painted by whatever is selected ─────────────
    # The polygons carry the fill and nothing else; the three line layers above them carry
    # every border. Which layers are visible is what the two controls actually change, so
    # the lines on the map are always exactly the boundaries of the current data unit.
    mp = "".join(f'<path class="pfd" data-u="{u}" data-p="{geom["parent"][u]}" d="{d}" '
                 'onclick="pfDistrict(this)"><title></title></path>'
                 for u, d in geom["paths"].items())
    mapsvg = (f'<svg id="pfmap" viewBox="0 0 {geom["w"]:.0f} {geom["h"]:.0f}" '
              f'xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">{mp}'
              f'<path id="pfcourtlines" d="{geom["lines"]["court"]}"/>'
              f'<path id="pftwinlines" d="{geom["lines"]["twin"]}"/>'
              f'<path id="pfokreslines" d="{geom["lines"]["okres"]}"/>'
              '<path id="pfhoverline"/><path id="pfselline"/></svg>')
    units = ('<span class="pfunitlab">Draw at</span>'
             '<button class="pfunit on" data-u="okres" onclick="pfUnit(this)">political okres'
             "</button>"
             '<button class="pfunit" data-u="court" onclick="pfUnit(this)">soudní okres</button>'
             '<span class="pfunitlab pfsep">City twins</span>'
             '<button class="pfunit on" data-pool="0" onclick="pfPool(this)">separate</button>'
             '<button class="pfunit" data-pool="1" onclick="pfPool(this)">pooled</button>')

    legend = "".join(
        f'<span class="pflg"><span class="sw" style="background:{_TIER_COLOUR[t][0]};'
        f'border-color:{_TIER_COLOUR[t][1]}"></span>{t} <i>{c}</i></span>'
        for t, c in _TIER_CONF)
    chips = ('<button class="wfchip on" data-m="l" onclick="pfMode(this)">Legionnaires</button>'
             '<button class="wfchip" data-m="h" onclick="pfMode(this)">Habsburg fallen</button>')
    panel = ('<aside class="pfpanel empty" id="pfpanel"><p class="pnote">Click any stage for what '
             "it does, what it refuses, which function owns it — and the strings it actually "
             "matched.</p></aside>")

    payload = {"n": {k: v["n"] for k, v in F.items()},
               "t": {k: v["t"] for k, v in F.items()},
               "geo": {k: v["geo"] for k, v in F.items()},
               "ex": {k: v["ex"] for k, v in F.items()},
               "court": {k: v.get("court", {}) for k, v in F.items()},
               "court_n": {k: v.get("court_n", 0) for k, v in F.items()},
               "cvo": {k: v.get("cvo", {}) for k, v in F.items()},
               "okres": {k: v.get("okres", {}) for k, v in F.items()},
               "bars": bars,
               "rib": {fr: {str(ln): ribbon(fr, ln) for ln in (0, 1)} for fr in ("l", "h")},
               "names": geom["names"], "info": info,
               "pool": geom["pool"], "poolname": geom["pool_name"],
               "poolmem": geom["pool_members"], "hutype": geom["hu_type"],
               "sel": geom["sel"], "selpool": geom["sel_pool"],
               "rate": {fr: round(_desert_rate(F[fr]), 4) for fr in ("l", "h")}}

    return (
        ix_head("How a birthplace becomes a district", ix=True, hover=True)
        + '<p class="note">Two legal frames, two lanes, one rule down both: <b>a pass accepts only '
        "what it can corroborate and refuses the rest to the next pass</b>. The ribbon down each "
        "lane is what is <i>still unplaced</i> — every step in it is a tier doing its work, and "
        "the bar inside a box is that tier against the largest in its lane. Colour is the "
        "confidence the match will carry in the data; ⊘ marks a stage with explicit refusal "
        "rules. <b>Click</b> a stage for the strings it actually matched and the map of where "
        "they landed; <b>untick</b> a tier to drop it from the sample below.</p>"
        f'<div class="pfbar">{chips}<span class="pflgs">{legend}</span></div>'
        f'<script>window.PF={json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False)};</script>'
        f'<div class="pflayout"><div class="pfwrap">{"".join(parts)}</div>{panel}</div>'
        '<div class="pfkeep" id="pfkeep"><div class="pfkeepn" id="pfkeepn"></div>'
        '<div class="pfkeepact"><button class="wfbtn sm" onclick="pfAll(1)">All tiers</button>'
        '<button class="wfbtn sm" onclick="pfAll(0)">None</button>'
        '<button class="wfbtn sm" onclick="pfCopyMask(this)">Copy the mask</button></div>'
        '<pre class="pfmask"><code id="pfmaskc"></code></pre></div>'
        + ix_head("Where the matches land", level=3, ix=True, hover=True)
        + '<p class="note">The same cascade, on the ground: Czech <i>okresy</i> from the MPIDR '
        "1910 boundaries and Upper-Hungary <i>járás</i> from GISta Hungarorum, the second "
        "re-projected onto the first so the two frames sit on one plane. Shading is records per "
        "district for the tiers ticked above; click a stage to isolate that tier, or click a "
        "district to see who was born there. The strong tiers should reproduce the population, "
        "so read those as a sanity check — it is <code>fuzzy</code>, <code>settlement</code> and "
        "<code>muni</code> that are worth looking at, where a tier piled onto one district would "
        "mean a rule firing on a name rather than on a place.</p>"
        '<p class="note">The mesh is finer than the measurement: the polygons are <b>court '
        "districts</b> (<i>soudní okresy</i>), the unit the boundary file draws, while the "
        "matching resolves to the <b>political okres</b> above them. Every edge is classified "
        "exactly — adjacent polygons share their border vertex for vertex — so <b>drawn at "
        "political okres only district boundaries are drawn at all</b>, and the court "
        "sub-divisions appear as pale hairlines only when you ask for them. Switch the unit "
        "to shade the courts themselves, from <code>birth_court_id</code>; that layer is "
        "<i>coordinate</i>-derived, so it covers fewer records and is a cross-check rather "
        "than a finer version of the same count.</p>"
        '<p class="note"><b>City twins.</b> Ten Czech seats name both a <i>Statutarstadt</i> '
        "and the rural okres around it — Brno and Brno&nbsp;(město), Olomouc and Olomouc "
        "(město). They are two okresy and the records are split between them, but the "
        "court-level census cannot separate nine of the ten, so the analytical unit is the "
        "<b>pooled</b> pair (<code>census_okres_id</code>, 148 units rather than 158; "
        '<a href="#decisions">Decisions</a> D-18). Switch <i>City twins</i> to see the map '
        "the census can actually support: the city border comes off and the two shares merge "
        "into one. Worth doing once on Brno or Olomouc, because the thing it removes is real "
        "— in <b>all ten</b> pairs the city is the <i>paler</i> patch, a small light core "
        "inside a darker rural ring (Brno 773 births against the ring's 2,118), so "
        "legionnaires were rural-born even relative to their own district town. Desertion "
        "runs the other way in the larger pairs and not at all in the smaller ones — Brno "
        "město 2.98&nbsp;% against the ring's 1.56&nbsp;%, Liberec 4.21 against 2.44, but "
        "Uherské Hradiště město none at all on 51 births. Pooling averages every one of those "
        "contrasts away, which is the price the census charges.</p>"
        # the district read-out sits BESIDE the map, not up beside the funnel: clicking a
        # district and then scrolling half a page to find out what you clicked is not reading
        f'<div class="pfmaplayout"><div class="pfmapwrap"><div class="pfunitbar">{units}'
        '<span class="pfunitnote" id="pfunitnote"></span></div>'
        f'<div class="pfmaphd" id="pfmaphd"></div>{mapsvg}'
        '<div class="pfmapleg" id="pfmapleg"></div>'
        '<p class="pfsumnote" id="pfsumnote"></p></div>'
        '<aside class="pfpanel empty" id="pfmappanel"><p class="pnote">Click any district '
        "for who was born there — how many, how often they deserted, which theatre they went "
        "to, and how far they fell on enrolment.</p></aside></div>"
        '<p class="note">The tiers are a single column in the data '
        "(<code>birth_okres_match</code> / <code>birth_jaras_match</code>), which is what makes "
        "the filter above reproducible in three lines. Why the weak tiers are kept rather than "
        'dropped at source is <a href="#decisions">Decisions</a> D-11.</p><hr>')

def education_figures() -> str:
    """The education charts from notebook 03, embedded on the ladder sheet.

    Globbed rather than named, so a chart the author adds later appears here
    without a code change — the same contract the Descriptives sheet offers.
    Silent when nothing is built: the site must render on a fresh checkout.
    """
    figs = sorted(p for p in ROOT.joinpath("output", "figures").rglob("*.png")
                  if p.stem.startswith("educ") and "_beamer" not in p.name)
    if not figs:
        return ""
    S = ["<h2>The ladder in the data</h2>",
         '<p class="note">Built by <code>notebooks/03_visualisation.ipynb</code> from '
         "<code>data/final</code>. The stack is coloured on the sequential ramp, not the "
         "categorical palette, because the variable is ordinal: light at the bottom rung, "
         "navy at the top. Click to enlarge.</p>",
         "<div class='figgrid'>"]
    for f in figs:
        b64 = base64.b64encode(f.read_bytes()).decode()
        cap = f.stem.replace("_", " ").capitalize()
        S.append(f'<figure><img src="data:image/png;base64,{b64}" '
                 f'alt="{_html.escape(cap)}" onclick="zoom(this)" title="Click to enlarge">'
                 f"<figcaption>{_html.escape(cap)}<br>"
                 f"<code>{f.relative_to(ROOT).as_posix()}</code></figcaption></figure>")
    S.append("</div>")
    return "".join(S)

def theatre_figures(src: Path = THEATRE_INTERIM) -> dict[str, str]:
    """The theatre sheet's three figures, keyed ``explainer`` / ``trend`` / ``map``.

    Each is '' when its inputs are not built, so the site renders on a fresh checkout.
    """
    need = {"panel": "place_year_panel.parquet", "court": "court_year_panel.parquet",
            "evidence": "theatre_evidence.csv"}
    if not all((src / f).is_file() for f in need.values()):
        return {}
    panel = pd.read_parquet(src / need["panel"])
    court = pd.read_parquet(src / need["court"], columns=["court_id", "year", "places_active_certain",
                                                          "places_active_possible"])
    evidence = pd.read_csv(src / need["evidence"], dtype={"source_key": str}, low_memory=False)
    return {"trend": _theatre_trend(panel), "map": _theatre_map(court),
            "explainer": _theatre_explainer(evidence, panel)}
