def lexikon_page() -> str:
    """The annotated page of the 1910 register, plus the plate and its vocabulary."""
    manifest = LEXIKON_FIGURE / "lexikon_figure.json"
    if not manifest.is_file():
        IX_WARNINGS.append(
            "lexikon-1910: reference/places/figure/ not built — run "
            "`python utils/lexikon_1910/build_lexikon_figure.py`")
        return ('<p class="note">The page figure has not been built. Run '
                "<code>python utils/lexikon_1910/build_lexikon_figure.py</code> and "
                "rebuild.</p>")
    payload = json.loads(manifest.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    counts = payload.get("counts", {})

    # ── the annotated pages ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
    cz, de = payload["pages"]["cz"], payload["pages"]["de"]
    tabs = (
        f'<button class="lxtab on" data-page="cz" onclick="lxTab(this)">'
        f'Čechy 1910 · p.&nbsp;{cz["printed"]}</button>'
        f'<button class="lxtab" data-page="de" onclick="lxTab(this)">'
        f'Böhmen 1910 · p.&nbsp;{de["printed"]}</button>')
    panel = ('<aside class="lxpanel empty" id="lxpanel">'
             '<p class="pnote">Click any box on the page. The same municipality is '
             "printed in both editions, on different pages and in a different position "
             "in the district.</p></aside>")

    zone_data = {}
    for key in ("cz", "de"):
        for z in payload["pages"][key]["zones"]:
            spec = LX_ZONES.get(z["id"], {})
            # The panel is a 320 px column and these crops are wide strips of
            # six-point type, so every one of them is click-to-enlarge. Only the
            # block table is legible at that width unaided.
            extra = ""
            if spec.get("table"):
                extra = _lx_block_table(payload)
            elif spec.get("entry"):
                extra = _lx_img(payload["crops"].get("entry", ""), cls="lxcrop",
                                zoom=True, alt="Brzice's entry")
            elif spec.get("entry_de"):
                extra = (_lx_img(payload["crops"].get("entry_de", ""), cls="lxcrop",
                                 zoom=True, alt="Brzitz's entry")
                         + '<p class="lxsrc">The German text layer reads this key as '
                           "<code>4, —)</code> and drops the two entries that follow "
                           "it altogether.</p>")
            elif spec.get("seat"):
                extra = _lx_img(payload["crops"].get("seat", ""), cls="lxcrop",
                                zoom=True, alt="Česká Skalice's entry")
            elif spec.get("legend"):
                extra = _lx_img(payload["crops"].get("legend", ""), cls="lxcrop",
                                zoom=True, alt="The postal and railway legend")
            zone_data[z["id"]] = dict(label=z["label"], what=spec.get("what", ""),
                                      why=spec.get("why", ""), read=z.get("read", ""),
                                      extra=extra)

    reader = (
        ix_head("One page, three documents", ix=True, hover=True)
        + '<p class="note">The volume\'s own <i>Návod</i> divides every page into three: '
          "a <b>table</b>, a <b>two-column apparatus</b> below it, and a <b>legend</b> under "
          "a rule at the foot. The table is what the text layer reads well. The apparatus is "
          "what the project is actually after, and it is mostly pictures. Both editions of "
          "the same municipality are here — click any box.</p>"
        f'<div class="lxbar">{tabs}'
        '<label class="lxtoggle"><input type="checkbox" checked '
        'onchange="lxBoxes(this.checked)"> Show the boxes</label></div>'
        f"<script>window.LX={json.dumps(zone_data, ensure_ascii=False)};</script>"
        '<div class="lxlayout"><div class="lxwrap">'
        + _lx_stage(payload, "cz", "Podrobný seznam míst — IX. Čechy",
                    f'scan {cz["scan"]:04d}, printed page {cz["printed"]} · '
                    f'{cz["rules_observed"]} of 18 rules found on this page', on=True)
        + _lx_stage(payload, "de", "Spezialortsrepertorium — IX. Böhmen",
                    f'scan {de["scan"]:04d}, printed page {de["printed"]} · '
                    "no rules in the text layer at all")
        + f"</div>{panel}</div>")

    # ── what Brzice had ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    entry = (
        ix_head("What one village had, and what three readers made of it")
        + '<p class="note">One printed line, read three ways. This is the whole difficulty '
          "of the source in four glyphs: the arithmetic upstairs has an identity to check "
          "itself against, and down here there is none.</p>"
        + _lx_entry_rows(payload)
        + '<p class="note">So Brzice in 1910 had a two-class primary school, a midwife, a '
          "fire brigade and one Raiffeisen credit union — and no post office, no doctor, no "
          "parish and no railway station. None of that is in the census; all of it is in "
          "this line.</p>")

    # ── the plate and the vocabulary ─────────────────────────────────────────
    plate = (
        ix_head("Výklad značek — the plate, and the vocabulary taken from it", ix=True)
        + '<p class="note">The volume defines its own pictograms once, on a plate in the '
          "front matter, and both editions print it. It is the only place in 756 pages where "
          "the designs are drawn large enough to recognise: <code>[school]</code> is "
          "112 × 48 px here, and an entry's whole printed line downstairs is <b>44 px</b> "
          "tall. Click either plate to enlarge.</p>"
        '<div class="lxplates">'
        f'<figure>{_lx_img(payload["plates"]["cz"]["image"], cls="lxplate", zoom=True, alt="Výklad značek")}'
        f'<figcaption>Czech edition, printed page XI '
        f'(scan {payload["plates"]["cz"]["scan"]:04d})</figcaption></figure>'
        f'<figure>{_lx_img(payload["plates"]["de"]["image"], cls="lxplate", zoom=True, alt="Zeichenerklärung")}'
        f'<figcaption>German edition, same plate '
        f'(scan {payload["plates"]["de"]["scan"]:04d})</figcaption></figure></div>'
        '<p class="note">That 0.45× is why matching the plate\'s own crops against the '
        "entries <b>does not work</b>, and it was measured rather than assumed: against its "
        "own source crop a template scores <b>1.000</b>; against a real entry line at the "
        "right scale it peaks at <b>0.644</b>, and over a whole section the detections "
        "cluster <b>0.62–0.83 with no separation at all</b> — the strongest hits being "
        "settlement symbols that cannot occur in an offices section and are in fact "
        "correlating with ordinary letters. Nothing downstream consumes it as an "
        "identification.</p>"
        + _lx_gallery(payload))

    # ── the numbers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    # No `_with_toc` here: this block is injected into a markdown sheet, and `main`
    # runs the contents strip over the whole sheet once the two are joined. Adding
    # one here would claim the strip for the figure and leave the prose out of it.
    return (reader + entry + _lx_register_walkthrough() + plate + _lx_grades(counts)
            + f"<script>{_LX_JS}</script><hr>")

def route_flow() -> str:
    """The reading route as a flow chart — the eight steps, and a mark's four ways out.

    Prose has to name the exits one at a time and in the middle of the step that produces
    them; a figure can put all four beside the spine with the share that took each, which is
    the design's whole claim. The page-set switch is the second thing worth drawing: the
    sealed half runs on *this* route, so changing the set changes which steps run and what
    has been read, and nothing else about the chart.
    """
    runs = {f"{key}:{ps}": _route_counts(f"{prefix}_{ps}")
            for key, _n, prefix, _t in _RT_EDITIONS for ps, *_rest in _RT_PAGESETS}
    have = [k for k, *_r in _RT_EDITIONS if any(runs[f"{k}:{ps}"] for ps, *_x in _RT_PAGESETS)]
    # a page set read for any edition is marked read; the note under the bar says which
    states = {ps: ("read" if any(runs[f"{k}:{ps}"] for k, *_r in _RT_EDITIONS) else state)
              for ps, _l, state, _d in _RT_PAGESETS}
    names = {k: n for k, n, _r, _t in _RT_EDITIONS}

    BW, BH, GAP, TOP = 452, 68, 16, 94
    SX, EX, EW, EH = 44, 568, 330, 58
    W, H = EX + EW + 14, TOP + len(_RT_STAGES) * (BH + GAP) + 10

    parts = [
        f'<svg id="rtsvg" viewBox="0 0 {W} {H}" width="{W}" height="{H}" '
        'xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><defs>'
        '<marker id="rtar" viewBox="0 0 8 8" refX="7" refY="4" markerWidth="7" '
        'markerHeight="7" orient="auto"><path d="M0,0 L8,4 L0,8z" fill="#b4bcc2"/></marker>'
        '</defs>',
        f'<text class="rthead" x="{SX}" y="34">THE FROZEN ROUTE — one edition, one page set</text>',
        f'<text class="rtsub" x="{SX}" y="54">notebooks/15_frozen_run.ipynb, every step in '
        'order; click a step</text>',
        f'<text class="rthead" x="{EX}" y="34">HOW A MARK IS SETTLED</text>',
        f'<text class="rtsub" x="{EX}" y="54">its four ways off the spine</text>']

    info: dict[str, dict] = {}
    stage_y: dict[str, float] = {}
    for i, st in enumerate(_RT_STAGES):
        y = TOP + i * (BH + GAP)
        stage_y[st["id"]] = y
        fill, stroke = _RT_KIND[st["kind"]]
        if i:
            parts.append(f'<path class="rtarrow" d="M{SX + BW / 2:.0f},{y - GAP} '
                         f'L{SX + BW / 2:.0f},{y - 3}" marker-end="url(#rtar)"/>')
        # The chips ride the title line, not the foot of the box: the gloss is the longest
        # text here and a chip over its tail is unreadable in exactly the two steps that
        # carry the most readers. Widths are from the glyph count, so a longer name pushes
        # the row left rather than overprinting the one beside it.
        chips, cx = "", BW - 12
        for who in reversed(st["who"]):
            wid = 8 + 5.4 * len(who)
            cx -= wid
            chips += (f'<g class="rtwho"><rect x="{cx:.0f}" y="12" width="{wid:.0f}" '
                      f'height="18" rx="9"/><text x="{cx + wid / 2:.0f}" y="24.5">'
                      f'{_html.escape(who)}</text></g>')
            cx -= 5
        dash = ';stroke-dasharray:5 3' if st["kind"] == "prep" else ""
        parts.append(
            f'<g class="rtstage" data-id="{st["id"]}" '
            f'transform="translate({SX},{y})" onclick="rtPick(this)">'
            f'<rect class="rtbox" width="{BW}" height="{BH}" rx="7" '
            f'style="fill:{fill};stroke:{stroke}{dash}"/>'
            f'<circle class="rtn" cx="26" cy="26" r="13" style="fill:{stroke}"/>'
            f'<text class="rtnt" x="26" y="30">{st["n"]}</text>'
            f'<text class="rtlab" x="50" y="25">{_html.escape(st["name"])}</text>'
            f'<text class="rtgloss" x="50" y="43">{_html.escape(st["gloss"])}</text>'
            + chips + "</g>")
        info[st["id"]] = dict(n=st["n"], name=_html.escape(st["name"]), kind=st["kind"],
                              gloss=_html.escape(st["gloss"]), what=st["what"], why=st["why"],
                              decisions=st["decisions"], setnote=st.get("setnote", {}),
                              exits=[k for k, src, *_r in _RT_FATES if src == st["id"]])

    # The exits are laid out as their own column, stacked from the first step that feeds
    # them: three hang off step 4 and one off step 5, so stacking them against their own
    # stages would overlap. Each keeps an elbow back to the step it belongs to.
    y0 = stage_y[_RT_FATES[0][1]] - 6
    for j, (ekey, src, elabel, egloss) in enumerate(_RT_FATES):
        ey = y0 + j * (EH + 12)
        col, soft = _RT_EXITS[ekey]
        mid = stage_y[src] + BH / 2
        parts.append(
            f'<path class="rtelbow" data-exit="{ekey}" style="stroke:{col}" '
            f'd="M{SX + BW},{mid:.0f} H{(SX + BW + EX) / 2:.0f} V{ey + EH / 2:.0f} '
            f'H{EX - 5:.0f}" marker-end="url(#rtar)"/>'
            f'<g class="rtexit" data-exit="{ekey}" transform="translate({EX},{ey:.0f})">'
            f'<rect width="{EW}" height="{EH}" rx="7" style="fill:{soft};stroke:{col}"/>'
            f'<text class="rtelab" x="14" y="24">{_html.escape(elabel)}</text>'
            f'<text class="rtegloss" x="14" y="42">{_html.escape(egloss)}</text>'
            f'<text class="rten" data-exit="{ekey}" x="{EW - 14}" y="27">—</text>'
            f'<text class="rtesh" data-exit="{ekey}" x="{EW - 14}" y="44">&#160;</text>'
            "</g>")
    parts.append("</svg>")

    first = have[0] if have else "cz"
    pills = "".join(
        f'<button class="rtpill{" on" if k == first else ""}" data-ed="{k}" '
        f'onclick="rtEdition(this)"{"" if k in have else " disabled"}>{_html.escape(name)}'
        f'<i>{_html.escape(title)}</i></button>'
        for k, name, _run, title in _RT_EDITIONS)
    sets = "".join(
        f'<button class="rtset{" on" if k == "gold" else ""}" data-set="{k}" '
        f'onclick="rtPages(this)">{_html.escape(label)}<i class="{states[k]}">{states[k]}</i></button>'
        for k, label, _state, _d in _RT_PAGESETS)

    if len(have) == len(_RT_EDITIONS):
        missing = ""
    elif not have:
        missing = ('<p class="note">No frozen run is present under <code>output/frozen/</code> '
                   "on this machine, so the chart draws the route without its numbers — run "
                   "notebook 15 and rebuild.</p>")
    else:
        missing = ('<p class="note">Only ' + " and ".join(_html.escape(names[k]) for k in have)
                   + " has been read on this machine, so the other edition's pill is disabled "
                     "and its numbers stay blank.</p>")

    payload = json.dumps({"runs": runs, "stages": info,
                          "sets": {k: dict(state=states[k], note=d) for k, _l, _s, d in _RT_PAGESETS}},
                         ensure_ascii=False)

    return (ix_head("The route a mark travels", ix=True, hover=True)
            + "<p>The eight steps below, and the four ways a mark can leave them. The spine "
              "is the runner's own order; the boxes on the right are the fates, with the "
              "share of marks that took each one in the run shown. Click a step for what it "
              "does and why it is there; the pills switch the edition and the page set. "
              "Every count is read from that run's own <code>final_inventory.csv</code> — "
              "the stages from <code>run_frozen.py</code>, nothing typed.</p>"
            + missing
            + f'<div class="rtctl"><span class="rtctll">Edition</span>{pills}'
              f'<span class="rtctll">Page set</span>{sets}</div>'
            + '<div class="rtlayout"><div class="rtwrap">' + "".join(parts) + "</div>"
            + '<aside class="rtpanel empty" id="rtpanel"><p class="pnote">Click a step for '
              "what it does, why it is there and the decisions that settled it. The four "
              "boxes on the right are the only ways a mark can be settled — the bar below "
              "carries their shares.</p></aside></div>"
            + '<div class="rtbar"><div class="rtbarhd">Of the <b id="rtbarn">—</b> marks '
              "this run settled, how each one was settled</div>"
              '<div class="rtmix" id="rtmix"></div><div class="rtmixlab" id="rtmixlab"></div>'
              '<p class="rtnote" id="rtnote"></p></div>'
            + f'<script>window.RT={payload};{_RT_JS}</script>')

def occupation_flow() -> str

The coding funnel, the class ladder and the gradient the two of them produce.

Three things prose cannot do on this sheet. The funnel carries the residual down the left as a tapering ribbon, so the fact that one rule does five sixths of the work is visible before a number is read. The ladder shows where the codes land, and in particular how much of the Legion sits on two rungs. The filter turns this sheet's own robustness claim into an action: untick the compound rules, and the desertion gradient below redraws on exact dictionary matches alone — with Wilson intervals, so the shrinking sample argues for itself.

Every count, ribbon width and example string is recomputed from data/final at build time, so the picture cannot drift from the data it describes.

Used only inside this module.

def occupation_flow() -> str:
    """The coding funnel, the class ladder and the gradient the two of them produce.

    Three things prose cannot do on this sheet. **The funnel** carries the residual down
    the left as a tapering ribbon, so the fact that one rule does five sixths of the work
    is visible before a number is read. **The ladder** shows where the codes land, and in
    particular how much of the Legion sits on two rungs. **The filter** turns this sheet's
    own robustness claim into an action: untick the compound rules, and the desertion
    gradient below redraws on exact dictionary matches alone — with Wilson intervals, so
    the shrinking sample argues for itself.

    Every count, ribbon width and example string is recomputed from ``data/final`` at build
    time, so the picture cannot drift from the data it describes.
    """
    F = _occupation_frame()
    n, ne = F["n"], F["n_nonempty"]

    BW, BH, VG, TOP = 300, 54, 15, 104
    LX, RW, SPD = 74, 40, 50                   # box left edge · max ribbon width · its offset
    LADX, LADW = 452, 250                      # the HISCLASS ladder column
    W, H = LADX + LADW + 108, TOP + (len(_OC_STAGES) + 1) * (BH + VG) + 40

    rows = _OC_STAGES + [(_OC_TERMINAL[0], _OC_TERMINAL[1], _OC_TERMINAL[2], _OC_TERMINAL[3],
                          False, _OC_TERMINAL[4], _OC_TERMINAL[5], _OC_TERMINAL[6])]

    def wide(v: int) -> float:
        return max(0.7, RW * v / max(n, 1))

    # ── the ribbon: what is still uncoded, as a staircase area ─────────────────────
    # Left edge straight, right edge stepping inward. The step at a stage IS what that
    # stage coded, so `exact` collapsing the ribbon almost to nothing is the finding.
    d, run = [f"M{LX - SPD},{TOP - VG}", f"L{LX - SPD + wide(n):.1f},{TOP - VG}"], n
    for i, row in enumerate(rows):
        y = TOP + i * (BH + VG) + BH / 2
        d.append(f"L{LX - SPD + wide(run):.1f},{y:.0f}")
        run -= F["t"].get(row[0], 0)
        d.append(f"L{LX - SPD + wide(run):.1f},{y:.0f}")
    y_end = TOP + len(rows) * (BH + VG) - VG / 2
    d += [f"L{LX - SPD + wide(run):.1f},{y_end:.0f}", f"L{LX - SPD},{y_end:.0f}Z"]

    parts = [f'<svg id="ocsvg" viewBox="0 0 {W} {H}" width="{W}" height="{H}" '
             'xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><defs>'
             '<marker id="ocar" viewBox="0 0 8 8" refX="7" refY="4" markerWidth="7" '
             'markerHeight="7" orient="auto"><path d="M0,0 L8,4 L0,8z" fill="#b4bcc2"/></marker>'
             "</defs>",
             f'<path class="ocrib" d="{"".join(d)}"/>',
             f'<text class="ochead" x="{LX}" y="46">EVERY RECORD → A HISCO CODE</text>',
             f'<text class="ocsub" x="{LX}" y="64">rules in the order the matcher tries them; '
             "an earlier rule wins</text>",
             f'<text class="ocribcap" x="{LX - SPD}" y="{TOP - VG - 9}">{n:,} in</text>',
             f'<text class="ochead" x="{LADX}" y="46">WHERE THE CODE LANDS</text>',
             f'<text class="ocsub" x="{LADX}" y="64">HISCLASS, coloured by the 5-class '
             "collapse</text>"]

    info: dict[str, dict] = {}
    biggest = max((F["t"].get(r[0], 0) for r in rows), default=1)
    for i, (key, tier, label, slab, keep, what, refus, sym) in enumerate(rows):
        y = TOP + i * (BH + VG)
        cnt = F["t"].get(key, 0)
        fill, stroke = (("#f4f5f7", "#8a939c") if tier in ("—", "none")
                        else _TIER_COLOUR.get("okres", ("#dbe4ec", CU_NAVY)))
        if tier in ("dual", "head"):
            fill, stroke = "#dfeaf1", "#3D7EA6"
        elif tier == "prefix":
            fill, stroke = "#f6ecd9", "#c7a548"
        if i:
            parts.append(f'<path class="ocarrow" d="M{LX + BW / 2:.0f},{y - VG} '
                         f'L{LX + BW / 2:.0f},{y - 3}" marker-end="url(#ocar)"/>')
        tick = ""
        if keep:
            tick = ('<g class="ockeepbox" onclick="ocKeep(event,this)">'
                    f'<rect x="10" y="{BH / 2 - 8:.0f}" width="16" height="16" rx="4"/>'
                    f'<path class="octick" d="M14,{BH / 2:.0f} l3,3.4 l6.5,-7.6"/>'
                    "<title>Tick to keep this rule in the sample below</title></g>")
        tx = 34 if keep else 12
        dash = ';stroke-dasharray:4 3' if tier in ("—", "none") else ""
        parts.append(
            f'<g class="ocstage{" term" if tier in ("—", "none") else ""}" data-id="{key}" '
            f'data-tier="{tier}"{" data-keep=\"1\"" if keep else ""} '
            f'transform="translate({LX},{y})" onclick="ocPick(this)">'
            f'<rect class="ocbox" width="{BW}" height="{BH}" rx="6" '
            f'style="fill:{fill};stroke:{stroke}{dash}"/>' + tick +
            f'<text class="oclab" x="{tx}" y="21">{label}</text>'
            # the empty-cell row is a share of *everything*; every rule below it is a share
            # of the non-empty values it actually runs on
            f'<text class="ocstat" x="{tx}" y="37">{cnt:,} · '
            f'{_pct(cnt, n) if key == "empty" else _pct(cnt, ne)}'
            f'{" of all records" if key == "empty" else " of non-empty"}</text>'
            f'<text class="octier" x="{BW - 12}" y="21">{tier}</text>'
            f'<text class="ocslab" x="{BW - 12}" y="37">{slab}</text>'
            f'<rect class="ocbart" x="{tx}" y="{BH - 12}" width="{BW - tx - 12}" height="4" '
            'rx="2"/>'
            f'<rect class="ocbarv" x="{tx}" y="{BH - 12}" '
            f'width="{(BW - tx - 12) * cnt / max(biggest, 1):.1f}" height="4" rx="2" '
            f'style="fill:{stroke}"><title>this rule against the largest</title>'
            "</rect></g>")
        if refus:
            cx, cy = LX + BW + 24, y + BH / 2
            parts.append(f'<g class="ocveto"><path class="ocvl" d="M{LX + BW},{cy} '
                         f'L{cx - 11},{cy}"/><circle cx="{cx}" cy="{cy}" r="11"/>'
                         f'<text x="{cx}" y="{cy + 4}">⊘</text>'
                         f'<title>{len(refus)} refusal rule(s) — click the stage</title></g>')
        info[key] = dict(kind="stage", label=label, tier=tier, sub=slab, what=what,
                         refus=refus, sym=sym, n=cnt)

    # ── the ladder: 13 rungs plus the deliberate no-class outflow ───────────────────
    LADT, RH, RG = TOP, 22, 5
    mx = max(list(F["hc"].values()) + [1])
    for k in range(1, 14):
        cnt = F["hc"][str(k)]
        y = LADT + (k - 1) * (RH + RG)
        fill, stroke = _OC_G_COLOUR[_OC_GROUP[k]]
        # Rung subtitle used to be the class's mean HISCAM. HISCAM was dropped in
        # occupations 1.2.0 (DECISIONS D-30) for being non-monotonic on this sample, so
        # the rung now carries the thing the sheet is actually arguing about.
        _cr = F["cls_rate"].get(str(k))
        _sub = f"{_cr[1] / _cr[0]:.2%} deserted" if _cr and _cr[0] else "—"
        info[f"c{k}"] = dict(kind="class", label=f"{k}. {F['hc_label'][str(k)]}",
                             tier=_OC_G_LABEL[_OC_GROUP[k]], sub=_sub, n=cnt)
        parts.append(
            f'<g class="occls" data-id="c{k}" transform="translate({LADX},{y})" '
            f'onclick="ocPick(this)">'
            f'<rect class="ocrowhit" x="-4" y="-2" width="{LADW + 60}" height="{RH + 4}" rx="4"/>'
            f'<text class="ocno" x="0" y="15">{k}</text>'
            f'<rect class="ocrung" x="18" y="4" width="{max(1.5, (LADW - 30) * cnt / mx):.1f}" '
            f'height="{RH - 8}" rx="3" style="fill:{fill};stroke:{stroke}"/>'
            f'<text class="occnt" x="{LADW + 52}" y="15">{cnt:,}</text>'
            f'<title>{_html.escape(F["hc_label"][str(k)])} — {cnt:,} '
            f'({_pct(cnt, sum(F["hc"].values()))})</title></g>')
    y = LADT + 13 * (RH + RG) + 8
    parts.append(
        f'<g class="occls term" data-id="noclass" transform="translate({LADX},{y})" '
        f'onclick="ocPick(this)">'
        f'<rect class="ocrowhit" x="-4" y="-2" width="{LADW + 60}" height="{RH + 4}" rx="4"/>'
        f'<text class="ocno" x="0" y="15">−1</text>'
        f'<rect class="ocrung dash" x="18" y="4" '
        f'width="{max(1.5, (LADW - 30) * F["hc_noclass"] / mx):.1f}" height="{RH - 8}" rx="3"/>'
        f'<text class="occnt" x="{LADW + 52}" y="15">{F["hc_noclass"]:,}</text></g>')
    parts.append(f'<text class="ocsub" x="{LADX}" y="{y + 42}">a code, but no class — '
                 "students and the other deliberate −1s</text>")
    info["noclass"] = dict(
        kind="class", label="Coded, but deliberately no class", tier="by design",
        sub="HISCO −1 with a status modifier", n=F["hc_noclass"],
        what="HISCO does not treat study as an occupation, and the HSN scheme excludes "
             f"status 41 from HISCLASS. The {F['n_students']:,} students therefore carry a "
             "code and a status but <b>no</b> social class — they stay identifiable through "
             "<code>occupation_status</code> rather than being dropped or forced onto a "
             "rung. Any value on <i>relation</i> is excluded the same way.",
        refus=["This is why HISCLASS coverage sits below HISCO coverage. The gap is a "
               "decision, not a shortfall."],
        sym="occupations._scales")
    parts.append("</svg>")

    payload = {k: F[k] for k in ("n", "n_nonempty", "t", "hc", "hc_label", "hc_noclass",
                                 "cls", "cls_rate", "ex", "grad", "coded",
                                 "n_distinct_un", "n_students")}
    payload["info"] = info
    payload["glabel"] = {str(k): v for k, v in _OC_G_LABEL.items()}
    payload["gcolour"] = {str(k): list(v) for k, v in _OC_G_COLOUR.items()}

    legend = "".join(
        f'<span class="oclg"><span class="sw" style="background:{_OC_G_COLOUR[g][0]};'
        f'border-color:{_OC_G_COLOUR[g][1]}"></span>{_OC_G_LABEL[g]}</span>'
        for g in (1, 2, 3, 4, 5))
    panel = ('<aside class="pfpanel empty" id="ocpanel"><p class="pnote">Click a rule for what '
             "it does, what it refuses, which function owns it — and the strings it actually "
             "matched. Click a rung for the trades on it.</p></aside>")

    return (
        ix_head("How a Czech word becomes a social class", ix=True, hover=True)
        + '<p class="note">One lane, four rules, tried in the order shown — <b>an earlier rule '
        "wins, and the later ones only ever see what it left</b>. The ribbon down the left is "
        "what is <i>still uncoded</i>; every step in it is a rule doing its work, and the bar "
        "inside a box is that rule against the largest. ⊘ marks a stage with explicit refusal "
        "rules. On the right, where the resolved codes land on the HISCLASS ladder. "
        "<b>Click</b> anything for the detail; <b>untick</b> a rule to drop it from the "
        "gradient below.</p>"
        f'<div class="pfbar"><span class="pflgs">{legend}</span></div>'
        f'<script>window.OC={json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False)};</script>'
        f'<div class="pflayout"><div class="pfwrap">{"".join(parts)}</div>{panel}</div>'
        + ix_head("Does the coding drive the result?", level=3, ix=True, hover=True)
        + '<p class="note">The three compound rules — <code>dual</code>, <code>head</code>, '
        "<code>prefix</code> — are the least externally-anchored part of this method: nothing "
        "outside the project vouches for them the way the German bridge and OccCANINE vouch "
        "for the codes themselves. So the question worth asking is whether they are "
        "<i>manufacturing</i> the class gradient. Untick them and watch. The rates are "
        "unadjusted means with 95% Wilson intervals, which is the interval that behaves when "
        "the sample shrinks and the event is rare — as the bars widen rather than move, that "
        "is the answer.</p>"
        '<div class="pfkeep" id="ockeep"><div class="pfkeepn" id="ockeepn"></div>'
        '<div class="pfkeepact"><button class="wfbtn sm" onclick="ocAll(1)">All rules</button>'
        '<button class="wfbtn sm" onclick="ocAll(0)">Exact only</button>'
        '<button class="wfbtn sm" onclick="ocCopyMask(this)">Copy the mask</button></div>'
        '<div class="ocgrad" id="ocgrad"></div>'
        '<pre class="pfmask"><code id="ocmaskc"></code></pre></div>'
        '<p class="note">The rule that fired is a single column in the data '
        "(<code>occupation_match</code>), which is what makes the filter above reproducible "
        "in three lines. Russia carries essentially all Legion desertion, so these levels are "
        "descriptive only — they are not conditioned on theatre, enrolment date or unit.</p>"
        "<hr>")

def reading_map() -> str:
    """Three routes through the sheets, for a reader meeting a 55-item sidebar cold.

    The sidebar is complete but unordered — it says what exists, not where to start. These
    are the three questions people actually arrive with.
    """
    titles = {s["id"]: s["title"] for s in SHEETS}
    NW, NH, GAP, LX, RH, TOP = 122, 40, 22, 172, 62, 52
    W = LX + 4 * NW + 3 * GAP + 20
    H = TOP + len(_PATHS) * RH + 10
    svg = [f'<svg id="pathmap" viewBox="0 0 {W} {H}" width="{W}" height="{H}" '
           'xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><defs>'
           '<marker id="pmar" viewBox="0 0 8 8" refX="7" refY="4" markerWidth="6" '
           'markerHeight="6" orient="auto"><path d="M0,0 L8,4 L0,8z" fill="#b4bcc2"/></marker>'
           '</defs><text class="pmh" x="0" y="24">START HERE</text>']
    for r, (q, gloss, col, ids) in enumerate(_PATHS):
        y = TOP + r * RH
        svg.append(f'<text class="pmq" x="0" y="{y + 20}">{_html.escape(q)}</text>'
                   f'<text class="pmg" x="0" y="{y + 34}">{_html.escape(gloss)}</text>')
        for i, sid in enumerate(ids):
            x = LX + i * (NW + GAP)
            if i:
                svg.append(f'<path class="pmarrow" d="M{x - GAP + 2},{y + NH / 2:.0f} '
                           f'L{x - 4},{y + NH / 2:.0f}" marker-end="url(#pmar)"/>')
            svg.append(
                f'<a href="#{sid}"><g class="pmnode" transform="translate({x},{y})">'
                f'<rect width="{NW}" height="{NH}" rx="5" style="stroke:{col}"/>'
                f'<text x="{NW / 2:.0f}" y="{NH / 2 + 4:.0f}">'
                f'{_html.escape(titles.get(sid, sid))}</text></g></a>')
    svg.append("</svg>")
    return ('<h2>Where to start</h2>'
            '<p class="note">Three routes through the sheets, for the three questions readers '
            "arrive with. Click any box.</p>"
            f'<div class="pmwrap">{"".join(svg)}</div>')

def ranks_bridge() -> str:
    """Habsburg ladder ↔ common grade ↔ Legion ladder, in one picture.

    ``rank_reset`` is a subtraction — ``legion_common − habsburg_common`` — but the prose
    below has to establish two ladders, a common scale and a NATO band before that sentence
    means anything. Drawn side by side the subtraction is simply a step up or down the middle
    column. The ladders are **imported** from ``utils.parsing.ranks``: this figure cannot
    disagree with the parser, because it is reading the parser's own tables.
    """
    from utils.parsing.ranks import (NONCOMBAT_STATUS, RANK_COMMON, RANK_EN_HABSBURG,
                                     RANK_EN_LEGION, RANK_ORDINAL_HABSBURG,
                                     RANK_ORDINAL_LEGION, _COMMON_TO_BAND)

    L = pd.read_parquet(FIN / "persons" / "legionnaires_clean.parquet")
    cols = set(L.columns)
    hn = L["habsburg_rank_clean"].value_counts().to_dict() if "habsburg_rank_clean" in cols else {}
    ln = L["legion_rank_clean"].value_counts().to_dict() if "legion_rank_clean" in cols else {}

    # The reset read in both directions. Forward (click a Habsburg rank): where those men
    # landed. Backward (click a Legion rank): where they came from — the same joint
    # distribution, conditioned the other way, which is the question the endogeneity story
    # actually asks ("who ends up a private?").
    dest: dict[str, dict] = {}
    orig: dict[str, dict] = {}
    need = {"habsburg_rank_clean", "legion_rank_clean", "rank_reset"}
    if need <= cols:
        keep = ["habsburg_rank_clean", "legion_rank_clean", "rank_reset"]
        sub = L.loc[L["habsburg_rank_clean"].notna() & L["legion_rank_clean"].notna(), keep]

        def _summarise(by: str, other: str, into: dict) -> None:
            for name, g in sub.groupby(by, observed=True):
                r = pd.to_numeric(g["rank_reset"], errors="coerce")
                top = g[other].value_counts().head(3)
                into[str(name)] = dict(
                    n=int(len(g)),
                    down=int((r < 0).sum()), same=int((r == 0).sum()), up=int((r > 0).sum()),
                    top=[[str(k), int(v)] for k, v in top.items()])

        _summarise("habsburg_rank_clean", "legion_rank_clean", dest)
        _summarise("legion_rank_clean", "habsburg_rank_clean", orig)

    # Senior ranks are so thin that aggregates are not checkable — a "31 majors" bar hides
    # whether those are 31 real majors or a parser artefact. For OF-3 and above, list the
    # records themselves so each one can be opened at source. IDs only, no names: the
    # published page stays free of named individuals.
    SENIOR_FROM = 15                                   # common grade 15 = OF-3 (major)
    roster: dict[str, list] = {}
    if {"legion_id"} <= cols:
        for side, rc in (("h", "habsburg_rank_clean"), ("l", "legion_rank_clean")):
            if rc not in cols:
                continue
            snr = L[L[rc].map(lambda v: RANK_COMMON.get(v, 0) >= SENIOR_FROM
                              if isinstance(v, str) else False)]
            for name, g in snr.groupby(rc, observed=True):
                rows = []
                for _, r in g.iterrows():
                    other = r.get("legion_rank_clean" if side == "h" else "habsburg_rank_clean")
                    rows.append([
                        "" if pd.isna(r["legion_id"]) else str(r["legion_id"]),
                        "" if pd.isna(r.get("birth_year")) else str(int(r["birth_year"])),
                        "" if not isinstance(other, str) else other,
                        "" if pd.isna(r.get("theater")) else str(r.get("theater")),
                    ])
                roster[f"{side}:{name}"] = sorted(rows, key=lambda x: x[0])

    # ── layout: one band per common grade, tall enough for whichever side has more labels ──
    by_grade: dict[int, tuple[list, list]] = {}
    unmapped: dict[str, list[str]] = {"Habsburg": [], "Legion": []}
    for side, (ladder, en) in enumerate([(RANK_ORDINAL_HABSBURG, RANK_EN_HABSBURG),
                                         (RANK_ORDINAL_LEGION, RANK_EN_LEGION)]):
        for name in ladder:
            g = RANK_COMMON.get(name)
            if g is None:
                unmapped["Habsburg" if side == 0 else "Legion"].append(name)
                continue
            by_grade.setdefault(g, ([], []))[side].append((name, en.get(name, name)))

    RH, BW, GW, PADT = 27, 232, 76, 74
    HX, GX = 30, 30 + 232 + 74
    LXX = GX + GW + 74
    W = LXX + BW + 34                                  # room for the outer grade numerals
    grades = sorted(by_grade, reverse=True)
    ytop: dict[int, int] = {}
    y = PADT
    for g in grades:
        ytop[g] = y
        y += max(len(by_grade[g][0]), len(by_grade[g][1]), 1) * RH + 6
    H = y + 16

    nmax = max([*hn.values(), *ln.values()], default=1)

    def _box(side: int, name: str, en: str, x: int, yy: int, grade: int) -> str:
        n = (hn if side == 0 else ln).get(name, 0)
        nc = name in NONCOMBAT_STATUS and side == 1
        senior = grade >= SENIOR_FROM
        cls = ("rkbox" + (" zero" if not n else "") + (" nc" if nc else "")
               + (" snr" if senior and n else ""))
        bar = (BW - 16) * (n ** .5 / nmax ** .5) if n else 0
        lab = f"{n:,}" if n else "0"
        # The fine common grade as a bare numeral, on the OUTER edge of each ladder — the
        # inner edges are where the connector fan attaches, so a number there would sit in
        # the lines. Left of the Habsburg boxes, right of the Legion ones.
        num = (f'<text class="rkg out" x="-9" y="15">{grade}</text>' if side == 0
               else f'<text class="rkg" x="{BW + 9}" y="15">{grade}</text>')
        return (f'<g class="{cls}" data-g="{grade}" data-name="{_html.escape(name)}" '
                f'data-side="{"h" if side == 0 else "l"}" transform="translate({x},{yy})" '
                'onclick="rkPick(this)">'
                f'<rect width="{BW}" height="{RH - 5}" rx="4"/>'
                + (f'<rect class="rkbar" x="8" y="{RH - 10}" width="{bar:.0f}" height="2.5"/>'
                   if bar else "")
                + num
                + f'<text class="rkcs" x="10" y="15">{_html.escape(name)}</text>'
                f'<text class="rkn" x="{BW - 10}" y="15">{lab}</text>'
                f'<title>{_html.escape(en)} — common grade {grade} '
                f'({_COMMON_TO_BAND.get(grade, "—")}) · n = {lab}</title></g>')

    svg = [f'<svg id="rksvg" viewBox="0 0 {W} {H}" width="{W}" height="{H}" '
           'xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><defs>'
           '<pattern id="rkhatch" width="6" height="6" patternTransform="rotate(45)" '
           'patternUnits="userSpaceOnUse"><line x1="0" y1="0" x2="0" y2="6" '
           'stroke="#d0687a" stroke-width="2.2" opacity=".45"/></pattern></defs>',
           f'<text class="rkhead" x="{HX}" y="30">HABSBURG LADDER</text>',
           f'<text class="rksub" x="{HX}" y="48">rank at capture</text>',
           f'<text class="rkhead" x="{GX - 6}" y="30">NATO BAND</text>',
           f'<text class="rksub" x="{GX - 6}" y="48">one rung per grade</text>',
           f'<text class="rkhead" x="{LXX}" y="30">LEGION LADDER</text>',
           f'<text class="rksub" x="{LXX}" y="48">rank on enrolment</text>']

    # Connectors. Each runs between a rank box (at its own row, ry) and the grade pill (at the
    # band's centre, gy) — so the y endpoints are ordered by DIRECTION, not by column: the left
    # lane leaves a box and arrives at the pill, the right lane leaves the pill and arrives at a
    # box. Using one order for both mirrored the right-hand fan.
    svg.append('<g id="rkedges">')
    for g in grades:
        gy = ytop[g] + max(len(by_grade[g][0]), len(by_grade[g][1]), 1) * RH / 2 - 3
        for side, (x1, x2) in ((0, (HX + BW, GX)), (1, (GX + GW, LXX))):
            for i, _ in enumerate(by_grade[g][side]):
                ry = ytop[g] + i * RH + (RH - 5) / 2
                ya, yb = (ry, gy) if side == 0 else (gy, ry)
                mx = (x1 + x2) / 2
                svg.append(f'<path class="rkedge" data-g="{g}" d="M{x1},{ya:.0f} '
                           f'C{mx:.0f},{ya:.0f} {mx:.0f},{yb:.0f} {x2},{yb:.0f}"/>')
    svg.append("</g>")

    for g in grades:
        rowsn = max(len(by_grade[g][0]), len(by_grade[g][1]), 1)
        gy = ytop[g] + rowsn * RH / 2 - 3
        svg.append(f'<g class="rkgrade" data-g="{g}" transform="translate({GX},{gy - 11:.0f})">'
                   f'<rect width="{GW}" height="22" rx="11"/>'
                   f'<text x="{GW / 2:.0f}" y="15">{_COMMON_TO_BAND.get(g, "—")}</text></g>')
        for side, x in ((0, HX), (1, LXX)):
            for i, (name, en) in enumerate(by_grade[g][side]):
                svg.append(_box(side, name, en, x, ytop[g] + i * RH, g))
    svg.append("</svg>")

    foot = ""
    if any(unmapped.values()):
        bits = "; ".join(f"{k}: " + ", ".join(f"<code>{_html.escape(v)}</code>" for v in vs)
                         for k, vs in unmapped.items() if vs)
        foot = ('<p class="note"><b>Not on the common scale.</b> These ranks carry a within-army '
                f"ordinal but no common grade, so no reset can be computed for them — {bits}.</p>")

    return (
        ix_head("The two ladders, and what the reset subtracts", ix=True, hover=True)
        + '<p class="note">Left, the k.u.k. ladder a man was on when he was captured; right, the '
        "Legion ladder he entered on. Neither army's own numbering can be subtracted from the "
        "other's, so both are pinned to one <b>common scale</b> down the middle, on which the same "
        "Czech word always scores the same rung — and <code>rank_reset</code> is nothing more than "
        "the step between the two. Each rung is labelled with its <b>NATO band</b> "
        "(APersP-01), which is the coarse robustness axis; where consecutive rungs carry the same "
        "band the band cannot tell them apart, and the three subaltern rungs all reading "
        "<b>OF-1</b> is exactly why the fine scale exists — the bare numeral on each ladder's "
        "outer edge is that finer rung. <b>Hover</b> a rank to light its rung and its counterpart "
        "in the other army. <b>Click</b> either side: a Habsburg rank shows where those men went, "
        "a Legion rank shows where they came from. Bars are √n; counts are from "
        "<code>data/final</code>.</p>"
        '<p class="note"><b>One rung is contested.</b> <i>svobodník</i> is coded <b>OR-3</b> here, '
        "but §G2 above reports the APersP-01 CZE note as <i>vojín, svobodník</i> = OR-1, and "
        "Bednařík's 1916 POW-camp pay anchor pays “pěšák a svobodník 15” — private and "
        "svobodník identically, with the first real step at <i>desátník</i>/<i>četař</i>. The band "
        "axis for the enlisted rungs is therefore the weakest part of this figure; it is logged as "
        "an open item in <a href='#decisions'>Decisions</a> (D-15) and affects only "
        "<code>rank_band</code>, not the headline <code>rank_reset</code>, which rides on the "
        "numeral rather than the band.</p>"
        '<div class="rkbar-legend"><span class="rklg"><span class="sw nc"></span>non-combat status '
        "(<code>legion_noncombat</code>) — scored at grade 1, but not a demotion</span>"
        '<span class="rklg"><span class="sw zero"></span>in the ladder, absent from the data'
        "</span>"
        '<span class="rklg"><span class="sw snr"></span>OF-3 and above — click for the individual '
        "records</span></div>"
        f"<script>window.RKDEST={json.dumps(dest, ensure_ascii=False)};"
        f"window.RKORIG={json.dumps(orig, ensure_ascii=False)};"
        f"window.RKROSTER={json.dumps(roster, ensure_ascii=False)};"
        f"window.RKSENIOR={SENIOR_FROM};</script>"
        f'<div class="rklayout"><div class="rkwrap">{"".join(svg)}</div>'
        '<aside class="rkpanel empty" id="rkpanel"><p class="pnote">Click either ladder. A '
        "<b>Habsburg</b> rank shows where those men went; a <b>Legion</b> rank shows where they "
        "came from. At <b>OF-3 and above</b> the panel lists the individual records, each linking "
        "to its csol.cz entry.</p></aside></div>"
        + foot + "<hr>")

def units_sheet() -> str:
    """The 'How it works' explainer for unit identity — prose + live numbers.

    Written after the Fidler validation added ``legion_army`` / ``unit_key`` and the
    unit-authority cross-check. Everything numeric is recomputed from ``data/final`` so
    the explanation and the data cannot drift apart.
    """
    L = pd.read_parquet(FIN / "persons" / "legionnaires_clean.parquet")
    f = _legion_flags(L)
    N = len(L)
    n_army = L["legion_army"].nunique(dropna=True)
    n_reg = L["regiment"].nunique(dropna=True)
    n_key = L["unit_key"].nunique(dropna=True)
    foreign = int((L["legion_army"].notna()
                   & ~L["legion_army"].astype("string").str.startswith("CS Legion", na=False)).sum())

    # army breakdown
    army = (L["legion_army"].value_counts(dropna=False).rename_axis("Army / formation")
            .reset_index(name="Records"))
    army["Army / formation"] = army["Army / formation"].fillna("— (none recorded)")
    army["%"] = (army["Records"] / N * 100).map("{:.1f}%".format)
    army["Records"] = army["Records"].map("{:,}".format)

    # verification status
    lab = {"match": "Verified — number exists in this theatre",
           "no-entry": "No Fidler entry for this number",
           "conflict": "Conflict — number never existed in this theatre",
           "n-a": "Not checkable (support unit / foreign army / no number)"}
    vs = f["unit_status"].value_counts()
    vrows = []
    for k in ["match", "no-entry", "conflict", "n-a"]:
        n = int(vs.get(k, 0))
        d = int((f["deserted"] & (f["unit_status"] == k)).sum())
        vrows.append({"Status": lab[k], "Records": f"{n:,}", "% of records": _pct(n, N),
                      "Deserters": f"{d:,}"})

    # the conflicts, concretely
    cf = L[f["unit_status"] == "conflict"]
    ct = (cf.groupby(["regiment", "theater"]).size().rename("Records")
          .reset_index().sort_values("Records", ascending=False).head(12))
    ct = ct.rename(columns={"regiment": "Regiment label", "theater": "Tagged theatre"})
    ct["Records"] = ct["Records"].map("{:,}".format)

    return _with_toc(
        "<h2>Unit identity — regiment, army, and unit_key</h2>"
        '<p class="note">The raw enrolment field is <code>label ( formation )</code>, e.g. '
        "<code>1.stř.pl. ( Čs. legie v Rusku )</code>. The parenthetical is the part that is "
        "easy to misread: it names an <b>army</b>, not merely a theatre. Regiment numbering "
        "restarts inside each army, so the bare number is <b>not</b> a unit identifier.</p>"
        f'<p class="note">Across the {N:,} records there are <b>{n_army}</b> distinct armies / '
        f"formations. <b>{foreign:,}</b> records ({_pct(foreign, N)}) sit under a "
        "<b>non-Czechoslovak</b> army — the French Foreign Legion (whose 1st regiment, "
        "<i>rota Nazdar</i> included, is <b>not</b> the Czechoslovak 1st Rifle), the French, "
        "Serbian, Russian and British armies. Collapsing on <code>regiment</code> alone would "
        "merge those with Legion units of the same number.</p>"
        + df_table(army)
        + "<h2>The three columns, and which to use</h2>"
        "<table class='tbl'><thead><tr><th>Column</th><th>What it is</th><th>Use for</th></tr>"
        "</thead><tbody>"
        f"<tr><td><code>regiment</code></td><td>display label, army stripped "
        f"({n_reg:,} distinct)</td><td>reading, plot facets</td></tr>"
        "<tr><td><code>legion_army</code></td><td>the formation, normalised</td>"
        "<td>splitting Legion from foreign service</td></tr>"
        f"<tr><td><code>unit_key</code></td><td><code>regiment @ army</code> "
        f"({n_key:,} distinct identities)</td><td><b>unit fixed effects, clustering, size "
        "denominators</b></td></tr></tbody></table>"
        f'<p class="note">{n_reg:,} labels resolve into {n_key:,} distinct '
        "<code>unit_key</code> identities — the gap is the regiment numbers shared across "
        "armies. See <a href='#pipeline'>Pipeline → units.py</a> and "
        "<a href='#variables'>Variables §5</a>.</p>"
        "<h2>Which units actually existed — the Fidler cross-check</h2>"
        "<p class='note'>Every Czechoslovak-Legion record whose regiment carries a number is "
        "checked against <a href='#unit-authority'>the unit authority</a> derived from Fidler "
        "(2025): did that regiment number exist in the theatre the record claims? Support "
        "companies, foreign-army units and unnumbered formations carry no number to check and "
        "are marked <i>not checkable</i> — that is not the same as wrong.</p>"
        + df_table(pd.DataFrame(vrows))
        + "<p class='note'>The <b>conflicts</b> are records whose regiment number never "
        "existed in the tagged theatre — the 21st–23rd rifle regiments were French, the "
        "31st–39th Italian, yet a handful are tagged Russia. These are contradictions "
        "<b>inside csol.cz</b>, reproduced rather than silently corrected, and flagged by a "
        "soft QA check. The <a href='#validation'>validation sheet</a> has the full account.</p>"
        + df_table(ct)
        + "<h2>What this feeds</h2>"
        "<p class='note'>The <a href='#descriptives'>Descriptives → analysis sample</a> "
        "waterfall lets you require a verified unit (or merely a non-contradicted one) and see "
        "the cost in sample size — the borderline decision this cross-check exists to inform.</p>",
        "units")

def live_sheets() -> tuple[str, str]

Build the two data-driven sheets — (descriptives, qa) — from data/final.

Everything here is computed at build time; no figure is transcribed. The QA half re-runs the invariants that correspond to bugs which were once real in this project (frame exclusivity, cross-frame attribute leakage, fabricated exit codes, coordinate accuracy), so a regression shows up as a red row rather than as silently wrong prose.

Returns

(descriptives_html, qa_html).

Used only inside this module.

def live_sheets() -> tuple[str, str]:
    """Build the two data-driven sheets — ``(descriptives, qa)`` — from ``data/final``.

    Everything here is computed at build time; no figure is transcribed. The QA half
    re-runs the invariants that correspond to bugs which were once real in this project
    (frame exclusivity, cross-frame attribute leakage, fabricated exit codes, coordinate
    accuracy), so a regression shows up as a red row rather than as silently wrong prose.

    Returns:
        ``(descriptives_html, qa_html)``.
    """
    from utils.parsing.exit_codes import CODES_CS, CODES_EN, parse_exit_codes

    L = pd.read_parquet(FIN / "persons" / "legionnaires_clean.parquet")
    H = pd.read_parquet(FIN / "persons" / "habsburg_clean.parquet")
    cen = pd.read_parquet(FIN / "census" / "census_okres_1910.parquet")
    _cen_pool_p = FIN / "census" / "census_okres_1910_pooled.parquet"
    cen_pool = pd.read_parquet(_cen_pool_p) if _cen_pool_p.exists() else None
    cen_hu = pd.read_parquet(FIN / "census" / "census_hu_jaras_1910.parquet")
    setl = pd.read_parquet(FIN / "geo" / "settlements_1910.parquet")
    setl_hu = pd.read_parquet(FIN / "geo" / "settlements_hu_1910.parquet")
    dist = pd.read_parquet(FIN / "geo" / "districts_1910.parquet")
    dist_hu = pd.read_parquet(FIN / "geo" / "districts_hu_1910.parquet")
    match = pd.read_csv(FIN / "persons" / "overlap_matches.csv")

    S: list[str] = []

    # ── datasets
    S.append("<h2>Datasets</h2>")
    S.append(df_table(pd.DataFrame([
        {"File": "persons/legionnaires_clean", "Unit": "legionnaire", "Rows": f"{len(L):,}", "Columns": L.shape[1]},
        {"File": "persons/habsburg_clean", "Unit": "fallen Habsburg soldier", "Rows": f"{len(H):,}", "Columns": H.shape[1]},
        {"File": "census/census_okres_1910", "Unit": "1910 political okres", "Rows": f"{len(cen):,}", "Columns": cen.shape[1]},
    ] + ([{"File": "census/census_okres_1910_pooled", "Unit": "1910 okres, city/rural twins pooled",
           "Rows": f"{len(cen_pool):,}", "Columns": cen_pool.shape[1]}] if cen_pool is not None else []) + [
        {"File": "census/census_hu_jaras_1910", "Unit": "1910 járás / town", "Rows": f"{len(cen_hu):,}", "Columns": cen_hu.shape[1]},
        {"File": "geo/districts_1910", "Unit": "court district", "Rows": f"{len(dist):,}", "Columns": dist.shape[1]},
        {"File": "geo/districts_hu_1910", "Unit": "járás / town", "Rows": f"{len(dist_hu):,}", "Columns": dist_hu.shape[1]},
        {"File": "geo/settlements_1910", "Unit": "Czech settlement", "Rows": f"{len(setl):,}", "Columns": setl.shape[1]},
        {"File": "geo/settlements_hu_1910", "Unit": "Slovak obec", "Rows": f"{len(setl_hu):,}", "Columns": setl_hu.shape[1]},
        {"File": "persons/overlap_matches", "Unit": "confirmed overlap", "Rows": f"{len(match):,}", "Columns": match.shape[1]},
    ])))

    # ── analysis-sample waterfalls (interactive) — legionnaires + Habsburg comparison
    S.append(waterfall_block(L, _legion_flags(L)))
    S.append(waterfall_block_habsburg(H))

    # ── outcome
    S.append("<h2>Outcome — exit from the Legions</h2>")
    rows = []
    for c in CODES_CS:
        n = int(L[f"exit_{c}"].sum())
        rows.append({"Code": c, "Meaning": CODES_EN[c], "n": f"{n:,}", "% of records": _pct(n, len(L))})
    nocode = int((L["exit_codes"].isna() | (L["exit_codes"].astype(str) == "")).sum())
    rows.append({"Code": "—", "Meaning": "No code recorded (censored)", "n": f"{nocode:,}",
                 "% of records": _pct(nocode, len(L))})
    S.append(df_table(pd.DataFrame(rows)))
    S.append(f'<p class="note"><b>D (deserted) = {int(L["deserted"].sum()):,}</b> is the primary '
             "outcome. Records with no exit code carry no outcome information and must be treated "
             "as <b>censored</b>, not as non-desertion.</p>")

    # ── desertion by theatre
    if "theater" in L:
        g = (L.groupby("theater").agg(n=("deserted", "size"), d=("deserted", "sum"))
             .sort_values("n", ascending=False).reset_index())
        g["Desertion rate"] = (g["d"] / g["n"] * 100).map("{:.2f}%".format)
        g = g.rename(columns={"theater": "Theatre", "n": "Legionnaires", "d": "Deserted"})
        g["Legionnaires"] = g["Legionnaires"].map("{:,}".format)
        g["Deserted"] = g["Deserted"].map("{:,}".format)
        S.append("<h2>Desertion by theatre</h2>")
        S.append(df_table(g))

    # ── rank reset
    if "rank_reset" in L:
        # the view toggle below belongs to this section, so the section heading carries the
        # chip — the toolbar itself must not (a chip in a toolbar is invisible to a reader
        # scanning headings, which is how this drifted in the first place)
        S.append(ix_head("Rank reset (headline regressor)",
                         ix="legion_noncombat" in L.columns, hover=True))
        rows = []
        for lab, col in [("Fine (ALT-1 common scale)", "rank_reset"),
                         ("Coarse (NATO OF/OR band)", "rank_reset_band")]:
            if col not in L:
                continue
            r = L[col].dropna()
            rows.append({"Measure": lab, "N resolved": f"{len(r):,}",
                         "Demoted": _pct((r < 0).sum(), len(r)),
                         "Unchanged": _pct((r == 0).sum(), len(r)),
                         "Promoted": _pct((r > 0).sum(), len(r)),
                         "Mean": f"{r.mean():.2f}"})
        S.append(df_table(pd.DataFrame(rows)))
        # combat-ranks-only view (default) vs the inclusive view. `legion_noncombat`
        # marks pracovník/občan entry statuses whose reset is an artifact (see the
        # Rank ladders sheet §H#1 / External validation §3); the toggle switches both
        # the histogram and the by-theatre areas between the two.
        if "legion_noncombat" in L.columns:
            combat = ~L["legion_noncombat"].fillna(False).astype(bool)
            n_nc = int((~combat).sum())
            S.append(
                '<div class="rrsec combatonly" id="rrsec">'
                '<div class="rrmodebar"><span class="h">Rank-reset view:</span>'
                '<button class="rrmode on" onclick="rrMode(this,\'combat\')">Combat ranks only</button>'
                '<button class="rrmode" onclick="rrMode(this,\'all\')">Include labour / civilian status</button>'
                f'<span class="rrmodenote">{n_nc:,} records carry a non-combat entry '
                "status (pracovník / občan); their reset differences a status against a "
                "rank and is shown only in the inclusive view.</span></div>"
                '<div class="rrvar rr-combat">' + rank_reset_hist(L, combat) + "</div>"
                '<div class="rrvar rr-all">' + rank_reset_hist(L, None) + "</div>"
                + ix_head("Rank reset by theatre", ix=True, hover=True)
                + '<div class="rrvar rr-combat">' + rank_reset_areas(L, mask=combat) + "</div>"
                '<div class="rrvar rr-all">' + rank_reset_areas(L, mask=None) + "</div>"
                "</div>")
        else:
            S.append(rank_reset_hist(L))
            S.append("<h2>Rank reset by theatre</h2>" + rank_reset_areas(L))

    # ── place matching
    S.append("<h2>Place matching — birth</h2>")
    rows = []
    for nm, d in (("Legionnaires", L), ("Habsburg fallen", H)):
        rows.append({
            "Dataset": nm, "Rows": f"{len(d):,}",
            "Czech okres_id": f"{int(d['birth_okres_id'].notna().sum()):,} ({_pct(int(d['birth_okres_id'].notna().sum()), len(d))})",
            "Slovak jaras_id": f"{int(d['birth_jaras_id'].notna().sum()):,} ({_pct(int(d['birth_jaras_id'].notna().sum()), len(d))})",
            "Court district": f"{int(d['birth_court_id'].notna().sum()):,}",
            "Coordinates": f"{int(d['birth_lat'].notna().sum()):,}",
        })
    S.append(df_table(pd.DataFrame(rows)))
    tiers = pd.DataFrame({
        "Legionnaires": L["birth_okres_match"].value_counts(),
        "Habsburg fallen": H["birth_okres_match"].value_counts(),
    }).fillna(0).astype(int).rename_axis("Czech tier").reset_index()
    tiers["Czech tier"] = tiers["Czech tier"].astype(str)
    S.append(df_table(tiers))
    tiers_sk = pd.DataFrame({
        "Legionnaires": L["birth_jaras_match"].value_counts(),
        "Habsburg fallen": H["birth_jaras_match"].value_counts(),
    }).fillna(0).astype(int).rename_axis("Slovak tier").reset_index()
    tiers_sk["Slovak tier"] = tiers_sk["Slovak tier"].astype(str)
    S.append(df_table(tiers_sk))
    S.append('<p class="note">Tiers are ordered strongest → weakest; <code>muni</code> and '
             "<code>fuzzy</code> are the soft ones a strict specification can drop. A record is "
             "placed in <b>at most one</b> 1910 frame.</p>")

    # ── linkage
    S.append("<h2>Cross-dataset linkage</h2>")
    lk = (match["confidence"].value_counts().rename_axis("Confidence")
          .reset_index(name="Pairs"))
    lk["Evidence"] = lk["Confidence"].map({"high": "Exact full date of birth + matching name",
                                           "medium": "VÚA legion note + birth okres + year + name"})
    S.append(df_table(lk[["Confidence", "Evidence", "Pairs"]]))
    S.append(f'<p class="note">{len(match):,} confirmed overlaps over '
             f'{match["vua_id"].nunique():,} distinct VÚA records; '
             f'{int((match["date_exact"] & match["note_legion"]).sum()):,} satisfy both criteria. '
             "The rule is precision-first: weaker name/year coincidences are dropped, not down-tiered.</p>")

    # ── coverage of key variables
    S.append("<h2>Coverage of key variables</h2>")
    keys = [("birth_date", "Date of birth"), ("birth_year", "Year of birth"),
            ("birth_okres", "Birth district (raw)"), ("education", "Education"),
            ("occupation", "Occupation"), ("religion", "Religion"),
            ("habsburg_rank", "Habsburg rank at capture"), ("legion_rank", "Legion rank at enrolment"),
            ("enroll_date", "Enrolment date"), ("exit_date", "Exit date"),
            ("death_date", "Date of death"), ("cause", "Cause of death")]
    rows = []
    for col, lab in keys:
        a = _pct(int(L[col].notna().sum()), len(L)) if col in L else "—"
        b = _pct(int(H[col].notna().sum()), len(H)) if col in H else "—"
        rows.append({"Variable": lab, "Column": col, "Legionnaires": a, "Habsburg fallen": b})
    S.append(df_table(pd.DataFrame(rows)))

    # ── figures
    S.append("<h2>Figures</h2>")
    S.append('<p class="note">Generated by <code>notebooks/03_visualisation.ipynb</code>; '
             "PDF and beamer variants of each live in <code>output/figures/</code>.</p>")
    figs = sorted(p for p in ROOT.joinpath("output", "figures").rglob("*.png")
                  if "_beamer" not in p.name)
    groups: dict[str, list[Path]] = {}
    for f in figs:
        groups.setdefault(f.parent.parent.name.replace("descriptives_habsburg", "Habsburg fallen")
                          .replace("descriptives", "Legionnaires"), []).append(f)
    for grp, items in groups.items():
        S.append(f"<h3>{_html.escape(grp)}</h3><div class='figgrid'>")
        for f in items:
            b64 = base64.b64encode(f.read_bytes()).decode()
            cap = f.stem.replace("_", " ").capitalize()
            S.append(f'<figure><img src="data:image/png;base64,{b64}" alt="{_html.escape(cap)}" '
                     f'onclick="zoom(this)" title="Click to enlarge">'
                     f"<figcaption>{_html.escape(cap)}<br><code>{f.relative_to(ROOT).as_posix()}</code>"
                     "</figcaption></figure>")
        S.append("</div>")

    # ══ QA sheet ══ — the invariants themselves live in utils/validation/data_checks.py,
    # which notebook 02 also calls as a gate, so the page and the pipeline cannot disagree.
    from utils.validation.data_checks import run_checks

    Q: list[str] = []
    checks = run_checks(FIN)
    npass = sum(c.ok for c in checks)
    hard_bad = sum(1 for c in checks if not c.ok and c.hard)

    Q.append(f'<h2>Invariants <span class="{"ok" if npass==len(checks) else "bad"}">'
             f"{npass}/{len(checks)} passing</span></h2>")
    Q.append('<p class="note">Defined once in <code>utils/validation/data_checks.py</code> and '
             "evaluated against the current <code>data/final</code> every time this page is built. "
             "Notebook 02 calls the same list as its final cell, so a run that produced broken data "
             "<b>fails</b> rather than reporting success. Each check corresponds to a bug that was "
             "real at some point in this project — see the "
             "<a href='#audit'>audits</a> of 2026-07-16 and 2026-09-22.<br>"
             "<b>FAIL</b> is a hard invariant that should never be violated; <b>WARN</b> is a soft "
             "one (it can drift for external reasons) that reports but does not block.</p>")
    Q.append('<div class="tblwrap"><table class="tbl qa"><thead><tr><th></th><th>Check</th>'
             "<th>If it fails</th></tr></thead><tbody>")
    for c in checks:
        badge = ('<span class="badge pass">PASS</span>' if c.ok else
                 '<span class="badge fail">FAIL</span>' if c.hard else
                 '<span class="badge warn">WARN</span>')
        Q.append(f"<tr><td>{badge}</td><td>{_html.escape(c.label)}"
                 + ("" if c.hard else ' <span class="soft">soft</span>')
                 + f'</td><td class="muted">{_html.escape(c.detail)}</td></tr>')
    Q.append("</tbody></table></div>")
    return _with_toc("\n".join(S), "desc"), "\n".join(Q), hard_bad

def working_tree() -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, set[str]]:
    """Uncommitted changes as (table, set of paths) — where this session's work lives."""
    status = {}
    for line in _git("status", "--porcelain").splitlines():
        if len(line) > 3:
            status[line[3:].strip().strip('"').split(" -> ")[-1]] = line[:2].strip()
    rows = []
    for line in _git("diff", "--numstat").splitlines():
        parts = line.split("\t")
        if len(parts) == 3:
            add, dele, path = parts
            rows.append({"File": path, "Added": add, "Removed": dele,
                         "Status": {"M": "modified", "A": "added", "R": "renamed",
                                    "??": "untracked"}.get(status.get(path, "M"), "modified")})
    tracked = {r["File"] for r in rows}
    for path, st in status.items():
        if path not in tracked and not path.endswith("/"):
            rows.append({"File": path, "Added": "—", "Removed": "—",
                         "Status": "untracked (new)" if st == "??" else "renamed"})
    df = pd.DataFrame(rows).sort_values("File").reset_index(drop=True) if rows else pd.DataFrame(
        columns=["File", "Added", "Removed", "Status"])
    return df, set(df["File"]) if len(df) else set()

def main() -> Path:
    """Assemble every sheet and write ``output/docs/index.html``.

    Returns:
        Path to the written page.
    """
    stamp = build_stamp()
    desc_html, qa_html, qa_failures = live_sheets()
    dirty_df, dirty_files = working_tree()
    scripts, symbols = collect_scripts(dirty_files)
    chlog = changelog_sheet(dirty_df, scripts)
    usage = usage_sheet(symbols)

    built: list[dict] = []
    for s in SHEETS:
        s = dict(s)
        if s["kind"] == "changelog":
            s["html"] = chlog
        elif s["kind"] == "graph":
            s["html"] = graph_sheet(dirty_files)
        elif s["kind"] == "units":
            s["html"] = units_sheet()
        elif s["kind"] == "provenance":
            s["html"] = provenance_sheet()
        elif s["kind"] == "references":
            s["html"] = references_sheet()
        elif s["kind"] == "usage":
            s["html"] = usage
        elif s["kind"] == "md":
            body = md_to_html((ROOT / s["src"]).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
            body = _promote_tldr(_strip_lead_h1(body))
            if s["id"] == "habsburg-army":
                body += _regiment_explorer()
            elif s["id"] == "places":
                body = _after_tldr(body, place_flow())
            elif s["id"] == "lexikon-1910":
                body = _after_tldr(body, lexikon_page())
            elif s["id"] == "occupations":
                # `VALIDATION_OCCUPATIONS.md` used to be appended here in full, so that the
                # method and its evidence read as one argument. That was right while it was
                # the only home the document had — but it is now its own sheet, filed with
                # the other external checks, and appending it as well would render every
                # word twice. What stays behind is the summary table in §9, which carries
                # each check's headline number and blind spot and links through.
                body = _after_tldr(body, occupation_flow())
            elif s["id"] == "education":
                body += education_figures()
            elif s["id"] == "theatre":
                figs = theatre_figures()
                body = _before_h2(body, "The rulings", figs.get("explainer", ""))
                body = _before_h2(body, "Open", figs.get("trend", "") + figs.get("map", ""))
            elif s["id"] == "ranks":
                body = _after_tldr(body, ranks_bridge())
            elif s["id"] == "decisions":
                body = _decision_badges(body)
            elif s["id"] == "register-route":
                body = _register_route(body)
            elif s["id"] == "audit":
                # the earlier audits, each appended under one heading of its own; their sections
                # step down a level so the contents strip lists the newest audit's parts plus
                # one entry for each old one, instead of interleaving them
                for heading, src in (("Second audit — 2026-09-22", "AUDIT_2026-09-22.md"),
                                     ("First audit — 2026-07-16", "AUDIT_2026-07-16.md")):
                    earlier = _strip_lead_h1(md_to_html(
                        (ROOT / "reference" / src).read_text(encoding="utf-8")))
                    earlier = re.sub(r"<(/?)h([2-5])([^>]*)>",
                                     lambda m: f"<{m.group(1)}h{int(m.group(2)) + 1}{m.group(3)}>",
                                     earlier)
                    body += f"<h2>{heading}</h2>" + earlier
            s["html"] = body
        elif s["kind"] == "csv":
            s["html"] = df_table(pd.read_csv(ROOT / s["src"]).fillna(""), searchable=True)
        elif s["kind"] == "live":
            s["html"] = desc_html
        elif s["kind"] == "qa":
            s["html"] = qa_html
        elif s["kind"] == "overview":
            readme = md_to_html((ROOT / s["src"]).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
            readme = _promote_tldr(_strip_lead_h1(readme))
            guide = pd.DataFrame([{"Sheet": x["title"], "Group": x["group"],
                                   "Contents": x["blurb"],
                                   "Source": x["src"] or "generated from data/final"}
                                  for x in SHEETS])
            s["html"] = (readme
                         + reading_map()
                         + "<h2>How to read this document</h2>"
                         + '<p class="note">This page is <b>generated</b> from the repository by '
                           "<code>utils/docs/build_docs.py</code>. The markdown files under "
                           "<code>reference/</code> are the canonical prose and every figure on the "
                           "Descriptives and Data QA sheets is recomputed from <code>data/final</code> "
                           "at build time — nothing here is transcribed by hand. To correct something, "
                           "edit its source and rebuild; do not edit the HTML.</p>"
                         + '<p class="note ixkey">Chips sit at the end of a figure\'s own heading, one '
                           "per affordance, and never anywhere else. " + IXBADGE
                         + " means the block has controls — click, toggle, drag or filter it. "
                         + HOVERBADGE + " means its marks carry tooltips; a block that does both "
                           "shows both. The red dot in the sidebar is <b>derived</b> from the chips "
                           "a sheet actually rendered, so the two cannot disagree. Long tables "
                           "announce themselves with a visible search box instead. Everything else "
                           "is a plain table or figure.</p>"
                         + df_table(guide)
                         + "<h2>Module index</h2>"
                         + '<p class="note">Every importable module, its version, and its purpose — '
                           "read straight from the source files. <a href='#pipeline'>Pipeline</a> "
                           "explains what each one does in context.</p>"
                         + df_table(module_index(), searchable=True))
        # the sidebar dot is READ OFF the page, never declared: a sheet is interactive iff it
        # rendered an ⇱ chip. Hand-maintained flags drifted (Place matching and Rank ladders
        # both showed a chip with no dot); a derived one cannot.
        _check_badges(s["id"], s["html"])
        s["interactive"] = '<span class="ixbadge">' in _strip_ixkey(s["html"])
        built.append(s)

    # per-script sheets go after "How it works"; index them from the Pipeline sheet
    idx = pd.DataFrame([{"Script": s["title"], "Role": s["role"], "Does": s["blurb"]}
                        for s in scripts])
    for s in built:
        if s["id"] == "pipeline":
            s["html"] = ('<h2>Script index</h2><p class="note">One sheet per module — its docstring, '
                         "public API, version, callers and git history, all read from the source. "
                         "Pick one in the sidebar under <b>Pipeline scripts</b>. The narrative below "
                         "explains how they fit together.</p>"
                         + df_table(idx, searchable=True) + "<hr>" + s["html"])
    # insert the script sheets after the LAST "How it works" sheet, so that group stays
    # contiguous in the sidebar (inserting mid-group renders its header twice)
    pos = max(i for i, s in enumerate(built) if s["group"] == "How it works") + 1
    built[pos:pos] = scripts

    # linkify inline author-year citations everywhere except the References sheet itself
    for s in built:
        if s["id"] != "references":
            s["html"] = _linkify_citations(s["html"])

    # ── the shared skeleton, applied in one place so no sheet can drift out of it ──────
    # (the contents strip used to be hand-attached to two sheets; the history wayfinder and
    # the see-also footer are new, and both are generated from the registry above)
    by_id = {s["id"]: s for s in built}
    hist = {sid for sid, *_ in _HISTORY_SHEETS}
    for s in built:
        s["gcol"] = GROUP_COLOUR.get(s["group"], CU_GREY)
        html = s["html"]
        # script sheets already open with a chip index; everything else gets the strip
        if '<nav class="toc">' not in html and 'class="chips"' not in html:
            html = _with_toc(html, s["id"])
        # after the contents strip, so the fold lands ABOVE it: `_after_tldr` always
        # inserts immediately under the summary card, so the last caller sits highest
        fold = _plain_english(s["id"])
        if fold:
            html = _after_tldr(html, fold)
        if s["id"] in hist:
            html = _wayfind(s["id"]) + html
        s["html"] = _number_figures(html) + _seealso(s["id"], by_id)

    # A method sheet added later without a plain-English entry is silent otherwise; the
    # doorway would just stop existing for that one sheet and nobody would notice.
    ids = {s["id"] for s in built}
    for sid in sorted(PLAIN_SHEETS - set(PLAIN_ENGLISH)):
        IX_WARNINGS.append(f"{sid}: in PLAIN_SHEETS but has no PLAIN_ENGLISH entry")
    for sid in sorted(set(PLAIN_ENGLISH) - ids):
        IX_WARNINGS.append(f"{sid}: PLAIN_ENGLISH entry for a sheet that does not exist")

    groups: list[tuple[str, list[dict], bool, str]] = []
    for s in built:
        if not groups or groups[-1][0] != s["group"]:
            groups.append((s["group"], [], s["group"] == "Pipeline scripts",
                           GROUP_COLOUR.get(s["group"], CU_GREY)))
        groups[-1][1].append(s)

    lazy_anchors = _split_script_sheets(built)

    html_out = TEMPLATE.render(
        fontfaces=_font_face_css(),
        title="The Fateful Adventures of the Good Soldiers — Project Documentation",
        project="Good Soldiers", subtitle="Desertion in a volunteer army · project documentation",
        sheets=built, groups=groups, stamp=stamp, qa_failures=qa_failures,
        sheet_ids=str([s["id"] for s in built]).replace("'", '"'),
        lazy_anchors=json.dumps(lazy_anchors, ensure_ascii=False), lazy_dir=LAZY_DIR,
        pygments_css=HtmlFormatter().get_style_defs(".highlight"),
        navy=CU_NAVY, red=CU_RED, grey=CU_GREY, favicon=favicon_href(),
        # noindex meta for link-only publishing (keeps the page out of search engines);
        # set by `--noindex` or DOCS_NOINDEX=1. Off for the local/private build.
        noindex=("--noindex" in sys.argv or os.environ.get("DOCS_NOINDEX") == "1"),
    )
    # Guard: an unbalanced inline tag leaks its styling into every following sheet (a literal
    # emphasis tag named in a docstring once bolded half the document). Count per sheet, and
    # only in the body — CSS/JS text that merely *names* a tag is not markup.
    for m in re.finditer(r'<section class="sheet" id="sheet-([\w.-]+)">(.*?)</section>',
                         html_out, re.S):
        _check_balanced(m.group(1), m.group(2))

    # The bibliography travels with the page: the .bib is a projection of the same list the
    # References sheet renders, written on every build so it cannot lag behind.
    (ROOT / "reference" / "references.bib").write_text(render_bib(), encoding="utf-8")

    OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    dest = OUT / "index.html"
    dest.write_text(html_out, encoding="utf-8")
    return dest
