{'pipeline': '<p>Somewhere on a Czech government server there are 133,000 web pages, one per legionnaire, each a little table of half-filled fields typed up from a paper card: born <i>Kolín</i>, trade <i>zámečník</i>, joined <i>12.3.1917</i>. A person can read one of those in a few seconds. Nobody can read 133,000, and no statistical model can read even one — a model wants a rectangle of numbers, and this is a heap of Czech sentences.</p><p>The pipeline is the machine that turns the heap into the rectangle, and it is built in three stages so that each can be checked. <b>Collect</b>: fetch the pages and store them exactly as they came, never touched again. <b>Clean</b>: read every field with a small specialist — one for dates, one for ranks, one for jobs, one for places — and write out a table where a column means the same thing in every row. <b>Visualise</b>: draw the pictures, and read <i>only</i> from that final table, so a figure can never quietly disagree with the data it claims to show.</p><p>The rule that makes the whole thing survivable is that the raw copy is sacred. Every judgement — every guess, every repair, every dropped record — happens in the middle stage, in code, where it can be read, argued with and undone. If a decision made in 2026 turns out to be wrong, the fix is one function and a re-run, not a dataset nobody can reconstruct.</p>', 'places': "<p>Imagine posting a letter addressed only to <i>Nová Ves, Bohemia</i>. There are dozens of Nová Ves — New Village is the Czech <i>Springfield</i> — and the one you want stopped existing under that name in 1918, was called something else in German, and has since been swallowed by a town. That is the problem on every one of these birth records, and it has to be solved 300,000 times, because a soldier's birthplace is how he gets attached to the 1910 census: how literate his district was, how many Czechs and Germans lived in it, how much of it farmed.</p><p>So the matcher works like a careful postal clerk rather than a clever one. It tries the strongest evidence first — does this string name a district outright? — then weaker and weaker readings: a court district, a village in the gazetteer, a near-miss spelling. Crucially it <b>writes down which rung it used</b>. Every record carries a label saying how confident the match is, so an analysis can throw the weak ones away and see whether the result survives.</p><p>Two things it refuses to do. It will not break a tie by picking whichever candidate the lookup table happened to list first — a coin-flip dressed as an answer. And it will not place a village in Slovakia just because a Slovak village has the same name, when the record says the man was born in Galicia. Where the evidence genuinely runs out, the field stays empty, and empty is a finding.</p>", 'lexikon-1910': '<p>In 1916 the imperial statistical office printed a book that lists every inhabited place in Bohemia — every village, every hamlet, every mill with a name. For each one it gives a row of numbers: how many hectares, how many houses, how many people, how many Catholics, how many spoke Czech. That part is a spreadsheet that happens to be made of paper, and a computer reads it about as well as you would expect: nine numbers in ten come out right.</p><p>The interesting part is underneath. In tiny type at the foot of every page, the book also records what each village <b>had</b> — a school, a midwife, a fire brigade, a savings bank, a post office, a Czech credit union rather than a German one. That is a completely different kind of fact from a headcount, and nothing else in this project comes close to it: you can measure whether a man grew up somewhere with institutions or somewhere with none. There is one problem. To save space, the 1916 typesetter printed those institutions not as words but as <b>little pictures</b> — a tiny open book for a school, a stylised helmet for a fire brigade — and defined them once, on a key page at the front.</p><p>A computer cannot read a picture it has never been shown. Text-recognition software sees the school symbol and confidently types <i>g</i>. Modern AI models, asked what the mark is, guess — and guess differently from each other: handed the identical symbol, two of them answered “doctor” and “curate”. Over one test page they agreed with each other about the <i>words</i> of an entry two times in three, and about the <i>symbols</i> about one time in ten.</p><p>So the work splits in two. The numbers upstairs are read by machine and then <b>made to prove themselves</b>: men plus women must equal the total, the villages must add up to their parish. Crucially the machine is never told what the answer should be — tell it the total and it will happily produce numbers that reach that total, and the test stops testing anything. Downstairs there is no such arithmetic, nothing adds up to anything, and the only defences are a fixed list of names a reader is allowed to use, and a human sitting down with the key page. A person reading those marks by hand got 286 of them and was unsure about none, which settles one thing at least: the difficulty is not the scan. It is that we are asking machines to recognise a picture nobody has drawn for them.</p>', 'occupations': "<p>Every soldier's card has one word for what he did: <i>rolník</i>, <i>zámečník</i>, <i>obchodní příručí</i>. To ask whether poor men deserted more often than comfortable ones, those words have to become something comparable — a rung on a ladder that a farmer in Moravia and a clerk in Prague can both stand on.</p><p>That is what HISCO is: an international coding scheme where every historical job has a five-digit number, and every number maps to a social class from 1 (elite) to 13 (unskilled). The trouble is that HISCO was built from Dutch, English and German records and contains <b>no Czech at all</b>. So the dictionary from Czech word to code is written here, by hand, one entry at a time — about 500 entries, which is enough to cover 98.5&nbsp;% of the men because occupations follow a brutal power law: a handful of trades account for most of a population.</p><p>The matching itself is deliberately stupid. It will accept a phrase only if a <i>whole run of words</i> is already in the dictionary — never a fragment inside a word. That stupidity is the safety feature: a cleverer matcher, allowed to look inside words, once found the rank <i>major</i> hiding inside <i>generálmajor</i> and demoted every general in the army. Here, if nothing matches, the answer is nothing.</p><p>And the honest part: about a fifth of the coded records rest on a judgement that could have gone the other way. <i>Rolník</i> — a sixth of the whole sample — is read as a farmer who works his own land rather than a hired farmhand, which is a four-class difference. That single call was tested against the 1910 census's own employment columns before it was allowed to stand, and it is flagged in the data so anyone can re-run the analysis without it.</p>", 'ranks': "<p>The central question of this project is what a demotion does to a man. A legionnaire had already deserted the Austrian army once; some of them were sergeants or lieutenants when they did. In the Czechoslovak Legion many started again as privates. Did the ones who fell furthest desert again?</p><p>To ask that, the two armies' rank systems have to be laid side by side, and they do not line up on their own — different languages, different numbers of grades, and titles that mean different things in each. So both are placed on one ordinal scale using the NATO officer codes as the bridge, and the drop is simply the difference: a Habsburg sergeant who becomes a Legion private has a <b>rank reset</b> of minus several rungs.</p><p>The trap here is a title that is not a grade at all. Some men were entered as <i>pracovník</i> (labour service) or <i>občan</i> (civilian) — administrative holding categories on the way in, not punishments. Scored naively, a Habsburg colonel entering as a <i>labourer</i> looks like the most spectacular demotion in the dataset, and it never happened. Those 7,696 records are flagged, and the headline result is computed without them.</p>", 'ranks-legal': '<p>When the war ended, hundreds of thousands of men who had worn one uniform had to be fitted into another — and the new Czechoslovak state had to decide what their old rank was worth. This sheet is the answer, dug out of the statute books.</p><p>The law was openly lopsided, and knowing that is the point. Legion service was a <b>reward</b>: preferential appointments, generous crediting of time served, seniority back-dated as far as 1914. Former Austro-Hungarian officers were let in grudgingly and often a grade down. Two men of identical ability ended the decade in different places purely because of which army they had been in.</p><p>It sits in the documentation because it explains a rumour the data would otherwise seem to support. Legionnaires believed officers were being demoted; the statutes show the opposite policy. So when the data shows a Habsburg officer entering the Legion at a low grade, the explanation is an entry procedure, not a punishment — and that distinction changes what the desertion result means.</p>', 'units': "<p>A soldier's record says he served in the <i>1st Regiment</i>. Which one? The Czechoslovak Legion in Russia had a 1st Regiment. So did the Legion in Italy. So did the French Foreign Legion, in which a Czech company also fought. Three different wars, three different sets of men, one number.</p><p>Treating them as one unit would be a real error, not a cosmetic one, because unit is how soldiers are grouped for almost every comparison in the project — how big was his company, how many of his comrades died, did his regiment desert as a bloc. Mix two regiments together and every one of those numbers is wrong.</p><p>The fix is to stop using the number alone and use <b>regiment plus army</b> as the identity. It sounds trivial; it moved 4,347 records, and it revealed that the records labelled <i>1st Regiment</i> are mostly Foreign Legion rather than the Czechoslovak 1st Rifles that everyone assumes.</p>", 'habsburg-army': "<p>The Habsburg army recruited locally on purpose. Each regiment had a home district it drew its men from, so a regiment was in effect a slice of one region — its language, its trades, its villages. That is the <i>Ergänzung</i> system, and it is why a regiment number is quietly also a place.</p><p>That link is worth a great deal here. It lets a man's pre-Legion unit be tied back to a census district even when his own birthplace field is unreadable, and it gives a way to ask whether men from the same home district behaved alike — the kind of comparison the whole literature on unit cohesion turns on.</p><p>It also explains the ambiguity next door: the Monarchy ran three parallel armies — the common army, the Austrian Landwehr and the Hungarian Honvéd — each numbering its own regiments from one, each with its own command language. A bare number is genuinely ambiguous, which is not sloppiness in the records but a fact about the state that kept them.</p>", 'provenance': '<p>A finished number in a paper — <i>desertion in Russia was four percent</i> — hides a chain of sources behind it: a scraped website, a census workbook, a shapefile, a hand-written dictionary. If any link is weak, the number is weak, and by the time it reaches a table nobody can tell which link it was.</p><p>This sheet keeps the chain visible. Every mechanism the project claims is drawn back to the source that grounds it, so the reader can see at a glance which claims rest on an official census, which on a scholarly encyclopedia, and which on a judgement made here.</p><p>It is also a defence against a specific kind of self-deception: a source used for two different purposes starts to look like two independent confirmations. Drawn as a graph, that shows up immediately as one node with two arrows out of it — which is one piece of evidence, not two.</p>', 'architecture': '<p>This project is about forty Python modules that call each other. That is small enough to feel manageable and quite large enough to hide a nasty surprise: you change how one function reads a date, and something four steps downstream that you had forgotten depends on it starts producing plausible, wrong answers.</p><p>So the import graph is drawn automatically from the source itself — never from a hand-kept list, which would be out of date within a week. Click a module and the map highlights everything that would feel a change to it.</p><p>The practical use is before an edit, not after. If the blast radius of a one-line change is eleven modules, that is worth knowing while the change is still an idea.</p>', 'validation-register': '<p>Most projects report the checks that passed. This one has a column for what each check <b>cannot see</b>, and that column is the honest half.</p><p>The distinction that organises it: an <b>external</b> check compares this project against a source that could genuinely contradict it — a published encyclopedia, an official census, an independently trained model. A <b>self-check</b> only confirms that the output obeys the rules it was built from. Self-checks are necessary and they are not evidence that the coding is right; a rule applied perfectly to the wrong data passes every one of them.</p><p>Reading the blind-spot column is the fastest way to find out what this project does not know. Place matching below the district level, for instance, has no external check at all — so it is written down as unchecked rather than left to look like it passed.</p>', 'validation': "<p>The best thing that can happen to a dataset is that somebody who has never seen it wrote down the answers first. In 2025 a historian published an encyclopedia of the Czechoslovak Legions: which units existed, where they fought, when they formed. That is an answer key produced with no knowledge of this project whatsoever.</p><p>Checked against it, the pipeline's theatre assignment agrees on 99.6&nbsp;% of records, and every officer rank resolves correctly. More usefully, it found two real bugs. The rank ladder had no general grades, so <i>generálmajor</i> matched the word <i>major</i> and every Legion general was recorded three rungs too low. And notes <i>about</i> a rank — <i>candidate for lieutenant</i>, <i>was not a soldier</i> — were being scored as that rank.</p><p>It also found roughly 130 records where the source website contradicts the historical record: regiments placed in Russia that only ever existed in France. Those are documented and left alone. Silently correcting a source is how a dataset stops being evidence about the source.</p>", 'validation-education': "<p>What a soldier wrote in the schooling box — <i>ob. 5 mě. 3</i> and the like — only means something if you know what those schools were. Until now that knowledge came from two modern history books. Neither counts schools; one of them starts its figures in 1924, in a different country.</p><p>This page checks the scheme against the thing itself: the Austrian government's own annual census of every school it ran, printed in Vienna in 1912 for the year 1908/09, with a table for each kind of school in each province and the language it taught in. It is the register the ladder should have been built on, and it says three things.</p><p>It <b>confirms</b> the awkward call at the heart of the variable. The <i>pokračovací</i> school — compulsory evening classes for apprentices — had been treated as a rung above the rest, which would have made an apprentice look better-educated than a grammar-school boy. The government filed it in a category of its own, and it was enormous: 504 of them in Bohemia teaching 50,836 pupils, against nine state trade schools teaching 3,518. Leaving it off the ladder was right.</p><p>It <b>breaks</b> something else. The code marks an elementary schooling “complete” at eight years, because the law required eight years of schooling. But the census counts schools by how many year-groups they actually had, and a <i>eight</i>-class elementary school existed ten times in the whole empire and twice in the Czech lands. Nearly four thousand men are recorded as having finished a school that was almost nowhere, and three thousand more who wrote down the ordinary full five years are marked as having dropped out. The column is being left alone until that is decided properly rather than patched.</p><p>And it shows that the evening classes are <b>badly under-recorded</b>: in life there were five of those pupils for every full-time trade-school pupil, but in these records there are fewer than one. Men simply did not write down the classes they were obliged to attend. So that flag counts some apprentices, not all of them.</p><p>What none of it touches is Hungary. The volume covers only the Austrian half of the monarchy, and about ten thousand men here were schooled in the Hungarian half under different laws. That gap is old, and it stays.</p>", 'validation-occupations': "<p>The Czech-to-HISCO dictionary is the part of this project with the most human judgement in it, so it gets three independent second opinions, each blind to the others — and then two more aimed at the single word that carries a sixth of the sample.</p><p><b>The German bridge</b> translates each Czech job into its 1910 German equivalent and looks that up in the international database — useful precisely because Habsburg records were kept in German, so the translation is contemporary rather than modern. <b>OccCANINE</b> is a neural network trained on millions of historical job titles in other languages; fed the same German glosses, it agrees on 88&nbsp;% of records at the class level. <b>CZ-ISCO</b> is the modern Czech statistical classification — the only source that tests the <i>Czech reading itself</i> rather than a translation of it.</p><p>Each is blind in a different place, which is the point of having three. The German bridge cannot catch a mistranslation. OccCANINE cannot tell a clerk from an attendant, because that distinction is administrative and not in the title. CZ-ISCO is 2025 usage, so where a trade has drifted in a century it disagrees for the right reason and the wrong period — and it reaches none of the old rural words the sample is actually full of.</p><p>Which leaves the word none of them can reach. <i>Rolník</i> is a sixth of the sample and the difference between reading it as a farmer who owns his land and a hired farmhand is four social classes. So it gets its own two checks. The 1910 census carries columns for whether a man farmed on his own account or for wages, district by district: where the census counts more own-account farmers, the legionnaires from that district are more owner-coded — which is an argument about districts and never about one man. The Vienna Database supplies the missing half, because it records people one at a time: among men aged 18–30, a <i>Bauer</i> is 97.5&nbsp;% a household head and 0.3&nbsp;% a son. A farmer's son is not what the word names. Wrong territory, and the title and the position were written down by the same clerk — so it narrows the doubt rather than closing it.</p>", 'decisions': "<p>Building a dataset means making hundreds of choices that could defensibly have gone the other way, and the danger is not making them badly — it is making them invisibly. Six months later nobody, including the author, can tell which numbers are measurements and which are consequences of a forgotten decision.</p><p>So every such choice gets a line here: what was decided, why, and whether it is <i>settled</i>, <i>provisional</i> (in force, but the alternative would change results) or <i>open</i>. The argument itself is not repeated — it stays in whichever document already makes it, and this is the index.</p><p>The provisional ones are the interesting ones. They are the places where the paper's results depend on a call that a reasonable person could reject, stated in advance rather than discovered by a referee.</p>", 'audit': '<p>Twice — once in July 2026 and again in September — the entire codebase was read line by line, deliberately looking for reasons to distrust it rather than reasons to ship it. This sheet is what the two passes found, newest first.</p><p>The September pass found its worst problem in the step that matches a legionnaire to the same man in the list of fallen Habsburg soldiers. Two records were called the same person when the names were similar enough — but the test scored the whole name at once, so a shared first name (there are a great many Františeks) could carry two different surnames over the line. A second rule trusted a note field that mostly says <i>which regiment keeps the death register</i>, not that the man served in the Legion. Once each part of the name had to match on its own and the note had to actually mention the Legion, the 2,239 matched men fell to 1,340. Fewer matches, but ones that are really the same person.</p><p>The July pass found the one below, and it is worth understanding even if you never touch the code.</p><p>It is the most dangerous shape a data bug takes. About 26,000 soldiers had a blank exit field — nothing was recorded about how their service ended. Somewhere in the chain, <i>blank</i> was converted to text, and the text of a missing value happens to begin with the letter N, which is also a valid exit code. So 26,000 blanks silently became 26,000 confident answers. Nothing crashed. Every total still added up. The true count was about 645.</p><p>That is why the checks that run on every build are mostly of the form <i>missing stays missing</i>. A bug that turns absence into a plausible value cannot be caught by looking at the output, because the output looks better than the truth.</p>'}

{'cz-head': dict(what='The head names the political district and the court district: <i>Most: Most. — Náchod: Česká Skalice.</i> A page is not a district — the register runs straight on — so this page carries the tail of okres Most and the head of okres Náchod.', why='Which is why blocks take their district from the summary rows in the row stream, not from the page. A page-level assignment is wrong by construction at every boundary, and a boundary falls mid-page constantly.'), 'cz-header': dict(what='Seventeen columns under eighteen printed rules: area, houses, present population by sex, four confessional columns, three language columns, foreigners, and two columns of keys.', why='The rules are <b>in the ALTO</b> as graphical elements, so the column boundaries are measured rather than inferred from where the digits happen to fall. The engine finds all eighteen on about a fifth of pages, so the grid is fitted once over the 161 pages with a complete set and snapped to whatever each page did report.'), 'cz-seq': dict(what='Column 1 runs two interleaved sequences: municipalities counting across the okres, osady restarting at 1 inside each.', why='The OCR mangles them — <code>o</code>, <code>í)</code>, <code>Г) o</code> — but the sequence is known in advance, so row identity is <b>reconstructed rather than read</b>. This is the one column whose contents never have to be believed.'), 'cz-area': dict(what='The area in hectares is printed on the municipality row and on none of its settlements. That is the block delimiter.', why='Typography cannot do this job: the NDK <code>TextStyle</code> entries are synthetic — Times New Roman, sizes 5–10 — and carry no weight at all, so the bold municipality line is not bold as far as the text layer is concerned.'), 'cz-lasttwo': dict(what="The last two columns are the <b>postal delivery district</b> and the <b>nearest station or halt, with the walking distance</b>. Neither prints a name — both print a key into the legend at the foot of the page. Brzice's postal key is <b>9</b>, which is Rychnovek.", why='The <i>Návod</i> is precise about the two sizes of figure: “Malé číslice v posledních dvou sloupcích poukazují na dole uvedená jména, <b>velké číslice v posledním sloupci označují vzdálenost</b> … v pochodových hodinách. Vzdálenost menší jedné hodiny se neudává.” And the keys are numbered per <b>soudní okres</b>, not per page, so a key here may only resolve on another page — which is why the legend is built district-wide, and why 85 of 535 keys in the pilot come back <code>legend truncated</code>.'), 'cz-summary': dict(what='Each district opens with a summary row carrying the aggregate for everything that follows — here <i>P. o. Náchod</i>, and below it <i>I. s. o. Česká Skalice</i>.', why="These rows carry an area, so they segmented as municipalities: a district's own total added back into the district. Summing okres Kraslice with its three summary rows left in gave roughly <b>four times</b> the true population. They are matched loosely, because the <code>o</code> is routinely read as a zero (<i>P. 0. Kralupy</i>) and the word <i>okres</i> itself comes back wrong often enough to matter — <i>II. soudní <b>oleres</b> Tannwald</i> was being read as a municipality."), 'cz-block': dict(what='One municipality block: Brzice, and the four osady printed under it — Brzice proper, Grund, Harcov and Žďár. This is the unit of work, the smallest object that carries its own checksum.', why="It checks out by hand: 80 + 1 + 2 + 5 = <b>88</b> houses, 378 + 8 + 13 + 21 = <b>420</b> people, 369 + 8 + 13 + 21 = <b>411</b> Czech-speaking. And it catches a real defect: a stray inverted comma before Žďár's male count makes that cell <code>‘ 11</code>, which is not a number. The row's <code>I1_sex</code> and the block's male sum both come back <b>unparseable</b> — not failed, and above all not repaired. The block is re-read; the grader does not guess what the press meant.", table=True), 'cz-notes-left': dict(what='The apparatus is a <b>flow</b>, not a layout: it runs down this column and continues at the top of the next. Two kinds of section alternate — <i>Části osad</i>, the parts each settlement consists of, and <i>Úřady, ústavy a t. d.</i>, what the place had.', why="Cutting on the printed divider makes reading order a property of the crop instead of an instruction a model has to be trusted to follow. Handed both columns as one image, a reader transcribes across the divider line by line and interleaves two districts' entries into one stream."), 'cz-notes-right': dict(what='The right column, carrying the two sections for soudní okres Česká Skalice.', why='Sections are sent one at a time rather than a column at a time: a median of <b>478 px</b> instead of a whole column, <b>1.77 crops a page</b> instead of 3, and <b>56 symbol tokens</b> in the prompt instead of 83.'), 'cz-heading-ok': dict(what='The same heading, correctly read, for the other district on this page.', why='Both are on one page, which is what makes this the page to look at.'), 'cz-heading-bad': dict(what='The printed heading is <i>Úřady, ústavy a t. d. v soudním okresu Česká Skalice:</i>. The text layer read <b>Hřady</b>.', why="The first word is set in a larger face the engine handles worst — <i>Úřady</i> comes back as <i>Hřady</i>, <i>tířady</i>, <i>TJřady</i>, <i>brady</i>; <i>Části</i> as <i>Ciísti</i>, <i>Gusti</i>, <i>t asti</i> — and a rule keyed on it lost <b>137 of 1,146 headings (12 %)</b> across the volume. .pmarrow{stroke:#b4bcc2;stroke-width:1.2;fill:none}\n/* print / PDF: every sheet, no chrome, one sheet per page */\n@media print{\n  #side,.printbtn,.seg,.archlegend,.toc,.tblfilter,#zoomer,.chips,\n  .wayfind,.seealso{display:none!important}\n  #wrap{display:block}\n  main{max-width:none;padding:0}\n  .sheet{display:block!important;break-before:page;page-break-before:always}\n .fn,figure,.tldr,.feyn,table{break-inside:avoid;page-break-inside:avoid}\n  details{display:block}\n  details>summary{display:none}\n  /* the source folds are unlabelled by design once expanded; this one is a titled section\n     and loses its meaning without the title, so it keeps its summary (minus the triangle) */\n  .feyn>summary{display:block;padding-bottom:0}\n  .feyn>summary::before{content:none}\n  a{text-decoration:none;color:#000}\n  body{font-size:10.5pt}\n}\n</style></head><body><div id="wrap">\n<nav id="side">\n  <h1>{{ project }}</h1>\n  <p class="sub">{{ subtitle }}</p>\n  <input id="search" placeholder="Search all sheets…" oninput="doSearch(this.value)" autocomplete="off">\n  <div id="results"></div>\n  {% for grp, items, coll, gcol in groups %}\n    {% if coll %}\n      <details class="navgrp" id="navgrp-{{ loop.index }}">\n        <summary class="grp"><span class="gdot" style="background:{{ gcol }}"></span>{{ grp }}\n          <span class="cnt">{{ items|length }}</span></summary>\n        {% set ns = namespace(role=\'\') %}\n        {% for s in items %}\n          {% if s.role != ns.role %}<div class="subgrp">{{ s.role }}</div>{% set ns.role = s.role %}{% endif %}\n          <a class="scriptlink" href="#{{ s.id }}" data-id="{{ s.id }}"\n             onclick="show(\'{{ s.id }}\');return true">{{ s.title }}</a>\n        {% endfor %}\n      </details>\n    {% else %}\n      <div class="grp"><span class="gdot" style="background:{{ gcol }}"></span>{{ grp }}</div>\n      {% for s in items %}\n        <a href="#{{ s.id }}" data-id="{{ s.id }}" onclick="show(\'{{ s.id }}\');return true">\n          {{ s.title }}{% if s.interactive %}<span class="ixdot" title="interactive"></span>{% endif %}<small>{{ s.blurb }}</small></a>\n      {% endfor %}\n    {% endif %}\n  {% endfor %}\n  <button class="printbtn" onclick="printDoc()" title="Expand everything and open the print dialog">\n    Print / save as PDF</button>\n  <div class="stamp">\n    <div><b>Built</b> {{ stamp.built }}</div>\n    <div><b>Data</b> {{ stamp.data_built }}</div>\n    <div><b>Commit</b> {{ stamp.sha }} ({{ stamp.branch }})\n      {% if stamp.git %}<span class="pill {{ \'dirty\' if stamp.dirty else \'clean\' }}">\n        {{ \'uncommitted changes\' if stamp.dirty else \'clean tree\' }}</span>\n      {% else %}<span class="pill dirty">built without git history</span>{% endif %}</div>\n    <div style="margin-top:8px">Generated by<br><code>utils/docs/build_docs.py</code></div>\n  </div>\n</nav>\n<div id="zoomer" onclick="this.classList.remove(\'on\')">\n  <img id="zoomimg" alt=""><div class="hint">click anywhere, or press Esc, to close</div></div>\n<main>\n<div id="freshness" data-built="{{ stamp.built_epoch }}" data-dirty="{{ 1 if stamp.dirty else 0 }}"\n     data-qafail="{{ qa_failures }}"></div>\n{% for s in sheets %}\n  <section class="sheet" id="sheet-{{ s.id }}">\n    <h1>{{ s.title }}<span class="grpchip" style="background:{{ s.gcol }}">{{ s.group }}</span></h1>\n    <p class="lede">{{ s.blurb }}{% if s.src %} · source: <code>{{ s.src }}</code>{% endif %}</p>\n    {{ s.html }}\n  </section>\n{% endfor %}\n</main></div>\n<script>\nconst SHEETS = {{ sheet_ids }};\n// The script sheets are fetched when first opened (scripts/<id>.html); LAZY maps every id\n// inside them to its sheet, so a link to a function\'s anchor still lands.\nconst LAZY = {{ lazy_anchors }};\nfunction loadSheet(id){\n  const sec=document.getElementById(\'sheet-\'+id), ph=sec && sec.querySelector(\'.lazysheet\');\n  if(!ph) return Promise.resolve();\n  if(ph._loading) return ph._loading;\n  ph._loading = fetch(ph.dataset.src).then(r=>{ if(!r.ok) throw new Error(r.status); return r.text(); })\n    .then(html=>{ ph.outerHTML = html; })\n    .catch(()=>{ ph._loading = null;\n      ph.innerHTML = \'<p class="note">This sheet is its own file (<code>\'+ph.dataset.src+\'</code>) \'\n        +\'and could not be fetched. Open the documentation through the live site or a local \'\n        +\'web server (<code>python -m http.server</code> in <code>output/docs</code>), not \'\n        +\'straight from disk.</p>\'; });\n  return ph._loading;\n}\nfunction show(id, keepScroll){\n  loadSheet(id);\n  SHEETS.forEach(s=>{const e=document.getElementById(\'sheet-\'+s); if(e) e.classList.toggle(\'on\', s===id);});\n  document.querySelectorAll(\'#side a[data-id]\').forEach(a=>{\n    const on = a.dataset.id===id;\n    a.classList.toggle(\'active\', on);\n    // a script sheet reached from search or a URL hash lives in a collapsed group — open it\n    if(on){ const d = a.closest(\'details\'); if(d) d.open = true; }\n  });\n  if(!keepScroll) window.scrollTo(0,0);\n}\n// Routing rule: a hash is EITHER a sheet id OR a heading inside one. Only the first was\n// handled, so a link to another sheet\'s section (#places-coverage…) changed the URL and\n// nothing else — every contents-strip anchor was unreachable from outside its own sheet.\nfunction route(hash){\n  const h = (hash||\'\').replace(/^#/,\'\');\n  if(!h){ show(SHEETS[0]); return true; }\n  if(SHEETS.includes(h)){ show(h); return true; }\n  if(LAZY[h] && !document.getElementById(h)){\n    show(LAZY[h], true);\n    loadSheet(LAZY[h]).then(()=>{ const t=document.getElementById(h); if(t) t.scrollIntoView({block:\'start\'}); });\n    return true;\n  }\n  const el = document.getElementById(h);\n  const sec = el && el.closest(\'section.sheet\');\n  if(!sec) return false;\n  show(sec.id.replace(/^sheet-/,\'\'), true);\n  el.scrollIntoView({block:\'start\'});\n  return true;\n}\n// Freshness / health banner. A static page cannot watch the filesystem, so it reports the\n// two things it CAN know: how old this build is (the pipeline may have moved on since), and\n// what was already wrong at build time — a dirty tree or a failing data-QA check.\n(function(){\n  const el=document.getElementById(\'freshness\'); if(!el) return;\n  const ageDays=(Date.now()/1000 - +el.dataset.built)/86400;\n  const msgs=[];\n  if(+el.dataset.qafail>0)\n    msgs.push([\'bad\', `${el.dataset.qafail} data-QA check(s) were failing when this page was `\n      +`built — see <a href="#qa" onclick="show(\'qa\')">Data QA</a> before trusting the numbers.`]);\n  if(+el.dataset.dirty)\n    msgs.push([\'warn\', \'Built from an <b>uncommitted</b> working tree, so these numbers \'\n      +\'correspond to no commit. <a href="#changelog" onclick="show(\\\'changelog\\\')">Commits &amp; \'\n      +\'versions</a>\']);\n  if(ageDays>7)\n    msgs.push([\'warn\', `This page was generated <b>${Math.floor(ageDays)} days ago</b>. If the `\n      +\'pipeline or <code>data/final</code> has changed since, rebuild: \'\n      +\'<code>python utils/docs/build_docs.py</code>\']);\n  if(!msgs.length) return;\n  el.className=\'fresh \'+(msgs.some(m=>m[0]===\'bad\')?\'bad\':\'warn\');\n  el.innerHTML=msgs.map(m=>\'<div>\'+m[1]+\'</div>\').join(\'\');\n})();\n// Print / PDF: the page is a set of hidden tabs with collapsed <details>, so printing it\n// raw would emit one sheet with everything folded shut. Expand first, restore afterwards.\nfunction printDoc(){\n  const closed=[...document.querySelectorAll(\'details:not([open])\')];\n  closed.forEach(d=>d.open=true);\n  const restore=()=>closed.forEach(d=>d.open=false);\n  window.addEventListener(\'afterprint\', restore, {once:true});\n  setTimeout(()=>{ window.print(); setTimeout(restore, 1500); }, 60);\n}\nfunction zoom(img){\n  const z=document.getElementById(\'zoomer\');\n  document.getElementById(\'zoomimg\').src=img.src;\n  z.classList.add(\'on\');\n}\ndocument.addEventListener(\'keydown\', e=>{\n  if(e.key===\'Escape\'){ document.getElementById(\'zoomer\').classList.remove(\'on\');\n                        if(typeof archClear===\'function\') archClear(); }\n});\nfunction filterTable(inp){\n  const q = inp.value.toLowerCase();\n  const tbl = inp.parentElement.querySelector(\'table\');\n  tbl.querySelectorAll(\'tbody tr\').forEach(tr=>{\n    tr.style.display = tr.textContent.toLowerCase().includes(q) ? \'\' : \'none\';\n  });\n}\n// ── analysis-sample waterfall: sum the precomputed joint distribution in the browser\n// combos are [flagBits, theatreIdx, count]; a record is \'deserted\' iff bit0 is set.\n// instance-scoped: each waterfall is #wf-<name> with data in window.WF[<name>]\nfunction wfActive(root){ return [...root.querySelectorAll(\'.wfchips input\')].filter(b=>b.checked)\n                          .map(b=>({bit:+b.dataset.bit, req:b.dataset.req})); }\nfunction wfPass(b, active){\n  for(const t of active){ const on=(b>>t.bit)&1; if(t.req===\'set\'?!on:on) return false; }\n  return true;\n}\nfunction wfCount(cfg, active){ let n=0,d=0;                // total N and highlighted subgroup\n  for(const [b,,c] of cfg.combos){ if(wfPass(b,active)){ n+=c; if(b&1) d+=c; } }\n  return [n,d];\n}\nfunction wfByTheatre(cfg, active){\n  const t={};\n  for(const [b,ti,c] of cfg.combos){ if(!wfPass(b,active)) continue;\n    if(!t[ti]) t[ti]=[0,0]; t[ti][0]+=c; if(b&1) t[ti][1]+=c; }\n  return t;\n}\nfunction wfSnippet(cfg, root, active){                     // the runnable pandas mask\n  const on=[...root.querySelectorAll(\'.wfchips input\')].filter(b=>b.checked)\n             .sort((a,b)=>a.dataset.bit-b.dataset.bit);\n  const [n,d]=wfCount(cfg,active);\n  let s=\'import pandas as pd\\ndf = pd.read_parquet("\'+cfg.parquet+\'")\\n\';\n  if(cfg.helper && on.some(b=>/unit_status/.test(b.dataset.pred))) s+=\'\\n\'+cfg.helper;\n  if(!on.length){ s+=\'\\nsample = df.copy()\'; IDs only — the published page carries no names.\nfunction rkRoster(rows, senior){\n  if(!senior || !rows.length) return \'\';\n  const tr=rows.map(([id,by,other,th])=>\'<tr><td>\'\n      +(id?\'<a href="https://www.csol.cz/legionar/\'+id+\'/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">\'\n           +id+\'</a>\':\'—\')\n      +\'</td><td>\'+(by||\'—\')+\'</td><td>\'+(other||\'—\')+\'</td><td>\'+(th||\'—\')+\'</td></tr>\').join(\'\');\n  return \'<h4>The \'+rows.length+\' record\'+(rows.length===1?\'\':\'s\')+\', individually</h4>\'\n    +\'<p class="rkmeta">Each id opens its csol.cz entry. Columns: id · birth year · rank on the \'\n    +\'other ladder · theatre.</p>\'\n    +\'<div class="rkroster"><table><tbody>\'+tr+\'</tbody></table></div>\';\n}\n(function(){\n  const svg=document.getElementById(\'rksvg\'); if(!svg) return;\n  const lite=(g)=>{\n    svg.classList.toggle(\'hl\', g!=null);\n    svg.querySelectorAll(\'.rkbox,.rkedge,.rkgrade\').forEach(\n      e=>e.classList.toggle(\'hi\', g!=null && e.dataset.g===g));\n  };\n  svg.querySelectorAll(\'.rkbox,.rkgrade\').forEach(b=>{\n    b.addEventListener(\'mouseenter\', ()=>lite(b.dataset.g));\n    b.addEventListener(\'mouseleave\', ()=>lite(null));\n  });\n})();\n\nconst IDX = SHEETS.map(id=>{\n  const e = document.getElementById(\'sheet-\'+id);\n  const h = e.querySelector(\'h1\').cloneNode(true);           // drop the group chip from the title\n  h.querySelectorAll(\'.grpchip\').forEach(c=>c.remove());\n  return {id, title: h.textContent.trim(), text: e.textContent};\n});\n// The script sheets\' text is not in the page: fetched once, on the first search, and swapped\n// into their entries. Until it arrives (or if it cannot be fetched) the search covers the rest.\nlet LAZY_TEXT = null;\nfunction lazyText(then){\n  if(LAZY_TEXT) return;\n  LAZY_TEXT = fetch(\'{{ lazy_dir }}/search.json\').then(r=>r.json()).then(t=>{\n    IDX.forEach(s=>{ if(t[s.id]) s.text = t[s.id]; }); then();\n  }).catch(()=>{});\n}\nfunction doSearch(q){\n  const box = document.getElementById(\'results\');\n  q = q.trim();\n  if(q.length < 3){ box.innerHTML=\'\'; return; }\n  lazyText(()=>doSearch(document.getElementById(\'search\').value));\n  const ql = q.toLowerCase(); n++;\n    }\n  });\n  box.innerHTML = out || \'<a class="hit" style="padding:6px 8px">No matches</a>\';\n}\n// architecture map: flowchart ⇄ network toggle, hover isolation, click-through\nlet archLayout = ()=>{}, archRole = ()=>{}, archClear = ()=>{},\n    archHulls = ()=>{}, archImpact = ()=>{};\n(function(){\n  const svg = document.getElementById(\'archsvg\');\n  if(!svg) return;\n  const NW=158, NH=26, ROLE={\n    "Notebooks":["#fbe3e6","#d98a95"], "Scraping":["#e7eaee","#a6b0bb"],\n    "Person parsing":["#e3edf4","#8fb0c6"], "Geography & census":["#e3f0e8","#89bfa0"],\n    "Linkage":["#f6edd0","#d3b768"], "Output & support":["#efe7f4","#b79dcf"]};\n  const nodes=[...svg.querySelectorAll(\'.node\')], edges=[...svg.querySelectorAll(\'.edge\')];\n  const byId={}; nodes.forEach(n=>byId[n.dataset.id]=n);\n  let mode=\'flow\';\n  const cur={};                        // live position per node (animated)\n  nodes.forEach(n=>{cur[n.dataset.id]={x:+n.dataset.lx,y:+n.dataset.ly};});\n\n  // edge endpoint on a node\'s border, toward the other node\'s centre\n  function border(cx,cy,tx,ty,w,h){\n    const dx=tx-cx,dy=ty-cy;\n    const s=Math.min(dx?(w/2)/Math.abs(dx):1e9, dy?(h/2)/Math.abs(dy):1e9);\n    return [cx+dx*s, cy+dy*s];\n  }\n  function sizeOf(id){ const n=byId[id], s=(mode===\'net\'? +n.dataset.scale : 1);\n                       return [NW*s, NH*s]; }\n  function drawEdges(){\n    edges.forEach(e=>{\n      const A=cur[e.dataset.a], B=cur[e.dataset.b]; if(!A||!B) return;\n      const [aw,ah]=sizeOf(e.dataset.a), [bw,bh]=sizeOf(e.dataset.b);\n      const ax=A.x+aw/2, ay=A.y+ah/2, bx=B.x+bw/2, by=B.y+bh/2;\n      const [x1,y1]=border(ax,ay,bx,by,aw,ah), [x2,y2]=border(bx,by,ax,ay,bw,bh);\n      if(mode===\'flow\'){            // horizontal bezier — the flowchart look\n        const mx=(x1+x2)/2;\n        e.setAttribute(\'d\', x2>x1 ? `M${x1},${y1} C${mx},${y1} ${mx},${y2} ${x2},${y2}`\n                                  : `M${x1},${y1} C${x1+40},${y1-26} ${x2-40},${y2-26} ${x2},${y2}`);\n      } else {                       // straight line — the network look\n        e.setAttribute(\'d\', `M${x1},${y1} L${x2},${y2}`);\n      }\n    });\n  }\n  drawEdges();\n\n  archLayout = function(m){\n    if(m===mode) return;\n    mode=m;\n    const W=+svg.dataset.w, H=(m===\'net\'?+svg.dataset.neth:+svg.dataset.flowh);\n    svg.setAttribute(\'viewBox\', `0 0 ${W} ${H}`);\n    svg.setAttribute(\'height\', H);\n    svg.classList.toggle(\'net\', m===\'net\');\n    document.getElementById(\'archFlow\').classList.toggle(\'on\', m===\'flow\');\n    document.getElementById(\'archNet\').classList.toggle(\'on\', m===\'net\');\n    document.querySelector(\'.archlegend\').classList.toggle(\'show\', m===\'net\');\n    nodes.forEach(n=>{\n      const tx=(m===\'net\'?+n.dataset.fx:+n.dataset.lx), ty=(m===\'net\'?+n.dataset.fy:+n.dataset.ly);\n      // in the network view a node\'s area scales with its size in lines\n      const sc=(m===\'net\'? +n.dataset.scale : 1);\n      n.style.transform=`translate(${tx}px,${ty}px) scale(${sc})`;\n      const r=n.querySelector(\'rect\');\n      if(m===\'net\'){ const c=ROLE[n.dataset.role]||ROLE["Output & support"];\n        r.style.fill=c[0]; r.style.stroke=c[1];\n        r.setAttribute(\'stroke-width\', 1 + Math.min(3, (+n.dataset.deg)/2)); }\n      else { r.style.fill=\'\'; r.style.stroke=\'\'; r.setAttribute(\'stroke-width\',1); }\n    });\n    // glide nodes for 600ms (CSS), redrawing edges each frame so they follow\n    const t0=performance.now(), from={}; Hovering previews it; clicking PINS it so you\n  // can actually read the result (a hover-only graph is unusable the moment you look away).\n  let pinned=null;\n  function focus(id){\n    if(!id){ svg.classList.remove(\'iso\');\n      edges.forEach(e=>e.classList.remove(\'hot\')); nodes.forEach(m=>m.classList.remove(\'hot\'));\n      return; }\n    svg.classList.add(\'iso\');\n    const kin=new Set([id]);\n    edges.forEach(e=>{const hot=e.dataset.a===id||e.dataset.b===id;\n      e.classList.toggle(\'hot\',hot); if(hot){kin.add(e.dataset.a);kin.add(e.dataset.b);}});\n    nodes.forEach(m=>m.classList.toggle(\'hot\', kin.has(m.dataset.id)));\n  }\n  function describe(id){\n    const out=edges.filter(e=>e.dataset.a===id).map(e=>e.dataset.b);\n    const inc=edges.filter(e=>e.dataset.b===id).map(e=>e.dataset.a);\n    document.getElementById(\'archPinned\').innerHTML = id\n      ? `<b>${id}</b> — imports ${out.length ? out.map(x=>\'<code>\'+x+\'</code>\').join(\' \') : \'<i>nothing</i>\'}`\n        + ` · imported by ${inc.length ? inc.map(x=>\'<code>\'+x+\'</code>\').join(\' \') : \'<i>nothing</i>\'}`\n        + ` · <a href="#" onclick="archClear();return false">clear</a>`\n      : \'Hover to trace · click a box to inspect it (Esc clears) · double-click to open the module\';\n  }\n  const esc=s=>String(s).replace(/[&<>"]/g,c=>({\'&\':\'&amp;\',\'<\':\'&lt;\',\'>\':\'&gt;\',\'"\':\'&quot;\'}[c]));\n  function archInfo(id){\n    const p=document.getElementById(\'archpanel\'); if(!p) return;\n    const m=(window.ARCHMETA||{})[id];\n    if(!m){ p.innerHTML=\'<div class="aempty">Click a module to inspect it.</div>\'; return; }\n    const c=ROLE[m.role]||ROLE["Output & support"];\n    const imp=(out[id]||[]).slice().sort(), by=(inn[id]||[]).slice().sort();\n    const chips=a=>a.length? a.map(x=>`<code onclick="archJump(\'${x}\')">${esc(x)}</code>`).join(\'\')\n                           : \'<span class="none">nothing</span>\';\n    p.innerHTML =\n      (m.dirty?\'<span class="adirty">changed · uncommitted</span>\':\'\')\n      +`<h3>${esc(id)}</h3>`\n      +`<div class="arole"><span class="dot" style="background:${c[0]};border-color:${c[1]}"></span>`\n      +`${esc(m.role)}${m.ver&&m.ver!==\'—\'?\' · v\'+esc(m.ver):\'\'}</div>`\n      +(m.doc?`<p class="adoc">${esc(m.doc)}</p>`:\'\')\n      +`<div class="astat"><span><b>${m.lines||\'—\'}</b>lines</span>`\n      +`<span><b>${imp.length}</b>imports</span><span><b>${by.length}</b>imported by</span></div>`\n      +`<div class="alist"><div class="h">Imports</div>${chips(imp)}</div>`\n      +`<div class="alist"><div class="h">Imported by</div>${chips(by)}</div>`\n      +(m.sheet?`<button class="aopen" onclick="show(\'${m.sheet}\')">Open module sheet →</button>`:\'\');\n  }\n  // clicking a chip inside the panel jumps focus to that module\n  window.archJump=function(x){\n    const n=nodes.find(z=>z.dataset.id===x); if(!n) return;\n    svg.classList.remove(\'path\'); nodes.forEach(z=>z.classList.remove(\'onpath\',\'ep\'));\n    pinned=x; focus(x); describe(x); archInfo(x);\n    nodes.forEach(z=>z.classList.toggle(\'pin\', z.dataset.id===x));\n  };\n  // ── path tracing: every module on an import path from A to B ────────────────\n  const out={}, inn={};\n  edges.forEach(e=>{(out[e.dataset.a]=out[e.dataset.a]||[]).push(e.dataset.b);\n                    (inn[e.dataset.b]=inn[e.dataset.b]||[]).push(e.dataset.a);});\n  function reach(start, adj){\n    const seen=new Set([start]), stack=[start];\n    while(stack.length){ const v=stack.pop();\n      (adj[v]||[]).forEach(w=>{ if(!seen.has(w)){ seen.add(w); stack.push(w); } }); }\n    return seen;\n  }\n  function tracePath(a,b){\n    // nodes on some a->b path = reachable-from-a ∩ reaches-b. }\n    const set=new Set(on);\n    if(!set.has(dir[0])||!set.has(dir[1])){\n      svg.classList.remove(\'path\');\n      document.getElementById(\'archPinned\').innerHTML =\n        `<b>${a}</b> and <b>${b}</b> — no import path in either direction. `\n        +`<a href="#" onclick="archClear();return false">clear</a>`;\n      return;\n    }\n    svg.classList.remove(\'iso\'); svg.classList.add(\'path\');\n    nodes.forEach(n=>{ n.classList.toggle(\'onpath\', set.has(n.dataset.id));\n                       n.classList.toggle(\'ep\', n.dataset.id===a||n.dataset.id===b); });\n    let hops=0;\n    edges.forEach(e=>{ const on2=set.has(e.dataset.a)&&set.has(e.dataset.b);\n                       e.classList.toggle(\'onpath\', on2); if(on2) hops++; });\n    document.getElementById(\'archPinned\').innerHTML =\n      `Path <b>${dir[0]}</b> → <b>${dir[1]}</b>: ${set.size} modules, ${hops} imports on the way. `\n      +`<a href="#" onclick="archClear();return false">clear</a>`;\n  }\n\n  archClear = function(){ pinned=null; focus(null); describe(null); archInfo(null);\n    svg.classList.remove(\'path\');\n    nodes.forEach(m=>m.classList.remove(\'pin\',\'onpath\',\'ep\'));\n    edges.forEach(e=>e.classList.remove(\'onpath\')); };\n\n  nodes.forEach(n=>{\n    const id=n.dataset.id;\n    n.addEventListener(\'mouseenter\', ()=>{ if(!pinned && !svg.classList.contains(\'path\')) focus(id); });\n    n.addEventListener(\'mouseleave\', ()=>{ if(!pinned && !svg.classList.contains(\'path\')) focus(null); });\n    n.addEventListener(\'click\', ev=>{\n      if(ev.shiftKey && pinned && pinned!==id){ tracePath(pinned, id); return; }\n      if(pinned===id){ archClear(); return; }\n      svg.classList.remove(\'path\');\n      nodes.forEach(m=>m.classList.remove(\'onpath\',\'ep\'));\n      edges.forEach(e=>e.classList.remove(\'onpath\'));\n      pinned=id; focus(id); describe(id); archInfo(id);\n      nodes.forEach(m=>m.classList.toggle(\'pin\', m.dataset.id===id));\n    });\n    n.addEventListener(\'dblclick\', ()=>{ if(n.dataset.sheet) show(n.dataset.sheet); }));\n    nodes.forEach(n=>n.classList.toggle(\'impacted\', hit.has(n.dataset.id)));\n    document.getElementById(\'archPinned\').innerHTML = dirty.length\n      ? `<b>${dirty.length}</b> module(s) changed but uncommitted (red); """
build_docs.py — generate the single-file HTML documentation site
================================================================
Renders every authored reference document, the tabular crosswalks, and a **live**
descriptives + QA sheet into one self-contained ``output/docs/index.html``.

Design rule: **nothing is written twice.**
------------------------------------------
The markdown files under ``reference/`` stay the canonical prose; this script only
*renders* them. Every number on the Descriptives and QA sheets is **computed from
``data/final`` at build time** — never typed. That is deliberate: the 2026-07-16 audit
found that every stale claim in the project (a README two reorgs out of date, a "91 %"
that was really 68 %, a documented ``illegitimacy_rate`` that did not exist, a linkage
"~90" that was 144) was a hand-maintained copy of a fact that lived somewhere else. A
hand-written HTML would have been the most authoritative-looking copy of all.

So: if a fact is wrong here, fix its **source** (the markdown, or the pipeline) and
rebuild. Do not edit the generated HTML.

Contents
--------
Overview (README + build stamp + module index) · Descriptives (live) · QA (live
invariants) · Pipeline · Place matching · Ranks · Variables · Data dictionary ·
Census codebook · Data sources · Decisions · Audit.

Dependencies: ``markdown``, ``pygments``, ``jinja2`` (all already required).
Optional: ``latex2mathml`` → self-contained offline math; without it the page falls
back to KaTeX from a CDN (needs a network on first view).

Run:
    python utils/docs/build_docs.py            # -> output/docs/index.html
Rebuild after any pipeline change or notebook re-run.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import ast

CU_NAVY, CU_RED, CU_GREY = "#003657", "#D22D40", "#6E6E6E"

# Affordance chips: mark which figures respond to input, so a reader knows what to click.
IXBADGE = '<span class="ixbadge">⇱ Interactive</span>'          # click / toggle / drag / filter
HOVERBADGE = '<span class="ixbadge hover">↕ Hover for values</span>'  # tooltips on the marks
# One chip per affordance, so a block that both toggles and has tooltips carries both.

# One rule, enforced in one place. A chip belongs at the END of the HEADING that introduces
# the block it describes — never in a toolbar, a caption or a paragraph, where a reader
# scanning headings will miss it. `ix_head` is the only sanctioned way to emit one, and the
# sidebar dot is derived from the chips a sheet actually rendered (see `main`), so the
# registry cannot drift out of step with the page the way it did before 2026-08-01.
IX_WARNINGS: list[str] = []


def ix_head(text: str, *, level: int = 2, ix: bool = False, hover: bool = False,
            attrs: str = "") -> str:
    """A section heading carrying its affordance chips.

    Args:
        text: Heading text, already HTML-safe.
        level: Heading level, 2 or 3.
        ix: The block has controls — click, toggle, drag, filter.
        hover: The block is static but reveals exact values on hover.
        attrs: Extra attributes for the tag (``id=…``, ``class=…``).

    Returns:
        The complete ``<hN>…</hN>`` element. Both chips may apply at once: a figure with a
        view toggle whose bars also carry tooltips is honestly both.
    """
    chips = (" " + IXBADGE if ix else "") + (" " + HOVERBADGE if hover else "")
    a = (" " + attrs.strip()) if attrs else ""
    return f"<h{level}{a}>{text}{chips}</h{level}>"


def _strip_ixkey(html: str) -> str:
    """Drop the Overview legend, whose chips are *quoted*, not applied to anything."""
    return re.sub(r'<p class="note ixkey">.*?</p>', "", html, flags=re.S)


def _check_badges(sheet_id: str, html: str) -> None:
    """Warn at build time if a chip escaped a heading — the one way this can regress."""
    html = _strip_ixkey(html)
    for m in re.finditer(r'<span class="ixbadge[^"]*">', html):
        before = html[:m.start()]
        open_h = before.rfind("<h")
        close_h = before.rfind("</h")
        if open_h < 0 or open_h < close_h or not re.match(r"<h[1-3][\s>]", before[open_h:]):
            IX_WARNINGS.append(f"{sheet_id}: interactive chip outside a heading "
                               f"(…{_html.escape(html[max(0, m.start() - 60):m.start()])})")

# Favicon. The page ships as ONE self-contained file (GitHub Pages, no assets dir), so the
# icon has to travel inside it: a data URI, URL-encoded rather than base64 so the mark stays
# legible in a diff.
#
# "FA" — *Fateful Adventures*, where the Hašek allusion in the title lives — set in the same
# Palatino stack as the body text, on a CU navy field with a CU red rule. Two glyphs is the
# most a 16 px browser tab renders legibly, which is the only size that actually matters.
# Do NOT extend this to the title's four initials: they spell an English slur.
FAVICON_SVG = (
    '<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 64 64">'
    f'<rect width="64" height="64" rx="10" fill="{CU_NAVY}"/>'
    '<text x="32" y="42" text-anchor="middle" font-size="33" fill="#fff" '
    'font-family="Palatino Linotype,Palatino,Georgia,serif">FA</text>'
    f'<rect x="16" y="49" width="32" height="4" rx="2" fill="{CU_RED}"/></svg>'
)


def favicon_href() -> str:
    """The favicon as a data: URI, ready for ``<link rel="icon">``."""
    return "data:image/svg+xml," + quote(FAVICON_SVG, safe="")

    "rank_ladders.md": "#ranks",
    "VALIDATION_FIDLER.md": "#validation", "unit_authority.csv": "#unit-authority",
    "ROADMAP.md": "#roadmap", "SITE_CHANGELOG.md": "#whatsnew",
    "DECISIONS.md": "#decisions",
    "rank_recognition_1918_1938.md": "#ranks-legal",
    "census_codebook.md": "#census-codebook", "census_codebook.csv": "#census-codebook",
    "README.md": "#overview",
    # The dated plan is folded at the foot of the reading-route sheet (2026-10-24).
    "SYMBOL_ACCURACY_PLAN.md": "#register-route-the-dated-plan",
    "LEXIKON_1910_ROUTE.md": "#register-route",
}

#: Links resolved on the END OF THE PATH, tried before the file name. The gold
#: transcription folder has a `README.md` of its own, and by file name alone a link to it
#: would land on the project Overview.
_MD_PATH_ANCHORS = {
    "transcription_gold/README.md": "#register-route-the-gold",
}


# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Markdown → HTML (code fences and math stashed first, then restored)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# LaTeX escapes latex2mathml passes through verbatim, in literal *or* numeric-entity form
# (it entity-encodes some characters, so "\_" can surface as "\&#x0005F;").
_UNESC = re.compile(r"\\(&#x[0-9A-Fa-f]+;|[_%{}&#$])")
MATH_WARNINGS: list[str] = []


def _unescape_text_nodes(mathml: str) -> str:
    return re.sub(r">([^<>]*)<", lambda m: ">" + _UNESC.sub(r"\1", m.group(1)) + "<", mathml)


def _render_math(tex: str, display: bool) -> str:
    if HAVE_MATHML:
        try:
            out = _unescape_text_nodes(_l2m.convert(tex, display="block" if display else "inline"))
        except Exception as e:                         # noqa: BLE001 — bad TeX → show source
            MATH_WARNINGS.append(f"convert failed: {tex[:60]!r} ({e})")
        else:
            # A surviving backslash means the converter mis-parsed (it cannot handle
            # \{ or \} inside \texttt{} — it splits the group and italicises the letters).
            # Surface it rather than ship silently-wrong maths.
            if "\\" in re.sub(r"</?[^>]+>", "", out):
                MATH_WARNINGS.append(f"backslash leaked: {tex[:60]!r}")
            return out
    cls = "math-src math-block" if display else "math-src"
    return f'<span class="{cls}" data-display="{int(display)}">{_html.escape(tex)}</span>'


def _render_fence(block: str) -> str:
    m = re.match(r"```([\w+-]*)\n(.*?)```", block, re.S)
    lang, code = (m.group(1), m.group(2)) if m else ("", block.strip("`"))
    try:
        lexer = get_lexer_by_name(lang) if lang else PythonLexer()
    except Exception:                                  # noqa: BLE001
        lexer = TextLexer()
    return highlight(code, lexer, HtmlFormatter(nowrap=False, cssclass="highlight"))


#: Inline maths, ``$…$`` on one line. **A closing ``$`` is never followed by a digit** —
#: that is a price, not a delimiter. Without the rule, two dollar amounts on one line were
#: read as a formula and everything between them was set as maths: ``$0.33 a 13-page pass
#: … at ≈ $6`` came out as a run of italic letters. Measured over every markdown source on
#: 2026-10-05: 33 of the 119 inline matches were prices (3 on the Decisions sheet, 3 on the
#: Roadmap, 1 in What's new, 26 in the symbol-accuracy plan), every one of them closed by a
#: ``$`` with a digit after it, and none of the 86 real formulas is.
INLINE_MATH_RE = re.compile(r"(?<![$\\])\$([^$\n]+?)(?<!\\)\$(?![$\d])")

#: The same shape, for the check that reports maths the stash missed.
STRAY_MATH_RE = re.compile(r"\$[^$\n]{2,}\$(?!\d)")


def md_to_html(text: str) -> str:
    """Convert markdown to HTML, protecting fenced code and $…$ math from the parser."""
    fences: list[str] = []
    def _stash_fence(m):
        fences.append(m.group(0))
        return f"\n\nZZFENCEZZ{len(fences)-1}ZZ\n\n"
    text = re.sub(r"```.*?```", _stash_fence, text, flags=re.S)

    maths: list[tuple[str, bool]] = []
    def _stash(tex: str, disp: bool) -> str:
        maths.append((tex.strip(), disp))
        return f"ZZMATHZZ{len(maths)-1}ZZ"
    text = re.sub(r"\$\$(.+?)\$\$", lambda m: _stash(m.group(1), True), text, flags=re.S)
    text = INLINE_MATH_RE.sub(lambda m: _stash(m.group(1), False), text)

    out = _md.markdown(text, extensions=["tables", "sane_lists", "attr_list", "toc", "def_list"],
                       output_format="html5")

    for i, block in enumerate(fences):
        rendered = _render_fence(block)
        out = out.replace(f"<p>ZZFENCEZZ{i}ZZ</p>", rendered).replace(f"ZZFENCEZZ{i}ZZ", rendered)
    for i, (tex, disp) in enumerate(maths):
        rendered = _render_math(tex, disp)
        if disp:
            rendered = f'<div class="mathblock">{rendered}</div>'
        out = out.replace(f"<p>ZZMATHZZ{i}ZZ</p>", rendered).replace(f"ZZMATHZZ{i}ZZ", rendered)

    # Any surviving "$...$" means the stash regex missed it (inline maths must sit on one
    # line). Markdown will then have eaten its underscores as emphasis — which is how a
    # stray </em> once leaked italics across a sheet. Surface it instead of shipping it.
    for stray in STRAY_MATH_RE.findall(re.sub(r"<(code|pre)[\s>].*?</\1>", "", out, flags=re.S)):
        MATH_WARNINGS.append(f"unconverted inline maths (wrap it onto one line): {stray[:60]!r}")

    # markdown tables get a scrolling wrapper — a wide table (the 9-column legal-sources
    # one) must scroll, not squeeze its columns until the headers break apart
    out = re.sub(r"<table>(.*?)</table>",
                 lambda m: f'<div class="tblwrap"><table>{m.group(1)}</table></div>',
                 out, flags=re.S)

    # cross-document links → anchors; dead relative links → inert code spans
    def _fix_link(m):
        href, inner = m.group(1), m.group(2)
        path = href.split("#")[0]
        for tail, anchor in _MD_PATH_ANCHORS.items():
            if path.endswith(tail):
                return f'<a href="{anchor}">{inner}</a>'
        base = href.split("/")[-1].split("#")[0]
        if base in _MD_ANCHORS:
            return f'<a href="{_MD_ANCHORS[base]}">{inner}</a>'
        if href.startswith(("http://", "https://", "#", "mailto:")):
            return m.group(0)
        return f"<code>{inner}</code>"                 # local path — not navigable from the HTML
    out = re.sub(r'<a href="([^"]+)">(.*?)</a>', _fix_link, out, flags=re.S)
    return out


# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Build stamp + module index
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
def _git(*args: str) -> str:
    try:
        return subprocess.run(["git", *args], cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True,
                              text=True, timeout=15).stdout.strip()
    except Exception:                                  # noqa: BLE001
        return ""


def build_stamp() -> dict:
    """Provenance of this build: when, from which commit, and whether the tree was clean.

    Shown in the sidebar so a reader can always tell what they are looking at. ``dirty``
    means the page was generated from uncommitted work — the numbers are real, but they
    correspond to no commit. ``data_built`` is the newest mtime under ``data/final``, so a
    page older than the data is visible at a glance.
    """
    sha = _git("rev-parse", "--short", "HEAD")
    branch = _git("rev-parse", "--abbrev-ref", "HEAD")
    dirty = bool(_git("status", "--porcelain"))
    newest = max((p.stat().st_mtime for p in FIN.rglob("*") if p.is_file()), default=0)
    now = _dt.datetime.now()
    return {
        "built": now.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M"),
        "built_epoch": int(now.timestamp()),
        "sha": sha or "—", "branch": branch or "—", "dirty": dirty,
        # False on a machine that holds the files but not the repository (a synced copy).
        # Without it an empty `git status` read as "clean tree" — a claim about a history
        # the build could not see.
        "git": bool(sha),
        "data_built": (_dt.datetime.fromtimestamp(newest).strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M")
                       if newest else "—"),
        # data newer than the page can only mean the pipeline was re-run after this build
        "data_epoch": int(newest),
        "mathml": HAVE_MATHML,
    }


# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Per-script sheets — everything read from the source with `ast` (no imports, so
# no side effects and no dependency on the module being importable)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
def _sig_of(node) -> str:
    """First declaration line of a def/class, from unparsed AST (decorators skipped)."""
    for line in ast.unparse(node).splitlines():
        s = line.strip()
        if s.startswith(("def ", "async def ", "class ")):
            return s.rstrip(":")
    return node.name


def _first_doc_line(node) -> str:
    doc = (ast.get_docstring(node) or "").strip()
    return doc.split("\n")[0] if doc else ""


def _split_tldr(body: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
    """Split a module docstring body into (first paragraph, remainder).

    The opening paragraph of every module docstring in this project already *is* the
    summary, so the TL;DR card is that paragraph promoted — not a second description
    written by hand, which would be one more thing that can drift.
    """
    parts = re.split(r"\n\s*\n", body.strip(), maxsplit=1)
    return (parts[0].strip(), parts[1].strip() if len(parts) > 1 else "")


def _module_doc_body(doc: str) -> str:
    """Drop the module docstring's title/underline banner — the sheet already has a title."""
    lines = doc.splitlines()
    while lines and (not lines[0].strip() or set(lines[0].strip()) <= {"=", "-", "~"}):
        lines.pop(0)
    if len(lines) >= 2 and set(lines[1].strip()) <= {"=", "-"} and lines[1].strip():
        lines = lines[2:]                              # title + its underline
    return "\n".join(lines).strip()


_SECTIONS = ("Parameters", "Args", "Arguments", "Returns", "Return", "Raises",
             "Yields", "Attributes", "Note", "Notes", "Example", "Examples")


def _param_block_to_deflist(lines: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    """Turn an indented parameter block into a markdown definition list.

    Handles both styles present in this codebase — Google (``name: description`` on one
    line) and numpy (``name`` then an indented description). Without this the whole
    section collapses into a single run-on paragraph ("start_id, end_id Inclusive ID
    range. output_dir Folder for …"), which is unreadable.
    """
    out: list[str] = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(lines):
        raw = lines[i]
        if not raw.strip():
            i += 1
            continue
        body = raw.strip()
        m = re.match(r"^([*\w][\w*, ]*?)\s*(\([^)]*\))?\s*:\s*(.*)$", body)
        if m and not body.startswith(("- ", "* ")):          # Google: "name: desc"
            names, _type, desc = m.group(1), m.group(2), m.group(3)
            i += 1
            cont = []
            while i < len(lines) and lines[i].strip() and (len(lines[i]) - len(lines[i].lstrip())) > 0 \
                    and not re.match(r"^\s*[*\w][\w*, ]*?\s*(\([^)]*\))?\s*:\s", lines[i]):
                cont.append(lines[i].strip())
                i += 1
            full = " ".join([desc] + cont).strip()
            out += [", ".join(f"`{n.strip()}`" for n in names.split(",") if n.strip()),
                    f":   {full}", ""]
            continue
        # numpy: bare name, then a more-indented description
        indent = len(raw) - len(raw.lstrip())
        desc: list[str] = []
        j = i + 1
        while j < len(lines) and lines[j].strip() and (len(lines[j]) - len(lines[j].lstrip())) > indent:
            desc.append(lines[j].strip())
            j += 1
        if desc:
            out += [", ".join(f"`{n.strip()}`" for n in body.split(",") if n.strip()),
                    f":   {' '.join(desc)}", ""]
            i = j
            continue
        out.append(body)
        i += 1
    return out


def _escape_stray_tags(text: str) -> str:
    """Neutralise tag-like text in a docstring — it is prose, never markup.

    ``scraper_csol.parse_record`` documents the page it scrapes with a sentence containing a
    literal ``<strong>``; rendered as markdown that became a real, never-closed tag, and every
    sheet after it inherited bold. One unbalanced tag silently restyles the rest of the
    document, so tag-like runs outside code spans are escaped. Backticked text is left alone —
    markdown escapes that itself.
    """
    out, i = [], 0
    for m in re.finditer(r"`[^`]*`", text):
        out.append(re.sub(r"</?[A-Za-z][^>]*>",
                          lambda t: _html.escape(t.group(0)), text[i:m.start()]))
        out.append(m.group(0))
        i = m.end()
    out.append(re.sub(r"</?[A-Za-z][^>]*>",
                      lambda t: _html.escape(t.group(0)), text[i:]))
    return "".join(out)


def _docstring_html(text: str) -> str:
    """Docstring → HTML, demoted and de-anchored so it cannot collide with the sheet skeleton.

    A docstring is *inside* a sheet that already owns the page's ``<h1>``, so any heading it
    carries of its own must sit below the sheet's own levels — one module docstring was
    emitting 13 extra ``<h1>``s. The markdown ``toc`` extension also gives every "Parameters"
    / "Returns" block an id, which on 32 script sheets means the same id 32 times; ids here
    are worth nothing (nothing links to them) and break ``getElementById`` routing.
    """
    html = md_to_html(_rst_to_md(text))
    html = re.sub(r"<(/?)h[12]\b", r"<\1h3", html)
    return re.sub(r'(<h[1-6])\s+id="[^"]*"', r"\1", html)


def _rst_to_md(text: str) -> str:
    """Light rST/Google/numpy docstring → markdown (they use ``code``, :mod:`x`, sections)."""
    text = _escape_stray_tags(text)
    text = re.sub(r":(?:mod|func|class|meth|data|attr):`~?([^`]+)`", r"`\1`", text)
    text = re.sub(r"``([^`]+)``", r"`\1`", text)
    text = re.sub(r"^(\s*)\* ", r"\1- ", text, flags=re.M)

    lines = text.splitlines()
    out: list[str] = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(lines):
        ln = lines[i]
        nxt = lines[i + 1] if i + 1 < len(lines) else ""
        head = None
        # numpy section: "Parameters" over "----------"
        if ln.strip() in _SECTIONS and nxt.strip() and set(nxt.strip()) <= {"-", "="}:
            head, skip = ln.strip(), 2
        # Google section: "Args:" / "Returns:"
        elif re.fullmatch(r"\s*(" + "|".join(_SECTIONS) + r"):\s*", ln):
            head, skip = ln.strip().rstrip(":"), 1
        if head:
            i += skip
            block: list[str] = []
            while i < len(lines) and not (
                    lines[i].strip() in _SECTIONS
                    and i + 1 < len(lines) and set(lines[i + 1].strip() or "x") <= {"-", "="}
            ) and not re.fullmatch(r"\s*(" + "|".join(_SECTIONS) + r"):\s*", lines[i]):
                block.append(lines[i])
                i += 1
            out.append(f"#### {head}")
            out += (_param_block_to_deflist(block)
                    if head in ("Parameters", "Args", "Arguments", "Raises", "Attributes")
                    else [x.strip() for x in block])
            continue
        # other rST underlines → heading
        if ln.strip() and nxt.strip() and set(nxt.strip()) <= {"-", "="} and len(nxt.strip()) >= 3:
            out.append(f"#### {ln.strip()}")
            i += 2
            continue
        out.append(ln)
        i += 1
    return "\n".join(out)


def _callers(mod: str) -> list[str]:
    """Which notebooks / modules reference this module by name."""
    hits = []
    pat = re.compile(rf"\b{re.escape(mod)}\b")
    for nb in sorted(ROOT.joinpath("notebooks").glob("*.ipynb")):
        if pat.search(nb.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")):
            hits.append(nb.name)
    for p in sorted(ROOT.joinpath("utils").rglob("*.py")):
        if p.stem == mod or "_archive" in p.parts:
            continue
        txt = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
        if re.search(rf"import\s+\w*\b{re.escape(mod)}\b|from\s+[\w.]*\b{re.escape(mod)}\b", txt):
            hits.append(str(p.relative_to(ROOT)).replace("\\", "/"))
    return hits


# ── call sites: where each public function is actually invoked ────────────────
def _strip_py_noise(txt: str) -> str:
    """Remove docstrings and comments — a *mention* of a call is not a call site.

    Without this, any module whose docstring shows ``cz.build_census_panel(...)`` in a Usage
    block, or a comment naming a function, is reported as calling it.

    Done with :mod:`ast`, not regex. A regex pairing of triple quotes silently misaligns on
    any file whose *source* contains a triple quote inside a string — such as this one, whose
    own docstring-stripping regex literals did exactly that (29 = an odd number of ``\"\"\"``),
    shifting every subsequent pair and deleting real ``def`` lines. Re-unparsing the AST drops
    comments for free and cannot mis-pair anything.
    """
    try:
        tree = ast.parse(txt)
    except SyntaxError:
        return txt
    for node in ast.walk(tree):
        if isinstance(node, (ast.Module, ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef, ast.ClassDef)):
            body = getattr(node, "body", None)
            if (body and isinstance(body[0], ast.Expr)
                    and isinstance(body[0].value, ast.Constant)
                    and isinstance(body[0].value.value, str)):
                body.pop(0)
                if not body:
                    body.append(ast.Pass())
    try:
        return ast.unparse(tree)
    except Exception:                                  # noqa: BLE001
        return txt


def _searchable_corpus() -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    """(label, text) for every notebook and pipeline module — scanned for call sites.

    Excludes ``library/`` (human reading, not pipeline) and archived code. This generator is
    deliberately *kept* in the corpus: :func:`_strip_py_noise` already removes the comments
    that made it look like a caller, and dropping it would hide its own modules' real
    internal usage.
    """
    corpus: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
    for nb in sorted(ROOT.joinpath("notebooks").glob("*.ipynb")):
        corpus.append((nb.name, nb.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")))
    for p in sorted(ROOT.rglob("*.py")):
        rel = str(p.relative_to(ROOT)).replace("\\", "/")
        if "_archive" in p.parts or ".venv" in p.parts or rel.startswith("library/"):
            continue
        corpus.append((rel, _strip_py_noise(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"))))
    return corpus


# Names too generic to attribute by a bare text search — a hit says nothing.
_GENERIC = {"main", "show", "convert", "parse", "build", "run", "fix"}


def _call_sites(name: str, own: str, corpus: list[tuple[str, str]]) -> tuple[list[str], bool]:
    """(external call sites, called_internally) for a public function.

    Text search for ``name(``. Deliberately simple: it cannot see dynamic dispatch, and a
    generic name could collide — hence :data:`_GENERIC` is excluded from the dead-code
    signal rather than reported wrongly.
    """
    if name in _GENERIC:
        return [], True
    # (?<!\w) only — NOT (?<![\w.]): the normal call form is qualified (`cz.build_census_panel(`),
    # so excluding a leading dot hides almost every real call site. It must still reject a name
    # merely *ending* with this one (`_build_census_panel(`), which \w handles.
    pat = re.compile(rf"(?<!\w){re.escape(name)}\s*\(")
    ext, internal = [], False
    for label, txt in corpus:
        if label == own:
            # a definition always "matches"; look for a second occurrence
            internal = len(pat.findall(txt)) > 1
            continue
        if pat.search(txt):
            ext.append(label)
    return ext, internal


def _const_summary(node) -> tuple[str, str]:
    """(type + size, literal source) for a module-level constant."""
    v = node.value
    if isinstance(v, ast.Dict):
        kind = f"dict · {len(v.keys)} entries"
    elif isinstance(v, ast.List):
        kind = f"list · {len(v.elts)} items"
    elif isinstance(v, (ast.Set,)):
        kind = f"set · {len(v.elts)} items"
    elif isinstance(v, ast.Tuple):
        kind = f"tuple · {len(v.elts)} items"
    elif isinstance(v, ast.Constant):
        kind = type(v.value).__name__
    else:
        kind = "value"
    try:
        return kind, ast.unparse(v)
    except Exception:                                  # noqa: BLE001
        return kind, ""


def _file_commits(rel: str) -> list[tuple[str, str, str]]:
    out = _git("log", "--follow", "--format=%h\x1f%ad\x1f%s", "--date=short", "--", rel)
    return [tuple(l.split("\x1f")) for l in out.splitlines() if l]   # type: ignore[misc]


def _sig_html(sig: str) -> str:
    """Syntax-colour a signature (pygments, no wrapper) so it reads as code, not a label."""
    return highlight(sig, PythonLexer(), HtmlFormatter(nowrap=True)).strip()


def _code(src: str, first_line: int | None = None) -> str:
    fmt = HtmlFormatter(cssclass="highlight", linenos="table" if first_line else False,
                        linenostart=first_line or 1)
    return highlight(src, PythonLexer(), fmt)


def collect_scripts(dirty_files: set[str]) -> tuple[list[dict], list[dict]]:
    """Per-module sheets + a flat record of every public symbol (for the usage index)."""
    corpus = _searchable_corpus()
    sheets: list[dict] = []
    symbols: list[dict] = []

    for p in sorted(ROOT.joinpath("utils").rglob("*.py")):
        if "_archive" in p.parts or p.name == "__init__.py":
            continue
        rel = str(p.relative_to(ROOT)).replace("\\", "/")
        src = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
        try:
            tree = ast.parse(src)
        except SyntaxError:
            continue
        doc = ast.get_docstring(tree) or ""
        ver = (re.search(r'^__version__\s*=\s*"([^"]+)"', src, re.M) or [None, "—"])[1]
        mid = rel.replace("/", "-").replace(".py", "")

        funcs = [n for n in tree.body
                 if isinstance(n, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef, ast.ClassDef))
                 and not n.name.startswith("_")]
        # public module constants: plain AND annotated assignments (RANK_ORDINAL_HABSBURG:
        # dict[str,int] = {...} is an AnnAssign — missing these would hide the rank ladders)
        consts = []
        for n in tree.body:
            names = []
            if isinstance(n, ast.Assign):
                names = [t.id for t in n.targets if isinstance(t, ast.Name)]
            elif isinstance(n, ast.AnnAssign) and isinstance(n.target, ast.Name):
                names = [n.target.id]
            for nm in names:
                if nm.isupper() and not nm.startswith("_"):
                    consts.append((nm, n))

        used_by = _callers(p.stem)
        doc_body = _module_doc_body(doc) if doc else ""
        tldr, rest = _split_tldr(doc_body)

        # TL;DR card — the summary paragraph promoted, with the facts you would otherwise
        # have to hunt for (role in the pipeline, size, API surface, who calls it)
        facts = [f"<b>{_html.escape(SCRIPT_ROLE.get(p.stem, 'Output & support'))}</b>",
                 f"v{_html.escape(ver)}", f"{len(src.splitlines()):,} lines",
                 f"{len(funcs)} public function{'s' if len(funcs) != 1 else ''}"]
        if consts:
            facts.append(f"{len(consts)} constant{'s' if len(consts) != 1 else ''}")
        facts.append("used by " + (", ".join(f"<code>{_html.escape(u)}</code>" for u in used_by[:3])
                                   + (" +%d" % (len(used_by) - 3) if len(used_by) > 3 else "")
                                   if used_by else "nothing else"))
        body = [f'<div class="tldr"><div class="tldr-h">TL;DR</div>'
                + (_docstring_html(tldr) if tldr else f"<p><code>{rel}</code></p>")
                + f'<p class="tldr-facts">{" · ".join(facts)}'
                + (' · <span class="pill dirty">uncommitted</span>' if rel in dirty_files else "")
                + f" · <code>{rel}</code></p></div>"]

        # contents strip — chips, not a table
        chips = "".join(f'<a class="chip" href="#fn-{mid}-{n.name}">{n.name}</a>' for n in funcs)
        chips += "".join(f'<a class="chip const" href="#c-{mid}-{c}">{c}</a>' for c, _ in consts)
        if chips:
            body.append(f'<div class="chips">{chips}</div>')

        if rest:
            body.append("<h2>How it works</h2>" + _docstring_html(rest))

        if funcs:
            body.append("<h2>Functions</h2>")
            for n in funcs:
                fdoc = ast.get_docstring(n) or ""
                fsrc = ast.get_source_segment(src, n) or ""
                ext, internal = _call_sites(n.name, rel, corpus)
                symbols.append({"Module": rel, "Symbol": n.name, "Kind":
                                "class" if isinstance(n, ast.ClassDef) else "function",
                                "Called by": ", ".join(ext) if ext else
                                ("(internal use only)" if internal else "— no call site found —")})
                blk = [f'<div class="fn" id="fn-{mid}-{n.name}">',
                       f'<pre class="sig">{_sig_html(_sig_of(n))}</pre>']
                if fdoc:
