                    blk.append('<div class="fndoc">' + _docstring_html(fdoc.strip()) + "</div>")
                if ext:
                    blk.append('<p class="calls"><b>Called by</b> '
                               + " ".join(f"<code>{_html.escape(x)}</code>" for x in ext) + "</p>")
                elif internal:
                    blk.append('<p class="calls muted">Used only inside this module.</p>')
                else:
                    blk.append('<p class="calls warn">No call site found in the notebooks or '
                               "<code>utils/</code> — possibly superseded or reserved for interactive use.</p>")
                if fsrc:
                    nlines = len(fsrc.splitlines())
                    blk.append(f'<details><summary>source · lines {n.lineno}–'
                               f"{n.lineno + nlines - 1} ({nlines} lines)</summary>"
                               + _code(fsrc, n.lineno) + "</details>")
                blk.append("</div>")
                body.append("\n".join(blk))

        if consts:
            body.append("<h2>Constants</h2>")
            for name, node in consts:
                kind, literal = _const_summary(node)
                nl = len(literal.splitlines())
                body.append(f'<div class="fn" id="c-{mid}-{name}">'
                            f'<pre class="sig">{_html.escape(name)}'
                            f'<span class="kind">{_html.escape(kind)}</span></pre>'
                            + (f"<details><summary>value</summary>{_code(literal)}</details>"
                               if literal and nl <= 400 else
                               f'<p class="muted">{len(literal):,} chars — read it in the source.</p>')
                            + "</div>")

        if used_by:
            body.append("<h2>Used by</h2><p>"
                        + " ".join(f"<code>{u}</code>" for u in used_by) + "</p>")

        commits = _file_commits(rel)
        body.append("<h2>History</h2>")
        if commits:
            body.append(df_table(pd.DataFrame(
                [{"Commit": c, "Date": d, "Subject": re.sub(r"\bA-H\b", "Habsburg", s)}
                 for c, d, s in commits])))
        else:
            body.append('<p class="muted">No commits touch this file yet.</p>')
        if rel in dirty_files:
            body.append('<p class="note">This file has <b>uncommitted</b> changes; the reasoning '
                        "is recorded in <a href='#decisions'>Decisions</a> and the diff is "
                        "summarised on <a href='#changelog'>Commits &amp; versions</a>.</p>")

        body.append(f"<h2>Full source</h2><details><summary>{rel} · "
                    f"{len(src.splitlines()):,} lines</summary>{_code(src, 1)}</details>")

        sheets.append(dict(
            id="script-" + mid,
            group="Pipeline scripts", title=p.name,
            blurb=(re.sub(r"^[\w./]+\.py\s*[—-]\s*", "", _module_doc_body(doc).split("\n")[0])[:70]
                   if doc else rel),
            src=rel, kind="script", role=SCRIPT_ROLE.get(p.stem, "Output & support"),
            html="\n".join(body),
        ))
    sheets.sort(key=lambda s: (SCRIPT_ORDER.index(s["role"]) if s["role"] in SCRIPT_ORDER else 99,
                               s["title"]))
    return sheets, symbols


# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Changelog — strictly what git and the working tree actually know
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Architecture map — module import graph, laid out and drawn as inline SVG
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
def _module_imports(tree: ast.AST, known: set[str]) -> set[str]:
    """Which project modules this AST imports (both `from utils.x import y` forms)."""
    out: set[str] = set()
    for n in ast.walk(tree):
        if isinstance(n, ast.ImportFrom) and (n.module or "").startswith("utils"):
            last = (n.module or "").split(".")[-1]
            if last in known:
                out.add(last)
            out |= {a.name for a in n.names if a.name in known}   # from utils.parsing import ranks
        elif isinstance(n, ast.Import):
            for a in n.names:
                if a.name.startswith("utils") and a.name.split(".")[-1] in known:
                    out.add(a.name.split(".")[-1])
    return out


def _notebook_imports(text: str, known: set[str]) -> set[str]:
    """Project modules a notebook imports, read from the raw .ipynb JSON.

    Must cope with the alias form the notebooks actually use — ``from utils.parsing import
    districts as dz``. Matching a bare name list missed every aliased import, so notebook 02
    appeared to depend on 11 modules when it really depends on twice that.
    """
    out: set[str] = set()
    for m in re.finditer(r"from\s+utils[\w.]*\.(\w+)\s+import", text):
        if m.group(1) in known:
            out.add(m.group(1))
    # capture the whole import list up to the JSON line break, then strip "as <alias>"
    for m in re.finditer(r"from\s+utils[\w.]*\s+import\s+([^\\\"\n]+)", text):
        for part in m.group(1).split(","):
            name = part.strip().split()[0] if part.strip() else ""
            if name in known:
                out.add(name)
    for m in re.finditer(r"import\s+utils[\w.]*\.(\w+)", text):
        if m.group(1) in known:
            out.add(m.group(1))
    return out


_ROLE_COLOUR = {                              # (fill, stroke) per role for the network view
    "Notebooks":          ("#fbe3e6", "#d98a95"),
    "Scraping":           ("#e7eaee", "#a6b0bb"),
    "Person parsing":     ("#e3edf4", "#8fb0c6"),
    "Geography & census": ("#e3f0e8", "#89bfa0"),
    "Linkage":            ("#f6edd0", "#d3b768"),
    "1910 register":      ("#f3e6dc", "#c99a76"),
    "Reference tools":    ("#e6f1f1", "#86b9b9"),
    "Output & support":   ("#efe7f4", "#b79dcf"),
}


def _hull_path(pts: list[tuple[float, float]], pad: float = 18.0) -> str:
    """Smoothed, outward-padded convex hull around *pts* — the cluster blob for a role.

    Andrew's monotone chain for the hull, each vertex pushed *pad* away from the centroid so
    the blob clears the boxes, then drawn through edge midpoints with quadratic curves so it
    reads as an organic region rather than a polygon.
    """
    pts = sorted(set(pts))
    if len(pts) < 3:                                   # 1–2 nodes: pad a box into a blob
        xs, ys = [p[0] for p in pts], [p[1] for p in pts]
        x0, x1, y0, y1 = min(xs) - pad, max(xs) + pad, min(ys) - pad, max(ys) + pad
        return f"M{x0},{y0} L{x1},{y0} L{x1},{y1} L{x0},{y1} Z"

    def half(seq):
        out: list[tuple[float, float]] = []
        for p in seq:
            while len(out) >= 2 and ((out[-1][0] - out[-2][0]) * (p[1] - out[-2][1])
                                     - (out[-1][1] - out[-2][1]) * (p[0] - out[-2][0])) <= 0:
                out.pop()
            out.append(p)
        return out[:-1]

    hull = half(pts) + half(reversed(pts))
    cx = sum(p[0] for p in hull) / len(hull)
    cy = sum(p[1] for p in hull) / len(hull)
    grown = []
    for x, y in hull:
        dx, dy = x - cx, y - cy
        d = (dx * dx + dy * dy) ** 0.5 or 1.0
        grown.append((x + dx / d * pad, y + dy / d * pad))

    mids = [((grown[i][0] + grown[(i + 1) % len(grown)][0]) / 2,
             (grown[i][1] + grown[(i + 1) % len(grown)][1]) / 2) for i in range(len(grown))]
    d = [f"M{mids[-1][0]:.1f},{mids[-1][1]:.1f}"]
    for i, (mx, my) in enumerate(mids):
        qx, qy = grown[i]
        d.append(f"Q{qx:.1f},{qy:.1f} {mx:.1f},{my:.1f}")
    return " ".join(d) + " Z"


def _force_layout(nodes: list[str], edges: list[tuple[str, str]], w: float, h: float,
                  dims: dict[str, tuple[float, float]], top_margin: float = 34, seed: int = 7,
                  iters: int = 600) -> dict[str, tuple[float, float]]:
    """Deterministic Fruchterman–Reingold layout + rectangle collision (numpy, build-time).

    Two passes: (1) a standard force sim for the overall shape — clusters pull together,
    hubs settle centrally; (2) a collision-resolution sweep that pushes apart any pair of
    the (wide) node rectangles that still overlap, because the force sim treats nodes as
    points and the boxes are 158px wide. Undirected for placement (arrowheads keep the
    direction). Seeded, so the map is byte-identical on every rebuild.

    Positions are the node *top-left* corner (matching the layered layout and the SVG
    ``translate``), so ``x``/``y`` centres are offset by ``nw/2`` / ``nh/2``.
    """
    import numpy as np

    idx = {n: i for i, n in enumerate(nodes)}
    n = len(nodes)
    W = np.array([dims[m][0] for m in nodes])          # per-node box, so a big module
    Hh = np.array([dims[m][1] for m in nodes])         # claims proportionally more space
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    pos = rng.random((n, 2)) * np.array([w, h]) * 0.6 + np.array([w, h]) * 0.2
    E = [(idx[a], idx[b]) for a, b in edges if a in idx and b in idx]
    k = 1.15 * np.sqrt(w * h / n)             # ideal edge length (roomy → less clumping)
    t = w / 8.0
    for _ in range(iters):
        disp = np.zeros((n, 2))
        for i in range(n):                    # repulsion (O(n²); n≈32 → trivial)
            d = pos[i] - pos
            dist = np.hypot(d[:, 0], d[:, 1]) + 1e-9
            f = ((k * k) / dist)[:, None] * (d / dist[:, None])
            f[i] = 0
            disp[i] += f.sum(0)
        for a, b in E:                        # spring attraction along edges
            d = pos[a] - pos[b]
            dist = np.hypot(*d) + 1e-9
            f = (dist * dist / k) * (d / dist)
            disp[a] -= f
            disp[b] += f
        length = np.hypot(disp[:, 0], disp[:, 1]) + 1e-9
        pos += (disp / length[:, None]) * np.minimum(length, t)[:, None]
        pos[:, 0] = np.clip(pos[:, 0], 0, w - W)
        pos[:, 1] = np.clip(pos[:, 1], top_margin, h - Hh)
        t *= 0.985

    for _ in range(160):                       # collision resolution — no boxes overlap
        moved = False
        cx, cy = pos[:, 0] + W / 2, pos[:, 1] + Hh / 2
        for i in range(n):
            for j in range(i + 1, n):
                dx, dy = cx[j] - cx[i], cy[j] - cy[i]
                mx = (W[i] + W[j]) / 2 + 10    # min centre separation for THIS pair
                my = (Hh[i] + Hh[j]) / 2 + 10
                ox, oy = mx - abs(dx), my - abs(dy)
                if ox > 0 and oy > 0:          # overlapping → push along the shallower axis
                    if ox <= oy:
                        s = ox / 2 * (1 if dx >= 0 else -1)
                        pos[i, 0] -= s; pos[j, 0] += s; cx[i] -= s; cx[j] += s
                    else:
                        s = oy / 2 * (1 if dy >= 0 else -1)
                        pos[i, 1] -= s; pos[j, 1] += s; cy[i] -= s; cy[j] += s
                    moved = True
        pos[:, 0] = np.clip(pos[:, 0], 0, w - W)
        pos[:, 1] = np.clip(pos[:, 1], top_margin, h - Hh)
        if not moved:
            break
    return {node: (float(pos[i, 0]), float(pos[i, 1])) for node, i in idx.items()}


def graph_sheet(dirty_files: set[str] | None = None) -> str:
    """Draw the import graph as interactive inline SVG (no library, no CDN).

    Two layouts of the same data, toggled in the browser:

    * **Flowchart** — modules in columns by pipeline role, left→right from the orchestrating
      notebooks to the leaf parsers; the idiom for a directional dependency graph.
    * **Network** — a build-time force-directed layout that lets clusters and hubs emerge by
      position; role is shown by colour instead of column.

    Hovering a node isolates its neighbourhood; clicking a module opens its sheet.
    """
    dirty_files = dirty_files or set()
    mods: dict[str, dict] = {}
    for p in sorted(ROOT.joinpath("utils").rglob("*.py")):
        if "_archive" in p.parts or p.name == "__init__.py":
            continue
        rel = str(p.relative_to(ROOT)).replace("\\", "/")
        src = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
        ver = (re.search(r'^__version__\s*=\s*"([^"]+)"', src, re.M) or [None, "—"])[1]
        try:
            doc = _first_doc_line(ast.parse(src))
        except SyntaxError:
            doc = ""
        # strip a leading "module.py — " prefix that many docstrings repeat, and the
        # markdown emphasis/code markers the docstrings use (rendered as plain text here)
        doc = re.sub(rf"^{re.escape(p.name)}\s*[—-]\s*", "", doc).strip()
        doc = re.sub(r"[*`]+", "", doc)
        mods[p.stem] = {"rel": rel, "role": SCRIPT_ROLE.get(p.stem, "Output & support"),
                        "sheet": "script-" + rel.replace("/", "-").replace(".py", ""),
                        "lines": len(src.splitlines()), "ver": ver, "doc": doc,
                        "dirty": rel in dirty_files}
    known = set(mods)
    edges: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
    for stem, meta in mods.items():
        try:
            tree = ast.parse((ROOT / meta["rel"]).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        except SyntaxError:
            continue
        for dep in _module_imports(tree, known) - {stem}:
            edges.append((stem, dep))
    nb_nodes = []
    for nb in sorted(ROOT.joinpath("notebooks").glob("*.ipynb")):
        deps = _notebook_imports(nb.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"), known)
        if deps:
            nb_nodes.append(nb.stem)
            edges += [(nb.stem, d) for d in deps]

    cols = ["Notebooks"] + SCRIPT_ORDER
    members: dict[str, list[str]] = {c: [] for c in cols}
    members["Notebooks"] = nb_nodes
    for stem, meta in sorted(mods.items()):
        members[meta["role"]].append(stem)

    NW, NH, VG, CG, PAD, TOP = 158, 26, 9, 62, 16, 46
    layered: dict[str, tuple[float, float]] = {}
    for ci, c in enumerate(cols):
        x = PAD + ci * (NW + CG)
        for ri, stem in enumerate(members[c]):
            layered[stem] = (x, TOP + ri * (NH + VG))
    W = PAD * 2 + len(cols) * NW + (len(cols) - 1) * CG
    H = TOP + max(len(v) for v in members.values()) * (NH + VG) + PAD

    deg: dict[str, int] = {}                   # in-degree = how many things import it
    for _a, b in edges:
        deg[b] = deg.get(b, 0) + 1

    def role_of(stem: str) -> str:
        return "Notebooks" if stem in nb_nodes else mods[stem]["role"]

    # network view: node area scales with the module's size, so ranks.py (764 lines) visibly
    # outweighs theater.py (129). sqrt keeps *area* roughly proportional to lines.
    lines = {s: mods[s]["lines"] for s in mods}
    lo, hi = (min(lines.values()), max(lines.values())) if lines else (1, 1)
    def scale_of(stem: str) -> float:
        if stem in nb_nodes:
            return 1.0
        f = (lines[stem] - lo) / (hi - lo) if hi > lo else 0.5
        return round(0.74 + 0.72 * (f ** 0.5), 3)

    scales = {s: scale_of(s) for s in layered}
    dims = {s: (NW * scales[s], NH * scales[s]) for s in layered}

    # the network view needs a taller canvas than the flowchart so the collision pass has
    # vertical room; JS swaps the SVG viewBox to NETH when that view is shown
    NETH = max(H, 40 + 12 * (NH + 16))
    all_nodes = list(layered)
    force = _force_layout(all_nodes, edges, W, NETH, dims)

    # cluster hulls: one soft blob per role, from the corners of that role's boxes
    hulls = []
    by_role: dict[str, list[tuple[float, float]]] = {}
    for stem, (fx, fy) in force.items():
        w_, h_ = dims[stem]
        by_role.setdefault(role_of(stem), []).extend(
            [(fx, fy), (fx + w_, fy), (fx + w_, fy + h_), (fx, fy + h_)])
    for role, pts in by_role.items():
        fill, stroke = _ROLE_COLOUR.get(role, _ROLE_COLOUR["Output & support"])
        hulls.append(f'<path class="hull" data-role="{_html.escape(role)}" '
                     f'd="{_hull_path(pts)}" fill="{fill}" stroke="{stroke}"/>')

    svg = [f'<svg id="archsvg" viewBox="0 0 {W} {H}" width="{W}" height="{H}" '
           f'data-w="{W}" data-flowh="{H}" data-neth="{NETH}" '
           f'xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">']
    svg.append('<defs><marker id="ah" viewBox="0 0 8 8" refX="7" refY="4" markerWidth="7" '
               'markerHeight="7" orient="auto"><path d="M0 0 L8 4 L0 8 z" fill="#9fb0bf"/>'
               "</marker></defs>")
    svg.append(f'<g id="archhulls">{"".join(hulls)}</g>')
    for ci, c in enumerate(cols):              # column labels (hidden in network mode via CSS)
        x = PAD + ci * (NW + CG)
        svg.append(f'<text class="collab" x="{x}" y="24">{_html.escape(c)}</text>')
    svg.append('<g id="archedges">')
    for a, b in edges:
        if a in layered and b in layered:
            svg.append(f'<path class="edge" data-a="{a}" data-b="{b}" marker-end="url(#ah)"/>')
    svg.append("</g><g id='archnodes'>")
    for stem, (lx, ly) in layered.items():
        fx, fy = force[stem]
        is_nb = stem in nb_nodes
        sheet = "" if is_nb else mods[stem]["sheet"]
        cls = "node nb" if is_nb else "node"
        if not is_nb and mods[stem]["dirty"]:
            cls += " dirty"
        label = stem if len(stem) <= 21 else stem[:20] + "…"
        svg.append(
            f'<g class="{cls}" data-id="{stem}" data-role="{_html.escape(role_of(stem))}" '
            f'data-lx="{lx:.0f}" data-ly="{ly:.0f}" data-fx="{fx:.0f}" data-fy="{fy:.0f}" '
            f'data-deg="{deg.get(stem, 0)}" data-sheet="{sheet}" data-scale="{scales[stem]}" '
            f'data-lines="{mods[stem]["lines"] if not is_nb else 0}" '
            + f'style="transform:translate({lx:.0f}px,{ly:.0f}px)">'
            f'<rect width="{NW}" height="{NH}" rx="4"/>'
            f'<text x="9" y="17">{_html.escape(label)}</text>'
            + (f'<text class="deg" x="{NW - 8}" y="17">{deg[stem]}</text>' if deg.get(stem) else "")
            + "</g>")
    svg.append("</g></svg>")

    legend = "".join(
        f'<button class="lg on" data-role="{_html.escape(r)}" onclick="archRole(this)">'
        f'<span class="sw" style="background:{f};border-color:{s}"></span>{_html.escape(r)}</button>'
        for r, (f, s) in _ROLE_COLOUR.items())

    hubs = sorted(deg.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])[:5]
    meta = {stem: {"role": role_of(stem), "ver": mods[stem]["ver"],
                   "lines": mods[stem]["lines"], "doc": mods[stem]["doc"],
                   "sheet": mods[stem]["sheet"], "deg": deg.get(stem, 0),
                   "dirty": mods[stem]["dirty"]}
            for stem in mods}
    meta.update({nb: {"role": "Notebooks", "ver": "—", "lines": 0,
                      "doc": "Stage notebook — orchestrates the modules for this pipeline stage.",
                      "sheet": "", "deg": deg.get(nb, 0), "dirty": False} for nb in nb_nodes})
    return (
        ix_head("How the scripts fit together", ix=True, hover=True)
        + '<p class="note">Every arrow is a real <code>import</code>, read from the source at build '
        "time — <b>A → B</b> means A imports B. Two views of the same graph: the "
        "<b>flowchart</b> lays modules out in columns by pipeline role (the natural reading of a "
        "directional dependency graph); the <b>network</b> is a force-directed layout where "
        "tightly-coupled modules pull together and the hubs settle in the middle. <b>Hover</b> a "
        "box to isolate what it touches; <b>click</b> a module to open its sheet.</p>"
        '<div class="archbar">'
        '<div class="seg"><button id="archFlow" class="on" onclick="archLayout(\'flow\')">Flowchart</button>'
        '<button id="archNet" onclick="archLayout(\'net\')">Network</button></div>'
        '<div class="seg"><button id="archHull" onclick="archHulls()">Clusters</button>'
        '<button id="archImpact" onclick="archImpact()">Change impact</button></div>'
        f'<div class="archlegend">{legend}</div></div>'
        '<div class="archhint" id="archPinned">Hover to trace · <b>click</b> a box to inspect it · '
        "<b>shift-click</b> a second box to trace the import path between them · "
        "<b>double-click</b> opens the module · Esc clears</div>"
        f'<div class="archstage"><div class="archwrap">{"".join(svg)}</div>'
        '<aside class="archpanel" id="archpanel">'
        '<div class="aempty">Click a module to inspect it — its role, size, one-line purpose, '
        "and exactly what it imports and is imported by.</div></aside></div>"
        f"<script>window.ARCHMETA={json.dumps(meta, ensure_ascii=False)};</script>"
        '<p class="note"><b>Most depended-on:</b> '
        + ", ".join(f"<code>{k}</code> ({v})" for k, v in hubs)
        + f" · {len(mods)} modules, {len(nb_nodes)} notebooks, {len(edges)} import edges. "
        "In the network view the number on a box is its in-degree; the hubs are the boxes "
        "everything points at.</p>")


def usage_sheet(symbols: list[dict]) -> str:
    """Render the symbol-usage index and the dead-code list.

    Args:
        symbols: one record per public symbol, from :func:`collect_scripts`.
    """
    df = pd.DataFrame(symbols)
    dead = df[df["Called by"] == "— no call site found —"]
    S = ["<h2>Where every public symbol is used</h2>",
         '<p class="note">Each public function/class in <code>utils/</code>, and every notebook or '
         "module that calls it. Found by searching for <code>name(</code> across the notebooks and "
         "<code>utils/</code>, so it cannot see dynamic dispatch, and a few deliberately generic "
         "names are excluded. Treat it as a strong hint, not proof.</p>"]
    if len(dead):
        S.append(f'<h3>No call site found <span class="bad">{len(dead)}</span></h3>')
        S.append('<p class="note">Public, but never called from a notebook or another module. '
                 "Either superseded, or a standalone/interactive helper — worth a look before it "
                 "quietly rots. (This is how <code>wikidata.add_birth_coords</code> was found to be "
                 "superseded by <code>records_geo.add_settlement_attrs</code>.)</p>")
        S.append(df_table(dead[["Module", "Symbol", "Kind"]].reset_index(drop=True)))
    S.append("<h3>Full symbol index</h3>")
    S.append(df_table(df, searchable=True))
    return "\n".join(S)


def changelog_sheet(dirty: pd.DataFrame, scripts: list[dict]) -> str:
    """Render what git and the working tree actually know about the project's history.

    Deliberately modest: this repository has a shallow, lumpy history (most modules were
    added in one commit and never revised), so the sheet reports the uncommitted tree, the
    commit list and current versions, and points at the audit for the reasoning rather than
    pretending to derive it.
    """
    S: list[str] = []
    S.append('<p class="note"><b>What this sheet can and cannot tell you.</b> The tables below are '
             "read from git and the working tree at build time, so they are always true — but they "
             "are only as informative as the history itself. This repository has a <b>shallow, lumpy "
             "history</b>: most modules were introduced in a single commit and never revised in git, "
             "so a per-file log shows one line. This sheet is the <b>machine</b> half of the record "
             "and deliberately says nothing about <i>why</i>: the calls are listed in "
             "<a href='#decisions'>Decisions</a>, the narrative is on "
             "<a href='#whatsnew'>What's new</a>, and each module's own docstring records its design "
             "choices. If you want this sheet to become genuinely useful, commit in meaningful units "
             "with messages that say <i>why</i>.</p>")

    if not _git("rev-parse", "--short", "HEAD"):
        # A synced copy of the files without the repository. Say so, rather than print
        # "clean" and "0 commits" about a history this build could not read.
        S.append('<h2>Built without git history</h2>'
                 '<p class="note">This page was built on a machine that holds the project\'s '
                 "files but not its repository, so the working-tree and commit tables that "
                 "normally stand here could not be read. That says nothing about the state of "
                 "the repository: the work described on <a href='#whatsnew'>What's new</a> may "
                 "be uncommitted. The module versions below are read from the source files and "
                 "are current.</p>")
    elif len(dirty):
        S.append(f'<h2>Uncommitted working tree <span class="bad">{len(dirty)} files</span></h2>')
        S.append('<p class="note">These changes exist on disk but in <b>no commit</b> — so their '
                 "rationale is not recoverable from git. It is written up in "
                 "<a href='#decisions'>Decisions</a> and on <a href='#whatsnew'>What's new</a>. "
                 "Committing them is what turns that write-up into durable history.</p>")
        S.append(df_table(dirty, searchable=True))
    else:
        S.append('<h2>Uncommitted working tree <span class="ok">clean</span></h2>')

    commits = [l.split("\x1f") for l in
               _git("log", "--format=%h\x1f%ad\x1f%an\x1f%s", "--date=short").splitlines() if l]
    if commits:
        S.append(f"<h2>Commit history <span class='muted'>({len(commits)} commits)</span></h2>")
        rows = []
        for sha, date, who, subj in commits:
            n = len([x for x in _git("show", "--name-only", "--format=", sha).splitlines() if x])
            # display-only: expand the "A-H" abbreviation to its full form so the site's
            # terminology is uniform (identical meaning; git history itself is untouched).
            subj = re.sub(r"\bA-H\b", "Habsburg", subj)
            rows.append({"Commit": sha, "Date": date, "Files": n, "Subject": subj})
        S.append(df_table(pd.DataFrame(rows), searchable=True))

    S.append("<h2>Module versions</h2>")
    S.append('<p class="note">Every module carries a <code>__version__</code>. Bumps are not '
             "individually logged in git (the history predates that discipline), so treat this as "
             "the <i>current</i> state — the <a href='#audit'>audits</a> record what changed in the "
             "2026-07-16/17 and 2026-09-22 passes.</p>")
    vt = pd.DataFrame([{"Module": s["src"], "Version": re.search(r"Version ([\w.]+)", s["html"]).group(1)
                        if re.search(r"Version ([\w.]+)", s["html"]) else "—",
                        "Role": s["role"],
                        "Uncommitted": "yes" if "uncommitted changes" in s["html"] else ""}
                       for s in scripts])
    S.append(df_table(vt, searchable=True))
    return "\n".join(S)


def module_index() -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Every importable module with its version and one-line purpose, read from source.

    Generated rather than listed by hand, so it cannot drift as modules are added.
    """
    rows = []
    for p in sorted(ROOT.joinpath("utils").rglob("*.py")):
        if "_archive" in p.parts or p.name == "__init__.py":
            continue
        txt = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
        ver = (re.search(r'^__version__\s*=\s*"([^"]+)"', txt, re.M) or [None, "—"])[1]
        doc = re.search(r'^"""(?:\s*\n)?(.+?)$', txt, re.M | re.S)
        first = ""
        if doc:
            for line in doc.group(1).splitlines():
                s = line.strip()
                if s and not set(s) <= {"=", "-", "~"}:
                    first = s
                    break
        first = re.sub(r"^[\w./]+\.py\s*[—-]\s*", "", first)
        rows.append({"module": str(p.relative_to(ROOT)).replace("\\", "/"),
                     "version": ver, "purpose": first})
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Tables
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
def df_table(df: pd.DataFrame, cls: str = "tbl", searchable: bool = False) -> str:
    """Render a DataFrame as an HTML table, optionally with a client-side row filter.

    Used for genuinely tabular content (the dictionary, the codebook, coverage counts).
    Deliberately *not* used for code: signatures and source belong in ``<pre>``, where
    they can be syntax-coloured and cannot be mangled by cell wrapping.

    Args:
        df: rows to render; NaN becomes an empty cell.
        cls: CSS class for the table element.
        searchable: prepend a filter box and a row count.
    """
    head = "".join(f"<th>{_html.escape(str(c))}</th>" for c in df.columns)
    body = []
    for _, r in df.iterrows():
        tds = "".join(f"<td>{_html.escape('' if pd.isna(v) else str(v))}</td>" for v in r)
        body.append(f"<tr>{tds}</tr>")
    filt = ('<input class="tblfilter" placeholder="Filter these rows…" '
            'oninput="filterTable(this)">') if searchable else ""
    n = f'<p class="muted">{len(df):,} rows</p>' if searchable else ""
    return (f'{filt}{n}<div class="tblwrap"><table class="{cls}"><thead><tr>{head}</tr>'
            f"</thead><tbody>{''.join(body)}</tbody></table></div>")


def _pct(n, d) -> str:
    return f"{n/d*100:.1f}%" if d else "—"


def _with_toc(html: str, sheet_id: str) -> str:
    """Give every ``<h2>`` a sheet-scoped id and insert a contents strip linking to them.

    The heading may already carry an id: markdown's ``toc`` extension adds one, and those
    ids are **not** scoped to a sheet — two sheets with a "Coverage" section would both own
    ``#coverage``, and a cross-sheet link would land on whichever came first in the document.
    Rewriting them as ``<sheet>-<slug>`` makes every anchor unique and addressable. (Matching
    only bare ``<h2>`` is also why the strip never appeared on a markdown sheet.)
    """
    heads: list[tuple[str, str]] = []

    def _tag(m):
        inner = m.group(2)
        # an affordance chip is a label on the figure, not part of the section's name —
        # drop it whole, or the contents strip reads "… ⇱ Interactive ↕ Hover for values"
        title = re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", "",
                       re.sub(r'<span class="ixbadge[^"]*">.*?</span>', "", inner, flags=re.S)
                       ).strip()
        anchor = f"{sheet_id}-{re.sub(r'[^a-z0-9]+', '-', title.lower()).strip('-')}"
        rest = re.sub(r'\s*id="[^"]*"', "", m.group(1))
        heads.append((anchor, title))
        return f'<h2 id="{anchor}"{rest}>{inner}</h2>'

    html = re.sub(r"<h2([^>]*)>(.*?)</h2>", _tag, html, flags=re.S)
    if len(heads) < 3:
        return html
    # the title came out of HTML, so its entities are already encoded — unescape before
    # re-escaping or "Resources &amp; references" ships as "Resources &amp;amp; references"
    toc = "".join(f'<a href="#{a}">{_html.escape(_html.unescape(t))}</a>' for a, t in heads)
    strip = f'<nav class="toc"><span>On this page</span>{toc}</nav>'
    return _after_tldr(html, strip)      # summary first, then the map of the sheet


# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Sheet skeleton — the same bones on every sheet
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Every sheet reads: H1 (from the registry) → lede → wayfinder (history sheets only) →
# TL;DR card → contents strip → body → see-also. Before this the skeleton was per-sheet
# improvisation: markdown sheets rendered *two* H1s (the template's and the file's own),
# and the contents strip existed on 2 sheets of 55.

def _strip_lead_h1(html: str) -> str:
    """Drop a markdown file's own leading ``<h1>`` — the registry title is the authority."""
    return re.sub(r"\A\s*<h1[^>]*>.*?</h1>\s*", "", html, count=1, flags=re.S)


def _promote_tldr(html: str) -> str:
    """Promote the opening paragraph into the TL;DR card the script sheets already use.

    Only a *plain* leading ``<p>`` qualifies: a paragraph that already carries a class is
    doing another job (``.note``, ``.lede2``), and a very short or very long opener is not
    a summary. Anything that fails the test is left exactly where the author put it.
    """
    m = re.match(r"\A\s*<p>(.*?)</p>", html, flags=re.S)
    if not m:
        return html
    text = re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", "", m.group(1))
    if not (60 <= len(text) <= 1000):
        return html
    card = ('<div class="tldr"><div class="tldr-h">In short</div>'
            f"<p>{m.group(1)}</p></div>")
    return card + html[m.end():]


def _after_tldr(html: str, block: str) -> str:
    """Insert a generated block just below the TL;DR card (or at the top if there is none)."""
    m = re.match(r'\A(<div class="tldr">.*?</p></div>)', html, flags=re.S)
    return html[:m.end()] + block + html[m.end():] if m else block + html


def _binom_cdf(k: int, n: int, p: float) -> float:
    return sum(math.comb(n, i) * p ** i * (1 - p) ** (n - i) for i in range(k + 1))


def _exact_bounds(k: int, n: int, conf: float = 0.95) -> tuple[float, float]:
    """Clopper–Pearson interval for k events in n, by bisection on the binomial CDF (no scipy)."""
    a = (1 - conf) / 2

    def solve(j: int, target: float) -> float:  # P(X ≤ j | p) falls in p; find where it = target
        lo, hi = 0.0, 1.0
        for _ in range(60):
            mid = (lo + hi) / 2
            lo, hi = (mid, hi) if _binom_cdf(j, n, mid) > target else (lo, mid)
        return (lo + hi) / 2

    lower = 0.0 if k == 0 else solve(k - 1, 1 - a)   # P(X ≥ k) = α/2
    upper = 1.0 if k == n else solve(k, a)            # P(X ≤ k) = α/2
    return lower, upper


def certification_power() -> str:
    """Is the sealed sample large enough? — computed from each certification score on disk.

    The scorer's page-clustered bootstrap is the result of record, but with eight clusters and
    four errors its upper end sits at 1.000, so this adds what the claims alone can bound
    (exact binomial, not clustered) and what each symbol's count can bound — the question a
    reader of the headline asks next.
    """
    blocks = []
    for f in sorted((ROOT / "output" / "frozen").glob("*_certification/certification_score.json")):
        s = json.loads(f.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        a = s["as_printed"]
        errs = a["false"] + a["missed"]
        rows = [("false claims, of the route's claims", a["false"], a["claims_route"]),
                ("missed claims, of the printed claims", a["missed"], a["claims_gold"]),
                ("any error, per printed claim", errs, a["claims_gold"])]
        over = "".join(
            f"<tr><td>{lab}</td><td>{k} of {n}</td><td>{100 * k / n:.2f} %</td>"
            f"<td>{100 * _exact_bounds(k, n)[1]:.2f} %</td></tr>" for lab, k, n in rows)
        bands = [("ten or more", 10, 10 ** 9), ("three to nine", 3, 9), ("one or two", 1, 2)]
        sym = []
        for lab, lo, hi in bands:
            ts = [t for t in a["symbols"] if lo <= t["gold"] <= hi]
            if not ts:
                continue
            worst = min(_exact_bounds(t["hit"], t["gold"])[0] for t in ts)
            sym.append(f"<tr><td>{lab}</td><td>{len(ts)}</td><td>{sum(t['gold'] for t in ts)}"
                       f"</td><td>{sum(t['missed'] for t in ts)}</td><td>{worst:.2f}</td></tr>")
        # instances of a symbol needed for its sensitivity's lower bound to clear a bar,
        # read with no miss: (α/2)^(1/n) ≥ bar
        need = {bar: math.ceil(math.log(0.025) / math.log(bar)) for bar in (0.90, 0.95)}
        blocks.append(
            f"<h3>Is the sample large enough? — "
            f"{ {'cz': 'Czech half', 'de-bohemia': 'German Böhmen', 'de-moravia': 'German Mähren', 'de-silesia': 'German Schlesien', 'de-pooled': 'German half, pooled (D-136)'}.get(s['edition'], s['edition'])}, "
            f"scored {_html.escape(s['scored'][:10])}</h3>"
            "<p>Computed at build time from <code>certification_score.json</code>. The "
            "page-clustered interval above is the result of record; the bounds here count "
            "claims as independent, so they are the floor of the uncertainty, not its "
            "ceiling.</p>"
            '<table class="tbl"><tr><th></th><th>observed</th><th>rate</th>'
            "<th>95 % upper bound (exact)</th></tr>" + over + "</table>"
            '<table class="tbl"><tr><th>instances of the symbol on the sealed pages</th>'
            "<th>symbols</th><th>claims</th><th>missed</th>"
            "<th>lowest 95 % lower bound on sensitivity</th></tr>" + "".join(sym) + "</table>"
            f"<p>A symbol needs about <b>{need[0.90]}</b> instances, read without a miss, for "
            f"its sensitivity's lower bound to reach 0.90, and <b>{need[0.95]}</b> for 0.95.</p>")
    return "".join(blocks)


#: Where the script sheets live, beside ``index.html`` (2026-10-25). They were 32 of the page's
#: 41 MB — 117 sheets, most of it Pygments' line-numbered source — and every visit parsed all
#: of them to show one. Each is now its own fragment, fetched the first time it is opened.
LAZY_DIR = "scripts"


def _check_balanced(sheet_id: str, body: str) -> None:
    """Warn on an unbalanced inline tag: it leaks its styling into every following sheet."""
    for tag in ("strong", "em", "b", "i", "code"):
        # attribute-aware: <code onclick="…"> is still an opening tag
        o = len(re.findall(rf"<{tag}(?:\s[^>]*)?>", body))
        c = len(re.findall(rf"</{tag}>", body))
        if o != c:
            print(f"[!] sheet '{sheet_id}': unbalanced <{tag}> ({o} open / {c} close) — "
                  "styling will leak into the following sheets")


def _split_script_sheets(built: list[dict]) -> dict:
    """Write each script sheet to ``scripts/<id>.html`` and leave a placeholder in its place.

    Returns ``{element id: sheet id}`` for every id inside those sheets, so a link to a
    function's anchor (``#fn-…``) still finds the sheet to load. Their text goes to
    ``scripts/search.json``, which the search box fetches the first time it is used: the
    search covered the source before and still does. No underscore in the names, which
    GitHub Pages' Jekyll would drop.
    """
    out = OUT / LAZY_DIR
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    for stale in out.glob("*.html"):
        stale.unlink()
    anchors, text = {}, {}
    for s in built:
        if s.get("kind") != "script":
            continue
        name = f"{s['id']}.html"
        _check_balanced(s["id"], s["html"])
        (out / name).write_text(s["html"], encoding="utf-8")
        anchors.update({a: s["id"] for a in re.findall(r'\sid="([^"]+)"', s["html"])})
        text[s["id"]] = _html.unescape(re.sub(r"\s+", " ", re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", " ", s["html"])))
        s["html"] = (f'<div class="lazysheet" data-src="{LAZY_DIR}/{name}">'
                     '<p class="muted">Loading this sheet…</p></div>')
    (out / "search.json").write_text(json.dumps(text, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
    return anchors


def _register_route(html: str) -> str:
    """The reading-route sheet, which replaced two sheets on 2026-10-24: their old anchors land
    here — ``#symbol-accuracy`` under the summary, ``#gold-transcription`` on *The gold* — and
    the dated plan they carried is folded at its foot, its sections a level down so the
    contents strip keeps to this sheet's own."""
    html = _after_tldr(html, '<span id="symbol-accuracy"></span>' + route_flow())
    html = html.replace("<p><strong>The German half waits",
                        certification_power() + "<p><strong>The German half waits", 1)
    html = re.sub(r"(<h2[^>]*>The gold</h2>)", r'<span id="gold-transcription"></span>\1', html, count=1)
    plan = _strip_lead_h1(md_to_html(
        (ROOT / "reference" / "SYMBOL_ACCURACY_PLAN.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8")))
    plan = re.sub(r"<(/?)h([2-5])([^>]*)>",
                  lambda m: f"<{m.group(1)}h{int(m.group(2)) + 1}{m.group(3)}>", plan)
    return (html + "<h2>The dated plan</h2>"
            "<p>How the route came to be, revision by revision, from August to 15 October 2026 — "
            "kept as it was written, and superseded wherever the sections above say otherwise.</p>"
            "<details><summary>Show the dated plan</summary>" + plan + "</details>")


def _decision_badges(html: str) -> str:
    """Colour the register's Status column with the badge classes the QA sheet already uses."""
    cls = {"Settled": "pass", "Provisional": "warn", "Open": "fail"}
    return re.sub(r"<td>(Settled|Provisional|Open)</td>",
                  lambda m: f'<td><span class="badge {cls[m.group(1)]}">{m.group(1)}</span></td>',
                  html)


# The six sheets that record how the project got here. Each answers exactly one question;
# the strip states that division so the reader never has to infer it from three overlapping
# lists (before this, What's new, the git changelog and the Roadmap's "done" section all
# narrated the same week).
_HISTORY_SHEETS = [
    ("roadmap", "Roadmap", "what is still open"),
    ("whatsnew", "What's new", "what changed, and why it mattered"),
    ("changelog", "Commits & versions", "the machine record"),
    ("decisions", "Decisions", "the register of choices"),
    ("audit", "Audits", "two dated reviews"),
    ("validation", "External validation", "checked against Fidler"),
]


def _wayfind(current: str) -> str:
    """The 'which of these do I read?' strip shared by every history sheet."""
    items = []
    for sid, label, gloss in _HISTORY_SHEETS:
        inner = f"{_html.escape(label)} <i>{_html.escape(gloss)}</i>"
        items.append(f'<span class="here">{inner}</span>' if sid == current
                     else f'<a href="#{sid}" onclick="show(\'{sid}\')">{inner}</a>')
    return ('<nav class="wayfind"><span class="wfl">Record of change</span>'
            + "".join(items) + "</nav>")


# Lateral links: what a reader of this sheet most often needs next. Rendered from the
# registry, so titles and blurbs cannot drift out of sync with the sheets themselves.
RELATED: dict[str, list[str]] = {
    "overview": ["descriptives", "pipeline", "decisions"],
    "descriptives": ["variables", "qa", "places"],
    "qa": ["validation-register", "decisions", "changelog"],
    "roadmap": ["decisions", "whatsnew"],
    "whatsnew": ["changelog", "decisions", "roadmap"],
    "pipeline": ["architecture", "variables", "sources"],
    "places": ["lexikon-1910", "occupations", "sources"],
    "lexikon-1910": ["places", "sources", "validation-register"],
    "register-data": ["lexikon-1910", "register-route", "places"],
    "occupations": ["validation-occupations", "places", "variables"],
    "ranks": ["ranks-legal", "variables", "decisions"],
    "ranks-legal": ["ranks", "references"],
    "units": ["habsburg-army", "unit-authority", "validation"],
    "habsburg-army": ["units", "unit-authority", "sources"],
    "provenance": ["sources", "references", "validation-register"],
    "architecture": ["pipeline", "usage"],
    "variables": ["dictionary", "descriptives", "occupations"],
    "dictionary": ["variables", "census-codebook"],
    "census-codebook": ["sources", "places", "lexikon-1910"],
    "sources": ["provenance", "references", "lexikon-1910"],
    "references": ["sources", "provenance"],
    "usage": ["architecture", "pipeline"],
    "unit-authority": ["units", "validation"],
    "changelog": ["whatsnew", "decisions"],
    "decisions": ["audit", "validation-register", "whatsnew"],
    "audit": ["decisions", "validation-register", "qa"],
    "validation-register": ["validation", "validation-occupations", "validation-education"],
    "validation": ["validation-register", "units", "ranks"],
    "validation-occupations": ["occupations", "validation-register", "decisions"],
    "validation-education": ["education", "validation-register", "decisions"],
}


def _seealso(sheet_id: str, by_id: dict[str, dict]) -> str:
    ids = [i for i in RELATED.get(sheet_id, []) if i in by_id]
    if not ids:
        return ""
    cards = "".join(
        f'<a href="#{i}" onclick="show(\'{i}\')"><b>{_html.escape(by_id[i]["title"])}</b>'
        f'<span>{_html.escape(by_id[i]["blurb"])}</span></a>' for i in ids)
    return f'<nav class="seealso"><span class="sal">See also</span>{cards}</nav>'


# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# The plain-English layer
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Every method sheet on this site opens in the register it has to be written in: precise,
# hedged, and assuming the reader already knows what a járás or a HISCLASS is. That register
# is correct and it is also a wall. This is the other side of it — the same mechanism
# explained the way you would explain it to a colleague from another field over coffee: an
# analogy first, then what the code actually does, then the honest limit. If a passage here
# cannot say what would make it wrong, it is not finished.
#
# It lives here rather than in the reference/*.md files on purpose. Those files are the
# record; this is the doorway. Mixing them would put an analogy about post offices in the
# middle of a document the data-construction appendix is built from.
#
# The sheets that are supposed to have one. Every "How it works" sheet, plus the validation
# and decision sheets — those are the ones an outside reader opens cold. Kept as an explicit
# list rather than derived from the group, because `changelog` sits in the same group and is
# a machine record with nothing to explain.
PLAIN_SHEETS = {
    "pipeline", "places", "lexikon-1910", "occupations", "ranks", "ranks-legal", "units",
    "habsburg-army", "provenance", "architecture",
    "validation-register", "validation", "validation-occupations", "validation-education",
    "decisions", "audit",
}

PLAIN_ENGLISH: dict[str, str] = {

    "pipeline": (
        "<p>Somewhere on a Czech government server there are 133,000 web pages, one per "
        "legionnaire, each a little table of half-filled fields typed up from a paper card: "
        "born <i>Kolín</i>, trade <i>zámečník</i>, joined <i>12.3.1917</i>. A person can read "
        "one of those in a few seconds. Nobody can read 133,000, and no statistical model can "
        "read even one — a model wants a rectangle of numbers, and this is a heap of Czech "
        "sentences.</p>"
        "<p>The pipeline is the machine that turns the heap into the rectangle, and it is "
        "built in three stages so that each can be checked. <b>Collect</b>: fetch the pages "
        "and store them exactly as they came, never touched again. <b>Clean</b>: read every "
        "field with a small specialist — one for dates, one for ranks, one for jobs, one for "
        "places — and write out a table where a column means the same thing in every row. "
        "<b>Visualise</b>: draw the pictures, and read <i>only</i> from that final table, so a "
        "figure can never quietly disagree with the data it claims to show.</p>"
        "<p>The rule that makes the whole thing survivable is that the raw copy is sacred. "
        "Every judgement — every guess, every repair, every dropped record — happens in the "
        "middle stage, in code, where it can be read, argued with and undone. If a decision "
        "made in 2026 turns out to be wrong, the fix is one function and a re-run, not a "
        "dataset nobody can reconstruct.</p>"
    ),

    "places": (
        "<p>Imagine posting a letter addressed only to <i>Nová Ves, Bohemia</i>. There are "
        "dozens of Nová Ves — New Village is the Czech <i>Springfield</i> — and the one you "
        "want stopped existing under that name in 1918, was called something else in German, "
        "and has since been swallowed by a town. That is the problem on every one of these "
        "birth records, and it has to be solved 300,000 times, because a soldier's birthplace "
        "is how he gets attached to the 1910 census: how literate his district was, how many "
        "Czechs and Germans lived in it, how much of it farmed.</p>"
        "<p>So the matcher works like a careful postal clerk rather than a clever one. It "
        "tries the strongest evidence first — does this string name a district outright? — "
        "then weaker and weaker readings: a court district, a village in the gazetteer, a "
        "near-miss spelling. Crucially it <b>writes down which rung it used</b>. Every record "
        "carries a label saying how confident the match is, so an analysis can throw the weak "
        "ones away and see whether the result survives.</p>"
        "<p>Two things it refuses to do. It will not break a tie by picking whichever "
        "candidate the lookup table happened to list first — a coin-flip dressed as an "
        "answer. And it will not place a village in Slovakia just because a Slovak village "
        "has the same name, when the record says the man was born in Galicia. Where the "
        "evidence genuinely runs out, the field stays empty, and empty is a finding.</p>"
    ),

    "lexikon-1910": (
        "<p>In 1916 the imperial statistical office printed a book that lists every "
        "inhabited place in Bohemia — every village, every hamlet, every mill with a name. "
        "For each one it gives a row of numbers: how many hectares, how many houses, how "
        "many people, how many Catholics, how many spoke Czech. That part is a spreadsheet "
        "that happens to be made of paper, and a computer reads it about as well as you "
        "would expect: nine numbers in ten come out right.</p>"
        "<p>The interesting part is underneath. In tiny type at the foot of every page, the "
        "book also records what each village <b>had</b> — a school, a midwife, a fire "
        "brigade, a savings bank, a post office, a Czech credit union rather than a German "
        "one. That is a completely different kind of fact from a headcount, and nothing else "
        "in this project comes close to it: you can measure whether a man grew up somewhere "
        "with institutions or somewhere with none. There is one problem. To save space, the "
        "1916 typesetter printed those institutions not as words but as <b>little "
        "pictures</b> — a tiny open book for a school, a stylised helmet for a fire brigade — "
        "and defined them once, on a key page at the front.</p>"
        "<p>A computer cannot read a picture it has never been shown. Text-recognition "
        "software sees the school symbol and confidently types <i>g</i>. Modern AI models, "
        "asked what the mark is, guess — and guess differently from each other: handed the "
        "identical symbol, two of them answered “doctor” and “curate”. Over one test page "
        "they agreed with each other about the <i>words</i> of an entry two times in three, "
        "and about the <i>symbols</i> about one time in ten.</p>"
        "<p>So the work splits in two. The numbers upstairs are read by machine and then "
        "<b>made to prove themselves</b>: men plus women must equal the total, the villages "
        "must add up to their parish. Crucially the machine is never told what the answer "
        "should be — tell it the total and it will happily produce numbers that reach that "
        "total, and the test stops testing anything. Downstairs there is no such arithmetic, "
        "nothing adds up to anything, and the only defences are a fixed list of names a "
        "reader is allowed to use, and a human sitting down with the key page. A person "
        "reading those marks by hand got 286 of them and was unsure about none, which "
        "settles one thing at least: the difficulty is not the scan. It is that we are "
        "asking machines to recognise a picture nobody has drawn for them.</p>"
    ),

    "occupations": (
        "<p>Every soldier's card has one word for what he did: <i>rolník</i>, <i>zámečník</i>, "
        "<i>obchodní příručí</i>. To ask whether poor men deserted more often than "
        "comfortable ones, those words have to become something comparable — a rung on a "
        "ladder that a farmer in Moravia and a clerk in Prague can both stand on.</p>"
        "<p>That is what HISCO is: an international coding scheme where every historical job "
        "has a five-digit number, and every number maps to a social class from 1 (elite) to "
        "13 (unskilled). The trouble is that HISCO was built from Dutch, English and German "
        "records and contains <b>no Czech at all</b>. So the dictionary from Czech word to "
        "code is written here, by hand, one entry at a time — about 500 entries, which is "
        "enough to cover 98.5&nbsp;% of the men because occupations follow a brutal power law: "
        "a handful of trades account for most of a population.</p>"
        "<p>The matching itself is deliberately stupid. It will accept a phrase only if a "
        "<i>whole run of words</i> is already in the dictionary — never a fragment inside a "
        "word. That stupidity is the safety feature: a cleverer matcher, allowed to look "
        "inside words, once found the rank <i>major</i> hiding inside <i>generálmajor</i> and "
        "demoted every general in the army. Here, if nothing matches, the answer is nothing.</p>"
        "<p>And the honest part: about a fifth of the coded records rest on a judgement that "
        "could have gone the other way. <i>Rolník</i> — a sixth of the whole sample — is read "
        "as a farmer who works his own land rather than a hired farmhand, which is a "
        "four-class difference. That single call was tested against the 1910 census's own "
        "employment columns before it was allowed to stand, and it is flagged in the data so "
        "anyone can re-run the analysis without it.</p>"
    ),

    "ranks": (
        "<p>The central question of this project is what a demotion does to a man. A "
        "legionnaire had already deserted the Austrian army once; some of them were sergeants "
        "or lieutenants when they did. In the Czechoslovak Legion many started again as "
        "privates. Did the ones who fell furthest desert again?</p>"
        "<p>To ask that, the two armies' rank systems have to be laid side by side, and they "
        "do not line up on their own — different languages, different numbers of grades, and "
        "titles that mean different things in each. So both are placed on one ordinal scale "
        "using the NATO officer codes as the bridge, and the drop is simply the difference: "
        "a Habsburg sergeant who becomes a Legion private has a <b>rank reset</b> of minus "
        "several rungs.</p>"
        "<p>The trap here is a title that is not a grade at all. Some men were entered as "
        "<i>pracovník</i> (labour service) or <i>občan</i> (civilian) — administrative "
        "holding categories on the way in, not punishments. Scored naively, a Habsburg "
        "colonel entering as a <i>labourer</i> looks like the most spectacular demotion in "
        "the dataset, and it never happened. Those 7,696 records are flagged, and the "
        "headline result is computed without them.</p>"
    ),

    "ranks-legal": (
        "<p>When the war ended, hundreds of thousands of men who had worn one uniform had to "
        "be fitted into another — and the new Czechoslovak state had to decide what their old "
        "rank was worth. This sheet is the answer, dug out of the statute books.</p>"
        "<p>The law was openly lopsided, and knowing that is the point. Legion service was a "
        "<b>reward</b>: preferential appointments, generous crediting of time served, "
        "seniority back-dated as far as 1914. Former Austro-Hungarian officers were let in "
        "grudgingly and often a grade down. Two men of identical ability ended the decade in "
        "different places purely because of which army they had been in.</p>"
        "<p>It sits in the documentation because it explains a rumour the data would "
        "otherwise seem to support. Legionnaires believed officers were being demoted; the "
        "statutes show the opposite policy. So when the data shows a Habsburg officer entering "
        "the Legion at a low grade, the explanation is an entry procedure, not a punishment — "
        "and that distinction changes what the desertion result means.</p>"
    ),

    "units": (
        "<p>A soldier's record says he served in the <i>1st Regiment</i>. Which one? The "
        "Czechoslovak Legion in Russia had a 1st Regiment. So did the Legion in Italy. So did "
        "the French Foreign Legion, in which a Czech company also fought. Three different "
        "wars, three different sets of men, one number.</p>"
        "<p>Treating them as one unit would be a real error, not a cosmetic one, because unit "
        "is how soldiers are grouped for almost every comparison in the project — how big was "
        "his company, how many of his comrades died, did his regiment desert as a bloc. Mix "
        "two regiments together and every one of those numbers is wrong.</p>"
        "<p>The fix is to stop using the number alone and use <b>regiment plus army</b> as "
        "the identity. It sounds trivial; it moved 4,347 records, and it revealed that the "
        "records labelled <i>1st Regiment</i> are mostly Foreign Legion rather than the "
        "Czechoslovak 1st Rifles that everyone assumes.</p>"
    ),

    "habsburg-army": (
        "<p>The Habsburg army recruited locally on purpose. Each regiment had a home district "
        "it drew its men from, so a regiment was in effect a slice of one region — its "
        "language, its trades, its villages. That is the <i>Ergänzung</i> system, and it is "
        "why a regiment number is quietly also a place.</p>"
        "<p>That link is worth a great deal here. It lets a man's pre-Legion unit be tied "
        "back to a census district even when his own birthplace field is unreadable, and it "
        "gives a way to ask whether men from the same home district behaved alike — the kind "
        "of comparison the whole literature on unit cohesion turns on.</p>"
        "<p>It also explains the ambiguity next door: the Monarchy ran three parallel armies "
        "— the common army, the Austrian Landwehr and the Hungarian Honvéd — each numbering "
        "its own regiments from one, each with its own command language. A bare number is "
        "genuinely ambiguous, which is not sloppiness in the records but a fact about the "
        "state that kept them.</p>"
    ),

    "provenance": (
        "<p>A finished number in a paper — <i>desertion in Russia was four percent</i> — hides "
        "a chain of sources behind it: a scraped website, a census workbook, a shapefile, a "
        "hand-written dictionary. If any link is weak, the number is weak, and by the time it "
        "reaches a table nobody can tell which link it was.</p>"
        "<p>This sheet keeps the chain visible. Every mechanism the project claims is drawn "
        "back to the source that grounds it, so the reader can see at a glance which claims "
        "rest on an official census, which on a scholarly encyclopedia, and which on a "
        "judgement made here.</p>"
        "<p>It is also a defence against a specific kind of self-deception: a source used for "
        "two different purposes starts to look like two independent confirmations. Drawn as a "
        "graph, that shows up immediately as one node with two arrows out of it — which is "
        "one piece of evidence, not two.</p>"
    ),

    "architecture": (
        "<p>This project is about forty Python modules that call each other. That is small "
        "enough to feel manageable and quite large enough to hide a nasty surprise: you "
        "change how one function reads a date, and something four steps downstream that you "
        "had forgotten depends on it starts producing plausible, wrong answers.</p>"
        "<p>So the import graph is drawn automatically from the source itself — never from a "
        "hand-kept list, which would be out of date within a week. Click a module and the map "
        "highlights everything that would feel a change to it.</p>"
        "<p>The practical use is before an edit, not after. If the blast radius of a "
        "one-line change is eleven modules, that is worth knowing while the change is still "
        "an idea.</p>"
    ),

    "validation-register": (
        "<p>Most projects report the checks that passed. This one has a column for what each "
        "check <b>cannot see</b>, and that column is the honest half.</p>"
        "<p>The distinction that organises it: an <b>external</b> check compares this project "
        "against a source that could genuinely contradict it — a published encyclopedia, an "
        "official census, an independently trained model. A <b>self-check</b> only confirms "
        "that the output obeys the rules it was built from. Self-checks are necessary and "
        "they are not evidence that the coding is right; a rule applied perfectly to the "
        "wrong data passes every one of them.</p>"
        "<p>Reading the blind-spot column is the fastest way to find out what this project "
        "does not know. Place matching below the district level, for instance, has no "
        "external check at all — so it is written down as unchecked rather than left to look "
        "like it passed.</p>"
    ),

    "validation": (
        "<p>The best thing that can happen to a dataset is that somebody who has never seen "
        "it wrote down the answers first. In 2025 a historian published an encyclopedia of "
        "the Czechoslovak Legions: which units existed, where they fought, when they formed. "
        "That is an answer key produced with no knowledge of this project whatsoever.</p>"
        "<p>Checked against it, the pipeline's theatre assignment agrees on 99.6&nbsp;% of "
        "records, and every officer rank resolves correctly. More usefully, it found two real "
        "bugs. The rank ladder had no general grades, so <i>generálmajor</i> matched the word "
        "<i>major</i> and every Legion general was recorded three rungs too low. And notes "
        "<i>about</i> a rank — <i>candidate for lieutenant</i>, <i>was not a soldier</i> — "
        "were being scored as that rank.</p>"
        "<p>It also found roughly 130 records where the source website contradicts the "
        "historical record: regiments placed in Russia that only ever existed in France. "
        "Those are documented and left alone. Silently correcting a source is how a dataset "
        "stops being evidence about the source.</p>"
    ),

    "validation-education": (
        "<p>What a soldier wrote in the schooling box — <i>ob. 5 mě. 3</i> and the like — only "
        "means something if you know what those schools were. Until now that knowledge came "
        "from two modern history books. Neither counts schools; one of them starts its figures "
        "in 1924, in a different country.</p>"
        "<p>This page checks the scheme against the thing itself: the Austrian government's own "
        "annual census of every school it ran, printed in Vienna in 1912 for the year 1908/09, "
        "with a table for each kind of school in each province and the language it taught in. "
        "It is the register the ladder should have been built on, and it says three things.</p>"
        "<p>It <b>confirms</b> the awkward call at the heart of the variable. The "
        "<i>pokračovací</i> school — compulsory evening classes for apprentices — had been "
        "treated as a rung above the rest, which would have made an apprentice look "
        "better-educated than a grammar-school boy. The government filed it in a category of "
        "its own, and it was enormous: 504 of them in Bohemia teaching 50,836 pupils, against "
        "nine state trade schools teaching 3,518. Leaving it off the ladder was right.</p>"
        "<p>It <b>breaks</b> something else. The code marks an elementary schooling "
        "“complete” at eight years, because the law required eight years of schooling. "
        "But the census counts schools by how many year-groups they actually had, and a "
        "<i>eight</i>-class elementary school existed ten times in the whole empire and twice in "
        "the Czech lands. Nearly four thousand men are recorded as having finished a school that "
        "was almost nowhere, and three thousand more who wrote down the ordinary full five years "
        "are marked as having dropped out. The column is being left alone until that is decided "
        "properly rather than patched.</p>"
        "<p>And it shows that the evening classes are <b>badly under-recorded</b>: in life there "
        "were five of those pupils for every full-time trade-school pupil, but in these records "
        "there are fewer than one. Men simply did not write down the classes they were obliged "
        "to attend. So that flag counts some apprentices, not all of them.</p>"
        "<p>What none of it touches is Hungary. The volume covers only the Austrian half of the "
        "monarchy, and about ten thousand men here were schooled in the Hungarian half under "
        "different laws. That gap is old, and it stays.</p>"
    ),

    "validation-occupations": (
        "<p>The Czech-to-HISCO dictionary is the part of this project with the most human "
        "judgement in it, so it gets three independent second opinions, each blind to the "
        "others — and then two more aimed at the single word that carries a sixth of the "
        "sample.</p>"
        "<p><b>The German bridge</b> translates each Czech job into its 1910 German "
        "equivalent and looks that up in the international database — useful precisely "
        "because Habsburg records were kept in German, so the translation is contemporary "
        "rather than modern. <b>OccCANINE</b> is a neural network trained on millions of "
        "historical job titles in other languages; fed the same German glosses, it agrees on "
        "88&nbsp;% of records at the class level. <b>CZ-ISCO</b> is the modern Czech "
        "statistical classification — the only source that tests the <i>Czech reading itself</i> "
        "rather than a translation of it.</p>"
        "<p>Each is blind in a different place, which is the point of having three. The "
        "German bridge cannot catch a mistranslation. OccCANINE cannot tell a clerk from an "
        "attendant, because that distinction is administrative and not in the title. CZ-ISCO "
        "is 2025 usage, so where a trade has drifted in a century it disagrees for the right "
        "reason and the wrong period — and it reaches none of the old rural words the sample "
        "is actually full of.</p>"
        "<p>Which leaves the word none of them can reach. <i>Rolník</i> is a sixth of the "
        "sample and the difference between reading it as a farmer who owns his land and a "
        "hired farmhand is four social classes. So it gets its own two checks. The 1910 "
        "census carries columns for whether a man farmed on his own account or for wages, "
        "district by district: where the census counts more own-account farmers, the "
        "legionnaires from that district are more owner-coded — which is an argument about "
        "districts and never about one man. The Vienna Database supplies the missing half, "
        "because it records people one at a time: among men aged 18–30, a <i>Bauer</i> is "
        "97.5&nbsp;% a household head and 0.3&nbsp;% a son. A farmer's son is not what the "
        "word names. Wrong territory, and the title and the position were written down by "
        "the same clerk — so it narrows the doubt rather than closing it.</p>"
    ),

    "decisions": (
        "<p>Building a dataset means making hundreds of choices that could defensibly have "
        "gone the other way, and the danger is not making them badly — it is making them "
        "invisibly. Six months later nobody, including the author, can tell which numbers are "
        "measurements and which are consequences of a forgotten decision.</p>"
        "<p>So every such choice gets a line here: what was decided, why, and whether it is "
        "<i>settled</i>, <i>provisional</i> (in force, but the alternative would change "
        "results) or <i>open</i>. The argument itself is not repeated — it stays in whichever "
        "document already makes it, and this is the index.</p>"
        "<p>The provisional ones are the interesting ones. They are the places where the "
        "paper's results depend on a call that a reasonable person could reject, stated in "
        "advance rather than discovered by a referee.</p>"
    ),

    "audit": (
        "<p>Twice — once in July 2026 and again in September — the entire codebase was read "
        "line by line, deliberately looking for reasons to distrust it rather than reasons to "
        "ship it. This sheet is what the two passes found, newest first.</p>"
        "<p>The September pass found its worst problem in the step that matches a legionnaire "
        "to the same man in the list of fallen Habsburg soldiers. Two records were called the "
        "same person when the names were similar enough — but the test scored the whole name "
        "at once, so a shared first name (there are a great many Františeks) could carry two "
        "different surnames over the line. A second rule trusted a note field that mostly says "
        "<i>which regiment keeps the death register</i>, not that the man served in the "
        "Legion. Once each part of the name had to match on its own and the note had to "
        "actually mention the Legion, the 2,239 matched men fell to 1,340. Fewer matches, but "
        "ones that are really the same person.</p>"
        "<p>The July pass found the one below, and it is worth understanding even if you never "
        "touch the code.</p>"
        "<p>It is the most dangerous shape a data bug takes. About 26,000 soldiers had a blank "
        "exit field — nothing was recorded about how their service ended. Somewhere in the "
        "chain, <i>blank</i> was converted to text, and the text of a missing value happens to "
        "begin with the letter N, which is also a valid exit code. So 26,000 blanks silently "
        "became 26,000 confident answers. Nothing crashed. Every total still added up. The "
        "true count was about 645.</p>"
        "<p>That is why the checks that run on every build are mostly of the form <i>missing "
        "stays missing</i>. A bug that turns absence into a plausible value cannot be caught "
        "by looking at the output, because the output looks better than the truth.</p>"
    ),
}


def _plain_english(sheet_id: str) -> str:
    """The 'Explain it simply' fold, or nothing for a sheet without an entry.

    A plain ``<details>``: no JavaScript, findable by the browser's own text search, and
    already handled by the print stylesheet, which expands every fold before printing. It
    carries no interactive chip on purpose — ``ix_head`` marks *figures that respond to
    input*, and the sidebar's interactive dot is derived from those chips. A disclosure
    triangle on a paragraph of prose is not that, and claiming it would make the dot lie.
    """
    body = PLAIN_ENGLISH.get(sheet_id)
    if not body:
        return ""
    return ('<details class="feyn"><summary>Explain it simply</summary>'
            f'<div class="feyn-b">{body}</div></details>')


def _number_figures(html: str) -> str:
    """Number the figures on a sheet: ``<figcaption>`` → 'Figure N — …'."""
    n = [0]

    def _cap(m):
        n[0] += 1
        return f'<figcaption><b class="figno">Figure {n[0]}</b> — {m.group(1)}'
    return re.sub(r"<figcaption>(?!<b class=\"figno\")(.*?)(?=</figcaption>)", _cap,
                  html, flags=re.S)


AUTHORITY = ROOT / "reference" / "units" / "unit_authority.csv"


def _fidler_regiment_theatres() -> dict[int, set[str]]:
    """{regiment number → {theatres it existed in}} from the Fidler authority (numbered
    rifle/infantry *pluky* only; the Italian 'zvláštní' series is a separate numbering)."""
    if not AUTHORITY.exists():
        return {}
    a = pd.read_csv(AUTHORITY, encoding="utf-8")
    regs = a[(a["kind"] == "unit") & a["number"].notna()
             & a["unit_cs"].str.contains(r"\bPLUK\b", na=False)
             & ~a["unit_cs"].str.contains("ZVLÁŠTNÍ", na=False)]
    exp: dict[int, set[str]] = {}
    for n, th in zip(regs["number"].astype(int), regs["theatre"]):
        exp.setdefault(n, set()).add(th)
    return exp


def _ehnl_match_sets() -> dict:
    """Regiment-number sets from the Tabelle I files, keyed for unit-string matching."""
    u = ROOT / "reference" / "units"
    inf = set(pd.read_csv(u / "ehnl_tabelle1_infantry.csv")["reg_no"])
    lw = set(pd.read_csv(u / "ehnl_tabelle1_landwehr.csv")["reg_no"])
    hv = set(pd.read_csv(u / "ehnl_tabelle1_honved.csv")["reg_no"])
    oob = pd.read_csv(u / "ehnl_tabelle1_other.csv")

    def a(name):
        return set(pd.to_numeric(oob.loc[oob["arm"] == name, "reg_no"], errors="coerce")
                   .dropna().astype(int))

    return dict(common=inf, landwehr=lw, honved=hv, feldjager=a("Feldjäger"),
                dragoner=a("Dragoner"), husar=a("Husar"), ulan=a("Ulan"))


def _legion_ah_matched(L: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series:
    """True where ``habsburg_unit_capture`` parses to a unit that exists in Tabelle I."""
    if "habsburg_unit_capture" not in L:
        return pd.Series(False, index=L.index)
    s = _ehnl_match_sets()

    def m(v):
        if pd.isna(v):
            return False
        mm = re.match(r"(\d+)\.?\s*(.+)", str(v))
        if not mm:
            return False
        n, r = int(mm.group(1)), mm.group(2)
        if r.startswith(("p.pl.", "pp")):           return n in s["common"]
        if r.startswith(("zem.p.pl.", "zem.pl.")):  return n in s["landwehr"]
        if r.startswith("honv.p.pl."):              return n in s["honved"]
        if r.startswith(("pr.pol.mys", "pol.mys")): return n in s["feldjager"]
        if r.startswith("drag"):                    return n in s["dragoner"]
        if r.startswith(("husar", "hus")):          return n in s["husar"]
        if r.startswith("hul"):                     return n in s["ulan"]
        return False

    return L["habsburg_unit_capture"].apply(m)


def _habsburg_ah_matched(H: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series:
    """True where the fallen soldier's unit (org + number + type) exists in Tabelle I."""
    s = _ehnl_match_sets()

    def rn(v):
        if pd.isna(v):
            return None
        mm = re.search(r"(\d+)", str(v))
        return int(mm.group(1)) if mm else None

    nums = H["ah_unit_primary"].apply(rn)

    def m(org, n, typ):
        if n is None:
            return False
        if typ == "Infantry":
            return (n in s["common"] if org == "Common army"
                    else n in s["landwehr"] if org == "Landwehr"
                    else n in s["honved"] if org == "Honvéd" else False)
        if typ in ("Rifle", "Jäger"):
            return n in s["feldjager"]
        if typ == "Cavalry":
            return n in s["dragoner"] or n in s["husar"] or n in s["ulan"]
        return False

    return pd.Series([m(o, n, t) for o, n, t in
                      zip(H["ah_unit_org"], nums, H["ah_unit_type"])], index=H.index)


def _legion_flags(L: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Per-record coverage + unit-vs-Fidler status, as one boolean frame.

    Shared by the sample-size waterfall and the Units sheet so both tell the same story
    from the same definitions. ``unit_status`` is the four-way outcome of checking a
    Czechoslovak-Legion numbered regiment against the authority (match / conflict /
    no-entry / n-a), where *n-a* means the unit carries no verifiable number (support
    companies, foreign armies) — unverifiable is not the same as wrong.
    """
    exp = _fidler_regiment_theatres()
    reg = L["regiment"].astype("string")
    num = reg.str.extract(r"^(\d+)\.")[0].astype("Float64")
    is_num = num.notna() & reg.str.contains(r"(?:stř|p)\.pl\.", na=False)
    is_cs = L["legion_army"].astype("string").str.startswith("CS Legion", na=False) \
        if "legion_army" in L else pd.Series(False, index=L.index)

    def _st(n, th, cs, numbered):
        if not (cs and numbered) or pd.isna(n):
            return "n-a"
        want = exp.get(int(n))
        if want is None:
            return "no-entry"
        return "match" if th in want else "conflict"

    status = pd.Series([_st(n, th, cs, nm) for n, th, cs, nm in
                        zip(num, L["theater"], is_cs, is_num)], index=L.index)

    f = pd.DataFrame(index=L.index)
    f["deserted"] = L["deserted"].fillna(False).astype(bool)
    f["theatre"] = L["theater"].notna() & (L["theater"] != "Unknown")
    f["unit"] = L["regiment"].notna()
    f["unit_verified"] = status == "match"
    f["unit_conflict"] = status == "conflict"
    f["birthplace"] = L["birth_okres_id"].notna() | L["birth_jaras_id"].notna()
    f["rank_reset"] = L["rank_reset"].notna()
    f["ah_unit"] = (L["habsburg_unit_capture"].notna()
                    if "habsburg_unit_capture" in L else pd.Series(False, index=L.index))
    f["ah_matched"] = _legion_ah_matched(L)
    f["unit_status"] = status
    return f


def rank_reset_hist(L: pd.DataFrame, mask: pd.Series | None = None) -> str:
    """Diverging histogram of ``rank_reset`` — the headline regressor's distribution.

    One bar per integer reset on the ALT-1 common scale: negative = demoted on Legion
    entry (red, left), 0 = unchanged (grey), positive = promoted (navy, right). Bar
    height is √count, because the unchanged bar (~77 %) would otherwise flatten the whole
    tail — the tail (who was demoted, and how far) is the part that carries the identifying
    variation. Exact counts are in each bar's tooltip. ``mask`` optionally restricts the
    rows (used for the combat-ranks-only view).
    """
    import math

    r = (L if mask is None else L[mask])["rank_reset"].dropna().astype(int)
    if r.empty:
        return ""
    vc = r.value_counts().sort_index()
    lo, hi = int(vc.index.min()), int(vc.index.max())
    vals = list(range(lo, hi + 1))
    counts = {int(k): int(v) for k, v in vc.items()}
    n = int(vc.sum())
    mx = max(counts.values())

    BW, GAP, PLOTH, TOP, PAD, LBL = 17, 4, 176, 14, 30, 26
    W = PAD * 2 + len(vals) * (BW + GAP)
    BASE = TOP + PLOTH
    H = BASE + LBL + 16

    def col(v):
        return (CU_RED, "#e88") if v < 0 else ((CU_NAVY, "#7fa0b8") if v > 0 else (CU_GREY, "#bcc3c9"))

    svg = [f'<svg viewBox="0 0 {W} {H}" width="{W}" height="{H}" class="rrhist" '
           'xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">']
    svg.append(f'<line x1="{PAD-6}" y1="{BASE}" x2="{W-PAD+6}" y2="{BASE}" stroke="#c9d4de"/>')
    for i, v in enumerate(vals):
        c = counts.get(v, 0)
        x = PAD + i * (BW + GAP)
        h = (math.sqrt(c) / math.sqrt(mx) * PLOTH) if c else 0
        fill, _ = col(v)
        if c:
            svg.append(f'<rect x="{x}" y="{BASE-h:.1f}" width="{BW}" height="{h:.1f}" rx="1.5" '
                       f'fill="{fill}"><title>reset {v:+d}: {c:,} ({c/n*100:.1f}%)</title></rect>')
        if v % 2 == 0 or abs(v) <= 3 or v in (lo, hi):
            svg.append(f'<text class="rrx" x="{x+BW/2:.0f}" y="{BASE+13}">{v:+d}</text>')
        if c and (c == mx or c >= 0.02 * n):
            svg.append(f'<text class="rrn" x="{x+BW/2:.0f}" y="{BASE-h-3:.1f}">'
                       f'{c/1000:.0f}k</text>' if c >= 1000 else
