                       f'<text class="rrn" x="{x+BW/2:.0f}" y="{BASE-h-3:.1f}">{c}</text>')
    svg.append(f'<text class="rrax" x="{PAD}" y="{H-2}">← demoted on Legion entry</text>')
    svg.append(f'<text class="rrax" x="{W-PAD}" y="{H-2}" text-anchor="end">promoted →</text>')
    svg.append("</svg>")

    dem, unc, pro = int((r < 0).sum()), int((r == 0).sum()), int((r > 0).sum())
    return (
        '<div class="rrwrap">' + "".join(svg) + "</div>"
        f'<p class="note">{n:,} records have both ranks resolved. '
        f'<b style="color:{CU_RED}">{_pct(dem, n)} demoted</b> · '
        f'{_pct(unc, n)} unchanged · '
        f'<b style="color:{CU_NAVY}">{_pct(pro, n)} promoted</b> · mean {r.mean():+.2f}. '
        "Bar height is √count so the tail stays visible; the flat majority at 0 is the "
        "reset the Legion did <i>not</i> impose. The asymmetry — a longer left tail — is the "
        "raw material for the relative-deprivation story (hover a bar for its exact count).</p>")


# theatre → (line, fill) colours for the overlaid charts (CU brand-adjacent)
_THEATRE_COL = {
    "Russia": ("#003657", "#003657"), "Italy": ("#2f8f6b", "#2f8f6b"),
    "France": ("#D22D40", "#D22D40"), "Serbia/Balkans": ("#b3862f", "#b3862f"),
    "Britain/Dominions": ("#6a5acd", "#6a5acd"), "Post-war (ČSA)": ("#6E6E6E", "#6E6E6E"),
    "Unknown": ("#9aa4ad", "#9aa4ad"),
}


def rank_reset_areas(L: pd.DataFrame, theatres=("Russia", "Italy", "France"),
                     mask: pd.Series | None = None) -> str:
    """Overlaid area chart of the rank-reset *shape* by theatre.

    One translucent area per theatre (solid border, 18 % fill), plotting the share of
    that theatre's resolved resets at each integer value — shares, not counts, so the
    theatres are comparable despite very different N. Height is √share for the same
    reason as the histogram: the ~75–88 % mass at 0 would otherwise flatten the tails,
    and the tails (how much more Russia demoted than Italy) are the comparison. Legend
    toggles each theatre.
    """
    import math

    r = (L if mask is None else L[mask])
    r = r[r["rank_reset"].notna()]
    if r.empty:
        return ""
    lo, hi = int(r["rank_reset"].min()), int(r["rank_reset"].max())
    vals = list(range(lo, hi + 1))
    series = {}
    for th in theatres:
        s = r[r["theater"] == th]["rank_reset"].astype(int)
        if len(s) < 200:
            continue
        vc = s.value_counts(normalize=True)
        series[th] = ({v: float(vc.get(v, 0.0)) for v in vals}, len(s))
    if not series:
        return ""
    peak = max(sh for sh, _ in series.values() for sh in sh.values())

    STEP, PLOTH, TOP, PAD, LBL = 20, 176, 14, 34, 30
    W = PAD * 2 + (len(vals) - 1) * STEP
    BASE = TOP + PLOTH
    H = BASE + LBL + 16

    def X(v): return PAD + (v - lo) * STEP
    def Y(sh): return BASE - (math.sqrt(sh) / math.sqrt(peak) * PLOTH if sh > 0 else 0)

    svg = [f'<svg viewBox="0 0 {W} {H}" width="{W}" height="{H}" class="rrarea" '
           'xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">']
    svg.append(f'<line x1="{PAD-6}" y1="{BASE}" x2="{W-PAD+6}" y2="{BASE}" stroke="#c9d4de"/>')
    svg.append(f'<line x1="{X(0)}" y1="{TOP-4}" x2="{X(0)}" y2="{BASE}" stroke="#dfe3e8" '
               'stroke-dasharray="3 3"/>')
    for i, (th, (sh, n)) in enumerate(series.items()):
        line, fill = _THEATRE_COL.get(th, ("#555", "#555"))
        pts = " ".join(f"{X(v):.0f},{Y(sh[v]):.1f}" for v in vals)
        area = f"M{X(lo)},{BASE} L" + pts.replace(" ", " L") + f" L{X(hi)},{BASE} Z"
        svg.append(f'<path class="rra" data-th="{_html.escape(th)}" d="{area}" '
                   f'fill="{fill}" fill-opacity="0.18" stroke="none"/>')
        svg.append(f'<polyline class="rral" data-th="{_html.escape(th)}" points="{pts}" '
                   f'fill="none" stroke="{line}" stroke-width="1.6"/>')
    for v in vals:
        if v % 2 == 0 or v in (lo, hi):
            svg.append(f'<text class="rrx" x="{X(v):.0f}" y="{BASE+13}">{v:+d}</text>')
    svg.append(f'<text class="rrax" x="{PAD}" y="{H-2}">← demoted</text>')
    svg.append(f'<text class="rrax" x="{W-PAD}" y="{H-2}" text-anchor="end">promoted →</text>')
    svg.append("</svg>")

    legend = "".join(
        f'<button class="rrlg on" data-th="{_html.escape(th)}" onclick="rrToggle(this)">'
        f'<span class="sw" style="background:{_THEATRE_COL.get(th, ("#555",""))[0]}"></span>'
        f'{_html.escape(th)} <i>{n:,}</i></button>' for th, (_s, n) in series.items())

    return (
        '<p class="note">The same reset, split by theatre and drawn as overlapping areas '
        "(share of each theatre's resolved resets; height is √share so the tails read). The "
        "shapes are not alike: Russia carries a visibly heavier <b>demotion</b> shoulder than "
        "Italy, whose mass sits almost entirely at 0. Click a theatre to toggle it.</p>"
        f'<div class="rrbar">{legend}</div>'
        f'<div class="rrwrap">{"".join(svg)}</div>'
        '<p class="note">Russia <b>−0.62</b> mean reset (23% demoted) vs Italy <b>−0.03</b> '
        "(7%) vs France <b>−0.23</b> (16%). The theatre that did the most rank-resetting is "
        "also the one that saw essentially all the desertion — which is exactly why the reset "
        "has to be read against theatre, not on its own.</p>")

# The two lists are one list: every cited work has a BibTeX form and vice versa.
assert set(BIBTEX) == {e["key"] for e in BIB}, (
    f"bibliography out of sync — only in BIB: {sorted({e['key'] for e in BIB} - set(BIBTEX))}; "
    f"only in BIBTEX: {sorted(set(BIBTEX) - {e['key'] for e in BIB})}")
assert len({v["_key"] for v in BIBTEX.values()}) == len(BIBTEX), "duplicate BibTeX citekey"
_BIB_BY_KEY = {e["key"]: e for e in BIB}
# entries rendered under "Data sources" rather than "Literature"
_BIB_DATA_KEYS = {"mpidr_2012", "majo_2012", "csol", "vua_db", "rumpler_seger_2010",
                  "csu_lexikon", "gista", "wikidata", "ehnl_1934", "schematismus_1914",
                  "ortsverzeichnis_1910", "vienna_db", "dbcad"}
# entries rendered under "Statutes and standards" — legislation and the NATO code standard
_BIB_LAW_KEYS = {"zakon_195_1920", "zakon_194_1920", "zakon_462_1919", "narizeni_141_1927",
                 "nato_apersp01_2022", "mocr_hodnosti"}

_BIB_HEADER = """\
% reference/references.bib — GENERATED by utils/docs/build_docs.py. Do not edit.
%
% Every work cited anywhere on the documentation site, projected from the `BIB` list in the
% generator. That list is the master: the References sheet and this file are two renderings
% of it, and a build-time assertion refuses to emit one without the other. To add a work,
% add it to `BIB` (with its `pats` so inline mentions linkify) and to `BIBTEX`, then rebuild.
%
% Citekeys are pinned for Better BibTeX, reusing the keys already in the Zotero library so a
% re-import updates records instead of forking them.
"""


def render_bib() -> str:
    """The whole bibliography as biblatex, ordered by citekey."""
    out = [_BIB_HEADER]
    for _, e in sorted(BIBTEX.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1]["_key"]):
        fields = {k: v for k, v in e.items() if not k.startswith("_")}
        width = max(len(k) for k in fields)
        body = ",\n".join(f"\t{k.ljust(width)} = {{{v}}}" for k, v in fields.items())
        out.append(f"@{e['_type']}{{{e['_key']},\n{body},\n}}")
    return "\n\n".join(out) + "\n"


def references_sheet() -> str:
    """The bibliography in APA 7 — Literature and Data sources — each with a source link."""

    def _block(keys: set[str]) -> str:
        items = sorted((e for e in BIB if e["key"] in keys), key=lambda e: e["apa"])
        out = []
        for e in items:
            src = (f' <a class="refsrc" href="{e["url"]}" target="_blank" rel="noopener">'
                   "source ↗</a>") if e["url"] else ""
            out.append(f'<div class="refitem" id="ref-{e["key"]}">{e["apa"]}{src}</div>')
        return f'<div class="reflist">{"".join(out)}</div>'

    lit_keys = {e["key"] for e in BIB} - _BIB_DATA_KEYS - _BIB_LAW_KEYS
    return (
        "<h2>References</h2>"
        f'<p class="note">Every work cited anywhere on this site — {len(BIB)} entries, in APA '
        "style. This list is the <b>master</b>: <code>reference/references.bib</code> is "
        "generated from it at build time, so the two cannot disagree and neither can omit a work "
        "the other has. Inline mentions elsewhere — "
        '<span class="cite">Author (year)</span> — are clickable and preview the full '
        "reference on hover.</p>"
        "<h3>Literature</h3>" + _block(lit_keys)
        + "<h3>Statutes &amp; standards</h3>"
        + '<p class="note">The interwar Czechoslovak statutes behind the rank framework, and the '
          "NATO code standard the common scale is expressed in. Full treatment on the "
          "<a href='#ranks-legal'>Rank recognition 1918–38</a> sheet.</p>"
        + _block(_BIB_LAW_KEYS)
        + "<h3>Data &amp; reference sources</h3>" + _block(_BIB_DATA_KEYS)
        + '<p class="note">Full provenance, licences and access notes for each dataset are '
        "on the <a href='#sources'>Data sources</a> sheet; dataset citations here follow "
        "APA data-set style (retrieval year for the live databases).</p>"
        "<script>window.BIB="
        + json.dumps({e["key"]: {"apa": e["apa"], "url": e["url"]} for e in BIB},
                     ensure_ascii=False) + ";</script>")


def _linkify_citations(html: str) -> str:
    """Wrap every inline citation of every work in a `.cite` link.

    Code, math, SVG, scripts and existing links are protected first, so only prose text is
    touched. Each work links to its References entry and previews on hover.

    Two rules that were once wrong here:
    *Every* pattern of a work is applied, not just the first one that hits. A work cited in
    two textual forms on the same sheet — ``Vaněk et al. (1925–1929)`` in one paragraph and
    ``Vaněk et al., 1925–1929`` in the next — used to have only the first form linked, because
    a successful match broke out of the pattern loop.
    And each anchor is stashed the moment it is created, so a later pattern cannot match
    inside markup an earlier one just inserted.
    """
    prot: list[str] = []

    def _stash(m):
        prot.append(m.group(0))
        return f"\x00{len(prot) - 1}\x00"

    tmp = re.sub(r"<(pre|code|a|script|style|svg|math)\b.*?</\1>", _stash, html, flags=re.S)
    for e in BIB:
        for pat in e["pats"]:
            def _link(m, key=e["key"]):
                prot.append(f'<a class="cite" data-ref="{key}" href="#references" '
                            f'onclick="return bibGo(event)">{m.group(0)}</a>')
                return f"\x00{len(prot) - 1}\x00"
            tmp = re.sub(pat, _link, tmp, count=0)
    return re.sub("\x00(\\d+)\x00", lambda m: prot[int(m.group(1))], tmp)


def _waterfall(name: str, df: pd.DataFrame, cfg: dict) -> str:
    """Generic instance-scoped analysis-sample waterfall (fixed bars + live filter panel).

    Two live on the page (legionnaires + Habsburg comparison population); the JS is keyed
    on the ``wf-{name}`` container, and each instance registers its precomputed joint
    distribution in ``window.WF[name]``. ``cfg`` supplies the title/intro, the boolean
    ``flags`` frame, the bit ``order`` (``order[0]`` is the highlighted subgroup, e.g.
    deserters), the cumulative ``steps``, the ``toggles``, the highlight labels, and an
    optional pandas ``snippet`` (parquet + helper) for reproduction.
    """
    f, order = cfg["flags"], cfg["order"]
    hl = order[0]                                     # the highlighted subgroup flag (bit 0)
    N, Nh = len(df), int(f[hl].sum())
    hlabel = cfg["highlight_label"]

    bars, prev = [], N
    for label, mask, why in cfg["steps"]:
        n = int(mask.sum())
        d = int((mask & f[hl]).sum())
        drop = prev - n
        bars.append(
            f'<div class="wfrow"><div class="wflab">{_html.escape(label)}</div>'
            f'<div class="wfbar"><span style="width:{n / N * 100:.2f}%"></span>'
            f'<b>{n:,}</b> <i>{n / N * 100:.1f}%</i>'
            f'<u>{d:,} {hlabel} · {_pct(d, n)}</u></div>'
            f'<div class="wfwhy">{_html.escape(why)}'
            + (f' <em>−{drop:,}</em>' if drop else "") + "</div></div>")
        prev = n
    if cfg.get("extra_note"):
        bars.append(cfg["extra_note"])

    # precomputed joint distribution over the flag bits × theatre
    bits = pd.Series(0, index=df.index)
    for i, c in enumerate(order):
        bits = bits + f[c].astype(bool).astype(int) * (1 << i)
    theatres = list(df["theater"].fillna("Unknown").value_counts().index)
    th_idx = {t: i for i, t in enumerate(theatres)}
    tcol = df["theater"].fillna("Unknown").map(th_idx)
    grp = pd.DataFrame({"b": bits, "t": tcol}).groupby(["b", "t"]).size()
    combos = [[int(b), int(t), int(c)] for (b, t), c in grp.items()]

    chips = "".join(
        f'<label class="wfchip"><input type="checkbox" data-bit="{bit}" data-req="{req}" '
        f'data-key="{key}" data-pred="{_html.escape(pred)}" onchange="wfUpdate(\'{name}\')"> '
        f'{_html.escape(lab)}<span class="wftip">{_html.escape(tip)}</span></label>'
        for lab, bit, req, tip, key, pred in cfg["toggles"])

    parquet = cfg.get("snippet_parquet", "")
    share = ""
    if parquet:
        share = (
            '<div class="wfshare">'
            '<button class="wfbtn" onclick="wfCopyLink(this)">Copy link to this sample</button>'
            '<input class="wflink" readonly onclick="this.select()"></div>'
            '<div class="wfsnipwrap"><div class="wfsniphead">Reproduce in a notebook'
            '<button class="wfbtn sm" onclick="wfCopySnip(this)">Copy code</button></div>'
            '<pre class="wfsnip"><code></code></pre></div>')

    data = {"combos": combos, "total": N, "theatres": theatres,
            "thcol": {t: _THEATRE_COL.get(t, ("#888", ""))[0] for t in theatres},
            "helper": cfg.get("helper", ""), "hlabel": hlabel,
            "ratelabel": cfg["rate_label"], "parquet": parquet,
            "anchor": cfg.get("anchor", "descriptives")}

    return (
        f'<div class="wfblock" id="wf-{name}">'
        + cfg["title"] + cfg["intro"]
        + f'<div class="wf">{"".join(bars)}</div>'
        + ix_head("Build your own sample", level=3, ix=True, attrs='class="wfh"')
        + cfg["build_note"]
        + f'<div class="wfchips">{chips}</div>'
        + f'<div class="wfout" data-n="{N}" data-nd="{Nh}"></div>'
        + share
        + f"<script>(window.WF=window.WF||{{}})['{name}']="
        + json.dumps(data, ensure_ascii=False) + ";</script></div>")


def waterfall_block(L: pd.DataFrame, f: pd.DataFrame) -> str:
    """Legionnaire analysis-sample waterfall — decide which borderline records to keep."""
    strict = int((f["theatre"] & f["unit_verified"] & f["birthplace"] & f["rank_reset"]).sum())
    helper = (
        '# Fidler unit cross-check — reads the external reference table, not data/final:\n'
        '_a = pd.read_csv("reference/units/unit_authority.csv")\n'
        '_rg = _a[(_a["kind"] == "unit") & _a["number"].notna()\n'
        '         & _a["unit_cs"].str.contains(r"\\bPLUK\\b", na=False)\n'
        '         & ~_a["unit_cs"].str.contains("ZVLÁŠTNÍ", na=False)]\n'
        '_exp = {}\n'
        'for _n, _t in zip(_rg["number"].astype(int), _rg["theatre"]):\n'
        '    _exp.setdefault(_n, set()).add(_t)\n'
        '_num = df["regiment"].astype("string").str.extract(r"^(\\d+)\\.")[0].astype("Float64")\n'
        '_cs  = df["legion_army"].astype("string").str.startswith("CS Legion", na=False)\n'
        '_nb  = _num.notna() & df["regiment"].astype("string").str.contains(r"(?:stř|p)\\.pl\\.", na=False)\n'
        'def _stat(n, th, cs, nb):\n'
        '    if not (cs and nb) or pd.isna(n): return "n-a"\n'
        '    w = _exp.get(int(n));  return "n-a" if w is None else ("match" if th in w else "conflict")\n'
        'unit_status = pd.Series([_stat(n, t, c, b) for n, t, c, b in\n'
        '                         zip(_num, df["theater"], _cs, _nb)], index=df.index)\n')
    ah_helper = (
        '\n# Habsburg unit at capture → does it resolve to a real 1914 regiment (Ehnl Tabelle I)?\n'
        '_p = "reference/units/"\n'
        '_S = {"p":   set(pd.read_csv(_p+"ehnl_tabelle1_infantry.csv")["reg_no"]),\n'
        '      "zem": set(pd.read_csv(_p+"ehnl_tabelle1_landwehr.csv")["reg_no"]),\n'
        '      "hon": set(pd.read_csv(_p+"ehnl_tabelle1_honved.csv")["reg_no"])}\n'
        'def _ahm(v):\n'
        '    if pd.isna(v): return False\n'
        '    m = re.match(r"(\\d+)\\.?\\s*(.+)", str(v))\n'
        '    if not m: return False\n'
        '    n, r = int(m.group(1)), m.group(2)\n'
        '    if r.startswith(("p.pl.","pp")):          return n in _S["p"]\n'
        '    if r.startswith(("zem.p.pl.","zem.pl.")): return n in _S["zem"]\n'
        '    if r.startswith("honv.p.pl."):            return n in _S["hon"]\n'
        '    return False   # (cavalry/Feldjäger arms add a few more; infantry shown here)\n'
        'ah_matched = df["habsburg_unit_capture"].apply(_ahm)\n')
    cfg = dict(
        flags=f, order=["deserted", "theatre", "unit", "unit_verified", "unit_conflict",
                        "birthplace", "rank_reset", "ah_unit", "ah_matched"],
        highlight_label="deserters", rate_label="desertion rate",
        title="<h2>Analysis sample — legionnaires</h2>",
        intro='<p class="note">Desertion is the <b>outcome</b>, so non-deserters are the '
              "controls, not losses — the cuts below are about <b>covariate coverage</b>. "
              "Bars are cumulative; the deserter count on each confirms the signal survives.</p>",
        build_note='<p class="note">Tick the requirements an estimation sample should impose. '
                   "The count updates instantly and breaks down by theatre; each unticked box "
                   "shows what it would cost to add. The link and pandas snippet reproduce the "
                   "sample you build.</p>",
        steps=[
            ("All legionnaires", pd.Series(True, index=L.index), "the full scraped population"),
            ("Theatre resolved", f["theatre"], "theatre ≠ Unknown"),
            ("Unit label present", f["theatre"] & f["unit"], "an enrolment unit is recorded"),
            ("Unit not contradicted by Fidler", f["theatre"] & f["unit"] & ~f["unit_conflict"],
             "drops the 266 records whose regiment never existed in their theatre"),
            ("Birthplace linked (okres/járás)",
             f["theatre"] & f["unit"] & ~f["unit_conflict"] & f["birthplace"],
             "a 1910 census district, so covariates can be merged"),
            ("Rank reset resolved",
             f["theatre"] & f["unit"] & ~f["unit_conflict"] & f["birthplace"] & f["rank_reset"],
             "both ranks parsed — the headline regressor is defined"),
            ("Habsburg unit at capture recorded",
             f["theatre"] & f["unit"] & ~f["unit_conflict"] & f["birthplace"] & f["rank_reset"]
             & f["ah_unit"],
             "the pre-capture Habsburg unit string is present"),
            ("Habsburg unit matched to Tabelle I",
             f["theatre"] & f["unit"] & ~f["unit_conflict"] & f["birthplace"] & f["rank_reset"]
             & f["ah_matched"],
             "that unit resolves to a real 1914 regiment → its home district & nationality"),
        ],
        extra_note=f'<p class="note wfnote"><b>Borderline:</b> requiring the unit positively '
                   f'<b>verified</b> in Fidler (not merely un-contradicted) drops the sample to '
                   f'<b>{strict:,}</b> — but most of that loss is support/rear units that carry '
                   f'no regiment number to check, <b>not</b> wrong data.</p>',
        toggles=[
            ("Deserters only", 0, "set", "restrict to Code-D records (the outcome, not a covariate)",
             "des", 'df["deserted"]'),
            ("Theatre linked", 1, "set", "theatre resolved",
             "theatre", '(df["theater"].notna() & df["theater"].ne("Unknown"))'),
            ("Unit linked", 2, "set", "an enrolment unit recorded", "unit", 'df["regiment"].notna()'),
            ("Unit verified in Fidler", 3, "set", "regiment number confirmed to exist in its theatre",
             "verified", '(unit_status == "match")'),
            ("Exclude Fidler conflicts", 4, "clear", "drop regiment/theatre combinations Fidler rules out",
             "noconflict", '(unit_status != "conflict")'),
            ("Birthplace linked", 5, "set", "okres or járás resolved",
             "birth", '(df["birth_okres_id"].notna() | df["birth_jaras_id"].notna())'),
            ("Rank reset resolved", 6, "set", "both ranks parsed", "reset", 'df["rank_reset"].notna()'),
            ("Habsburg unit recorded (present)", 7, "set",
             "the pre-capture Habsburg unit string is present (not yet checked against Ehnl)",
             "ahunit", 'df["habsburg_unit_capture"].notna()'),
            ("Habsburg unit matched to Tabelle I", 8, "set",
             "the unit resolves to a real 1914 regiment → its Ergänzung home district & nationality",
             "ahmatch", "ah_matched"),
        ],
        snippet_parquet="data/final/persons/legionnaires_clean.parquet", helper=helper + ah_helper)
    return _waterfall("legion", L, cfg)


def _habsburg_flags(H: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Coverage flags for the Habsburg comparison-population waterfall.

    ``control`` is the defining membership: a *valid* comparison-group member is a fallen
    soldier who did **not** cross into the Legions. A legion link (``in_other_dataset``)
    disqualifies him — such a man revealed the very choice the control group is meant to
    lack — so ``control = ~linked``.
    """
    g = pd.DataFrame(index=H.index)
    linked = H["in_other_dataset"].fillna(False).astype(bool) if "in_other_dataset" in H \
        else pd.Series(False, index=H.index)
    g["control"] = ~linked
    g["theatre"] = H["theater"].notna() & (H["theater"] != "Unknown")
    g["birthplace"] = H["birth_okres_id"].notna() | H["birth_jaras_id"].notna()
    g["home"] = (H["home_okres_id"].notna() | H["home_jaras_id"].notna()) if "home_okres_id" in H \
        else pd.Series(False, index=H.index)
    g["unit"] = H["ah_unit_primary"].notna() if "ah_unit_primary" in H else pd.Series(False, index=H.index)
    g["unit_matched"] = (_habsburg_ah_matched(H) if "ah_unit_primary" in H
                         else pd.Series(False, index=H.index))
    g["cause"] = H["cause"].notna() if "cause" in H else pd.Series(False, index=H.index)
    return g


def waterfall_block_habsburg(H: pd.DataFrame) -> str:
    """Habsburg fallen-soldier waterfall — covariate coverage of the comparison population."""
    g = _habsburg_flags(H)
    n_linked = int((~g["control"]).sum())
    ah_helper_hab = (
        '\n# Habsburg unit (org + number + type) → does it exist in Ehnl Tabelle I (1914)?\n'
        '_p = "reference/units/"\n'
        '_S = {"Common army": set(pd.read_csv(_p+"ehnl_tabelle1_infantry.csv")["reg_no"]),\n'
        '      "Landwehr":    set(pd.read_csv(_p+"ehnl_tabelle1_landwehr.csv")["reg_no"]),\n'
        '      "Honvéd":      set(pd.read_csv(_p+"ehnl_tabelle1_honved.csv")["reg_no"])}\n'
        '_num = df["ah_unit_primary"].str.extract(r"(\\d+)")[0].astype("Float64")\n'
        'def _hm(org, n, typ):\n'
        '    if pd.isna(n): return False\n'
        '    if typ == "Infantry": return int(n) in _S.get(org, set())\n'
        '    return False   # (Jäger/cavalry arms add a few more; infantry shown here)\n'
        'unit_matched = pd.Series([_hm(o, n, t) for o, n, t in\n'
        '                          zip(df["ah_unit_org"], _num, df["ah_unit_type"])], index=df.index)\n')
    cfg = dict(
        flags=g, order=["control", "theatre", "birthplace", "home", "unit", "cause", "unit_matched"],
        highlight_label="valid controls", rate_label="valid-control share",
        title="<h2>Analysis sample — Habsburg comparison population</h2>",
        intro='<p class="note">The ~186k fallen Habsburg soldiers are the <b>control group</b>: '
              "men who did <b>not</b> cross into the Legions. The "
              f"<b>{n_linked:,}</b> who <i>are</i> legion-linked (they appear in the csol.cz "
              "records too) revealed exactly the choice a control is meant to lack, so they are "
              "<b>disqualified</b> as controls — the valid comparison group is the unlinked "
              "majority. The highlighted count on each bar is the <b>valid controls</b> that "
              "survive that covariate; the first toggle enforces the exclusion.</p>",
        build_note='<p class="note">Tick the covariates a comparison sample should require. '
                   "The first box drops the legion-linked (the disqualified crossovers); the "
                   "rest are coverage requirements. The count and its theatre composition update "
                   "instantly.</p>",
        steps=[
            ("All fallen soldiers", pd.Series(True, index=H.index),
             f"the full scraped population — {n_linked:,} are legion-linked and disqualified"),
            ("Theatre resolved", g["theatre"], "front ≠ Unknown"),
            ("Birthplace linked (okres/járás)", g["theatre"] & g["birthplace"],
             "a 1910 census district, so covariates can be merged"),
            ("Habsburg unit recorded", g["theatre"] & g["birthplace"] & g["unit"],
             "the Austro-Hungarian unit string is present"),
            ("Habsburg unit matched to Tabelle I",
             g["theatre"] & g["birthplace"] & g["unit"] & g["unit_matched"],
             "that unit resolves to a real 1914 regiment → its Ergänzung home district & nationality"),
            ("Cause of death known",
             g["theatre"] & g["birthplace"] & g["unit"] & g["unit_matched"] & g["cause"],
             "the competing-risk death category is defined"),
        ],
        toggles=[
            ("Valid controls only (exclude legion-linked)", 0, "set",
             "keep only soldiers who did NOT enter the Legions — a legion link disqualifies a control",
             "control", '(~df["in_other_dataset"].fillna(False))'),
            ("Theatre linked", 1, "set", "front resolved",
             "theatre", '(df["theater"].notna() & df["theater"].ne("Unknown"))'),
            ("Birthplace linked", 2, "set", "okres or járás resolved",
             "birth", '(df["birth_okres_id"].notna() | df["birth_jaras_id"].notna())'),
            ("Home place linked", 3, "set", "domicile okres or járás resolved",
             "home", '(df["home_okres_id"].notna() | df["home_jaras_id"].notna())'),
            ("Habsburg unit recorded (present)", 4, "set",
             "Austro-Hungarian unit string present",
             "unit", 'df["ah_unit_primary"].notna()'),
            ("Habsburg unit matched to Tabelle I", 6, "set",
             "unit resolves to a real 1914 regiment → home district & nationality",
             "unit_matched", "unit_matched"),
            ("Cause of death known", 5, "set", "death category defined",
             "cause", 'df["cause"].notna()'),
        ],
        snippet_parquet="data/final/persons/habsburg_clean.parquet", helper=ah_helper_hab)
    return _waterfall("habsburg", H, cfg)

def provenance_sheet() -> str:
    """Interactive bipartite map: each source (left) → the mechanisms it grounds (right).

    Positions are computed at build time and baked into the SVG, so nothing depends on
    runtime geometry (which would read as zero while the sheet is hidden). Clicking a
    node highlights its incident edges and the nodes at their far end; the highlight is
    pure CSS keyed on ``data-*`` attributes.
    """
    NW, NH, VG, PAD, TOP = 236, 34, 12, 14, 52
    GAP = 300                                  # horizontal room for the edge bundle
    src_y = {sid: TOP + i * (NH + VG) for i, (sid, *_1) in enumerate(_PV_SOURCES)}
    mech_y = {mid: TOP + i * (NH + VG) for i, (mid, *_2) in enumerate(_PV_MECH)}
    Lx, Rx = PAD, PAD + NW + GAP
    W = Rx + NW + PAD
    H = TOP + max(len(_PV_SOURCES), len(_PV_MECH)) * (NH + VG) + PAD

    def _node(nid, cat, label, note, x, y):
        fill, stroke = _PV_COLOUR.get(cat, _PV_COLOUR["data"])
        disp = label if len(label) <= 30 else label[:29] + "…"
        return (f'<g class="pvnode" data-id="{nid}" data-cat="{cat}" '
                f'transform="translate({x},{y})"><title>{_html.escape(label)} — '
                f'{_html.escape(note)}</title>'
                f'<rect width="{NW}" height="{NH}" rx="6" style="fill:{fill};stroke:{stroke}"/>'
                f'<text x="12" y="{NH/2+4:.0f}">{_html.escape(disp)}</text></g>')

    svg = [f'<svg id="pvsvg" viewBox="0 0 {W} {H}" width="{W}" height="{H}" '
           'xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">']
    svg.append('<text class="pvcol" x="%d" y="30">SOURCES</text>' % Lx)
    svg.append('<text class="pvcol" x="%d" y="30">MECHANISMS · LADDERS · MAPPINGS</text>' % Rx)
    svg.append('<g id="pvedges">')
    for s, m in _PV_EDGES:
        y1, y2 = src_y[s] + NH / 2, mech_y[m] + NH / 2
        x1, x2 = Lx + NW, Rx
        mx = (x1 + x2) / 2
        cat = next(c for i, c, *_ in _PV_SOURCES if i == s)
        svg.append(f'<path class="pvedge" data-s="{s}" data-m="{m}" data-cat="{cat}" '
                   f'd="M{x1},{y1:.0f} C{mx:.0f},{y1:.0f} {mx:.0f},{y2:.0f} {x2},{y2:.0f}"/>')
    svg.append("</g><g id='pvnodes'>")
    for sid, cat, label, note in _PV_SOURCES:
        svg.append(_node(sid, cat, label, note, Lx, src_y[sid]))
    for mid, cat, label, note in _PV_MECH:
        svg.append(_node(mid, cat, label, note, Rx, mech_y[mid]))
    svg.append("</g></svg>")

    legend = "".join(
        f'<button class="pvlg on" data-cat="{c}" onclick="pvCat(this)">'
        f'<span class="sw" style="background:{_PV_COLOUR[c][0]};border-color:{_PV_COLOUR[c][1]}">'
        f'</span>{_html.escape(lbl)}</button>' for c, lbl in _PV_CATLABEL.items())

    # per-node detail baked for the side panel (robust — notes may contain " — ")
    adj_src: dict[str, list[str]] = {sid: [] for sid, *_ in _PV_SOURCES}
    adj_mech: dict[str, list[str]] = {mid: [] for mid, *_ in _PV_MECH}
    for s, m in _PV_EDGES:
        adj_src[s].append(m)
        adj_mech[m].append(s)
    pvinfo: dict[str, dict] = {}
    for sid, cat, label, note in _PV_SOURCES:
        d = dict(label=label, cat=cat, catLabel=_PV_CATLABEL[cat],
                 note=note, role="src", links=adj_src[sid])
        bk = _PV_REF.get(sid)
        if bk and bk in _BIB_BY_KEY:                       # bake the citation for the panel
            d["ref"] = bk
            d["refApa"] = _BIB_BY_KEY[bk]["apa"]
        pvinfo[sid] = d
    for mid, cat, label, note in _PV_MECH:
        pvinfo[mid] = dict(label=label, cat=cat, catLabel=_PV_CATLABEL[cat],
                           note=note, role="mech", links=adj_mech[mid])
    pv_data = ("<script>window.PVINFO=%s;window.PVCOL=%s;</script>"
               % (json.dumps(pvinfo, ensure_ascii=False), json.dumps(_PV_COLOUR)))
    panel_empty = ('<aside class="pvpanel empty" id="pvpanel"><div class="pbody">'
                   '<p class="pnote">Click any box to open its detail here — what it is, the '
                   'kind of source, and every link it makes.</p></div></aside>')

    return (
        ix_head("What each mechanism rests on", ix=True, hover=True)
        + '<p class="note">The pipeline’s ladders, mappings and validations are only as good as '
        "the sources under them. Each line runs from a <b>source</b> (left) to a <b>mechanism</b> "
        "it grounds (right). <b>Click</b> any box to isolate its links <i>and open a detail panel "
        "on the right</i> — a source lists everything it feeds; a mechanism lists everything it "
        "depends on, each entry clickable. Colour is the kind of source. <b>Esc</b> or click empty "
        "space clears.</p>"
        f'<div class="pvbar">{legend}'
        '<span class="pvhint" id="pvhint">Click a box to trace its provenance.</span></div>'
        f'{pv_data}<div class="pvlayout"><div class="pvwrap">{"".join(svg)}</div>{panel_empty}</div>'
        "<p class='note'>Sources are catalogued in <a href='#sources'>Data sources</a>; the "
        "validation that added Fidler as a check is on the <a href='#validation'>External "
        "validation</a> sheet.</p>")
