# ── the evidence behind a tier: what it matched, and where ──────────────────────
# A tier is a claim about a matching rule. The counts say how loud the claim is; only the
# strings it actually accepted say whether it is true. `fuzzy` and `muni` are the tiers a
# sceptical reader distrusts, so those are exactly the ones worth printing verbatim.
_EX_N = 9                                   # example rows kept per tier and frame

# Which recorded field each tier reads, and which resolved name it writes.
_TIER_SRC = {"cz:settlement": "birth_municipality", "cz:muni": "birth_municipality",
             "sk:settlement": "birth_municipality"}
_TIER_OUT = {"cz": "birth_okres_cs", "sk": "birth_jaras_sk"}


def _place_frame(fname: str) -> dict:
    """Everything the figure needs about one frame, recomputed from ``data/final``.

    Returns a dict with ``n`` (records), ``t`` (per-tier counts), ``none`` (placed by
    neither frame), ``geo`` (per tier, ``{district uid: records}`` for the map) and ``ex``
    (per tier, the commonest ``recorded string → resolved district`` pairs).

    District uids are namespaced — ``cz301072`` / ``huM2801`` — because the two frames
    number their units independently and the map draws both.
    """
    cols = ["birth_okres_match", "birth_jaras_match", "birth_okres_id", "birth_jaras_id",
            "birth_okres", "birth_municipality", "birth_okres_cs", "birth_jaras_sk",
            "birth_megye_sk", "birth_court_id",
            "theater", "deserted", "rank_reset", "legion_noncombat"]
    have = [c for c in cols if c in pq.ParquetFile(FIN / "persons" / fname).schema.names]
    df = pd.read_parquet(FIN / "persons" / fname, columns=have)

    out: dict = {"n": int(len(df)), "t": {}, "geo": {}, "ex": {}}
    for pre, mcol, idcol, uidp in (("cz", "birth_okres_match", "birth_okres_id", "cz"),
                                   ("sk", "birth_jaras_match", "birth_jaras_id", "hu")):
        if mcol not in df:
            continue
        for tier, n in df[mcol].value_counts(dropna=True).items():
            key = f"{pre}:{tier}"
            sub = df[df[mcol] == tier]
            out["t"][key] = int(n)
            if idcol in sub:
                out["geo"][key] = {f"{uidp}{k}": int(v) for k, v in
                                   sub[idcol].dropna().value_counts().items()}
            src = _TIER_SRC.get(key, "birth_okres")
            res = "birth_megye_sk" if tier == "megye" else _TIER_OUT[pre]
            if src in sub and res in sub:
                pairs = (pd.DataFrame({"a": sub[src], "b": sub[res]}).dropna()
                         .value_counts().head(_EX_N))
                out["ex"][key] = [[str(a), str(b), int(v)] for (a, b), v in pairs.items()]

    # the coordinate layer is not a placing tier — it runs *over* whatever the name passes
    # resolved, so it gets the map but no step in the cascade
    if "birth_court_id" in df and "birth_okres_id" in df:
        c = df.loc[df["birth_court_id"].notna(), "birth_okres_id"].dropna()
        out["geo"]["cz:coord"] = {f"cz{k}": int(v) for k, v in c.value_counts().items()}
        out["t"]["cz:coord"] = int(df["birth_court_id"].notna().sum())

    # court-district counts, for the finer map mode. This is a genuinely different measurement,
    # not the same one drawn smaller: a court is only known where the birth village is geocoded,
    # so its coverage is the coordinate layer's, not the name layer's.
    if "birth_court_id" in df:
        out["court"] = {f"cc{k}": int(v) for k, v in
                        df["birth_court_id"].dropna().value_counts().items()}
        out["court_n"] = int(df["birth_court_id"].notna().sum())
        # Why the two layers do not add up — the question the map otherwise invites and
        # never answers. A reader who totals the courts inside a district and compares it to
        # the district is doing the obvious thing, and the numbers are honest but not
        # comparable: different denominators, plus a residual disagreement.
        if "birth_okres_id" in df:
            has_o, has_c = df["birth_okres_id"].notna(), df["birth_court_id"].notna()
            both = has_o & has_c
            parent = (df["birth_court_id"] // 1000).astype("Int64")
            out["cvo"] = {"okres_n": int(has_o.sum()),
                          "court_n": int(has_c.sum()),
                          "okres_only": int((has_o & ~has_c).sum()),
                          "both": int(both.sum()),
                          "elsewhere": int((both & (parent != df["birth_okres_id"])).sum())}

    out["okres"] = _okres_outcomes(df)

    placed = sum(v for k, v in out["t"].items() if k != "cz:coord")
    out["placed"], out["none"] = placed, int(len(df)) - placed
    # two pseudo-tiers so the figure can print them the same way as the real ones: what the
    # Czech lane handed on (= what the Slovak lane actually runs on) and the final residual
    out["t"]["_handoff"] = int(len(df)) - sum(
        v for k, v in out["t"].items() if k.startswith("cz:") and k != "cz:coord")
    out["t"]["_none"] = out["none"]
    return out


# Theatres worth naming in a per-district mix; everything else folds into "other".
_PF_THEATRES = ("Russia", "Italy", "France")


def _desert_rate(frame: dict) -> float:
    """National desertion rate over the districts the map can show — the panel's benchmark."""
    tot = sum(v["n"] for v in frame.get("okres", {}).values())
    des = sum(v.get("d", 0) for v in frame.get("okres", {}).values())
    return des / tot if tot else 0.0


def _okres_outcomes(df: pd.DataFrame) -> dict:
    """Per birth okres: how many were born there and what became of them.

    The map exists to attach a district to a man; this is the other direction — click a
    district and see the men. Desertion is the thesis's outcome, so it leads; it is suppressed
    below 30 births because a rate on 11 records is noise wearing a percentage sign.

    Runs over **both** frames. The map draws Czech okresy and Upper-Hungary járás on one
    plane and shades both, so a panel that only knew the Czech side told every reader who
    clicked a Slovak district that nobody was born there — while the district sat shaded in
    front of them. Ranks and the national benchmark are therefore computed across the pooled
    set: a "#1 of the districts" that silently meant "of the Czech ones" would be worse than
    no rank at all.
    """
    out: dict[str, dict] = {}
    parts = [("birth_okres_id", "cz"), ("birth_jaras_id", "hu")]
    frames = [(c, p) for c, p in parts if c in df.columns]
    if not frames:
        return {}

    counts: dict[str, int] = {}
    rows: dict[str, dict] = {}
    for id_col, tag in frames:
        g = df.dropna(subset=[id_col])
        if not len(g):
            continue
        # the Czech okres id is numeric, the járás id is a GISta string ("M3210") — key on
        # whatever the frame actually uses, and let the uid prefix keep the two apart
        key = g[id_col].astype(int) if tag == "cz" else g[id_col].astype(str)
        n_by = key.value_counts()
        des = (g.groupby(key)["deserted"].agg(["size", "sum"])
               if "deserted" in g else None)
        rr = rrn = None
        if "rank_reset" in g:
            combat = ~g["legion_noncombat"].fillna(False).astype(bool) \
                if "legion_noncombat" in g else pd.Series(True, index=g.index)
            grp = g[combat].groupby(key[combat])["rank_reset"]
            rr, rrn = grp.mean(), grp.count()
        th = None
        if "theater" in g:
            th = (g.assign(_t=g["theater"].where(g["theater"].isin(_PF_THEATRES), "Other"))
                  .groupby([key, "_t"]).size().unstack(fill_value=0))
        for oid, n in n_by.items():
            row: dict = {"n": int(n)}
            if des is not None and oid in des.index:
                row["d"] = int(des.loc[oid, "sum"])
            if rr is not None and oid in rr.index and pd.notna(rr[oid]):
                # the mean AND its denominator: pooling a city into its ring has to re-weight
                # the two means, and a mean without its n cannot be pooled at all
                row["rr"] = round(float(rr[oid]), 2)
                row["rrn"] = int(rrn.get(oid, 0))
            if th is not None and oid in th.index:
                row["th"] = {c: int(v) for c, v in th.loc[oid].items() if v}
            uid = f"{tag}{oid}"
            rows[uid] = row
            counts[uid] = int(n)

    # one ranking over every district the map draws, both frames together
    order = sorted(counts.values(), reverse=True)
    for uid, row in rows.items():
        row["rank"] = order.index(counts[uid]) + 1
        out[uid] = row
    return out


# ── the map: one projection, both frames ────────────────────────────────────────
# The Czech okres polygons (MPIDR, EPSG:3035) and the Upper-Hungary járás polygons (GISta
# Hungarorum, EPSG:3857) are drawn on ONE plane: the Hungarian coordinates are inverted back
# to lon/lat and re-projected through the same LAEA forward as the Czech side. Validated
# against `okres_centroids_1910.csv` (median 3.1 km) and against the known coordinates of
# Bratislava, Košice, Prešov and Žilina (1–8 km) — i.e. the two frames really do line up.
_MERC_R = 6378137.0
_MAP_W = 940.0                              # SVG user units across the full extent


def _stitch(edges: set[tuple]) -> str:
    """Chain a set of undirected segments into as few polylines as possible.

    Emitting a district boundary as 20,000 separate ``M…L…`` moves is both enormous and
    ugly: every segment gets its own line caps, so a stroked boundary reads as a dotted
    scribble at any width above a hairline. Chained, the same boundary is a few hundred
    polylines that join cleanly.

    Walks greedily and starts from odd-degree vertices first, so an open chain is finished
    from its end rather than cut in half by a start in the middle. Closed rings have no odd
    vertex and are picked up by the second pass.
    """
    adj: dict[tuple, list[tuple]] = {}
    for a, b in edges:
        adj.setdefault(a, []).append(b)
        adj.setdefault(b, []).append(a)
    left = set(edges)
    out: list[str] = []

    def walk(start: tuple) -> list[tuple]:
        chain, cur = [start], start
        while True:
            nxt = None
            for cand in adj[cur]:
                key = (cur, cand) if (cur, cand) in left else (cand, cur)
                if key in left:
                    left.discard(key)
                    nxt = cand
                    break
            if nxt is None:
                return chain
            chain.append(nxt)
            cur = nxt

    for odd_first in (True, False):
        for node in adj:
            if odd_first and len(adj[node]) % 2 == 0:
                continue
            while any(((node, c) in left or (c, node) in left) for c in adj[node]):
                ch = walk(node)
                if len(ch) > 1:
                    out.append("M" + "L".join(f"{x:g},{y:g}" for x, y in ch))
    return "".join(out)


def _district_map() -> dict:
    """District polygons for both frames as SVG paths, with the two border classes separated.

    The **drawing** unit is the finest one the source has — a Czech *soudní okres* (court
    district) or an Upper-Hungary járás — while the **data** unit is the political okres a
    court belongs to. Drawing courts and colouring them by their parent means every internal
    court line reads as a district boundary unless the two are told apart, so they are:

    adjacent MPIDR polygons share their boundary **vertex for vertex** (verified: of 7,622
    distinct Czech-lands edges every interior one is used by exactly two polygons and none by
    more than two — a clean planar partition), so an edge whose two owners sit in the same
    okres is a court line and every other edge is an okres boundary. No geometry library, no
    dissolve, and the classification is exact rather than approximate.

    Returns ``{"w", "h", "paths": {uid: d}, "parent": {uid: data uid}, "names", "lines":
    {"court": d, "okres": d}}``; uids are ``cc<court_id>`` / ``hu<unit_id>`` for the drawing
    units and ``cz<okres_id>`` / ``hu<unit_id>`` for the data units.
    """
    from utils.parsing.districts import read_dbf
    from utils.parsing.records_geo import build_twin_pairs
    from utils.parsing.spatial import laea_forward, read_polygons

    # the stem carries dots ("…_v.1.0"), so name the files rather than swapping a suffix
    mp = ROOT / "reference" / "places" / "mpidr"
    mp_dbf = mp / "Austro_Hungarian_Empire_1910_v.1.0.dbf"
    mp_shp = mp / "Austro_Hungarian_Empire_1910_v.1.0.shp"
    rings: dict[str, list[np.ndarray]] = {}
    parent: dict[str, str] = {}

    dcz = pd.read_parquet(FIN / "geo" / "districts_1910.parquet")
    okres_id = dcz["okres_code"].map(
        lambda c: "cz" + str(int(c.split("-")[0]) * 1000 + int(c.split("-")[1])))
    names: dict[str, str] = dict(zip(okres_id, dcz["okres_cs"]))
    court_name = dict(zip(dcz["court_id"].astype(str), dcz["gerichtsbezirk_cs"]))
    twins = build_twin_pairs(dcz)              # {okres_id → (rural_id, city_id, name keys)}
    for rec, poly in zip(read_dbf(mp_dbf), read_polygons(mp_shp)):
        if rec.get("LAND") not in {"BOEHMEN", "MAEHREN", "SCHLESIEN"} or not poly:
            continue
        uid = f"cc{rec['ID_1']}"
        rings.setdefault(uid, []).extend(poly)
        parent[uid] = f"cz{int(rec['REGION']) * 1000 + int(rec['DISTRICT'])}"
        names[uid] = court_name.get(str(rec["ID_1"]), rec.get("NAME") or "")

    hu_dir = ROOT / "data" / "raw" / "census_hu" / "shp"
    hu = pd.read_parquet(FIN / "geo" / "districts_hu_1910.parquet")
    # Twenty-six Upper-Hungary names belong to TWO units — the járás and the chartered town
    # at its centre — and the backbone stores both under the same ``name_sk``. Unlabelled,
    # the map showed two adjacent polygons both reading "Trnava" with different numbers, and
    # no way to tell which was which. The Czech backbone solves this in the source ("Brno
    # (město)"); the Hungarian one carries it in ``unit_type`` instead, so the label is
    # assembled here. rtv. = rendezett tanácsú város, tjv. = törvényhatósági jogú város.
    hu_type = dict(zip(hu["unit_id"], hu["unit_type"]))
    names.update({f"hu{u}": (s if isinstance(s, str) else h)
                  + ("" if t == "járás" else " (mesto)")
                  for u, s, h, t in zip(hu["unit_id"], hu["name_sk"], hu["name_hu"],
                                        hu["unit_type"])})
    wanted = set(hu["unit_id"])
    hu_dbf = read_dbf(hu_dir / "MO_JarasVaros.dbf", encodings=("utf-8", "cp1250"))
    for rec, poly in zip(hu_dbf, read_polygons(hu_dir / "MO_JarasVaros.shp")):
        if rec.get("IDJaras") not in wanted or not poly:
            continue
        uid = f"hu{rec['IDJaras']}"
        parent[uid] = uid                      # a járás has no sub-unit; it is its own data unit
        for ring in poly:
            lon = ring[:, 0] / _MERC_R * 180 / math.pi
            lat = (2 * np.arctan(np.exp(ring[:, 1] / _MERC_R)) - math.pi / 2) * 180 / math.pi
            x, y = laea_forward(lon, lat)
            rings.setdefault(uid, []).append(np.column_stack([x, y]))

    allpts = np.vstack([r for v in rings.values() for r in v])
    x0, y0 = allpts.min(0)
    x1, y1 = allpts.max(0)
    scale = _MAP_W / (x1 - x0)

    # Snap to an integer grid rather than Douglas-Peucker: DP thins each ring independently and
    # would keep different vertices on the two sides of a shared boundary, destroying exactly
    # the vertex identity the classification depends on. Identical rounding cannot — both sides
    # of a shared edge start from the same numbers and land on the same grid point. At this
    # scale one unit is about a kilometre, which is finer than the source is generalised anyway.
    paths: dict[str, str] = {}
    owners: dict[tuple, set[str]] = {}         # edge → the data units touching it
    uses: dict[tuple, int] = {}                # edge → how many polygons use it
    for uid, rs in rings.items():
        d = []
        for ring in rs:
            scr = np.column_stack([(ring[:, 0] - x0) * scale,
                                   (y1 - ring[:, 1]) * scale]).round(0)
            keep = np.ones(len(scr), bool)
            keep[1:] = np.abs(np.diff(scr, axis=0)).sum(1) > 0
            scr = scr[keep]
            if len(scr) < 4:
                continue
            d.append("M" + "L".join(f"{a:g},{b:g}" for a, b in scr) + "Z")
            for a, b in zip(scr[:-1], scr[1:]):
                key = tuple(sorted([(a[0], a[1]), (b[0], b[1])]))
                owners.setdefault(key, set()).add(parent[uid])
                uses[key] = uses.get(key, 0) + 1
        if d:
            paths[uid] = "".join(d)

    # Every edge falls into exactly one of three classes, and each is drawn as its own layer
    # so the map can show precisely the boundaries of whatever unit is currently the data
    # unit. Over-printing the court lines in pale grey (the old approach) put light strokes
    # on top of dark fills, which read as noise rather than as a weaker class of line.
    #
    #   court  — both sides sit in the same political okres: a sub-division, never a boundary
    #   twin   — the two sides are the city and ring of a pooled pair. A real okres boundary,
    #            and NOT a boundary of the census unit, because the court-level census cannot
    #            separate nine of the ten pairs (D-18). Whether it is drawn is the reader's
    #            call, which is the whole point of separating it out.
    #   okres  — everything else, including an edge used once (the outer frontier)
    pool = {f"cz{m}": f"cz{rural}" for m, (rural, _city, _k) in twins.items()}
    cls: dict[str, set[tuple]] = {"court": set(), "twin": set(), "okres": set()}
    for edge, who in owners.items():
        if uses[edge] > 1 and len(who) == 1:
            k = "court"
        elif uses[edge] > 1 and len({pool.get(w, w) for w in who}) == 1:
            k = "twin"
        else:
            k = "okres"
        cls[k].add(edge)

    # One outline per data unit, for hover and selection. Stroking the member polygons
    # instead — which is what the map used to do — outlines every court division inside the
    # district too, so "this okres" was drawn as a bundle of smaller shapes rather than as
    # the one shape it is. A unit's outline is simply every non-court edge it owns.
    sel_edges: dict[str, set[tuple]] = {}
    for edge, who in owners.items():
        if edge in cls["court"]:
            continue
        for w in who:
            sel_edges.setdefault(w, set()).add(edge)

    pool_members = {p: sorted(m for m in pool if pool[m] == p) for p in set(pool.values())}
    # A pooled pair's outline is the union of its members' minus the border between them —
    # the one edge that stops being a boundary the moment the two are treated as one unit.
    sel_pool = {head: _stitch(set().union(*(sel_edges.get(m, set()) for m in mem)) - cls["twin"])
                for head, mem in pool_members.items()}

    pool_name = {f"cz{rural}": f"{names.get(f'cz{rural}', '')} + město"
                 for _m, (rural, _c, _k) in twins.items()}
    return {"w": _MAP_W, "h": round((y1 - y0) * scale, 1), "paths": paths, "parent": parent,
            "lines": {k: _stitch(v) for k, v in cls.items()},
            "sel": {u: _stitch(e) for u, e in sel_edges.items()}, "sel_pool": sel_pool,
            "pool": pool, "pool_name": pool_name, "pool_members": pool_members,
            "hu_type": {f"hu{u}": t for u, t in hu_type.items()},
            "names": {k: v for k, v in names.items()
                      if k in paths or k in set(parent.values())}}


def place_flow() -> str:
    """The place-matching cascade: a funnel, a filter and a map, all off ``data/final``.

    Three things a reader needs that a static waterfall cannot give. **The funnel** carries
    the residual down the left of each lane as a tapering ribbon, so the fact that one tier
    does almost all the work is visible before a single number is read. **The filter** lets
    the tiers be ticked off — this sheet has always claimed an analysis can drop the weak
    ones and see what moves, and this is where that becomes an action rather than a sentence;
    the readout hands back the exact pandas mask. **The map** shows where each tier's matches
    land, because a rule resting on a bare unique name is only trustworthy if what it matched
    is spread like a population rather than piled on one district.

    Every count, ribbon width and example string is recomputed at build time, so the picture
    cannot drift from the data it describes.
    """
    F = {"l": _place_frame("legionnaires_clean.parquet"),
         "h": _place_frame("habsburg_clean.parquet")}
    geom = _district_map()

    BW, BH, VG, TOP = 258, 54, 14, 104
    LX = [64, 452]                            # box left edge; the ribbon runs to its left
    RW, SPD = 38, 46                          # max ribbon width · ribbon offset left of box
    W = LX[1] + BW + 96
    H = TOP + (len(_CZ_STAGES) + 1) * (BH + VG) + 34

    def fmt(key: str, fr: str) -> str:
        n = F[fr]["t"].get(key, 0)
        return f"{n:,} · {_pct(n, F[fr]['n'])}" if n else "—"

    def entry(fr: str, lane: int) -> int:
        """Records the lane actually runs on: everything, then the Czech lane's residual."""
        return F[fr]["n"] if lane == 0 else F[fr]["t"]["_handoff"]

    # ── the ribbon: what is still unplaced, as a staircase area ─────────────────────
    # Left edge straight, right edge stepping inward — an area chart stood on end. The step
    # at a stage IS what that stage placed, so `okres` collapsing the ribbon by two thirds
    # is the finding rather than a caption about it.
    def ribbon(fr: str, lane: int) -> str:
        stages = _CZ_STAGES if lane == 0 else _SK_STAGES
        pre = "cz" if lane == 0 else "sk"
        total = max(F[fr]["n"], 1)
        left = LX[lane] - SPD

        def wide(v: int) -> float:
            return max(0.7, RW * v / total)

        run = entry(fr, lane)
        d = [f"M{left},{TOP - VG}", f"L{left + wide(run):.1f},{TOP - VG}"]
        for i, stage in enumerate(stages):
            tier = stage[1]
            if tier == "coord":                                # a layer over the lane, not a step
                continue
            y = TOP + i * (BH + VG) + BH / 2
            d.append(f"L{left + wide(run):.1f},{y:.0f}")
            run -= F[fr]["t"].get(f"{pre}:{tier}", 0)
            d.append(f"L{left + wide(run):.1f},{y:.0f}")
        y_end = TOP + len(stages) * (BH + VG) - VG / 2
        d.append(f"L{left + wide(run):.1f},{y_end:.0f}")
        d.append(f"L{left},{y_end:.0f}Z")
        return "".join(d)

    parts: list[str] = [
        f'<svg id="pfsvg" viewBox="0 0 {W} {H}" width="{W}" height="{H}" '
        'xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><defs>'
        '<marker id="pfar" viewBox="0 0 8 8" refX="7" refY="4" markerWidth="7" markerHeight="7" '
        'orient="auto"><path d="M0,0 L8,4 L0,8z" fill="#b4bcc2"/></marker></defs>']
    info: dict[str, dict] = {}
    bars: dict[str, dict[str, float]] = {"l": {}, "h": {}}

    lanes = [(_CZ_STAGES, LX[0], "CZECH LANDS → political okres", "runs on every birth record"),
             (_SK_STAGES, LX[1], "UPPER HUNGARY → járás",
              "runs only on what the Czech lane left unplaced")]
    for lane, (stages, x, head, sub) in enumerate(lanes):
        pre = "cz" if lane == 0 else "sk"
        parts.append(f'<path class="pfrib" data-lane="{lane}" d="{ribbon("l", lane)}"/>')
        parts.append(f'<text class="pfhead" x="{x}" y="46">{head}</text>')
        parts.append(f'<text class="pfsub" x="{x}" y="64">{sub}</text>')
        tail = " in" if lane == 0 else " in — the Czech lane's residual"
        parts.append(
            f'<text class="pfribcap" x="{x - SPD}" y="{TOP - VG - 9}" data-lane="{lane}" '
            f'data-l="{entry("l", lane):,}{tail}" data-h="{entry("h", lane):,}{tail}">'
            f'{entry("l", lane):,}{tail}</text>')

        for i, (key, tier, label, slab, what, refus, sym) in enumerate(stages):
            y = TOP + i * (BH + VG)
            fill, stroke = _TIER_COLOUR[tier]
            tkey = f"{pre}:{tier}"
            step = tier != "coord"
            for fr in ("l", "h"):
                mx = max((F[fr]["t"].get(f"{pre}:{t}", 0) for _k, t, *_r in stages), default=1)
                bars[fr][key] = round(F[fr]["t"].get(tkey, 0) / max(mx, 1), 4)
            legion, hab = fmt(tkey, "l"), fmt(tkey, "h")
            if i:
                parts.append(f'<path class="pfarrow" d="M{x + BW / 2:.0f},{y - VG} '
                             f'L{x + BW / 2:.0f},{y - 3}" marker-end="url(#pfar)"/>')
            tick = ""
            if step:
                tick = ('<g class="pfkeepbox" onclick="pfKeep(event,this)">'
                        f'<rect x="10" y="{BH / 2 - 8:.0f}" width="16" height="16" rx="4"/>'
                        f'<path class="pftick" d="M14,{BH / 2:.0f} l3,3.4 l6.5,-7.6"/>'
                        "<title>Tick to keep this tier in the sample below</title></g>")
            tx, keepattr = (34, ' data-keep="1"') if step else (12, "")
            parts.append(
                f'<g class="pfstage{"" if step else " layer"}" data-id="{key}" '
                f'data-tier="{tier}" data-key="{tkey}"{keepattr} '
                f'transform="translate({x},{y})" onclick="pfPick(this)">'
                f'<rect class="pfbox" width="{BW}" height="{BH}" rx="6" '
                f'style="fill:{fill};stroke:{stroke}"/>' + tick +
                f'<text class="pflab" x="{tx}" y="21">{_html.escape(label)}</text>'
                f'<text class="pfstat" x="{tx}" y="37" data-l="{_html.escape(legion)}" '
                f'data-h="{_html.escape(hab)}">{_html.escape(legion)}</text>'
                f'<text class="pftier" x="{BW - 12}" y="21">{tier}</text>'
                f'<text class="pfslab" x="{BW - 12}" y="37">{_html.escape(slab)}</text>'
                f'<rect class="pfbart" x="{tx}" y="{BH - 12}" width="{BW - tx - 12}" height="4" '
                'rx="2"/>'
                f'<rect class="pfbarv" data-k="{key}" x="{tx}" y="{BH - 12}" '
                f'width="{(BW - tx - 12) * bars["l"][key]:.1f}" height="4" rx="2" '
                f'style="fill:{stroke}"><title>this tier against the largest in its lane</title>'
                "</rect></g>")
            if refus:
                cx, cy = x + BW + 26, y + BH / 2
                parts.append(
                    f'<g class="pfveto"><path class="pfvl" d="M{x + BW},{cy} L{cx - 11},{cy}"/>'
                    f'<circle cx="{cx}" cy="{cy}" r="11"/>'
                    f'<text x="{cx}" y="{cy + 4}">⊘</text>'
                    f'<title>{len(refus)} refusal rule(s) — click the stage</title></g>')
            # label/sub are plain text and go through innerHTML in the panel — escape them;
            # what/refus are authored HTML above and are passed through as written
            info[key] = dict(label=_html.escape(label), tier=tier, sub=_html.escape(slab),
                             what=what, refus=refus, sym=sym, tkey=tkey if step else "cz:coord",
                             lane="Czech lands" if lane == 0 else "Upper Hungary")

        y = TOP + len(stages) * (BH + VG)
        f2, s2 = _TIER_COLOUR["none"]
        if lane == 0:
            # the hand-off: the second lane does not run on the dataset, it runs on this
            parts.append(
                f'<g class="pfstage term" data-id="handoff" data-tier="none" data-key="_handoff" '
                f'transform="translate({x},{y})" onclick="pfPick(this)">'
                f'<rect class="pfbox" width="{BW}" height="{BH}" rx="6" style="fill:{f2};'
                f'stroke:{s2};stroke-dasharray:4 3"/>'
                '<text class="pflab" x="12" y="21">Handed to the second frame</text>'
                f'<text class="pfstat" x="12" y="37" data-l="{fmt("_handoff", "l")}" '
                f'data-h="{fmt("_handoff", "h")}">{fmt("_handoff", "l")}</text>'
                f'<text class="pfslab hand" x="{BW - 12}" y="37">= what the second lane runs on'
                "</text></g>")
            info["handoff"] = dict(
                label="Handed to the second frame", tier="none", sub="no Czech-lands candidate",
                what="What the Czech lane cannot corroborate is not a failure — it is the input "
                     "to the Upper-Hungary lane, which is why the ribbon starts again over there "
                     "at exactly this width. The two frames are <b>exclusive</b>: notebook 02 §4 "
                     "asserts that no record is placed in both.",
                refus=[], sym="", tkey="", lane="between the frames")
            # No routed connector: a line from the bottom of one lane to the top of the next
            # has to loop around the whole figure and reads as a box drawn round lane two.
            # The link is carried by the number instead — this box and the second lane's
            # inlet caption are the same count, and the caption says so.
        else:
            parts.append(
                f'<g class="pfstage term" data-id="none" data-tier="none" data-key="_none" '
                f'transform="translate({x},{y})" onclick="pfPick(this)">'
                f'<rect class="pfbox" width="{BW}" height="{BH}" rx="6" style="fill:{f2};'
                f'stroke:{s2};stroke-dasharray:4 3"/>'
                '<text class="pflab" x="12" y="21">Left unplaced, on purpose</text>'
                f'<text class="pfstat" x="12" y="37" data-l="{fmt("_none", "l")}" '
                f'data-h="{fmt("_none", "h")}">{fmt("_none", "l")}</text>'
                f'<text class="pfslab" x="{BW - 12}" y="37">no honest candidate</text></g>')
            info["none"] = dict(
                label="Left unplaced, on purpose", tier="none", sub="no honest candidate",
                what="Every guard above prefers &lt;NA&gt; to a plausible-looking guess. The "
                     "residual is mostly Subcarpathian Rus, region labels rather than places, and "
                     "names that collide across the two frames.",
                refus=["&lt;NA&gt; is a decision, not a gap — it is what refusal looks like "
                       "in the data."],
                sym="", tkey="", lane="both")
    parts.append("</svg>")

    # ── the map: static geometry, fills painted by whatever is selected ─────────────
    # The polygons carry the fill and nothing else; the three line layers above them carry
    # every border. Which layers are visible is what the two controls actually change, so
    # the lines on the map are always exactly the boundaries of the current data unit.
    mp = "".join(f'<path class="pfd" data-u="{u}" data-p="{geom["parent"][u]}" d="{d}" '
                 'onclick="pfDistrict(this)"><title></title></path>'
                 for u, d in geom["paths"].items())
    mapsvg = (f'<svg id="pfmap" viewBox="0 0 {geom["w"]:.0f} {geom["h"]:.0f}" '
              f'xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">{mp}'
              f'<path id="pfcourtlines" d="{geom["lines"]["court"]}"/>'
              f'<path id="pftwinlines" d="{geom["lines"]["twin"]}"/>'
              f'<path id="pfokreslines" d="{geom["lines"]["okres"]}"/>'
              '<path id="pfhoverline"/><path id="pfselline"/></svg>')
    units = ('<span class="pfunitlab">Draw at</span>'
             '<button class="pfunit on" data-u="okres" onclick="pfUnit(this)">political okres'
             "</button>"
             '<button class="pfunit" data-u="court" onclick="pfUnit(this)">soudní okres</button>'
             '<span class="pfunitlab pfsep">City twins</span>'
             '<button class="pfunit on" data-pool="0" onclick="pfPool(this)">separate</button>'
             '<button class="pfunit" data-pool="1" onclick="pfPool(this)">pooled</button>')

    legend = "".join(
        f'<span class="pflg"><span class="sw" style="background:{_TIER_COLOUR[t][0]};'
        f'border-color:{_TIER_COLOUR[t][1]}"></span>{t} <i>{c}</i></span>'
        for t, c in _TIER_CONF)
    chips = ('<button class="wfchip on" data-m="l" onclick="pfMode(this)">Legionnaires</button>'
             '<button class="wfchip" data-m="h" onclick="pfMode(this)">Habsburg fallen</button>')
    panel = ('<aside class="pfpanel empty" id="pfpanel"><p class="pnote">Click any stage for what '
             "it does, what it refuses, which function owns it — and the strings it actually "
             "matched.</p></aside>")

    payload = {"n": {k: v["n"] for k, v in F.items()},
               "t": {k: v["t"] for k, v in F.items()},
               "geo": {k: v["geo"] for k, v in F.items()},
               "ex": {k: v["ex"] for k, v in F.items()},
               "court": {k: v.get("court", {}) for k, v in F.items()},
               "court_n": {k: v.get("court_n", 0) for k, v in F.items()},
               "cvo": {k: v.get("cvo", {}) for k, v in F.items()},
               "okres": {k: v.get("okres", {}) for k, v in F.items()},
               "bars": bars,
               "rib": {fr: {str(ln): ribbon(fr, ln) for ln in (0, 1)} for fr in ("l", "h")},
               "names": geom["names"], "info": info,
               "pool": geom["pool"], "poolname": geom["pool_name"],
               "poolmem": geom["pool_members"], "hutype": geom["hu_type"],
               "sel": geom["sel"], "selpool": geom["sel_pool"],
               "rate": {fr: round(_desert_rate(F[fr]), 4) for fr in ("l", "h")}}

    return (
        ix_head("How a birthplace becomes a district", ix=True, hover=True)
        + '<p class="note">Two legal frames, two lanes, one rule down both: <b>a pass accepts only '
        "what it can corroborate and refuses the rest to the next pass</b>. The ribbon down each "
        "lane is what is <i>still unplaced</i> — every step in it is a tier doing its work, and "
        "the bar inside a box is that tier against the largest in its lane. Colour is the "
        "confidence the match will carry in the data; ⊘ marks a stage with explicit refusal "
        "rules. <b>Click</b> a stage for the strings it actually matched and the map of where "
        "they landed; <b>untick</b> a tier to drop it from the sample below.</p>"
        f'<div class="pfbar">{chips}<span class="pflgs">{legend}</span></div>'
        f'<script>window.PF={json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False)};</script>'
        f'<div class="pflayout"><div class="pfwrap">{"".join(parts)}</div>{panel}</div>'
        '<div class="pfkeep" id="pfkeep"><div class="pfkeepn" id="pfkeepn"></div>'
        '<div class="pfkeepact"><button class="wfbtn sm" onclick="pfAll(1)">All tiers</button>'
        '<button class="wfbtn sm" onclick="pfAll(0)">None</button>'
        '<button class="wfbtn sm" onclick="pfCopyMask(this)">Copy the mask</button></div>'
        '<pre class="pfmask"><code id="pfmaskc"></code></pre></div>'
        + ix_head("Where the matches land", level=3, ix=True, hover=True)
        + '<p class="note">The same cascade, on the ground: Czech <i>okresy</i> from the MPIDR '
        "1910 boundaries and Upper-Hungary <i>járás</i> from GISta Hungarorum, the second "
        "re-projected onto the first so the two frames sit on one plane. Shading is records per "
        "district for the tiers ticked above; click a stage to isolate that tier, or click a "
        "district to see who was born there. The strong tiers should reproduce the population, "
        "so read those as a sanity check — it is <code>fuzzy</code>, <code>settlement</code> and "
        "<code>muni</code> that are worth looking at, where a tier piled onto one district would "
        "mean a rule firing on a name rather than on a place.</p>"
        '<p class="note">The mesh is finer than the measurement: the polygons are <b>court '
        "districts</b> (<i>soudní okresy</i>), the unit the boundary file draws, while the "
        "matching resolves to the <b>political okres</b> above them. Every edge is classified "
        "exactly — adjacent polygons share their border vertex for vertex — so <b>drawn at "
        "political okres only district boundaries are drawn at all</b>, and the court "
        "sub-divisions appear as pale hairlines only when you ask for them. Switch the unit "
        "to shade the courts themselves, from <code>birth_court_id</code>; that layer is "
        "<i>coordinate</i>-derived, so it covers fewer records and is a cross-check rather "
        "than a finer version of the same count.</p>"
        '<p class="note"><b>City twins.</b> Ten Czech seats name both a <i>Statutarstadt</i> '
        "and the rural okres around it — Brno and Brno&nbsp;(město), Olomouc and Olomouc "
        "(město). They are two okresy and the records are split between them, but the "
        "court-level census cannot separate nine of the ten, so the analytical unit is the "
        "<b>pooled</b> pair (<code>census_okres_id</code>, 148 units rather than 158; "
        '<a href="#decisions">Decisions</a> D-18). Switch <i>City twins</i> to see the map '
        "the census can actually support: the city border comes off and the two shares merge "
        "into one. Worth doing once on Brno or Olomouc, because the thing it removes is real "
        "— in <b>all ten</b> pairs the city is the <i>paler</i> patch, a small light core "
        "inside a darker rural ring (Brno 773 births against the ring's 2,118), so "
        "legionnaires were rural-born even relative to their own district town. Desertion "
        "runs the other way in the larger pairs and not at all in the smaller ones — Brno "
        "město 2.98&nbsp;% against the ring's 1.56&nbsp;%, Liberec 4.21 against 2.44, but "
        "Uherské Hradiště město none at all on 51 births. Pooling averages every one of those "
        "contrasts away, which is the price the census charges.</p>"
        # the district read-out sits BESIDE the map, not up beside the funnel: clicking a
        # district and then scrolling half a page to find out what you clicked is not reading
        f'<div class="pfmaplayout"><div class="pfmapwrap"><div class="pfunitbar">{units}'
        '<span class="pfunitnote" id="pfunitnote"></span></div>'
        f'<div class="pfmaphd" id="pfmaphd"></div>{mapsvg}'
        '<div class="pfmapleg" id="pfmapleg"></div>'
        '<p class="pfsumnote" id="pfsumnote"></p></div>'
        '<aside class="pfpanel empty" id="pfmappanel"><p class="pnote">Click any district '
        "for who was born there — how many, how often they deserted, which theatre they went "
        "to, and how far they fell on enrolment.</p></aside></div>"
        '<p class="note">The tiers are a single column in the data '
        "(<code>birth_okres_match</code> / <code>birth_jaras_match</code>), which is what makes "
        "the filter above reproducible in three lines. Why the weak tiers are kept rather than "
        'dropped at source is <a href="#decisions">Decisions</a> D-11.</p><hr>')


# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# The 1910 register — one page of the source, annotated
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Every other figure on this site is drawn from a table. This one is a photograph of a
# printed page with boxes over it, because the argument of the sheet is about a *page*:
# what is on it, which parts a machine can read, and which parts it cannot.
#
# The images and the boxes are not made here. `utils/lexikon_1910/build_lexikon_figure.py`
# renders the pages out of two PDFs — one of them 3.34 GB and gitignored — and derives
# every box from the ALTO geometry the parser already uses, then writes a small tracked
# JSON beside the JPEGs. This function only reads that. The split is deliberate: the docs
# build must run on a machine that has `data/final` and nothing from `library/`.
#
# The overlay is one `<svg viewBox="0 0 100 100" preserveAspectRatio="none">` per page,
# stretched over the image by CSS, so a box is a percentage of the page and no image
# dimension is carried anywhere. Strokes carry `vector-effect="non-scaling-stroke"`,
# without which the non-uniform stretch would make the same 1 px border thick on one axis
# and hairline on the other.

LEXIKON_FIGURE = ROOT / "reference" / "places" / "figure"


def education_figures() -> str:
    """The education charts from notebook 03, embedded on the ladder sheet.

    Globbed rather than named, so a chart the author adds later appears here
    without a code change — the same contract the Descriptives sheet offers.
    Silent when nothing is built: the site must render on a fresh checkout.
    """
    figs = sorted(p for p in ROOT.joinpath("output", "figures").rglob("*.png")
                  if p.stem.startswith("educ") and "_beamer" not in p.name)
    if not figs:
        return ""
    S = ["<h2>The ladder in the data</h2>",
         '<p class="note">Built by <code>notebooks/03_visualisation.ipynb</code> from '
         "<code>data/final</code>. The stack is coloured on the sequential ramp, not the "
         "categorical palette, because the variable is ordinal: light at the bottom rung, "
         "navy at the top. Click to enlarge.</p>",
         "<div class='figgrid'>"]
    for f in figs:
        b64 = base64.b64encode(f.read_bytes()).decode()
        cap = f.stem.replace("_", " ").capitalize()
        S.append(f'<figure><img src="data:image/png;base64,{b64}" '
                 f'alt="{_html.escape(cap)}" onclick="zoom(this)" title="Click to enlarge">'
                 f"<figcaption>{_html.escape(cap)}<br>"
                 f"<code>{f.relative_to(ROOT).as_posix()}</code></figcaption></figure>")
    S.append("</div>")
    return "".join(S)


# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Amateur-theatre measure — the trend, the map, and one place's records
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Read from what the theatre runner writes (`run_amateur_theatre_pilot.py` →
# data/interim/theatre/), never recomputed here, so the figures are the build. Silent until
# the runner has been run. The chronicle's prose never leaves data/ (amateur_theatre's own
# rule): the explainer shows facts only — sources, names, places, years.
THEATRE_INTERIM = ROOT / "data" / "interim" / "theatre"
THEATRE_RAW = ROOT / "data" / "raw" / "theatre"
_TH_SOURCES = {                      # evidence source → (label, colour), in drawing order
    "ensemble": ("Ensemble list", CU_NAVY),
    "ensemble_decade": ("Listed decade (ensemble page)", "#5f89a8"),
    "ensemble_chronicle": ("Ensemble's own chronicle", "#2f8f6b"),
    "chronicle": ("Place chronicle", "#b3862f"),
    "first_report": ("First report (první zpráva)", CU_RED),
}
_TH_MILESTONES = {1848: "1848: school and church theatre counts from here (B6)",
                  1867: "1867: the association law"}
_TH_EXPLAIN_PLACES = 8


def _th_runs(years) -> list[list[int]]:
    """Sorted years as closed runs: [1880, 1881, 1890] → [[1880, 1881], [1890, 1890]]."""
    runs: list[list[int]] = []
    for y in sorted(int(v) for v in years):
        if runs and y == runs[-1][1] + 1:
            runs[-1][1] = y
        else:
            runs.append([y, y])
    return runs


def theatre_figures(src: Path = THEATRE_INTERIM) -> dict[str, str]:
    """The theatre sheet's three figures, keyed ``explainer`` / ``trend`` / ``map``.

    Each is '' when its inputs are not built, so the site renders on a fresh checkout.
    """
    need = {"panel": "place_year_panel.parquet", "court": "court_year_panel.parquet",
            "evidence": "theatre_evidence.csv"}
    if not all((src / f).is_file() for f in need.values()):
        return {}
    panel = pd.read_parquet(src / need["panel"])
    court = pd.read_parquet(src / need["court"], columns=["court_id", "year", "places_active_certain",
                                                          "places_active_possible"])
    evidence = pd.read_csv(src / need["evidence"], dtype={"source_key": str}, low_memory=False)
    return {"trend": _theatre_trend(panel), "map": _theatre_map(court),
            "explainer": _theatre_explainer(evidence, panel)}


def _theatre_trend(panel: pd.DataFrame) -> str:
    """Places, companies and performances per year, the certain line inside the possible band."""
    by_year = panel.groupby("year")
    years = by_year.size().index.astype(int).tolist()
    measures = {}
    for key, label, base in (("places", "Places with Czech theatre", "any_activity"),
                             ("companies", "Companies active", "ensembles_active"),
                             ("performances", "Performances recorded", "performances_min")):
        measures[key] = {"label": label,
                         "c": by_year[f"{base}_certain"].sum().astype(int).tolist(),
                         "p": by_year[f"{base}_possible"].sum().astype(int).tolist()}
    payload = {"years": years, "m": measures, "ms": {str(k): v for k, v in _TH_MILESTONES.items()}}
    buttons = "".join(f'<button class="thbtn{" on" if i == 0 else ""}" data-m="{k}" '
                      f'onclick="thTrend(this)">{_html.escape(m["label"])}</button>'
                      for i, (k, m) in enumerate(measures.items()))
    last_c, last_p = measures["places"]["c"][-1], measures["places"]["p"][-1]
    return (ix_head("Czech theatre over time", ix=True, hover=True)
            + '<p class="note">Every place-year summed over the database\'s '
            f"{panel['geo_id'].nunique():,} places. The solid line is what the records make "
            "<b>certain</b>, the dashed edge of the band what they make <b>possible</b>; the "
            f"gap between them is the uncertainty the rulings keep. In {years[-1]} Czech theatre "
            f"is certain in <b>{last_c:,}</b> places and possible in <b>{last_p:,}</b>. "
            "Performances count only those printed to one year, so they are a floor.</p>"
            f'<div class="thbar" id="thtrendbar">{buttons}</div>'
            '<div class="thwrap" id="thtrend"><svg viewBox="0 0 760 290" '
            'xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"></svg><div class="thtip"></div></div>'
            f"<script>window.THT={json.dumps(payload)};{_TH_TREND_JS}</script>")


def _theatre_map(court: pd.DataFrame) -> str:
    """Share of each 1910 court district's settlements with Czech theatre, by year."""
    from utils.parsing import amateur_theatre as at

    frame = at.settlement_frame(pd.read_parquet(FIN / "geo" / "settlements_1910.parquet"))
    size = frame[frame["in_1910"]].groupby("court_id").size()
    geom = _district_map()
    paths = {u: d for u, d in geom["paths"].items() if u.startswith("cc")}
    xy = np.array([tuple(map(float, p.split(","))) for d in paths.values()
                   for p in re.findall(r"-?[\d.]+,-?[\d.]+", d)])
    (x0, y0), (x1, y1) = xy.min(0) - 4, xy.max(0) + 4
    court = court.sort_values(["court_id", "year"])
    first = int(court["year"].min())
    data = {}
    for cid, g in court.groupby("court_id"):
        n = int(size.get(cid, 0))
        if n:
            data[f"cc{int(cid)}"] = {"n": n, "c": ",".join(map(str, g["places_active_certain"])),
                                     "p": ",".join(map(str, g["places_active_possible"]))}
    final = court[court["year"] == court["year"].max()]
    shares = final["places_active_possible"] / final["court_id"].map(size)
    cap = float(np.nanquantile(shares[np.isfinite(shares)], 0.95)) or 1.0
    names = {u: geom["names"].get(u, "") for u in paths}
    svg = "".join(f'<path class="thc" data-u="{u}" d="{d}"/>' for u, d in paths.items())
    last = int(court["year"].max())
    payload = {"d": data, "names": names, "y0": first, "cap": cap}
    return (ix_head("Where Czech theatre was", ix=True, hover=True)
            + '<p class="note">Each 1910 court district (<i>soudní okres</i>) shaded by the share '
            "of its 1910 settlements with Czech theatre in the chosen year — hamlets and parts "
            "included, so the shares are low and best read against one another. White lines are "
            f"the political okresy. The colour scale stops at {cap:.0%}, the 95th percentile of "
            f"possible shares in {last}. A German-speaking district with no Czech company is a "
            "true zero of the treatment, not a gap; hatched districts have no 1910 settlement in "
            "the frame to count. Drag the year, or press play.</p>"
            '<div class="thctl" id="thmapbar"><button class="thbtn" id="thplay" '
            'onclick="thPlay()">▶ play</button>'
            f'<input type="range" id="thyear" min="{first}" max="{last}" value="{last}">'
            f'<span class="thyear" id="thyearlab">{last}</span>'
            '<button class="thbtn on" data-b="c" onclick="thMapBound(this)">certain</button>'
            '<button class="thbtn" data-b="p" onclick="thMapBound(this)">possible</button>'
            f'<span class="thscale"><i>0</i><span class="thramp"></span><i>{cap:.0%}+</i></span></div>'
            f'<div class="thwrap thmap" id="thmap"><svg viewBox="{x0:g} {y0:g} {x1 - x0:g} {y1 - y0:g}" '
            'xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><defs><pattern id="thnodata" width="5" height="5" '
            'patternUnits="userSpaceOnUse" patternTransform="rotate(45)"><rect width="5" height="5" '
            'fill="#fff"/><line x1="0" y1="0" x2="0" y2="5" stroke="#b4bcc2" stroke-width="1.6"/>'
            f'</pattern></defs>{svg}<path id="thokres" d="{geom["lines"]["okres"]}"/>'
            '</svg><div class="thtip"></div></div>'
            f"<script>window.THM={json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False)};{_TH_MAP_JS}</script>")


def _th_record(r, names: dict[int, str], last: int) -> dict | None:
    """One evidence row as the explainer draws it, or None when it reaches no panel year."""
    from utils.parsing import amateur_theatre as at

    certain, possible = at.year_bounds(r.start_lo, r.start_hi, r.end_lo, r.end_hi,
                                       bool(r.open_end), bool(r.hedged), last)
    clip = lambda b: None if b is None or b[1] < 1780 or b[0] > last else [max(b[0], 1780), min(b[1], last)]  # noqa: E731
    certain, possible = clip(certain), clip(possible)
    if possible is None:
        return None
    key = str(r.source_key)
    if r.source in ("ensemble", "ensemble_decade", "ensemble_chronicle"):
        ensemble_id = int(key.split(".")[0])
        label = names.get(ensemble_id, f"ensemble {ensemble_id}")
        if r.source == "ensemble_decade":
            label = f"{label} · {key.split('.')[1][:3]}x"
    elif r.source == "chronicle":
        label = f"line {key.split('.')[0]}, clause {key.split('.')[1]}"
    else:
        label = "the place page"
    span = lambda a, b: "" if pd.isna(a) else (f"{a:.0f}" if a == b else f"{a:.0f}–{b:.0f}")  # noqa: E731
    printed = " → ".join(s for s in (span(r.start_lo, r.start_hi), span(r.end_lo, r.end_hi)) if s)
    flags = [("czech_activity", "Czech activity"), ("company", "a company"), ("performance", "a performance"),
             ("german", "German"), ("puppet", "puppet"), ("hedged", "hedged (B4)"),
             ("open_end", "open end (B1)"), ("pause", "a pause (B12)")]
    role = ", ".join(text for flag, text in flags if bool(getattr(r, flag))) or "event column only"
    return {"s": r.source, "label": label[:46], "printed": printed or "—", "role": role,
            "c": certain, "p": possible}


def _theatre_explainer(evidence: pd.DataFrame, panel: pd.DataFrame) -> str:
    """A few real places: each record's certain and possible years, and the place's result."""
    last = int(panel["year"].max())
    ensembles = (pd.read_csv(THEATRE_RAW / "ensembles.csv", usecols=["ensemble_id", "name"])
                 if (THEATRE_RAW / "ensembles.csv").is_file() else pd.DataFrame(columns=["ensemble_id", "name"]))
    names = dict(zip(ensembles["ensemble_id"].astype(int), ensembles["name"].astype(str)))
    places = (pd.read_csv(THEATRE_RAW / "places.csv", usecols=["geo_id", "name", "okres"])
              if (THEATRE_RAW / "places.csv").is_file() else pd.DataFrame(columns=["geo_id", "name", "okres"]))
    place_name = {int(g): f"{n} (okr. {o})" for g, n, o in zip(places["geo_id"], places["name"], places["okres"])}
    records: dict[int, list[dict]] = {}
    for r in evidence.itertuples(index=False):
        rec = _th_record(r, names, last)
        if rec is not None:
            records.setdefault(int(r.geo_id), []).append(rec)
    order = list(_TH_SOURCES)
    ranked = sorted(((len({x["s"] for x in recs}), len(recs), g) for g, recs in records.items()
                     if 5 <= len(recs) <= 14 and {"ensemble_decade", "ensemble_chronicle"} <= {x["s"] for x in recs}),
                    key=lambda t: (-t[0], -t[1], t[2]))[:_TH_EXPLAIN_PLACES]
    if not ranked:
        return ""
    chosen = {}
    for _, _, g in ranked:
        recs = sorted(records[g], key=lambda x: (order.index(x["s"]) if x["s"] in order else 9, x["p"][0]))
        rows = panel[panel["geo_id"] == g]
        chosen[str(g)] = {"name": place_name.get(g, f"place {g}"), "records": recs,
                          "from": max(1780, min(x["p"][0] for x in recs) - 2),
                          "c": _th_runs(rows.loc[rows["any_activity_certain"], "year"]),
                          "p": _th_runs(rows.loc[rows["any_activity_possible"], "year"])}
    options = "".join(f'<option value="{g}">{_html.escape(v["name"])}</option>' for g, v in chosen.items())
    payload = {"places": chosen, "last": last, "src": {k: list(v) for k, v in _TH_SOURCES.items()}}
    legend = "".join(f'<span class="thkey"><span class="sw" style="background:{colour}"></span>'
                     f"{_html.escape(label)}</span>" for label, colour in _TH_SOURCES.values())
    return (ix_head("From records to the panel, place by place", ix=True, hover=True)
            + '<p class="note">Every dated record of one place, one lane each: the pale bar is '
            "the years the record makes <b>possible</b>, the solid bar the years it makes "
            "<b>certain</b>. The last two lanes are what the place gets in the panel — the union "
            "over its Czech-activity records. The places are picked by rule: those with the "
            "most kinds of evidence, the ensemble pages among them, and 5–14 records. Hover a "
            "lane for what the record printed and how it was read.</p>"
            f'<div class="thctl"><select id="thexsel" class="thsel" onchange="thExplain(this.value)">'
            f"{options}</select>{legend}</div>"
            '<div class="thwrap" id="thex"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"></svg>'
            '<div class="thtip"></div></div>'
            f"<script>window.THX={json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False)};{_TH_EXPLAIN_JS}</script>")


def _before_h2(body: str, title: str, block: str) -> str:
    """Insert ``block`` before the ``<h2>`` whose text starts with ``title`` (else append)."""
    m = re.search(r"<h2[^>]*>\s*" + re.escape(title), body)
    return body[:m.start()] + block + body[m.start():] if m else body + block


# shared by the three figures, so each script carries it: function declarations only, which a
# second <script> may repeat (a top-level const may not)
_TH_SVG_JS = """
function thEl(tag, attrs, text){ const e=document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', tag);
  for(const k in attrs) e.setAttribute(k, attrs[k]); if(text!=null) e.textContent=text; return e; }
function thTip(box, tip, e, html){ tip.innerHTML=html; tip.classList.add('on');
  const b=box.getBoundingClientRect(); let x=e.clientX-b.left+14;
  if(x>b.width-tip.offsetWidth-8) x=e.clientX-b.left-tip.offsetWidth-14;
  tip.style.left=Math.max(0,x)+'px'; tip.style.top=(e.clientY-b.top+12)+'px'; }
function thFmt(v){ return Number(v).toLocaleString('en-US'); }
"""

_TH_TREND_JS = _TH_SVG_JS + """
(function(){
  const T=window.THT, box=document.getElementById('thtrend'); if(!T||!box) return;
  const svg=box.querySelector('svg'), tip=box.querySelector('.thtip');
  const W=760, H=290, L=56, R=16, TOP=16, B=30, Y0=T.years[0], Y1=T.years[T.years.length-1];
  const X=y=>L+(y-Y0)/(Y1-Y0)*(W-L-R);
  let key='places';
  function ticks(max){ const raw=max/4, p=Math.pow(10, Math.floor(Math.log10(raw||1)));
    const s=[1,2,5,10].map(f=>f*p).find(v=>v>=raw); const out=[];
    for(let v=0; v<max+s; v+=s) out.push(v); return out; }
  function draw(){
    const m=T.m[key], tk=ticks(Math.max(1, ...m.p)), top=tk[tk.length-1];
    const Y=v=>TOP+(1-v/top)*(H-TOP-B);
    svg.innerHTML='';
    tk.forEach(v=>{ svg.appendChild(thEl('line',{x1:L,x2:W-R,y1:Y(v),y2:Y(v),class:'thgrid'}));
      svg.appendChild(thEl('text',{x:L-6,y:Y(v)+3,class:'thax','text-anchor':'end'}, thFmt(v))); });
    for(let y=Math.ceil(Y0/20)*20; y<=Y1; y+=20)
      svg.appendChild(thEl('text',{x:X(y),y:H-B+15,class:'thax','text-anchor':'middle'}, y));
    Object.keys(T.ms).forEach(y=>{ svg.appendChild(thEl('line',{x1:X(+y),x2:X(+y),y1:TOP,y2:H-B,class:'thms'}));
      svg.appendChild(thEl('text',{x:X(+y)+4,y:TOP+9,class:'thmslab'}, y)); });
    const up=T.years.map((y,i)=>X(y).toFixed(1)+','+Y(m.p[i]).toFixed(1));
    const dn=T.years.map((y,i)=>X(y).toFixed(1)+','+Y(m.c[i]).toFixed(1));
    svg.appendChild(thEl('polygon',{points:up.concat(dn.slice().reverse()).join(' '),class:'thband'}));
    svg.appendChild(thEl('polyline',{points:up.join(' '),class:'thposs'}));
    svg.appendChild(thEl('polyline',{points:dn.join(' '),class:'thcert'}));
    svg.appendChild(thEl('line',{x1:L,x2:W-R,y1:H-B,y2:H-B,class:'thbase'}));
    const cur=thEl('line',{y1:TOP,y2:H-B,class:'thcur'}); svg.appendChild(cur);
    const hit=thEl('rect',{x:L,y:TOP,width:W-L-R,height:H-TOP-B,fill:'transparent'}); svg.appendChild(hit);
    hit.addEventListener('mousemove', e=>{
      const r=svg.getBoundingClientRect(), sx=(e.clientX-r.left)*W/r.width;
      const i=Math.max(0, Math.min(T.years.length-1, Math.round((sx-L)/(W-L-R)*(Y1-Y0))));
      const yr=T.years[i]; cur.setAttribute('x1',X(yr)); cur.setAttribute('x2',X(yr)); cur.classList.add('on');
      thTip(box, tip, e, '<b>'+yr+'</b> · '+m.label+(T.ms[yr]?'<br><i>'+T.ms[yr]+'</i>':'')
        +'<br>certain <b>'+thFmt(m.c[i])+'</b><br>possible <b>'+thFmt(m.p[i])+'</b>'); });
    hit.addEventListener('mouseleave', ()=>{ cur.classList.remove('on'); tip.classList.remove('on'); });
  }
  window.thTrend=function(btn){ key=btn.dataset.m;
    document.querySelectorAll('#thtrendbar .thbtn').forEach(b=>b.classList.toggle('on', b===btn)); draw(); };
  draw();
})();
"""

_TH_MAP_JS = _TH_SVG_JS + """
(function(){
  const M=window.THM, box=document.getElementById('thmap'); if(!M||!box) return;
  const tip=box.querySelector('.thtip'), slider=document.getElementById('thyear'),
        lab=document.getElementById('thyearlab'), paths=box.querySelectorAll('path.thc');
  for(const u in M.d){ M.d[u].c=M.d[u].c.split(',').map(Number); M.d[u].p=M.d[u].p.split(',').map(Number); }
  const LO=[240,243,246], HI=[0,54,87];
  let bound='c', timer=null;
  const colour=s=>{ if(s==null) return 'url(#thnodata)'; const t=Math.min(1, Math.sqrt(s/M.cap));
    return 'rgb('+LO.map((a,i)=>Math.round(a+(HI[i]-a)*t)).join(',')+')'; };
  const idx=()=>+slider.value-M.y0;
  function paint(){ lab.textContent=slider.value; const i=idx();
    paths.forEach(p=>{ const d=M.d[p.dataset.u]; p.style.fill=colour(d ? d[bound][i]/d.n : null); }); }
  slider.addEventListener('input', paint);
  window.thMapBound=function(btn){ bound=btn.dataset.b;
    document.querySelectorAll('#thmapbar .thbtn[data-b]').forEach(b=>b.classList.toggle('on', b===btn)); paint(); };
  window.thPlay=function(){ const btn=document.getElementById('thplay');
    if(timer){ clearInterval(timer); timer=null; btn.textContent='▶ play'; return; }
    if(+slider.value>=+slider.max) slider.value=slider.min;
    btn.textContent='❚❚ pause';
    timer=setInterval(()=>{ if(+slider.value>=+slider.max){ window.thPlay(); return; }
      slider.value=+slider.value+1; paint(); }, 90); };
  box.addEventListener('mousemove', e=>{ const p=e.target.closest && e.target.closest('path.thc');
    if(!p){ tip.classList.remove('on'); return; } const d=M.d[p.dataset.u], i=idx();
    thTip(box, tip, e, '<b>'+(M.names[p.dataset.u]||'')+'</b> <span class="thmut">soudní okres</span><br>'
      +(d ? slider.value+': certain <b>'+d.c[i]+'</b>, possible <b>'+d.p[i]+'</b><br>of '+d.n+' settlements in 1910'
          : 'no 1910 settlement in the frame')); });
  box.addEventListener('mouseleave', ()=>tip.classList.remove('on'));
  paint();
})();
"""

_TH_EXPLAIN_JS = _TH_SVG_JS + """
(function(){
  const X=window.THX, box=document.getElementById('thex'); if(!X||!box) return;
  const svg=box.querySelector('svg'), tip=box.querySelector('.thtip');
  const W=760, LW=230, R=12, LH=21, TOP=24;
  function lane(y, label, colour, bold){ if(colour) svg.appendChild(thEl('rect',{x:0,y:y+5,width:9,height:9,rx:2,fill:colour}));
    svg.appendChild(thEl('text',{x:colour?14:0,y:y+13,class:'thlane'+(bold?' b':'')}, label)); }
  window.thExplain=function(key){
    const P=X.places[key], recs=P.records, y0=P.from, y1=X.last;
    const XS=y=>LW+(y-y0)/(y1-y0+1)*(W-LW-R);
    const H=TOP+(recs.length+2)*LH+16;
    svg.setAttribute('viewBox','0 0 '+W+' '+H); svg.innerHTML='';
    const step=(y1-y0)>60?20:10;
    for(let y=Math.ceil(y0/step)*step; y<=y1; y+=step){
      svg.appendChild(thEl('line',{x1:XS(y),x2:XS(y),y1:TOP-4,y2:H-14,class:'thgrid'}));
      svg.appendChild(thEl('text',{x:XS(y),y:TOP-9,class:'thax','text-anchor':'middle'}, y)); }
    const bar=(r, y, cls, colour)=>svg.appendChild(thEl('rect',{x:XS(r[0]),y:y,width:Math.max(2,XS(r[1]+1)-XS(r[0])),
      height:cls==='c'?10:14,class:'thx'+cls,fill:colour}));
    recs.forEach((r,i)=>{ const y=TOP+i*LH, s=X.src[r.s]||[r.s,'#888'];
      lane(y, r.label, s[1]);
      bar(r.p, y+3, 'p', s[1]); if(r.c) bar(r.c, y+5, 'c', s[1]);
      const hit=thEl('rect',{x:0,y:y,width:W,height:LH,fill:'transparent'}); svg.appendChild(hit);
      hit.addEventListener('mousemove', e=>thTip(box, tip, e, '<b>'+s[0]+'</b><br>'+r.label
        +'<br>printed: '+r.printed+'<br>read as: '+r.role
        +'<br>certain: <b>'+(r.c?(r.c[0]===r.c[1]?r.c[0]:r.c[0]+'–'+r.c[1]):'no year')+'</b>'
        +' · possible: <b>'+(r.p[0]===r.p[1]?r.p[0]:r.p[0]+'–'+r.p[1])+'</b>'));
      hit.addEventListener('mouseleave', ()=>tip.classList.remove('on')); });
    const yr=TOP+recs.length*LH+4;
    svg.appendChild(thEl('line',{x1:0,x2:W,y1:yr-2,y2:yr-2,class:'thbase'}));
    [['Czech activity, certain', P.c, 'c'], ['Czech activity, possible', P.p, 'p']].forEach(([label, runs, cls], j)=>{
      const y=yr+j*LH; lane(y, label, null, true);
      runs.forEach(run=>bar(run, y+(cls==='c'?5:3), cls, '#003657')); });
  };
  const sel=document.getElementById('thexsel'); if(sel) window.thExplain(sel.value);
})();
"""


def _lx_data(name: str) -> str:
    """One figure asset as a data: URI, or '' when it has not been built."""
    path = LEXIKON_FIGURE / name
    if not name or not path.is_file():
        return ""
    mime = "image/png" if path.suffix == ".png" else "image/jpeg"
    return f"data:{mime};base64,{base64.b64encode(path.read_bytes()).decode()}"


def _lx_img(name: str, cls: str = "", alt: str = "", zoom: bool = False) -> str:
    src = _lx_data(name)
    if not src:
        return ""
    click = ' onclick="zoom(this)" title="Click to enlarge"' if zoom else ""
    return (f'<img class="{cls}" src="{src}" alt="{_html.escape(alt)}" '
            f'loading="lazy"{click}>')
