    "de-header": dict(
        what="The same seventeen columns, in German.",
        why="With <b>no printed rules in the text layer</b> — <code>page.rects</code> and "
            "<code>page.lines</code> are empty — so the grid has to be fitted from the right "
            "edges of the numeric words themselves, and the scans are not consistently "
            "cropped (511–541 pt wide across a sample of 80 pages), so absolute positions "
            "smear into unusable bands."),
    "de-block": dict(
        what="Brzitz, with the identical figures: 541 ha, 88 houses, 420 inhabitants, "
             "208 male and 212 female, 420 Catholic, 411 Czech-speaking and 9 "
             "German-speaking, over the same four osady.",
        why="Two compositors, two proof readings, one set of returns — which is what makes "
            "the German volume a free second keying rather than a translation."),
    "de-above": dict(
        what="The municipality printed immediately before Brzitz: Böhmisch Skalitz.",
        why="In the Czech volume Brzice is the <b>first</b> municipality of the district and "
            "Česká Skalice the third. Each edition sorts an okres alphabetically in "
            "<b>its own language</b>."),
    "de-below": dict(
        what="And the one immediately after: Cerwena Hora.",
        why="So the same municipality carries running number <b>1</b> in one volume and "
            "<b>3</b> in the other. A join on the printed number pairs unrelated "
            "municipalities while looking entirely well-behaved, which is why the editions "
            "are matched <b>by name</b>, within a court, with ties refused rather than "
            "broken on lookup order — and, where the German reader left a place unnamed, "
            "<b>by its position in the German alphabet</b>, which the Czech table's German "
            "names predict (D-150; worked through for this court "
            '<a href="#lexikon-1910-from-the-printed-line-to-the-place-authority">below</a>).'),
    "de-notes": dict(
        what="The apparatus, in two columns as on the Czech side.",
        why="The divider between them is printed, but it is <b>ink and not vector</b> here, "
            "so there is nothing to find it with except the column of blank paper beside "
            "it. This box is bounded by the widest run of x with no word over it — a guess "
            "where the Czech page has a measurement."),
    "de-notes-right": dict(
        what="<i>Ämter, Anstalten usw. im Gerichtsbezirk Böhmisch Skalitz</i> — the same "
             "section as on the Czech page, for the same district.",
        why="And numbered against the German ordering, so its entry keys do not match the "
            "Czech ones."),
    "de-entry": dict(
        what="Brzitz's institutions, printed <code>3, 1)</code> — the same four symbols the "
             "Czech volume prints against <code>1, 1)</code>.",
        why="", entry_de=True),
}


#: Shipped with the figure rather than added to the template's own script block, so a
#: sheet that is not built drags nothing along with it. The three handlers have to be
#: global because the boxes carry inline `onclick` — an SVG rect is created here, not
#: bound at load, and the sheet is `display:none` until selected.
_LX_JS = """
(function(){
  const root=document.getElementById('sheet-lexikon-1910'); if(!root) return;
  function esc(s){const e=document.createElement('span');e.textContent=s;return e.innerHTML;}
  window.lxTab=function(btn){
    const key=btn.dataset.page;
    root.querySelectorAll('.lxtab').forEach(b=>b.classList.toggle('on',b===btn));
    root.querySelectorAll('.lxstage').forEach(s=>s.classList.toggle('on',s.dataset.page===key));
    lxClear();
  };
  window.lxBoxes=function(on){ root.classList.toggle('lxhide', !on); };
  function lxClear(){
    root.querySelectorAll('.lxz.sel').forEach(r=>r.classList.remove('sel'));
    const p=document.getElementById('lxpanel'); if(!p) return;
    p.className='lxpanel empty'; p.innerHTML=LXEMPTY;
  }
  window.lxPick=function(rect){
    const d=(window.LX||{})[rect.dataset.id], p=document.getElementById('lxpanel');
    if(!d||!p) return;
    const on=!rect.classList.contains('sel');
    root.querySelectorAll('.lxz.sel').forEach(r=>r.classList.remove('sel'));
    if(!on){ lxClear(); return; }
    rect.classList.add('sel');
    p.className='lxpanel';
    let h='<div class="phead"><b>'+esc(d.label)+'</b></div>';
    if(d.what) h+='<p>'+d.what+'</p>';
    if(d.read) h+='<h4>What the text layer read</h4><pre class="lxpre">'+esc(d.read)+'</pre>';
    if(d.extra) h+=d.extra;
    if(d.why) h+='<h4>Why it matters</h4><p>'+d.why+'</p>';
    p.innerHTML=h;
    p.scrollIntoView({block:'nearest'});
  };
  const p0=document.getElementById('lxpanel');
  const LXEMPTY=p0?p0.innerHTML:'';
  const q=document.getElementById('lxgq'), gal=document.getElementById('lxgal');
  if(q&&gal){
    const cards=[...gal.querySelectorAll('.lxgc')];
    q.addEventListener('input',()=>{
      const s=(q.value||'').toLowerCase().trim();
      cards.forEach(c=>{c.style.display=(!s||c.dataset.q.includes(s))?'':'none';});
    });
  }
})();
"""


def _lx_stage(payload: dict, key: str, label: str, sub: str, *, on: bool = False) -> str:
    """One page: the image, and an SVG of percentage boxes stretched over it."""
    page = payload["pages"][key]
    src = _lx_data(page["image"])
    if not src:
        return ""
    cls = "lxstage on" if on else "lxstage"
    boxes = "".join(
        f'<rect class="lxz {z.get("kind", "zone")}" data-id="{z["id"]}" '
        f'x="{z["x"] * 100:.3f}" y="{z["y"] * 100:.3f}" '
        f'width="{z["w"] * 100:.3f}" height="{z["h"] * 100:.3f}" '
        f'vector-effect="non-scaling-stroke" onclick="lxPick(this)">'
        f'<title>{_html.escape(z["label"])}</title></rect>'
        for z in page["zones"])
    return (f'<div class="{cls}" id="lxstage-{key}" data-page="{key}">'
            f'<div class="lxcap"><b>{label}</b> <span>{sub}</span></div>'
            f'<div class="lxframe"><img src="{src}" alt="{_html.escape(label)}">'
            f'<svg class="lxsvg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" preserveAspectRatio="none">'
            f"{boxes}</svg></div></div>")


def _lx_block_table(payload: dict) -> str:
    """The Brzice block as the parser read it, with the one cell it refused."""
    show = ["seq", "name", "area_ha", "houses", "pop_total", "pop_male", "pop_female",
            "conf_catholic", "lang_german", "lang_czech", "post_key"]
    head = "".join(f"<th>{c}</th>" for c in show)
    rows = []
    for r in payload["block"]["rows"]:
        cells = []
        for col in show:
            value = r.get(col) or ""
            bad = col not in ("seq", "name", "post_key") and value and not str(
                value).replace(" ", "").replace(".", "").isdigit()
            cls = ' class="bad"' if bad else ""
            cells.append(f"<td{cls}>{_html.escape(str(value))}</td>")
        cls = ' class="muni"' if r.get("municipality") else ""
        rows.append(f"<tr{cls}>{''.join(cells)}</tr>")
    return (f'<table class="lxtbl"><thead><tr>{head}</tr></thead>'
            f"<tbody>{''.join(rows)}</tbody></table>")


def lexikon_page() -> str:
    """The annotated page of the 1910 register, plus the plate and its vocabulary."""
    manifest = LEXIKON_FIGURE / "lexikon_figure.json"
    if not manifest.is_file():
        IX_WARNINGS.append(
            "lexikon-1910: reference/places/figure/ not built — run "
            "`python utils/lexikon_1910/build_lexikon_figure.py`")
        return ('<p class="note">The page figure has not been built. Run '
                "<code>python utils/lexikon_1910/build_lexikon_figure.py</code> and "
                "rebuild.</p>")
    payload = json.loads(manifest.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    counts = payload.get("counts", {})

    # ── the annotated pages ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
    cz, de = payload["pages"]["cz"], payload["pages"]["de"]
    tabs = (
        f'<button class="lxtab on" data-page="cz" onclick="lxTab(this)">'
        f'Čechy 1910 · p.&nbsp;{cz["printed"]}</button>'
        f'<button class="lxtab" data-page="de" onclick="lxTab(this)">'
        f'Böhmen 1910 · p.&nbsp;{de["printed"]}</button>')
    panel = ('<aside class="lxpanel empty" id="lxpanel">'
             '<p class="pnote">Click any box on the page. The same municipality is '
             "printed in both editions, on different pages and in a different position "
             "in the district.</p></aside>")

    zone_data = {}
    for key in ("cz", "de"):
        for z in payload["pages"][key]["zones"]:
            spec = LX_ZONES.get(z["id"], {})
            # The panel is a 320 px column and these crops are wide strips of
            # six-point type, so every one of them is click-to-enlarge. Only the
            # block table is legible at that width unaided.
            extra = ""
            if spec.get("table"):
                extra = _lx_block_table(payload)
            elif spec.get("entry"):
                extra = _lx_img(payload["crops"].get("entry", ""), cls="lxcrop",
                                zoom=True, alt="Brzice's entry")
            elif spec.get("entry_de"):
                extra = (_lx_img(payload["crops"].get("entry_de", ""), cls="lxcrop",
                                 zoom=True, alt="Brzitz's entry")
                         + '<p class="lxsrc">The German text layer reads this key as '
                           "<code>4, —)</code> and drops the two entries that follow "
                           "it altogether.</p>")
            elif spec.get("seat"):
                extra = _lx_img(payload["crops"].get("seat", ""), cls="lxcrop",
                                zoom=True, alt="Česká Skalice's entry")
            elif spec.get("legend"):
                extra = _lx_img(payload["crops"].get("legend", ""), cls="lxcrop",
                                zoom=True, alt="The postal and railway legend")
            zone_data[z["id"]] = dict(label=z["label"], what=spec.get("what", ""),
                                      why=spec.get("why", ""), read=z.get("read", ""),
                                      extra=extra)

    reader = (
        ix_head("One page, three documents", ix=True, hover=True)
        + '<p class="note">The volume\'s own <i>Návod</i> divides every page into three: '
          "a <b>table</b>, a <b>two-column apparatus</b> below it, and a <b>legend</b> under "
          "a rule at the foot. The table is what the text layer reads well. The apparatus is "
          "what the project is actually after, and it is mostly pictures. Both editions of "
          "the same municipality are here — click any box.</p>"
        f'<div class="lxbar">{tabs}'
        '<label class="lxtoggle"><input type="checkbox" checked '
        'onchange="lxBoxes(this.checked)"> Show the boxes</label></div>'
        f"<script>window.LX={json.dumps(zone_data, ensure_ascii=False)};</script>"
        '<div class="lxlayout"><div class="lxwrap">'
        + _lx_stage(payload, "cz", "Podrobný seznam míst — IX. Čechy",
                    f'scan {cz["scan"]:04d}, printed page {cz["printed"]} · '
                    f'{cz["rules_observed"]} of 18 rules found on this page', on=True)
        + _lx_stage(payload, "de", "Spezialortsrepertorium — IX. Böhmen",
                    f'scan {de["scan"]:04d}, printed page {de["printed"]} · '
                    "no rules in the text layer at all")
        + f"</div>{panel}</div>")

    # ── what Brzice had ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    entry = (
        ix_head("What one village had, and what three readers made of it")
        + '<p class="note">One printed line, read three ways. This is the whole difficulty '
          "of the source in four glyphs: the arithmetic upstairs has an identity to check "
          "itself against, and down here there is none.</p>"
        + _lx_entry_rows(payload)
        + '<p class="note">So Brzice in 1910 had a two-class primary school, a midwife, a '
          "fire brigade and one Raiffeisen credit union — and no post office, no doctor, no "
          "parish and no railway station. None of that is in the census; all of it is in "
          "this line.</p>")

    # ── the plate and the vocabulary ─────────────────────────────────────────
    plate = (
        ix_head("Výklad značek — the plate, and the vocabulary taken from it", ix=True)
        + '<p class="note">The volume defines its own pictograms once, on a plate in the '
          "front matter, and both editions print it. It is the only place in 756 pages where "
          "the designs are drawn large enough to recognise: <code>[school]</code> is "
          "112 × 48 px here, and an entry's whole printed line downstairs is <b>44 px</b> "
          "tall. Click either plate to enlarge.</p>"
        '<div class="lxplates">'
        f'<figure>{_lx_img(payload["plates"]["cz"]["image"], cls="lxplate", zoom=True, alt="Výklad značek")}'
        f'<figcaption>Czech edition, printed page XI '
        f'(scan {payload["plates"]["cz"]["scan"]:04d})</figcaption></figure>'
        f'<figure>{_lx_img(payload["plates"]["de"]["image"], cls="lxplate", zoom=True, alt="Zeichenerklärung")}'
        f'<figcaption>German edition, same plate '
        f'(scan {payload["plates"]["de"]["scan"]:04d})</figcaption></figure></div>'
        '<p class="note">That 0.45× is why matching the plate\'s own crops against the '
        "entries <b>does not work</b>, and it was measured rather than assumed: against its "
        "own source crop a template scores <b>1.000</b>; against a real entry line at the "
        "right scale it peaks at <b>0.644</b>, and over a whole section the detections "
        "cluster <b>0.62–0.83 with no separation at all</b> — the strongest hits being "
        "settlement symbols that cannot occur in an offices section and are in fact "
        "correlating with ordinary letters. Nothing downstream consumes it as an "
        "identification.</p>"
        + _lx_gallery(payload))

    # ── the numbers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    # No `_with_toc` here: this block is injected into a markdown sheet, and `main`
    # runs the contents strip over the whole sheet once the two are joined. Adding
    # one here would claim the strip for the figure and leave the prose out of it.
    return (reader + entry + _lx_register_walkthrough() + plate + _lx_grades(counts)
            + f"<script>{_LX_JS}</script><hr>")


def _lx_entry_rows(payload: dict) -> str:
    """The printed line, the text layer's version of it, and the human reading."""
    crop = _lx_img(payload["crops"].get("entry", ""), cls="lxcrop", zoom=True,
                   alt="1, 1) [school] II, [midwife], [fire-brigade], [cooperative]: R.")
    crop_de = _lx_img(payload["crops"].get("entry_de", ""), cls="lxcrop", zoom=True,
                      alt="3, 1) [school] II, [midwife], [fire-brigade], [cooperative]: R.")
    glyphs = {g["token"]: g for g in payload.get("glyphs", [])}

    def glyph(token: str, trail: str = "") -> str:
        g = glyphs.get(token)
        if not g:
            return f"<code>{_html.escape(token)}</code>{trail}"
        src = _lx_data(g["file"])
        return (f'<span class="lxg"><img src="{src}" alt="{_html.escape(token)}">'
                f'<i>{_html.escape(g["gloss"])}</i></span>{trail}')

    read = ("1,\t1) g II, $, f,\tR.")
    truth = ("<b>1,</b> <b>1)</b> " + glyph("[school]", " II,") + " "
             + glyph("[midwife]", ",") + " " + glyph("[fire-brigade]", ",") + " "
             + glyph("[cooperative]", ": R."))
    return (
        '<div class="lxrows">'
        f'<div class="lxrow"><span class="lxk">What the page prints</span>'
        f'<div class="lxv">{crop}</div></div>'
        f'<div class="lxrow"><span class="lxk">What the text layer read</span>'
        f'<div class="lxv"><pre class="lxpre">{_html.escape(read)}</pre>'
        '<p class="lxsrc">Four printed marks; <b>one</b> unresolved slot. A pictogram the '
        "engine rendered as <code>Щ</code>, <code>ф</code> or <code>$</code> becomes a slot; "
        "the same pictogram rendered as <code>g</code>, <code>f</code>, <code>p</code> or "
        "<code>S</code> — the commoner outcome — is indistinguishable from type and is never "
        "emitted at all.</p></div></div>"
        f'<div class="lxrow"><span class="lxk">What is actually printed</span>'
        f'<div class="lxv"><div class="lxglyphs">{truth}</div>'
        '<p class="lxsrc">Hand-keyed against the plate. Across the whole worksheet: '
        "<b>286 symbols over 55 entries, every one marked certain</b>, none unidentifiable — "
        "so the distinctions are on the paper at 399 DPI and the limit is the readers, not "
        "the scan.</p></div></div>"
        + (f'<div class="lxrow"><span class="lxk">And the German volume</span>'
           f'<div class="lxv">{crop_de}'
           '<p class="lxsrc">The same four marks, set by a different compositor in a '
           "different city, printed against key <b>3</b> because the German edition sorts "
           "the district alphabetically in German. This is the closest thing the project has "
           "to an independent second keying of the apparatus — and the only reason it can be "
           "used is that the two are matched by <i>name</i>, or by position in the German "
           "alphabet, and never by the printed number.</p></div></div>" if crop_de else "")
        + "</div>")


def _lx_kv_table(rows: list[tuple], head: tuple, cls: str = "lxtbl lxwalk") -> str:
    """A small table of already-escaped cells."""
    th = "".join(f"<th>{h}</th>" for h in head)
    body = "".join("<tr>" + "".join(f"<td>{c}</td>" for c in r) + "</tr>" for r in rows)
    return f'<table class="{cls}"><thead><tr>{th}</tr></thead><tbody>{body}</tbody></table>'


def _lx_cap(name: str) -> str:
    """A lexikon headword in reading case: ``DOUBRAVICE U ČESKÉ SKALICE`` → ``Doubravice u České
    Skalice`` (the Czech prepositions stay lower-case)."""
    small = {"u", "nad", "pod", "v", "na", "ve", "za", "při"}
    words = str(name).lower().split()
    return " ".join(w if (i and w in small) else w[:1].upper() + w[1:] for i, w in enumerate(words))


def _lx_walk_places(w: dict) -> str:
    """Step 1: Brzice and its osady, each anchored to settlements_1910."""
    esc = _html.escape
    rows, via_1910 = [], []
    for p in w["places"]:
        a = p["authority"] or {}
        where = esc(_lx_cap(a.get("cs_name", "")))
        if a.get("name_1910"):
            where += f" <span class=\"lxsrc\">(1910: {esc(a['name_1910'])})</span>"
        if a.get("status_1910") in ("osada", "cast") and a.get("parent_1910"):
            where += f" <span class=\"lxsrc\">{esc(a['status_1910'])} of {esc(a['parent_1910'])}</span>"
        if a.get("name_1910") and p["printed_name"].split(",")[0].strip() == a["name_1910"]:
            via_1910.append((p["printed_name"], _lx_cap(a.get("cs_name", ""))))
        rows.append(("municipality" if p["settlement_seq"] == 0 else f"osada {p['settlement_seq']}",
                     f"{esc(p['printed_name'])} <span class=\"lxsrc\">{esc(p['name_source'])}</span>",
                     f"<code>{esc(str(p['settlement_id']))}</code>", where, esc(p["status"]),
                     f"{p['score']} / {p['runner_up']}"))
    cands = ", ".join(f"{esc(_lx_cap(c['cs_name']))} {c['score']}" for c in w["candidates"])
    okres = (w["places"][0]["authority"] or {}).get("okres_1910", "")
    note_1910 = "".join(
        f" <b>{esc(printed)}</b> is anchored through its 1910 name: the lexikon files it under "
        f"its modern headword {esc(cs)}." for printed, cs in via_1910)
    return (
        "<h3>1. The place — a key into <code>settlements_1910</code></h3>"
        + _lx_kv_table(rows, ("place", "printed name · source", "settlement_id", "in the authority",
                              "status", "score / runner-up"))
        + f'<p class="note">The candidates are the settlements of okres {esc(okres)} '
          f"(<code>{w['court']['okres_id']}</code>), the okres of the section's 1910 court, "
          f"{esc(w['court']['court_cs'])} "
          f"(<code>courts.csv</code>). For the municipality's cell the best three are {cands}: a "
          "match needs a similarity of at least 84 and a lead of 5 over the runner-up, a tie is "
          "refused and never broken on lookup order, and each settlement is taken once per okres. "
          "The names come from the table reader's rows; the run folder itself holds none."
          + note_1910 + "</p>")


def _lx_walk_claims(w: dict) -> str:
    """Steps 2 and 3: the claims, and the municipality's one row."""
    esc = _html.escape
    inst = _lx_kv_table(
        [(f"osada {i['settlement_seq']}" if i["settlement_seq"] else "municipality",
          f"<code>{esc(i['mark'])}</code>", i["count"], esc(i["rule"]), esc(i["settled_by"]),
          f"<code>{esc(i['common_category'] or '—')}</code>") for i in w["institutions"]],
        ("place", "mark", "count", "rule", "settled by", "common category"))
    m = w["municipality"]
    shown = [(f"<code>{esc(k)}</code>", "<i>&lt;NA&gt;</i>" if v is None else esc(str(v)))
             for k, v in m.items()]
    half = (len(shown) + 1) // 2
    grid = (f'<div class="lxwalk2">{_lx_kv_table(shown[:half], ("column", "value"))}'
            f'{_lx_kv_table(shown[half:], ("column", "value"))}</div>')
    return (
        "<h3>2. What it had — <code>register_institutions</code></h3>" + inst
        + '<p class="note">One row per place and mark, with the rule the frozen run settled it '
          "by and the mark's category across the volumes' plates (D-147): a Mähren Lokalie and a "
          "Bohemian parish meet on <code>[rc-cure-seat]</code>. The Raiffeisen credit union is the "
          "letter <b>R</b> after the cooperative mark, a <i>text</i> abbreviation; those reach the "
          "tables through <code>final_abbreviations.csv</code>, which no run has written yet.</p>"
        + "<h3>3. One row per municipality — <code>register_municipalities</code></h3>" + grid
        + '<p class="note">Built from the long tables by code and keyed by '
          "<code>settlement_id</code>, so it joins onto a legionnaire's birthplace without a second "
          "match. Columns that are zero for Brzice are left out here. <code>n_coop</code> is "
          "<i>&lt;NA&gt;</i>, not 0: the letters were not read, which is not the same as none "
          "printed.</p>")


def _lx_walk_german(w: dict) -> str:
    """Step 4: Brzitz, No. 3 in the German volume, found through the Czech one (D-150)."""
    esc = _html.escape
    g = w["german"]
    later = {p["cz_muni"]: p for p in g["with_the_later_page"]["pairs"]}
    gold = {p["de_muni"]: p for p in g["gold_page_only"]["pairs"]}
    printed = {r["muni_seq"]: r["name"] for r in g["german_printed"]}
    extra = [p for p in g["with_the_later_page"]["pairs"] if p["cz_muni"] not in
             {r["muni_seq"] for r in g["czech_by_german_name"]}]
    rows = [(f"<i>later page</i>", esc(p["cz_name"]), "—", p["de_muni"],
             esc(printed.get(p["de_muni"], "")), "refused — no candidate on the gold page")
            for p in extra]
    for r in g["czech_by_german_name"]:
        de = later.get(r["muni_seq"], {}).get("de_muni")
        how = gold.get(de, {}).get("how", "") if de else ""
        rows.append((r["muni_seq"], esc(r["printed_name"]), f"<code>{esc(r['german_key'])}</code>",
                     de or "", esc(printed.get(de, "")) if de else "<span class=\"lxsrc\">beyond the figure</span>",
                     esc(how)))
    key = sorted(rows, key=lambda r: str(r[2]) if r[2] != "—" else "")
    h = w["holdout"]
    filled = [p for p in g["with_the_later_page"]["pairs"] if p["how"] == "order"]
    return (
        "<h3>4. Brzitz in the German volume — through the Czech one</h3>"
        '<p class="note">The German volume prints Brzitz as <b>No. 3</b>, because it sorts the '
        "court by German names. The Czech table prints every municipality's German name as the "
        "last form of its cell, so sorting the Czech cells by that name, accents folded, predicts "
        "the German numbers. The table is in that order; the German numbers are read off the "
        "German page in the figure above.</p>"
        + _lx_kv_table(key, ("Czech No.", "Czech cell", "German name, folded", "German No.",
                             "German page prints", "paired on the gold by"))
        + '<p class="note">On the gold, the German places Nos. 2–4 pair with the Czech ones by '
          "name. Suppose German No. 1 had no name on the reader's list, as 32 German "
          "municipalities on the gold do not. The order step looks at the gap before Böhmisch "
          "Skalitz: <b>one</b> German slot and <b>no</b> Czech candidate, because Aujezdetz is "
          "Újezdec, printed later in the Czech alphabet on a page the gold did not read. The "
          "counts differ, so it refuses (<code>"
          + esc(g["gold_page_only"]["status"]) + "</code>), rather than slide a neighbour into "
          "the hole. With that page read, one slot and one candidate: German No. 1 is "
          + ", ".join(f"<b>{esc(p['cz_name'])}</b>" for p in filled)
          + " (<code>via_czech_order</code>). Because the German numbers between two pairs are a "
            "closed run, an equal count proves no municipality is missing, and a wrong fill cannot "
            "happen silently.</p>"
        + f'<p class="note">Tested by leave-one-out on the German gold: each of the <b>{h["pairs"]}</b> '
          "pairs the German volume anchored on its own was dropped and the order step asked to "
          f"find it again. It filled <b>{h['predicted']}</b>, all <b>{h['correct']}</b> correctly, "
          "and left the rest open. The German shortfall was never the print, which carries both "
          "names, but the reader's list, which leaves many places out; the anchoring rates before "
          'and after are on <a href="#register-data">the municipal data sheet</a>.</p>')


def _lx_register_walkthrough() -> str:
    """Brzice, carried past the frozen run into the place authority (D-148, D-150)."""
    path = LEXIKON_FIGURE / "register_walkthrough.json"
    if not path.is_file():
        IX_WARNINGS.append("lexikon-1910: reference/places/figure/register_walkthrough.json not "
                           "built — run `python utils/lexikon_1910/build_register_walkthrough.py`")
        return ""
    w = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    return (
        ix_head("From the printed line to the place authority")
        + '<p class="note">The frozen run settles what Brzice\'s entry prints, but it keeps no '
          "place name and no link outside the book. The step after it (D-148) gives every "
          "municipality and part a key into <code>settlements_1910</code>, the table the "
          "legionnaires' birthplaces already resolve to, so the merge onto persons is a plain "
          f"join. Everything below is computed by that code on the Czech gold run, which holds "
          f"this page (<code>lexikon_1910_register</code> {esc_v(w['register'])}, built "
          f"{_html.escape(w['built'])}). Columns and caveats: "
          '<a href="#register-data">1910 register — the municipal data</a>.</p>'
        + _lx_walk_places(w) + _lx_walk_claims(w) + _lx_walk_german(w))


def esc_v(text) -> str:
    return _html.escape(str(text))


def _lx_gallery(payload: dict) -> str:
    """The closed vocabulary, as printed marks — searchable."""
    glyphs = payload.get("glyphs", [])
    if not glyphs:
        return ""
    cards = "".join(
        f'<div class="lxgc" data-q="{_html.escape((g["token"] + " " + g["gloss"]).lower())}">'
        f'<img src="{_lx_data(g["file"])}" alt="{_html.escape(g["token"])}">'
        f'<b>{_html.escape(g["gloss"])}</b><code>{_html.escape(g["token"])}</code></div>'
        for g in sorted(glyphs, key=lambda g: g["gloss"].lower()))
    return (
        f'<p class="note">Those {len(glyphs)} designs, cut off the plate and given names, '
        "are the <b>closed list</b> a reader is allowed to answer from — with "
        "<code>[?]</code> for a mark it cannot place, so that an unknown symbol has "
        "somewhere to go that is not a wrong answer. There is no arithmetic identity below "
        "the rule to catch a confabulated symbol, so this is the only defence there "
        "is.</p>"
        '<input class="tblfilter" id="lxgq" placeholder="Filter these symbols…">'
        f'<div class="lxgal" id="lxgal">{cards}</div>')


def _lx_grades(counts: dict) -> str:
    """The pilot's own numbers — the arithmetic, then the symbols."""
    if not counts:
        return ""
    checks = counts.get("checks", {})
    order = ["I1_sex", "I2_confession", "I3_language", "I5_sequence", "I8_parts"]
    rows = []
    for name in order:
        c = checks.get(name)
        if not c:
            continue
        rows.append(dict(Check=name, Passed=f"{c['passed']:,}", Failed=f"{c['failed']:,}",
                         Unreadable=f"{c['unparseable']:,}",
                         **{"Not applicable": f"{c['na']:,}", "Pass rate": f"{c['rate']}%"}))
    block = [c for k, c in checks.items() if k.startswith("I4_block:")]
    if block:
        passed = sum(c["passed"] for c in block)
        graded = sum(c["graded"] for c in block)
        rows.append(dict(Check="I4_block (all columns)", Passed=f"{passed:,}",
                         Failed=f"{sum(c['failed'] for c in block):,}",
                         Unreadable=f"{sum(c['unparseable'] for c in block):,}",
                         **{"Not applicable": f"{sum(c['na'] for c in block):,}",
                            "Pass rate": f"{100 * passed / graded:.1f}%" if graded else "—"}))
    out = [ix_head("How well it comes out"),
           '<p class="note">Over a 20-page pilot. <b>Not applicable</b> is never counted as '
           "a pass — a rate that silently absorbs the rows it could not read measures "
           "nothing — and a failing block is re-read, never repaired. The readers are never "
           "shown these identities: a model told what the numbers must add up to returns "
           "numbers that add up.</p>",
           df_table(pd.DataFrame(rows))]

    agree = counts.get("agreement", {})
    if agree:
        out.append(
            "<p class='note'>Below the rules there is nothing to add up, and it shows. Over "
            f"the same pages, <b>{agree['markers']}</b> printed marks were compared across "
            f"<b>{agree['readers']}</b> passes — two local vision models with and without "
            "the plate in the prompt, and one human. <b>Every one of them is contested</b>: "
            f"none is claimed by all five, and <b>{agree['single_reader']}</b> are claimed by "
            "exactly one. Two models given the identical mark returned <code>[doctor]</code> "
            "and <code>[rc-curate]</code>; over the pilot they agreed on symbol identity "
            "<b>9.5 %</b> of the time while agreeing on the <i>words</i> of the same entries "
            "<b>68.7 %</b> of the time. They are not failing to read — they are being asked "
            "to name a glyph they have never seen drawn. And agreement <b>bounds</b> "
            "accuracy without measuring it: two readers agreeing 21.5 % is equally "
            "consistent with both being 45 % right and independent, or both being 22 % "
            "right.</p>")
    join = counts.get("join", {})
    if join:
        only_image = join.get("only_image", 0)
        only_text = join.get("only_text", 0)
        out.append(
            "<p class='note'>Which is why the division of labour the pipeline was designed "
            "around — <i>the text layer knows where every marker is, the image read knows "
            "what it is</i> — <b>is false</b>. Joining the two over the pilot leaves "
            f"<b>{only_image}</b> marks the image found and the text layer never emitted, "
            f"against <b>{only_text}</b> the other way: the text layer sees roughly a third "
            "of what is printed, and which third is decided by how the OCR happened to fail. "
            "For the apparatus the image read has to be the primary record and the text "
            "layer's slots a lower bound.</p>")
    return "".join(out)


# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# The 1910 register — the reading route, drawn
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# The sheet's own eight steps, with the thing prose reads worst on top of them: **where a
# mark leaves the route**. A mark is accepted because all four readings agree, or it is the
# reader of record's alone, or Opus settles it, or the author rules it — four fates, and
# the whole design argument is about their proportions. The figure hangs them off the spine
# as branches and carries the share that actually took each one.
#
# What is authored here is the gloss on each step and which decisions settled it. The
# counts are read from the run's own output directory (`output/frozen/<run>/`): the `rule`
# column of `final_inventory.csv` states how every mark was settled, and a rule this figure
# has no band for is counted and named rather than dropped — a flow chart that quietly
# loses a category is worse than no flow chart.
#
# The one rule the figure obeys: **a count belongs to the run it was read from.** Each
# edition × page set reads its own `output/frozen/<edition>_<pages>/`; a set not yet read
# blanks every number and says why, instead of showing the gold's figures under another
# label. That is also the page's argument made visible — certification is the same route,
# not a different one.

#: Shipped with the figure, like `_LX_JS`, so a sheet that is not built drags nothing along
#: with it. The handlers are global because the SVG groups carry inline `onclick`, and the
#: sheet is `display:none` until it is selected.
_RT_JS = """
(function(){
  const root=document.getElementById('sheet-register-route'); if(!root) return;
  const RT=window.RT||{}, S=RT.stages||{}, R=RT.runs||{};
  const EXITS=['agreed','record','opus','author'];
  const NAME={agreed:'agreed',record:'reader of record',opus:'Opus',author:'the author'};
  const COL={agreed:'#8FA31E',record:'#8a939c',opus:'#D22D40',author:'#003657'};
  let ed=(Object.keys(R).find(k=>R[k]&&R[k].claims)||'cz:gold').split(':')[0], pages='gold', sel='';
  function esc(s){const e=document.createElement('span');e.textContent=s==null?'':s;return e.innerHTML;}
  function num(n){return (n==null)?'\\u2014':n.toLocaleString('en-US');}
  function pc(a,b){if(!b||a==null) return ''; const r=100*a/b;
    return (r>99.5||r===0?r.toFixed(0):r.toFixed(1))+' %';}
  function run(){return R[ed+':'+pages]||{};}
  function live(){return !!run().claims;}
  function dec(ds){return (ds||[]).map(d=>'<a href="#decisions" onclick="show(\\'decisions\\')">'
      +esc(d)+'</a>').join(' · ');}

  function facts(id,r){
    if(!live()) return '<h4>In this run</h4><p class="rtnone">Not read yet — the figures '+
      'below the chart stay blank too, rather than borrow the gold run\\'s.</p>';
    const L=[];
    if(id==='read'&&(r.passes||[]).length)
      L.push(['Passes on file',(r.passes||[]).map(p=>'<code>'+esc(p)+'</code>').join(' ')]);
    if(id==='check'){
      if(r.order_flags!=null) L.push(['Marks the order rule flagged',num(r.order_flags)+
        (r.order_verdicts?' <i>('+Object.entries(r.order_verdicts).map(e=>e[1]+' '+esc(e[0]))
          .join(', ')+')</i>':'')]);
      if(r.dino) L.push(['DINOv3 here', r.dino.used
        ? 'judges '+pc(r.dino.judged,1)+' of claims, keeps '+pc(r.dino.keep,1)+
          ' of the true ones and catches '+pc(r.dino.catch,1)+' of the false'
        : '<b>off</b> \\u2014 '+esc(r.dino.why||'it did not pass its gate')]);
    }
    if(id==='opus'||id==='author'){
      EXITS.forEach(k=>{ if(r[k]!=null&&((S[id]||{}).exits||[]).includes(k))
        L.push([NAME[k].charAt(0).toUpperCase()+NAME[k].slice(1),
                num(r[k])+' <i>'+pc(r[k],r.claims)+' of marks</i>']);});
      if(id==='opus'&&r.opus_calls!=null) L.push(['Verify calls made',num(r.opus_calls)]);
    }
    if(id==='ledger') L.push(['The inventory it wrote',num(r.claims)+' claims in '+
      num(r.munis)+' municipalities, over '+num(r.pages)+' pages']);
    if(id==='measure'&&r.sample!=null) L.push(['Validation marks drawn',num(r.sample)]);
    if(!L.length) return '';
    return '<h4>In this run</h4><table class="rtfacts">'+L.map(x=>'<tr><td>'+x[0]+
      '</td><td>'+x[1]+'</td></tr>').join('')+'</table>';
  }

  function panel(){
    const p=document.getElementById('rtpanel'); if(!p) return;
    const d=S[sel];
    if(!d){ p.className='rtpanel empty'; p.innerHTML=EMPTY; return; }
    p.className='rtpanel';
    let h='<div class="phead"><b>'+esc(d.n==='0'?'Freeze':d.n+'. '+d.name)+'</b>'+
      '<span class="rtkind">'+esc(d.kind)+'</span></div>'+
      '<p class="pmeta">'+esc(d.gloss)+'</p>';
    const sn=(d.setnote||{})[pages];
    if(sn) h+='<p class="rtoff">On this page set: '+sn+'</p>';
    h+='<h4>What it does</h4><p>'+d.what+'</p>'+facts(sel,run())+
       '<h4>Why it is there</h4><p>'+d.why+'</p>';
    if((d.decisions||[]).length) h+='<p class="psym">Decided in '+dec(d.decisions)+'</p>';
    p.innerHTML=h;
  }

  function paint(){
    root.querySelectorAll('.rtpill').forEach(b=>b.classList.toggle('on',b.dataset.ed===ed));
    root.querySelectorAll('.rtset').forEach(b=>b.classList.toggle('on',b.dataset.set===pages));
    const r=run(), L=live();
    EXITS.forEach(k=>{
      const n=root.querySelector('.rten[data-exit="'+k+'"]');
      const s=root.querySelector('.rtesh[data-exit="'+k+'"]');
      if(n) n.textContent=L?num(r[k]):'\\u2014';
      if(s) s.textContent=L?(pc(r[k],r.claims)||'0 %'):'not read yet';
    });
    const mix=document.getElementById('rtmix'), lab=document.getElementById('rtmixlab');
    const hd=document.getElementById('rtbarn'), note=document.getElementById('rtnote');
    if(hd) hd.textContent=L?num(r.claims):'\\u2014';
    if(mix) mix.innerHTML=!L?'':EXITS.filter(k=>r[k]).map(k=>'<span style="width:'+
      (100*r[k]/r.claims).toFixed(2)+'%;background:'+COL[k]+'" title="'+NAME[k]+': '+
      num(r[k])+'"></span>').join('');
    if(lab) lab.innerHTML=!L?'':EXITS.map(k=>'<span><i style="background:'+COL[k]+'"></i>'+
      NAME[k]+' <b>'+num(r[k]||0)+'</b> '+(pc(r[k]||0,r.claims)||'0 %')+'</span>').join('');
    if(note){
      const set=(RT.sets||{})[pages]||{};
      let t=set.note||'';
      if(pages==='gold'&&!L) t='This edition has not been read on this machine.';
      else if(!L) t='Not read yet \\u2014 the numbers above stay blank rather than borrow the '+
        'gold run\\'s. '+t;
      else if(r.other) t+=' <b>'+num(r.other)+'</b> marks carry a rule this figure has no '+
        'band for ('+(r.other_rules||[]).map(esc).join(', ')+').';
      note.innerHTML=t;
    }
    panel();
  }

  window.rtEdition=function(b){ if(b.disabled) return; ed=b.dataset.ed; paint(); };
  window.rtPages=function(b){ pages=b.dataset.set; paint(); };
  window.rtPick=function(g){
    const id=g.dataset.id, was=sel===id;
    root.querySelectorAll('.rtstage.sel').forEach(x=>x.classList.remove('sel'));
    root.querySelectorAll('.rtexit.lit,.rtelbow.lit').forEach(x=>x.classList.remove('lit'));
    sel=was?'':id;
    if(sel){
      g.classList.add('sel');
      ((S[id]||{}).exits||[]).forEach(k=>root.querySelectorAll(
        '.rtexit[data-exit="'+k+'"],.rtelbow[data-exit="'+k+'"]')
        .forEach(x=>x.classList.add('lit')));
    }
    panel();
  };
  const p0=document.getElementById('rtpanel'), EMPTY=p0?p0.innerHTML:'';
  paint();
})();
"""


def _route_counts(run: str) -> dict:
    """What one frozen run's own outputs say — nothing in the figure is typed.

    ``final_inventory.csv`` carries a ``rule`` column stating how each mark was settled.
    Anything it holds that this figure has no band for comes back under ``other`` with its
    rule strings, and the figure prints them: a category that disappears silently is how a
    flow chart starts misdescribing the flow.
    """
    d = ROOT / "output" / "frozen" / run
    inv = d / "final_inventory.csv"
    if not inv.exists():
        return {}
    f = pd.read_csv(inv, dtype=str).fillna("")
    rule = f["rule"]
    known = {"agreed": rule == "agreed", "opus": rule == "opus",
             "record": rule.str.startswith("not asked"),
             "author": rule.str.startswith("author")}
    out = {k: int(v.sum()) for k, v in known.items()}
    rest = ~(known["agreed"] | known["opus"] | known["record"] | known["author"])
    out["other"] = int(rest.sum())
    out["other_rules"] = sorted(set(rule[rest])) if out["other"] else []
    out["claims"] = len(f)
    out["pages"] = int(f["page"].nunique())
    out["munis"] = int(f.groupby(["page", "district", "muni_seq"]).ngroups)

    flags = d / "order_flags.csv"
    if flags.exists():
        g = pd.read_csv(flags, dtype=str).fillna("")
        out["order_flags"] = len(g)
        out["order_verdicts"] = {str(k): int(v) for k, v in g["verdict"].value_counts().items()}
    sheet = d / "validation_sheet.csv"
    if sheet.exists():
        out["sample"] = len(pd.read_csv(sheet))
    usage = sorted(d.glob("opus*/usage.csv"))
    if usage:
        out["opus_calls"] = sum(len(pd.read_csv(p)) for p in usage)
    # The gate file holds both editions' figures and the verdict for the German side, so it
    # is read wherever it was written rather than from this run's own directory.
    gate = next(iter(sorted((ROOT / "output" / "frozen").glob("*/e3/gate.json"))), None)
    if gate:
        try:
            g = json.loads(gate.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        except (ValueError, OSError):
            g = {}
        side = g.get("de" if run.startswith("de") else "cz", {})
        if side:
            out["dino"] = dict(judged=side.get("judged_share"), keep=side.get("keep_true"),
                               catch=side.get("catch_false"), why=g.get("why", ""),
                               used=True if not run.startswith("de") else bool(g.get("use_dino")))
    out["passes"] = (sorted(p.stem for p in (d / "reads").glob("*.done"))
                     if (d / "reads").is_dir() else [])
    return out


def route_flow() -> str:
    """The reading route as a flow chart — the eight steps, and a mark's four ways out.

    Prose has to name the exits one at a time and in the middle of the step that produces
    them; a figure can put all four beside the spine with the share that took each, which is
    the design's whole claim. The page-set switch is the second thing worth drawing: the
    sealed half runs on *this* route, so changing the set changes which steps run and what
    has been read, and nothing else about the chart.
    """
    runs = {f"{key}:{ps}": _route_counts(f"{prefix}_{ps}")
            for key, _n, prefix, _t in _RT_EDITIONS for ps, *_rest in _RT_PAGESETS}
    have = [k for k, *_r in _RT_EDITIONS if any(runs[f"{k}:{ps}"] for ps, *_x in _RT_PAGESETS)]
    # a page set read for any edition is marked read; the note under the bar says which
    states = {ps: ("read" if any(runs[f"{k}:{ps}"] for k, *_r in _RT_EDITIONS) else state)
              for ps, _l, state, _d in _RT_PAGESETS}
    names = {k: n for k, n, _r, _t in _RT_EDITIONS}

    BW, BH, GAP, TOP = 452, 68, 16, 94
    SX, EX, EW, EH = 44, 568, 330, 58
    W, H = EX + EW + 14, TOP + len(_RT_STAGES) * (BH + GAP) + 10

    parts = [
        f'<svg id="rtsvg" viewBox="0 0 {W} {H}" width="{W}" height="{H}" '
        'xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><defs>'
        '<marker id="rtar" viewBox="0 0 8 8" refX="7" refY="4" markerWidth="7" '
        'markerHeight="7" orient="auto"><path d="M0,0 L8,4 L0,8z" fill="#b4bcc2"/></marker>'
        '</defs>',
        f'<text class="rthead" x="{SX}" y="34">THE FROZEN ROUTE — one edition, one page set</text>',
        f'<text class="rtsub" x="{SX}" y="54">notebooks/15_frozen_run.ipynb, every step in '
        'order; click a step</text>',
        f'<text class="rthead" x="{EX}" y="34">HOW A MARK IS SETTLED</text>',
        f'<text class="rtsub" x="{EX}" y="54">its four ways off the spine</text>']

    info: dict[str, dict] = {}
    stage_y: dict[str, float] = {}
    for i, st in enumerate(_RT_STAGES):
        y = TOP + i * (BH + GAP)
        stage_y[st["id"]] = y
        fill, stroke = _RT_KIND[st["kind"]]
        if i:
            parts.append(f'<path class="rtarrow" d="M{SX + BW / 2:.0f},{y - GAP} '
                         f'L{SX + BW / 2:.0f},{y - 3}" marker-end="url(#rtar)"/>')
        # The chips ride the title line, not the foot of the box: the gloss is the longest
        # text here and a chip over its tail is unreadable in exactly the two steps that
        # carry the most readers. Widths are from the glyph count, so a longer name pushes
        # the row left rather than overprinting the one beside it.
        chips, cx = "", BW - 12
        for who in reversed(st["who"]):
            wid = 8 + 5.4 * len(who)
            cx -= wid
            chips += (f'<g class="rtwho"><rect x="{cx:.0f}" y="12" width="{wid:.0f}" '
                      f'height="18" rx="9"/><text x="{cx + wid / 2:.0f}" y="24.5">'
                      f'{_html.escape(who)}</text></g>')
            cx -= 5
        dash = ';stroke-dasharray:5 3' if st["kind"] == "prep" else ""
        parts.append(
            f'<g class="rtstage" data-id="{st["id"]}" '
            f'transform="translate({SX},{y})" onclick="rtPick(this)">'
            f'<rect class="rtbox" width="{BW}" height="{BH}" rx="7" '
            f'style="fill:{fill};stroke:{stroke}{dash}"/>'
            f'<circle class="rtn" cx="26" cy="26" r="13" style="fill:{stroke}"/>'
            f'<text class="rtnt" x="26" y="30">{st["n"]}</text>'
            f'<text class="rtlab" x="50" y="25">{_html.escape(st["name"])}</text>'
            f'<text class="rtgloss" x="50" y="43">{_html.escape(st["gloss"])}</text>'
            + chips + "</g>")
        info[st["id"]] = dict(n=st["n"], name=_html.escape(st["name"]), kind=st["kind"],
                              gloss=_html.escape(st["gloss"]), what=st["what"], why=st["why"],
                              decisions=st["decisions"], setnote=st.get("setnote", {}),
                              exits=[k for k, src, *_r in _RT_FATES if src == st["id"]])

    # The exits are laid out as their own column, stacked from the first step that feeds
    # them: three hang off step 4 and one off step 5, so stacking them against their own
    # stages would overlap. Each keeps an elbow back to the step it belongs to.
    y0 = stage_y[_RT_FATES[0][1]] - 6
    for j, (ekey, src, elabel, egloss) in enumerate(_RT_FATES):
        ey = y0 + j * (EH + 12)
        col, soft = _RT_EXITS[ekey]
        mid = stage_y[src] + BH / 2
        parts.append(
            f'<path class="rtelbow" data-exit="{ekey}" style="stroke:{col}" '
            f'd="M{SX + BW},{mid:.0f} H{(SX + BW + EX) / 2:.0f} V{ey + EH / 2:.0f} '
            f'H{EX - 5:.0f}" marker-end="url(#rtar)"/>'
            f'<g class="rtexit" data-exit="{ekey}" transform="translate({EX},{ey:.0f})">'
            f'<rect width="{EW}" height="{EH}" rx="7" style="fill:{soft};stroke:{col}"/>'
            f'<text class="rtelab" x="14" y="24">{_html.escape(elabel)}</text>'
            f'<text class="rtegloss" x="14" y="42">{_html.escape(egloss)}</text>'
            f'<text class="rten" data-exit="{ekey}" x="{EW - 14}" y="27">—</text>'
            f'<text class="rtesh" data-exit="{ekey}" x="{EW - 14}" y="44">&#160;</text>'
            "</g>")
    parts.append("</svg>")

    first = have[0] if have else "cz"
    pills = "".join(
        f'<button class="rtpill{" on" if k == first else ""}" data-ed="{k}" '
        f'onclick="rtEdition(this)"{"" if k in have else " disabled"}>{_html.escape(name)}'
        f'<i>{_html.escape(title)}</i></button>'
        for k, name, _run, title in _RT_EDITIONS)
    sets = "".join(
        f'<button class="rtset{" on" if k == "gold" else ""}" data-set="{k}" '
        f'onclick="rtPages(this)">{_html.escape(label)}<i class="{states[k]}">{states[k]}</i></button>'
        for k, label, _state, _d in _RT_PAGESETS)

    if len(have) == len(_RT_EDITIONS):
        missing = ""
    elif not have:
        missing = ('<p class="note">No frozen run is present under <code>output/frozen/</code> '
                   "on this machine, so the chart draws the route without its numbers — run "
                   "notebook 15 and rebuild.</p>")
    else:
        missing = ('<p class="note">Only ' + " and ".join(_html.escape(names[k]) for k in have)
                   + " has been read on this machine, so the other edition's pill is disabled "
                     "and its numbers stay blank.</p>")

    payload = json.dumps({"runs": runs, "stages": info,
                          "sets": {k: dict(state=states[k], note=d) for k, _l, _s, d in _RT_PAGESETS}},
                         ensure_ascii=False)

    return (ix_head("The route a mark travels", ix=True, hover=True)
            + "<p>The eight steps below, and the four ways a mark can leave them. The spine "
              "is the runner's own order; the boxes on the right are the fates, with the "
              "share of marks that took each one in the run shown. Click a step for what it "
              "does and why it is there; the pills switch the edition and the page set. "
              "Every count is read from that run's own <code>final_inventory.csv</code> — "
              "the stages from <code>run_frozen.py</code>, nothing typed.</p>"
            + missing
            + f'<div class="rtctl"><span class="rtctll">Edition</span>{pills}'
              f'<span class="rtctll">Page set</span>{sets}</div>'
            + '<div class="rtlayout"><div class="rtwrap">' + "".join(parts) + "</div>"
            + '<aside class="rtpanel empty" id="rtpanel"><p class="pnote">Click a step for '
              "what it does, why it is there and the decisions that settled it. The four "
              "boxes on the right are the only ways a mark can be settled — the bar below "
              "carries their shares.</p></aside></div>"
            + '<div class="rtbar"><div class="rtbarhd">Of the <b id="rtbarn">—</b> marks '
              "this run settled, how each one was settled</div>"
              '<div class="rtmix" id="rtmix"></div><div class="rtmixlab" id="rtmixlab"></div>'
              '<p class="rtnote" id="rtnote"></p></div>'
            + f'<script>window.RT={payload};{_RT_JS}</script>')


# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Occupation → HISCO — the coding funnel, the class ladder, and the gradient
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# The sibling of `place_flow`, and the same argument in a different material: a birthplace
# resolves through tiers of decreasing confidence, and so does an occupation string. The
# difference worth drawing is what sits at the end — a place resolves to a district and
# stops, an occupation carries on into a social class, and the class is what the analysis
# actually consumes. So the figure is two columns: how the string was resolved, and where
# the resolved code landed on the ladder.

_OC_EX_N = 8                                    # example strings per stage in the panel

# HISCLASS 1–13 → the 5-class collapse, and one colour per collapsed group. Same mapping
# and same palette as the notebook 03 figures, so the site and the paper cannot disagree.
_OC_GROUP = {1: 1, 2: 1, 3: 2, 4: 2, 5: 2, 6: 2, 7: 3, 9: 3, 8: 4, 10: 5, 11: 5, 12: 5, 13: 5}
_OC_G_LABEL = {1: "Elite", 2: "Lower middle class", 3: "Skilled workers",
               4: "Farmers", 5: "Unskilled"}
_OC_G_COLOUR = {1: ("#dbe4ec", CU_NAVY), 2: ("#dfeaf1", "#3D7EA6"), 3: ("#e8eaec", CU_GREY),
                4: ("#e9edd8", "#8FA31E"), 5: ("#f7dfe2", CU_RED)}

# One row per matching rule, in the order `split_occupations` tries them — which is the
# order that matters, since an earlier rule wins and the later ones only ever see what it
# left. `keep` marks the rules the filter below can switch off; the empty-cell stage is a
# step in the funnel but not a tier anyone can choose to keep.
_OC_STAGES = [
    ("empty", "—", "No occupation recorded", "left &lt;NA&gt;, deliberately", False,
     "The field is blank on these records. <code>code_occupation(pd.NA)</code> returns "
     "<code>None</code> and <b>every</b> output column stays <code>&lt;NA&gt;</code> — "
     "asserted in the notebook 02 QA gate, because this is the exact shape of the "
     "2026-07 audit's worst defect, where ~26k empty cells were fabricated into a real "
     "exit code.",
     ["A missing occupation is missing. It is never imputed from rank, education or unit."],
     "occupations._norm → None"),
    ("exact", "exact", "The whole key is curated", "one dictionary entry, no compounding",
     True,
     "The normalised string <i>is</i> a curated key. Normalisation lowercases, splits on "
     "<code>, ; / -</code>, drops the connectors <i>a</i> / <i>i</i> / <i>nebo</i>, and "
     "expands abbreviations — but <b>only</b> tokens carrying a trailing period and only "
     "inside a longer phrase. Diacritics are kept, with a folded fallback at lookup.",
     ["Abbreviation stems that are themselves trades (<code>cihlář</code>, "
      "<code>stavitel</code>) are not expanded on the bare stem — the period is the anchor.",
      "An uncoded skeleton row behaves exactly like an absent one."],
     "occupations.split_occupations → \"exact\""),
    ("dual", "dual", "Two curated keys, both coded", "farms his fields and works a trade",
     True,
     "The string splits cleanly into two curated keys — <code>rolník zámečník</code>, "
     "<code>rolník a obuvník</code>. HISCO practice codes the first title; here "
     "<b>both</b> are coded, the second into the <code>*_2</code> columns, and which one "
     "matters is left to the analysis rather than decided by the parser.",
     ["The earliest split wins, which keeps the longest tail intact.",
      "<code>occupation_hisclass_high</code> carries the better of the two and never "
      "invents a class of its own — a QA invariant."],
     "occupations.split_occupations → \"dual\""),
    ("head", "head", "Adjective(s) + a curated head noun", "the head noun carries the code",
     True,
     "<code>mlynářský dělník</code> is a <i>dělník</i>; <code>tovární dozorce</code> is a "
     "<i>dozorce</i>. The longest matching suffix wins, so <code>obchodní příručí</code> "
     "is preferred over the bare <code>příručí</code> where both are curated.",
     ["Token boundaries only. <b>No substring test is ever performed</b> — this is the "
      "deliberate difference from <code>education.py</code>, and the reason "
      "<code>major</code> cannot be found inside <code>generálmajor</code>."],
     "occupations.split_occupations → \"head\""),
    ("prefix", "prefix", "A curated key + something uncurated", "the key carries it", True,
     "<code>soustružník železa</code> is a <i>soustružník</i> working a named material. "
     "The longest matching prefix wins. This is the weakest of the four rules and the "
     "first one an analysis should switch off — which is what the filter below is for.",
     ["Still token-bounded: the prefix must be a whole run of tokens that is itself a "
      "curated key."],
     "occupations.split_occupations → \"prefix\""),
]

_OC_TERMINAL = (
    "unmatched", "none", "No rule matched — left &lt;NA&gt;", "guessing is not coding",
    "The surviving tail averages barely over one record per distinct string: misspellings, "
    "one-off compounds and genuinely rare trades. It is left uncoded rather than guessed, "
    "the same policy <code>religion.py</code> follows. Fuzzy repair was considered and "
    "refused — an edit-distance rule that turns <code>rolnlík</code> into "
    "<code>rolník</code> would as happily turn one real trade into another, so the "
    "frequent misspellings are curated as <b>explicit</b> dictionary entries instead.",
    ["&lt;NA&gt; is a decision, not a gap."],
    "occupations.split_occupations → \"none\"")


def _occupation_frame() -> dict:
    """Everything the occupation figure needs, recomputed from ``data/final`` at build time.

    Returns a dict carrying the funnel counts (``t``), the HISCLASS ladder (``hc``), the
    per-tier × per-class desertion cells the live gradient sums over (``grad``), the
    commonest ``recorded string → English HISCO label`` pairs per tier (``ex``), and the
    per-class occupation mix (``cls``).

    The gradient is stored **disaggregated** — one cell per (match tier, HISCLASS-5) — so
    the browser can re-derive the whole chart for any subset of tiers without another
    build. That is the point of the figure: the robustness check this sheet argues in prose
    becomes something the reader can perform.
    """
    cols = ["occupation", "occupation_match", "occupation_hisco", "occupation_en",
            "occupation_hisclass", "occupation_hisclass_label", "occupation_hisclass_5",
            "occupation_status", "occupation_qualifier", "deserted", "theater"]
    have = [c for c in cols
            if c in pq.ParquetFile(FIN / "persons" / "legionnaires_clean.parquet").schema.names]
    df = pd.read_parquet(FIN / "persons" / "legionnaires_clean.parquet", columns=have)

    nonempty = df["occupation"].notna()
    out: dict = {"n": int(len(df)),
                 "n_nonempty": int(nonempty.sum()),
                 "t": {"empty": int((~nonempty).sum())},
                 "ex": {}, "grad": {}, "hc": {}, "cls": {}, "cls_rate": {}}

    # ── the funnel: one count and one example table per matching rule ───────────────
    for tier in ("exact", "dual", "head", "prefix"):
        sub = df[df["occupation_match"].eq(tier)]
        out["t"][tier] = int(len(sub))
        if "occupation_en" in sub:
            pairs = (pd.DataFrame({"a": sub["occupation"], "b": sub["occupation_en"]})
                     .dropna().value_counts().head(_OC_EX_N))
            out["ex"][tier] = [[str(a), str(b), int(v)] for (a, b), v in pairs.items()]

    # unmatched is nonempty-and-uncoded, which is exactly where occupation_match is null
    un = df[nonempty & df["occupation_match"].isna()]
    out["t"]["unmatched"] = int(len(un))
    out["ex"]["unmatched"] = [[str(a), "—", int(v)]
                              for a, v in un["occupation"].value_counts().head(_OC_EX_N).items()]
    out["n_distinct_un"] = int(un["occupation"].nunique())
    out["coded"] = int(df["occupation_hisco"].notna().sum())

    # ── the ladder: HISCLASS 1..13, plus what carries a code but deliberately no class ──
    lab = {}
    if "occupation_hisclass_label" in df:
        pair = df[["occupation_hisclass", "occupation_hisclass_label"]].dropna()
        lab = {int(k): str(v) for k, v in
               pair.drop_duplicates("occupation_hisclass").itertuples(index=False)}
    hc = df["occupation_hisclass"].dropna().astype(int)
    for k in range(1, 14):
        out["hc"][str(k)] = int((hc == k).sum())
    out["hc_label"] = {str(k): lab.get(k, f"Class {k}") for k in range(1, 14)}
    out["hc_noclass"] = int((df["occupation_hisco"].notna()
                             & df["occupation_hisclass"].isna()).sum())
    out["n_students"] = int(df["occupation_status"].astype("string").eq("41").sum()) \
        if "occupation_status" in df else 0

    for k in range(1, 14):
        m = df["occupation_hisclass"].eq(k)
        if not m.any():
            continue
        if "deserted" in df:
            out["cls_rate"][str(k)] = [int(m.sum()), int(df.loc[m, "deserted"].sum())]
        out["cls"][str(k)] = [[str(a), int(v)] for a, v in
                              df.loc[m, "occupation_en"].value_counts().head(6).items()]

    # ── the gradient cells: (match tier × HISCLASS-5) → [records, deserters] ────────
    # Kept as raw pairs rather than rates so the browser can pool any subset of tiers and
    # still get an honest Wilson interval out the other end.
    if {"occupation_hisclass_5", "deserted"} <= set(df.columns):
        g = df.dropna(subset=["occupation_hisclass_5", "occupation_match"])
        for tier in ("exact", "dual", "head", "prefix"):
            cell = {}
            s = g[g["occupation_match"].eq(tier)]
            for grp, part in s.groupby(s["occupation_hisclass_5"].astype(int)):
                cell[str(int(grp))] = [int(len(part)), int(part["deserted"].sum())]
            out["grad"][tier] = cell
    return out


def occupation_flow() -> str:
    """The coding funnel, the class ladder and the gradient the two of them produce.

    Three things prose cannot do on this sheet. **The funnel** carries the residual down
    the left as a tapering ribbon, so the fact that one rule does five sixths of the work
    is visible before a number is read. **The ladder** shows where the codes land, and in
    particular how much of the Legion sits on two rungs. **The filter** turns this sheet's
    own robustness claim into an action: untick the compound rules, and the desertion
    gradient below redraws on exact dictionary matches alone — with Wilson intervals, so
    the shrinking sample argues for itself.

    Every count, ribbon width and example string is recomputed from ``data/final`` at build
    time, so the picture cannot drift from the data it describes.
    """
    F = _occupation_frame()
    n, ne = F["n"], F["n_nonempty"]

    BW, BH, VG, TOP = 300, 54, 15, 104
    LX, RW, SPD = 74, 40, 50                   # box left edge · max ribbon width · its offset
    LADX, LADW = 452, 250                      # the HISCLASS ladder column
    W, H = LADX + LADW + 108, TOP + (len(_OC_STAGES) + 1) * (BH + VG) + 40

    rows = _OC_STAGES + [(_OC_TERMINAL[0], _OC_TERMINAL[1], _OC_TERMINAL[2], _OC_TERMINAL[3],
                          False, _OC_TERMINAL[4], _OC_TERMINAL[5], _OC_TERMINAL[6])]

    def wide(v: int) -> float:
        return max(0.7, RW * v / max(n, 1))

    # ── the ribbon: what is still uncoded, as a staircase area ─────────────────────
    # Left edge straight, right edge stepping inward. The step at a stage IS what that
    # stage coded, so `exact` collapsing the ribbon almost to nothing is the finding.
    d, run = [f"M{LX - SPD},{TOP - VG}", f"L{LX - SPD + wide(n):.1f},{TOP - VG}"], n
    for i, row in enumerate(rows):
        y = TOP + i * (BH + VG) + BH / 2
        d.append(f"L{LX - SPD + wide(run):.1f},{y:.0f}")
        run -= F["t"].get(row[0], 0)
        d.append(f"L{LX - SPD + wide(run):.1f},{y:.0f}")
    y_end = TOP + len(rows) * (BH + VG) - VG / 2
    d += [f"L{LX - SPD + wide(run):.1f},{y_end:.0f}", f"L{LX - SPD},{y_end:.0f}Z"]

    parts = [f'<svg id="ocsvg" viewBox="0 0 {W} {H}" width="{W}" height="{H}" '
             'xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><defs>'
             '<marker id="ocar" viewBox="0 0 8 8" refX="7" refY="4" markerWidth="7" '
             'markerHeight="7" orient="auto"><path d="M0,0 L8,4 L0,8z" fill="#b4bcc2"/></marker>'
             "</defs>",
             f'<path class="ocrib" d="{"".join(d)}"/>',
             f'<text class="ochead" x="{LX}" y="46">EVERY RECORD → A HISCO CODE</text>',
             f'<text class="ocsub" x="{LX}" y="64">rules in the order the matcher tries them; '
             "an earlier rule wins</text>",
             f'<text class="ocribcap" x="{LX - SPD}" y="{TOP - VG - 9}">{n:,} in</text>',
             f'<text class="ochead" x="{LADX}" y="46">WHERE THE CODE LANDS</text>',
             f'<text class="ocsub" x="{LADX}" y="64">HISCLASS, coloured by the 5-class '
             "collapse</text>"]

    info: dict[str, dict] = {}
    biggest = max((F["t"].get(r[0], 0) for r in rows), default=1)
    for i, (key, tier, label, slab, keep, what, refus, sym) in enumerate(rows):
        y = TOP + i * (BH + VG)
        cnt = F["t"].get(key, 0)
        fill, stroke = (("#f4f5f7", "#8a939c") if tier in ("—", "none")
                        else _TIER_COLOUR.get("okres", ("#dbe4ec", CU_NAVY)))
        if tier in ("dual", "head"):
            fill, stroke = "#dfeaf1", "#3D7EA6"
        elif tier == "prefix":
            fill, stroke = "#f6ecd9", "#c7a548"
        if i:
            parts.append(f'<path class="ocarrow" d="M{LX + BW / 2:.0f},{y - VG} '
                         f'L{LX + BW / 2:.0f},{y - 3}" marker-end="url(#ocar)"/>')
        tick = ""
        if keep:
            tick = ('<g class="ockeepbox" onclick="ocKeep(event,this)">'
                    f'<rect x="10" y="{BH / 2 - 8:.0f}" width="16" height="16" rx="4"/>'
                    f'<path class="octick" d="M14,{BH / 2:.0f} l3,3.4 l6.5,-7.6"/>'
                    "<title>Tick to keep this rule in the sample below</title></g>")
        tx = 34 if keep else 12
        dash = ';stroke-dasharray:4 3' if tier in ("—", "none") else ""
        parts.append(
            f'<g class="ocstage{" term" if tier in ("—", "none") else ""}" data-id="{key}" '
            f'data-tier="{tier}"{" data-keep=\"1\"" if keep else ""} '
            f'transform="translate({LX},{y})" onclick="ocPick(this)">'
            f'<rect class="ocbox" width="{BW}" height="{BH}" rx="6" '
            f'style="fill:{fill};stroke:{stroke}{dash}"/>' + tick +
            f'<text class="oclab" x="{tx}" y="21">{label}</text>'
            # the empty-cell row is a share of *everything*; every rule below it is a share
            # of the non-empty values it actually runs on
            f'<text class="ocstat" x="{tx}" y="37">{cnt:,} · '
            f'{_pct(cnt, n) if key == "empty" else _pct(cnt, ne)}'
            f'{" of all records" if key == "empty" else " of non-empty"}</text>'
            f'<text class="octier" x="{BW - 12}" y="21">{tier}</text>'
            f'<text class="ocslab" x="{BW - 12}" y="37">{slab}</text>'
            f'<rect class="ocbart" x="{tx}" y="{BH - 12}" width="{BW - tx - 12}" height="4" '
            'rx="2"/>'
            f'<rect class="ocbarv" x="{tx}" y="{BH - 12}" '
            f'width="{(BW - tx - 12) * cnt / max(biggest, 1):.1f}" height="4" rx="2" '
            f'style="fill:{stroke}"><title>this rule against the largest</title>'
            "</rect></g>")
        if refus:
            cx, cy = LX + BW + 24, y + BH / 2
            parts.append(f'<g class="ocveto"><path class="ocvl" d="M{LX + BW},{cy} '
                         f'L{cx - 11},{cy}"/><circle cx="{cx}" cy="{cy}" r="11"/>'
                         f'<text x="{cx}" y="{cy + 4}">⊘</text>'
                         f'<title>{len(refus)} refusal rule(s) — click the stage</title></g>')
        info[key] = dict(kind="stage", label=label, tier=tier, sub=slab, what=what,
                         refus=refus, sym=sym, n=cnt)

    # ── the ladder: 13 rungs plus the deliberate no-class outflow ───────────────────
    LADT, RH, RG = TOP, 22, 5
    mx = max(list(F["hc"].values()) + [1])
    for k in range(1, 14):
        cnt = F["hc"][str(k)]
        y = LADT + (k - 1) * (RH + RG)
        fill, stroke = _OC_G_COLOUR[_OC_GROUP[k]]
        # Rung subtitle used to be the class's mean HISCAM. HISCAM was dropped in
        # occupations 1.2.0 (DECISIONS D-30) for being non-monotonic on this sample, so
        # the rung now carries the thing the sheet is actually arguing about.
        _cr = F["cls_rate"].get(str(k))
        _sub = f"{_cr[1] / _cr[0]:.2%} deserted" if _cr and _cr[0] else "—"
        info[f"c{k}"] = dict(kind="class", label=f"{k}. {F['hc_label'][str(k)]}",
                             tier=_OC_G_LABEL[_OC_GROUP[k]], sub=_sub, n=cnt)
        parts.append(
            f'<g class="occls" data-id="c{k}" transform="translate({LADX},{y})" '
            f'onclick="ocPick(this)">'
            f'<rect class="ocrowhit" x="-4" y="-2" width="{LADW + 60}" height="{RH + 4}" rx="4"/>'
            f'<text class="ocno" x="0" y="15">{k}</text>'
            f'<rect class="ocrung" x="18" y="4" width="{max(1.5, (LADW - 30) * cnt / mx):.1f}" '
            f'height="{RH - 8}" rx="3" style="fill:{fill};stroke:{stroke}"/>'
            f'<text class="occnt" x="{LADW + 52}" y="15">{cnt:,}</text>'
            f'<title>{_html.escape(F["hc_label"][str(k)])} — {cnt:,} '
            f'({_pct(cnt, sum(F["hc"].values()))})</title></g>')
    y = LADT + 13 * (RH + RG) + 8
    parts.append(
        f'<g class="occls term" data-id="noclass" transform="translate({LADX},{y})" '
        f'onclick="ocPick(this)">'
        f'<rect class="ocrowhit" x="-4" y="-2" width="{LADW + 60}" height="{RH + 4}" rx="4"/>'
        f'<text class="ocno" x="0" y="15">−1</text>'
        f'<rect class="ocrung dash" x="18" y="4" '
        f'width="{max(1.5, (LADW - 30) * F["hc_noclass"] / mx):.1f}" height="{RH - 8}" rx="3"/>'
        f'<text class="occnt" x="{LADW + 52}" y="15">{F["hc_noclass"]:,}</text></g>')
    parts.append(f'<text class="ocsub" x="{LADX}" y="{y + 42}">a code, but no class — '
                 "students and the other deliberate −1s</text>")
    info["noclass"] = dict(
        kind="class", label="Coded, but deliberately no class", tier="by design",
        sub="HISCO −1 with a status modifier", n=F["hc_noclass"],
        what="HISCO does not treat study as an occupation, and the HSN scheme excludes "
             f"status 41 from HISCLASS. The {F['n_students']:,} students therefore carry a "
             "code and a status but <b>no</b> social class — they stay identifiable through "
             "<code>occupation_status</code> rather than being dropped or forced onto a "
             "rung. Any value on <i>relation</i> is excluded the same way.",
        refus=["This is why HISCLASS coverage sits below HISCO coverage. The gap is a "
               "decision, not a shortfall."],
        sym="occupations._scales")
    parts.append("</svg>")

    payload = {k: F[k] for k in ("n", "n_nonempty", "t", "hc", "hc_label", "hc_noclass",
                                 "cls", "cls_rate", "ex", "grad", "coded",
                                 "n_distinct_un", "n_students")}
    payload["info"] = info
    payload["glabel"] = {str(k): v for k, v in _OC_G_LABEL.items()}
    payload["gcolour"] = {str(k): list(v) for k, v in _OC_G_COLOUR.items()}

    legend = "".join(
        f'<span class="oclg"><span class="sw" style="background:{_OC_G_COLOUR[g][0]};'
        f'border-color:{_OC_G_COLOUR[g][1]}"></span>{_OC_G_LABEL[g]}</span>'
        for g in (1, 2, 3, 4, 5))
    panel = ('<aside class="pfpanel empty" id="ocpanel"><p class="pnote">Click a rule for what '
             "it does, what it refuses, which function owns it — and the strings it actually "
             "matched. Click a rung for the trades on it.</p></aside>")

    return (
        ix_head("How a Czech word becomes a social class", ix=True, hover=True)
        + '<p class="note">One lane, four rules, tried in the order shown — <b>an earlier rule '
        "wins, and the later ones only ever see what it left</b>. The ribbon down the left is "
        "what is <i>still uncoded</i>; every step in it is a rule doing its work, and the bar "
        "inside a box is that rule against the largest. ⊘ marks a stage with explicit refusal "
        "rules. On the right, where the resolved codes land on the HISCLASS ladder. "
        "<b>Click</b> anything for the detail; <b>untick</b> a rule to drop it from the "
        "gradient below.</p>"
        f'<div class="pfbar"><span class="pflgs">{legend}</span></div>'
        f'<script>window.OC={json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False)};</script>'
        f'<div class="pflayout"><div class="pfwrap">{"".join(parts)}</div>{panel}</div>'
        + ix_head("Does the coding drive the result?", level=3, ix=True, hover=True)
        + '<p class="note">The three compound rules — <code>dual</code>, <code>head</code>, '
        "<code>prefix</code> — are the least externally-anchored part of this method: nothing "
        "outside the project vouches for them the way the German bridge and OccCANINE vouch "
        "for the codes themselves. So the question worth asking is whether they are "
        "<i>manufacturing</i> the class gradient. Untick them and watch. The rates are "
        "unadjusted means with 95% Wilson intervals, which is the interval that behaves when "
        "the sample shrinks and the event is rare — as the bars widen rather than move, that "
        "is the answer.</p>"
        '<div class="pfkeep" id="ockeep"><div class="pfkeepn" id="ockeepn"></div>'
        '<div class="pfkeepact"><button class="wfbtn sm" onclick="ocAll(1)">All rules</button>'
        '<button class="wfbtn sm" onclick="ocAll(0)">Exact only</button>'
        '<button class="wfbtn sm" onclick="ocCopyMask(this)">Copy the mask</button></div>'
        '<div class="ocgrad" id="ocgrad"></div>'
        '<pre class="pfmask"><code id="ocmaskc"></code></pre></div>'
        '<p class="note">The rule that fired is a single column in the data '
        "(<code>occupation_match</code>), which is what makes the filter above reproducible "
        "in three lines. Russia carries essentially all Legion desertion, so these levels are "
        "descriptive only — they are not conditioned on theatre, enrolment date or unit.</p>"
        "<hr>")


# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Rank ladders — the two armies bridged by the common scale
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
_PATHS = [
    ("I want the numbers", "what the data says", CU_NAVY,
     ["descriptives", "variables", "dictionary"]),
    ("I want the method", "how it was built", "#5f89a8",
     ["pipeline", "places", "ranks", "units"]),
    ("I want to trust it", "why it holds", "#c7a548",
     ["qa", "validation", "decisions"]),
]


def reading_map() -> str:
    """Three routes through the sheets, for a reader meeting a 55-item sidebar cold.

    The sidebar is complete but unordered — it says what exists, not where to start. These
    are the three questions people actually arrive with.
    """
    titles = {s["id"]: s["title"] for s in SHEETS}
    NW, NH, GAP, LX, RH, TOP = 122, 40, 22, 172, 62, 52
    W = LX + 4 * NW + 3 * GAP + 20
    H = TOP + len(_PATHS) * RH + 10
    svg = [f'<svg id="pathmap" viewBox="0 0 {W} {H}" width="{W}" height="{H}" '
           'xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><defs>'
           '<marker id="pmar" viewBox="0 0 8 8" refX="7" refY="4" markerWidth="6" '
           'markerHeight="6" orient="auto"><path d="M0,0 L8,4 L0,8z" fill="#b4bcc2"/></marker>'
           '</defs><text class="pmh" x="0" y="24">START HERE</text>']
    for r, (q, gloss, col, ids) in enumerate(_PATHS):
        y = TOP + r * RH
        svg.append(f'<text class="pmq" x="0" y="{y + 20}">{_html.escape(q)}</text>'
                   f'<text class="pmg" x="0" y="{y + 34}">{_html.escape(gloss)}</text>')
        for i, sid in enumerate(ids):
            x = LX + i * (NW + GAP)
            if i:
                svg.append(f'<path class="pmarrow" d="M{x - GAP + 2},{y + NH / 2:.0f} '
                           f'L{x - 4},{y + NH / 2:.0f}" marker-end="url(#pmar)"/>')
            svg.append(
                f'<a href="#{sid}"><g class="pmnode" transform="translate({x},{y})">'
                f'<rect width="{NW}" height="{NH}" rx="5" style="stroke:{col}"/>'
                f'<text x="{NW / 2:.0f}" y="{NH / 2 + 4:.0f}">'
                f'{_html.escape(titles.get(sid, sid))}</text></g></a>')
    svg.append("</svg>")
    return ('<h2>Where to start</h2>'
            '<p class="note">Three routes through the sheets, for the three questions readers '
            "arrive with. Click any box.</p>"
            f'<div class="pmwrap">{"".join(svg)}</div>')


def ranks_bridge() -> str:
    """Habsburg ladder ↔ common grade ↔ Legion ladder, in one picture.

    ``rank_reset`` is a subtraction — ``legion_common − habsburg_common`` — but the prose
    below has to establish two ladders, a common scale and a NATO band before that sentence
    means anything. Drawn side by side the subtraction is simply a step up or down the middle
    column. The ladders are **imported** from ``utils.parsing.ranks``: this figure cannot
    disagree with the parser, because it is reading the parser's own tables.
    """
    from utils.parsing.ranks import (NONCOMBAT_STATUS, RANK_COMMON, RANK_EN_HABSBURG,
                                     RANK_EN_LEGION, RANK_ORDINAL_HABSBURG,
                                     RANK_ORDINAL_LEGION, _COMMON_TO_BAND)

    L = pd.read_parquet(FIN / "persons" / "legionnaires_clean.parquet")
    cols = set(L.columns)
    hn = L["habsburg_rank_clean"].value_counts().to_dict() if "habsburg_rank_clean" in cols else {}
    ln = L["legion_rank_clean"].value_counts().to_dict() if "legion_rank_clean" in cols else {}

    # The reset read in both directions. Forward (click a Habsburg rank): where those men
    # landed. Backward (click a Legion rank): where they came from — the same joint
    # distribution, conditioned the other way, which is the question the endogeneity story
    # actually asks ("who ends up a private?").
    dest: dict[str, dict] = {}
    orig: dict[str, dict] = {}
    need = {"habsburg_rank_clean", "legion_rank_clean", "rank_reset"}
    if need <= cols:
        keep = ["habsburg_rank_clean", "legion_rank_clean", "rank_reset"]
        sub = L.loc[L["habsburg_rank_clean"].notna() & L["legion_rank_clean"].notna(), keep]

        def _summarise(by: str, other: str, into: dict) -> None:
            for name, g in sub.groupby(by, observed=True):
                r = pd.to_numeric(g["rank_reset"], errors="coerce")
                top = g[other].value_counts().head(3)
                into[str(name)] = dict(
                    n=int(len(g)),
                    down=int((r < 0).sum()), same=int((r == 0).sum()), up=int((r > 0).sum()),
                    top=[[str(k), int(v)] for k, v in top.items()])

        _summarise("habsburg_rank_clean", "legion_rank_clean", dest)
        _summarise("legion_rank_clean", "habsburg_rank_clean", orig)

    # Senior ranks are so thin that aggregates are not checkable — a "31 majors" bar hides
    # whether those are 31 real majors or a parser artefact. For OF-3 and above, list the
    # records themselves so each one can be opened at source. IDs only, no names: the
    # published page stays free of named individuals.
    SENIOR_FROM = 15                                   # common grade 15 = OF-3 (major)
    roster: dict[str, list] = {}
    if {"legion_id"} <= cols:
        for side, rc in (("h", "habsburg_rank_clean"), ("l", "legion_rank_clean")):
            if rc not in cols:
                continue
            snr = L[L[rc].map(lambda v: RANK_COMMON.get(v, 0) >= SENIOR_FROM
                              if isinstance(v, str) else False)]
            for name, g in snr.groupby(rc, observed=True):
                rows = []
                for _, r in g.iterrows():
                    other = r.get("legion_rank_clean" if side == "h" else "habsburg_rank_clean")
                    rows.append([
                        "" if pd.isna(r["legion_id"]) else str(r["legion_id"]),
                        "" if pd.isna(r.get("birth_year")) else str(int(r["birth_year"])),
                        "" if not isinstance(other, str) else other,
                        "" if pd.isna(r.get("theater")) else str(r.get("theater")),
                    ])
                roster[f"{side}:{name}"] = sorted(rows, key=lambda x: x[0])

    # ── layout: one band per common grade, tall enough for whichever side has more labels ──
    by_grade: dict[int, tuple[list, list]] = {}
    unmapped: dict[str, list[str]] = {"Habsburg": [], "Legion": []}
